scope_rule: A tagged theorem represents only its stated hypotheses and conclusions. Presence of a statement does not assert full coverage of a catalogue family.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_const
declarations.doc: Constant random variables converge in probability to their constant value.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_mEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.23: consistency from uniform convergence and a separated maximum. Pointwise bounds avoid any unmentioned measurability of a supremum.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_pearson_statistic
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.31: Pearson's chi-squared statistic `∑ (Nᵢ - n pᵢ)² / (n pᵢ)` for i.i.d. observations with `k ≥ 2` categories of positive probabilities `pᵢ` converges in law to `χ²_{k-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_argmax_of_compact
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.33, the argmax theorem with a deterministic limit on a compact space. If the criteria `Mₙ` converge uniformly in probability to a continuous `M` with a unique maximizer `θ`, then maximizers `Tₙ` of `Mₙ` converge in probability to `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCDF
declarations.doc: The empirical distribution function `t ↦ #{i < n | X i ω ≤ t} / n` of the first `n` real observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleQuantile
declarations.doc: The left empirical `p`-quantile `inf {t | p ≤ Fₙ(t)}`; it is used for nonempty samples and probabilities in `(0, 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.uStatistic
declarations.doc: The U-statistic of order `m` with kernel `h`: the average of `h (x ∘ f)` over the injections `f : Fin m → Fin n` (ordered `m`-tuples of distinct indices).

declarations.name: CKSD.IsContiguous
declarations.doc: Contiguity of `Q n` with respect to `P n` (written `Q n ◁ P n`) on a common measurable space: `P n (A n) → 0` implies `Q n (A n) → 0` for measurable sets `A n`. For probability measures it is Statlib's `Contiguous5` (`CKSD.isContiguous_iff_contiguous5`).

declarations.name: CKSD.kolmogorovDistance
declarations.doc: The Kolmogorov distance `sup_t |F_P(t) - F_Q(t)|` between laws on the line, with the distribution functions `ProbabilityTheory.cdf`; their values lie in `[0, 1]`, so the real supremum is that of a bounded set.

declarations.name: CKSD.huberScore
declarations.doc: The Huber score `ψ_k(x) = max (-k) (min k x)`, the identity clipped to `[-k, k]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_of_tendstoInMeasure_sub_of_measurable
declarations.doc: Slutsky-type perturbation: if `Xₙ` converges in law to `Z` and `Yₙ - Xₙ` converges to `0` in probability, then `Yₙ` converges in law to `Z`. This generalizes Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.tendstoInDistribution_of_tendstoInMeasure_sub` for measurable `Xₙ` and `Yₙ`: no second countability of `F` is assumed (Mathlib uses it for the measurability of `Yₙ - Xₙ`); the difference need not be measurable, since convergence in measure is measured by the outer measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_measureReal_lt_norm_le_of_tendstoInDistribution
declarations.doc: A sequence converging in law is bounded in probability in norm: for every `ε > 0` there is `M > 0` with `P(‖Xₙ‖ > M) ≤ ε` eventually.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_zero_of_forall_eventually_le
declarations.doc: A nonnegative real sequence that is eventually below every positive level tends to `0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_delta_method_remainder
declarations.doc: The remainder of the delta method is negligible in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_delta_method
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.1: the delta method and its stochastic linearization in Banach spaces. If `√n (Tₙ - θ)` converges in law to `Z`, then `√n (g Tₙ - g θ)` converges in law to `D Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_add_zero
declarations.doc: Sum of two sequences tending to `0` in probability tends to `0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_in_measure_zero_of_abs_le
declarations.doc: Domination: if eventually, for almost every `ω`, `|Yₙ| ≤ |Xₙ|` whenever `|Uₙ| < δ`, and `Xₙ, Uₙ → 0` in probability, then `Yₙ → 0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_const_of_tendsto
declarations.doc: A deterministic sequence tending to `0` tends to `0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_comp_of_continuousAt
declarations.doc: Continuous mapping for convergence in probability to a constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_const_mul_zero
declarations.doc: Constant multiples preserve convergence to `0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.isBoundedInProbability_of_tendstoInDistribution
declarations.doc: A real sequence converging in law is bounded in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.isBoundedInProbability_of_tendstoInMeasure
declarations.doc: A real sequence converging in probability to a constant is bounded in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_mul_zero_of_isBoundedInProbability
declarations.doc: A sequence bounded in probability times a sequence tending to `0` in probability tends to `0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIndependentIdenticallyDistributed.pairwise_indepFun_comp
declarations.doc: Measurable real statistics `s ∘ X i` of an i.i.d. sequence are pairwise independent.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIndependentIdenticallyDistributed.identDistrib_comp
declarations.doc: Measurable real statistics `s ∘ X i` of an i.i.d. sequence are identically distributed.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sampleMean_of_iid
declarations.doc: Weak law of large numbers for a measurable integrable statistic of an iid sequence, in the form of convergence in probability, deduced from Mathlib's strong law.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_inv_sqrt_mul_sum_of_iid
declarations.doc: Central limit theorem for a centred square-integrable measurable statistic `s` of an iid sequence with law `P`, with limit law `N(0, ∫ s² dP)`; an adapter for Mathlib's `tendstoInDistribution_inv_sqrt_mul_sum_sub`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleEmpiricalCDF
declarations.doc: Empirical distribution function of a finite sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteSampleMean
declarations.doc: Mean of a finite sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteSampleSD
declarations.doc: Standard deviation of a finite sample with divisor `n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.supEDist
declarations.doc: Extended supremum distance between real functions on the line.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBoundedLipschitzOne
declarations.doc: Test functions of the bounded Lipschitz metric: bounded by one and `1`-Lipschitz for the supremum distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.bootstrapEmpiricalProcess
declarations.doc: The bootstrap empirical process `√n (F*ₙ - Fₙ)` of the resample `x ∘ σ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.bootstrapBoundedLipschitzDistance
declarations.doc: Bounded Lipschitz distance between the conditional law of the bootstrap empirical process given the sample `x` and the law of a process `Z` on `(Ω', P')`. The conditional expectation is the average over all `n^n` resampling index maps.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbability_bootstrapBoundedLipschitzDistance
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.52: conditional convergence of the bootstrap empirical process. For iid real observations with distribution function `F`, the bounded Lipschitz distance between the conditional law of `√n (F*ₙ - Fₙ)` and the law of the `F`-Brownian bridge `B⁰ ∘ F` tends to zero in outer probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.studentized_bootstrap_mean_second_order_accuracy
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.60, for the studentized mean in dimension one (`d = 1`, `g = id`). Assume all moments are finite, the variance is positive, and Cramér's condition holds for `(X, X²)`. With `T = √n (X̄ - μ)/σ̂` and its resampling analogue `T* = √n (X̄* - X̄)/σ̂*`: the Kolmogorov distance between the conditional law of `T*` and the law of `T` is `O_P(n⁻¹)`; the Kolmogorov distance between the law of `T` and `N(0,1)` is `n^{-1/2} sup_x |p₁(x) φ(x)| + o(n^{-1/2})` with `p₁(x) = γ (2x² + 1)/6`, `γ` the skewness; and the one-sided percentile-`t` interval `(-∞, X̄ - n^{-1/2} σ̂ v̂_α]` has coverage `1 - α + O(n⁻¹)`. The coverage statements for the normal-theory, percentile, two-sided, and symmetric intervals are outside this scope.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_measure_exists_abs_sub_of_convexOn
declarations.doc: **Convexity lemma, uniform part.** If random convex functions `gₙ` on a finite-dimensional space converge pointwise in probability to a continuous function `q`, then the convergence is uniform on every ball: `μ {ω | ∃ h, ‖h‖ ≤ R ∧ ε ≤ |gₙ ω h - q h|} → 0` for all `R` and `ε > 0`. No measurability in `ω` is assumed; the measure is the outer measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_lt_of_convexOn_of_abs_sub_lt
declarations.doc: **Convexity lemma, deterministic argmin bound.** Let `f` be convex and uniformly within `c δ² / 4` of the quadratic `C + ½ ⟪h - β, A (h - β)⟫` on the closed ball of radius `δ` about `β`, where `⟪h, A h⟫ ≥ c ‖h‖²`. Then every `α` with `f α ≤ f β` satisfies `‖α - β‖ < δ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sub_of_convexOn_of_isMinOn
declarations.doc: **Convexity lemma, basic corollary** (Hjort–Pollard). Let `Zₙ` be random convex functions on a finite-dimensional inner product space with `Zₙ(h) = -⟪Uₙ, h⟫ + ½ ⟪h, A h⟫ + rₙ(h)` where `rₙ(h) → 0` in probability for each `h`, `Uₙ` is bounded in probability, and `A` is self-adjoint with `⟪h, A h⟫ ≥ c ‖h‖²`, `c > 0`, with right inverse `B`. Then every (almost sure) minimizer `αₙ` of `Zₙ` satisfies `αₙ - B Uₙ → 0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_sq_inv_sqrt_mul_inner
declarations.doc: The weighted sum of squared scaled predictors is the quadratic form of the weighted design moment matrix: `∑ᵢ wᵢ (n^{-1/2} ⟪xᵢ, h⟫)² = hᵀ (n⁻¹ ∑ᵢ wᵢ xᵢ xᵢᵀ) h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_sum_mul_sq_inv_sqrt_mul_inner
declarations.doc: Convergence of the weighted design moment matrices gives convergence of the weighted sums of squared scaled predictors to the limiting quadratic form.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_inv_sqrt_smul_sum_smul
declarations.doc: **Central limit theorem for the weighted score.** Let `eᵢ` be independent, with `ψ(eᵢ)` centred, of common variance `σ²`, and with uniformly integrable squares. If `n⁻¹ ∑_{i<n} xᵢ xᵢᵀ → D₀` and `maxᵢ ‖xᵢ‖ / √n → 0`, then `n^{-1/2} ∑_{i<n} ψ(eᵢ) xᵢ ⇒ N(0, σ² D₀)`. The proof applies the Lindeberg–Feller theorem to every scalar projection and concludes by the Cramér–Wold device.

declarations.name: CKSD.add_mul_sub_le_of_convexOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt
declarations.doc: A convex function on `ℝ` lies above its right-derivative tangent lines: if `ψ u` is the right derivative of the convex function `ρ` at `u`, then `ρ u + ψ u (v - u) ≤ ρ v` for all `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.monotone_of_convexOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt
declarations.doc: The right derivative of a convex function on `ℝ` is monotone.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_remainder_sub_le
declarations.doc: **Curvature of the expected convex loss.** Let `ρ` be convex on `ℝ` with right derivative `ψ`, `Z ∼ P` with `E ψ(Z) = 0`, and suppose that `G(s) = E ψ(Z - s)` satisfies `|G(s) + γ s| ≤ η |s|` for `|s| ≤ |t|`. Then the expected remainder satisfies `|E [ρ(Z - t) - ρ(Z) + t ψ(Z)] - γ t² / 2| ≤ η t²`. The proof writes the remainder as `∫₀ᵗ (ψ(Z) - ψ(Z - s)) ds` and exchanges the integrals.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_pos_mul_sq_le_inner_toEuclideanCLM
declarations.doc: A positive definite matrix `D` has a uniformly positive quadratic form: `⟪h, D h⟫ ≥ c ‖h‖²` for some `c > 0` (the least eigenvalue).

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_and_tendstoInDistribution_convexRegression
declarations.doc: **Asymptotics of fixed-design convex regression M-estimators.** Let `eᵢ` be independent errors and `ρ` a convex loss with subgradient `ψ` (`ρ v ≥ ρ u + ψ u (v - u)`), with * `ψ(eᵢ)` centred, square integrable with variance `σ²`, with uniformly integrable squares; * `L²` continuity uniform in `i`: `E (ψ(eᵢ - t) - ψ(eᵢ))² → 0` as `t → 0`; * uniform curvature: `E [ρ(eᵢ - t) - ρ(eᵢ) + t ψ(eᵢ)] = γᵢ t² / 2 + o(t²)` uniformly in `i`; * design: `n⁻¹ ∑ xᵢ xᵢᵀ → D₀`, `n⁻¹ ∑ γᵢ xᵢ xᵢᵀ → D₁ ≻ 0`, `maxᵢ ‖xᵢ‖ / √n → 0`. Then every measurable minimizer `T̂ₙ` of `b ↦ ∑_{i<n} ρ(eᵢ - ⟪xᵢ, b - β⟫)` satisfies `√n (T̂ₙ - β) - D₁⁻¹ n^{-1/2} ∑ ψ(eᵢ) xᵢ → 0` in probability, `n^{-1/2} ∑ ψ(eᵢ) xᵢ ⇒ N(0, σ² D₀)` and `√n (T̂ₙ - β) ⇒ N(0, σ² D₁⁻¹ D₀ D₁⁻¹)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.residualKernel
declarations.doc: The residual kernel records the output minus the observed input.

declarations.name: CKSD.residualKernel_apply
declarations.doc: A residual row is the translated output distribution.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_kernel_of_bounded_complete
declarations.doc: A boundedly complete family identifies Markov kernels up to almost-everywhere equality.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_kernel_of_multivariateGaussian_comp_eq
declarations.doc: Equal randomizations of every nondegenerate Gaussian shift identify their kernels Lebesgue-almost everywhere.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_covariant_kernel_of_gaussian_shift_laws
declarations.doc: Gaussian shift equivariance forces almost-everywhere translation covariance of the randomization kernel.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_residualKernel_add_eq_of_ae_covariant
declarations.doc: Translation covariance of output rows makes the corresponding residual rows invariant.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_map_add_of_residualKernel_ae_eq_const
declarations.doc: A constant residual law gives the original kernel rows as translates of that law.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_convolution_of_gaussian_shift_kernel
declarations.doc: Every equivariant Gaussian randomization has an independent-noise convolution law.

declarations.name: CKSD.TendstoInProbabilityZeroENNReal
declarations.doc: Convergence to zero in (outer) probability of nonnegative extended-real random quantities. An infinite value counts as exceeding every threshold.

declarations.name: CKSD.missingDataObservation
declarations.doc: Observed part `(R, X, R Y)` of a full-data triple `(R, X, Y)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.crossFittedAverage_missingMean_asymptotically_linear
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.39: asymptotic linearity of the cross-fitted augmented inverse-probability estimator of a missing mean. The full-data triples `(R, X, Y)` are iid with law `P`, the response is missing at random with propensity `π₀`, and `m₀` is the regression of `Y` on `X`, both expressed by their defining integral identities. The estimators `(m̂, π̂)` on fold `k` are computed from the observed data `(R, X, RY)` outside fold `k`. On each fold the `L²(P_X)` errors of `m̂` and `π̂` tend to zero in probability, their product is `o_P(n^{-1/2})`, and the `L²(P)` distance between the estimated and true scores, with the nuisance estimates held fixed, tends to zero in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.SatisfiesCramerCondition
declarations.doc: Cramér's condition `limsup_{‖t‖→∞} |E e^{i⟨t,X⟩}| < 1`, in the equivalent form of a uniform bound by a constant `c < 1` outside a ball.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_edgeworth_expansion_smooth_function_of_means
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.50: Edgeworth expansion of order `j` for a smooth function of a vector mean. Here `A` has `j+2` continuous derivatives on a neighbourhood of the mean `m`, `A m = 0`, and `σ² = ∇A(m)ᵀ Σ ∇A(m)` is written as the variance of the linear statistic `DA(m) X`. Under a moment of order `j+2` and Cramér's condition, there are polynomials `p_r`, `1 ≤ r ≤ j`, of degree at most `3r-1` and of parity opposite to `r`, such that the distribution function of `√n A(X̄)/σ` equals `Φ + Σ_r n^{-r/2} p_r φ` up to `o(n^{-j/2})` uniformly. The identification of the coefficients of `p_r` through the moments of order at most `r+2` and the derivatives of `A` is outside this scope.

declarations.name: CKSD.saddlepoint_approximation_sampleAverage_density
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.55: the saddlepoint approximation to the density of a sample mean. The cumulant generating function `K = cgf id P` is finite near the origin, `ŝ` lies in the interior of its domain with `K'(ŝ) = x`, `P` has a density, and the normalized tilted characteristic function `t ↦ |E e^{(ŝ+it)X}| / E e^{ŝX}` is in `L^ν` for some `ν ≥ 1`. Then for `n > ν` the mean of `n` observations has a continuous density `fₙ`, bounded when the characteristic function of `X` is also in `L^ν`, and `fₙ(x) = (n/(2π K''(ŝ)))^{1/2} e^{n(K(ŝ)-ŝx)} (1 + O(1/n))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isContiguous_of_integral_likelihood_ratio_limit_eq_one
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.12: Le Cam's first lemma, for absolutely continuous alternatives. If `Q n ≪ P n` and the likelihood ratios `dQ n / dP n` under `P n` converge in law to a limit `ν` with mean one, then `Q n` is contiguous with respect to `P n`: `P n (A n) → 0` implies `Q n (A n) → 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_of_log_likelihood_ratio
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.14: Le Cam's third lemma in change-of-law form, for observation spaces `Ω n` depending on the sample size. If `Q n = exp (Λ n) · P n` and `(S n, Λ n)` under `P n` converges in law to `ν` with `∫ exp z₂ dν(z) = 1`, then `S n` under `Q n` converges in law to the first marginal `L` of `exp z₂ · ν` (a probability measure by the mean condition, supplied as `L` with its instance). Taking a joint Gaussian limit gives the mean shift stated in GAPS.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_local_normal_power
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.21: local power of a test with a normal limit. If `T n` converges in law to `N(a, 1)` under the alternatives `P n`, the power `P n {T n > z}` tends to `1 - Φ(z - a)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_and_tendsto_sqrt_likelihood_ratio_of_dqm
declarations.doc: The deterministic step of LAN under differentiability in quadratic mean. For the root likelihood ratios `gₙ = √(f (θ₀ + h / √n) / f θ₀) - 1` and their linearizations `uₙ = gₙ - (h / √n) / 2 · ℓ̇` with the score `ℓ̇`, each `uₙ` is in `L²(P θ₀)`, `n E[uₙ²] → 0`, and `n E[gₙ] → -h² I / 8`, where `I = E[ℓ̇²]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_log_likelihood_ratio_sub_of_dqm
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.13: differentiability in quadratic mean implies local asymptotic normality, for a scalar parameter and common strictly positive densities. If `√f θ` is differentiable in quadratic mean at `θ₀` with score `ℓ̇` (centred, square-integrable) and `I = E[ℓ̇²]`, then for an i.i.d. sample from `P θ₀` and every `h`, the log likelihood ratio of `θ₀ + h / √n` against `θ₀` satisfies `∑ log (f (θ₀ + h/√n) (Xᵢ) / f θ₀ (Xᵢ)) = (h / √n) ∑ ℓ̇(Xᵢ) - h² I / 2 + o_P(1)`. The proof follows van der Vaart, *Asymptotic Statistics*, Theorem 7.2.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_score_and_log_likelihood_ratio_expansion_of_dqm
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.13: local asymptotic normality from differentiability in quadratic mean, with the central sequence: the normalized score sum `n^{-1/2} ∑ ℓ̇(Xᵢ)` converges in law to `N(0, I)`, and the log likelihood ratio has the expansion of `tendstoInMeasure_log_likelihood_ratio_sub_of_dqm`.

declarations.name: CKSD.outerExpectation
declarations.doc: Outer expectation of a nonnegative function, as the infimum over measurable majorants.

declarations.name: CKSD.TendstoInOuterDistribution
declarations.doc: Weak convergence in the outer-expectation sense, allowing nonmeasurable random elements. Shifting a bounded continuous test by its norm makes the integrand nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.TendstoInProbabilityZero
declarations.doc: Convergence to zero in probability, `P n {ε < |X n|} → 0` for every `ε > 0`, for observation spaces and laws varying with `n`. On a fixed probability space it is `TendstoInMeasure μ X atTop (fun _ ↦ 0)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLittleOInProbability
declarations.doc: Stochastic little-o with an eventually positive deterministic scale.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBigOInProbability
declarations.doc: Stochastic big-O with an eventually positive deterministic scale.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasHadamardFDerivAt
declarations.doc: Sequential tangential Hadamard differentiability, with a continuous linear extension.

declarations.name: CKSD.LocalExperiment
declarations.doc: A local experiment with observation space depending on sample size.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLocallyAsymptoticallyNormal
declarations.doc: Local asymptotic normality: Gaussian central sequence and log-likelihood expansion.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsRegularEstimator
declarations.doc: Regularity of a locally scaled estimator: its centred limit law `L` is independent of the local parameter.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_gaussian_shift_kernel_of_local_limits
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.15: the asymptotic representation theorem. In a LAN experiment with information `I`, if statistics `T n` with values in a Polish space have limit laws `L h` under every local parameter `h`, there is a Markov kernel `K` with `L h = K ∘ₘ N(h, I⁻¹)` for all `h`, i.e. the limit is a randomized statistic in the Gaussian shift experiment.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_convolution_of_isRegularEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.16: Hájek's convolution theorem. In a LAN experiment with information `I`, the limit law `L` of a regular estimator sequence is the convolution of `N(0, I⁻¹)` with a probability measure `M`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_risk_le_local_asymptotic_minimax
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.17: the local asymptotic minimax theorem. In a LAN experiment with information `I`, for a lower semicontinuous, symmetric, quasiconvex (bowl-shaped) loss `ℓ ≥ 0`, every estimator sequence satisfies `E ℓ(N(0, I⁻¹)) ≤ sup_c liminf_n sup_{‖h‖ ≤ c} E_h ℓ(T n - h)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_of_hasHadamardFDerivAt
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.28: functional delta method for measurable maps and a closed tangent space. The outer version for nonmeasurable empirical processes uses `TendstoInOuterDistribution`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fisherRaoMetric
declarations.doc: Fisher–Rao bilinear form on the open finite probability simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.amariChentsovTensor
declarations.doc: Amari–Chentsov symmetric cubic tensor on the open probability simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.openProbabilitySimplex
declarations.doc: The open probability simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexTangentSpace
declarations.doc: Tangent space of the probability simplex, represented by zero-sum vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.CongruentSimplexEmbedding
declarations.doc: A congruent embedding splits each input category into a nonempty block of output categories.

declarations.name: CKSD.CongruentSimplexEmbedding.map
declarations.doc: The map `p ↦ (p (block j) · weight j)ⱼ` of a congruent simplex embedding; it is the restriction of a linear map, and so is its own derivative.

declarations.name: CKSD.fisherRaoMetric_congruent_embedding
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.58: the Fisher–Rao metric `∑ uᵢ vᵢ / pᵢ` on the open simplex is invariant under congruent embeddings (Chentsov's defining invariance).

declarations.name: CKSD.isContiguous_iff_contiguous5
declarations.doc: For probability measures, `CKSD.IsContiguous` is Statlib's direct set formulation `Contiguous5` of contiguity.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_add_preimage_le_of_convex_symmetric
declarations.doc: For a symmetric measure with the Prékopa–Leindler property, a symmetric convex set has maximum mass when centered at zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasPrekopaLeindler_stdGaussian
declarations.doc: Standard Gaussian measures satisfy Prékopa–Leindler, including in dimension zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasPrekopaLeindler_multivariateGaussian_zero
declarations.doc: A centered multivariate Gaussian inherits Prékopa–Leindler from the standard Gaussian through its covariance square-root map. Degenerate covariance is allowed.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateGaussian_add_preimage_le
declarations.doc: Anderson's inequality: translating a symmetric convex set cannot increase its mass under a centered multivariate Gaussian.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_multivariateGaussian_loss_le_shift
declarations.doc: A measurable symmetric bowl-shaped loss has minimal Gaussian risk at zero shift. The loss may be unbounded or take the value infinity.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_multivariateGaussian_loss_le_convolution
declarations.doc: Adding independent residual noise cannot reduce the Gaussian risk of a symmetric bowl-shaped loss.

declarations.name: CKSD.comp_map_comap_eq_map_comp_map
declarations.doc: Mapping a kernel's output and pulling back its input commute with integrating against a law.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_add_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: Translating a Gaussian observation translates its mean without changing covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.translatedKernel_comp_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: Translating the input and output of a Gaussian decision kernel preserves its averaged law up to the same shift of the Gaussian mean and output.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_multivariateGaussian_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The Gaussian location family is complete among integrable measurable functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.isCompleteStatistic_multivariateGaussian_location
declarations.doc: The identity statistic of a nondegenerate Gaussian location family is complete.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_zero_of_bounded_integral_multivariateGaussian_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A bounded measurable function whose mean is zero under every Gaussian location vanishes Lebesgue-almost everywhere.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_gaussian_eq_zero_of_bounded_integral_multivariateGaussian_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Gaussian location completeness also gives equality almost everywhere under any member of the same nondegenerate Gaussian family.

declarations.name: CKSD.isBoundedlyCompleteStatistic_multivariateGaussian_location
declarations.doc: The identity statistic of a nondegenerate Gaussian location family is boundedly complete.

declarations.name: CKSD.inv_covariance_apply_covariance
declarations.doc: Inverse covariance cancels covariance on Euclidean vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.covariance_quadratic_sub_covariance
declarations.doc: Completing the square in a Gaussian covariance quadratic form.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateGaussian_withDensity_exp_inner
declarations.doc: Gaussian likelihood ratios shift the mean by covariance times the tilt vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_covariance_multivariateGaussian_inverse
declarations.doc: The Gaussian score coordinate sends the shift experiment to covariance-shifted means.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_gaussianShift_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: Covariance coordinates identify the Gaussian shift experiment with its likelihood tilt.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_exp_inner_sub_half_covariance
declarations.doc: The limiting Gaussian LAN likelihood ratio has expectation one.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateGaussian_affine_score_zero
declarations.doc: A nonzero Gaussian LAN score has no atom at zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_gaussianPDFReal_mul_pow
declarations.doc: The standard Gaussian density times `x ^ n` is Lebesgue integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_max_sub_gaussianReal
declarations.doc: For a standard Gaussian, `∫ x (x - k)⁺ dΦ = P(X > k)`; proved by integrating `x (x - k) φ(x) = (-(x - k) φ(x))' + φ(x)` over `(k, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_mul_max_sub_gaussianReal
declarations.doc: `x (x - k)⁺` is integrable for the standard Gaussian.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_huberScore_gaussianReal
declarations.doc: For `k ≥ 0` and a standard Gaussian, `∫ x ψ_k(x) dΦ = 2Φ(k) - 1`, where `ψ_k` is the clipped Huber score.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_huberScore_le
declarations.doc: The clipped Huber score is bounded by the clipping constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_huberScore
declarations.doc: The clipped Huber score is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_huberScore_sq_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.44, Hampel optimality part of the Huber statement. Under the standard Gaussian model, with `a = 2 Φ(k) - 1`, the normalized Huber score `ψ_k / a` has the smallest second moment among measurable scores `φ` bounded by `k / a` with `∫ x φ(x) dΦ(x) = 1`; that is, it minimizes the asymptotic variance among location M-estimators with gross-error sensitivity at most `k / a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_uniform_edgeworth_expansion
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.49: the one-term Edgeworth expansion of the standardized mean. For an i.i.d. sequence with mean zero, variance one, finite third absolute moment `ρ = E X³`, and a nonlattice law, the distribution function of `√n X̄ₙ` is `Φ(t) - φ(t) (t² - 1) ρ / (6 √n) + o(n^{-1/2})` uniformly in `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_bootstrap_mean_kolmogorovDistance
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.51: bootstrap consistency for the mean. For an i.i.d. sequence with finite positive variance `σ²`, the Kolmogorov distance between the bootstrap law of `√n (X̄*ₙ - X̄ₙ)` (resampling from the empirical measure) and `N(0, σ²)` tends to zero in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.comp_eq_conv_of_ae_eq_map_add
declarations.doc: A kernel that is almost everywhere a translate of one fixed law acts by convolution.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_const_of_forall_add_ae_eq
declarations.doc: A measurable function invariant almost everywhere under every translation is constant almost everywhere for a nonzero invariant measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_ae_eq_const_kernel_of_forall_add_ae_eq
declarations.doc: A Markov kernel invariant under every translation is almost everywhere constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_of_dist_small_in_probability
declarations.doc: Metric Slutsky perturbations allow both observation spaces and probability measures to vary.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_joint_subsequence_limit_of_marginal_limits
declarations.doc: Convergent Polish marginals admit one joint weakly convergent subsequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_of_joint_rnDeriv
declarations.doc: Le Cam's change-of-law lemma using the actual Radon–Nikodym density, without finite-sample absolute continuity. Unit mean of the limiting density forces the singular part of the alternatives to vanish.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_measureReal_eq_zero_of_tendstoInDistribution
declarations.doc: A closed null event under a real weak limit has asymptotically zero probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_fst_withDensity_map_graph
declarations.doc: Tilting a statistic-density graph and projecting back is the original tilt.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_joint_rnDeriv_of_log
declarations.doc: Weak convergence of a log likelihood with no limiting atom at zero also gives weak convergence of the actual likelihood, despite the convention `Real.log 0 = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_withDensity_of_real_integral_one
declarations.doc: A nonnegative integrable density of real mass one defines a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_of_joint_rnDeriv_graph
declarations.doc: A limiting likelihood given by a density graph tilts the underlying joint limit.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_sub_integral_rnDeriv_mul_le
declarations.doc: The discrepancy between integration under an alternative law and its absolutely continuous likelihood contribution is controlled by the missing likelihood mass.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_sqrt_mul_sqrt_of_forall_two_mul_le
declarations.doc: A real number `x` with `2 x ≤ δ A + B / δ` for every `δ > 0` satisfies `x ≤ √A √B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_mul_le_sqrt_mul_sqrt
declarations.doc: The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for real integrals of square-integrable functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_le_abs_sum_sub_le_of_iid
declarations.doc: Chebyshev's inequality for a sum of a measurable square-integrable statistic of an iid sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sum_sub_of_iid
declarations.doc: A triangular-array weak law: if `n ∫ φₙ² dP → 0`, then the centred sums `∑_{i<n} (φₙ(Xᵢ) - ∫ φₙ dP)` of an iid sequence tend to zero in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sum_sq_of_iid
declarations.doc: Markov's inequality for sums of squares: if `n ∫ φₙ² dP → 0`, then `∑_{i<n} φₙ(Xᵢ)²` tends to zero in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_two_mul_log_one_add_sub_le
declarations.doc: A one-term logarithmic expansion: for `|g| ≤ 1/2`, `|2 log (1 + g) - (2 g - g²)| ≤ 4 |g|³`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_mul_measureReal_lt_abs_of_integrable_sq
declarations.doc: Uniform integrability of a square-integrable function along `√n`: for `c > 0`, `n P(|s| > c √n) → 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_deriv_param
declarations.doc: The derivative in a real parameter of a family of measurable functions, differentiable in the parameter, is measurable in the observation.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_deriv_sub_taylor_le
declarations.doc: A second-order Taylor bound for the derivative of a `C³` function whose third derivative is bounded by `M` on a ball.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sub_taylor_two_le
declarations.doc: A second-order Taylor bound for a `C³` function whose third derivative is bounded by `M` on a ball: the remainder is at most `M |t - θ₀|³`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sub_div_le_of_score_equation
declarations.doc: Deterministic core of Cramér's argument: from the linearized score equation `Z + W B + q = 0` with `B` close to `-I` and a quadratic remainder `q`, the scaled error `W` is within `4 κ |Z| / I²` of `Z / I`.

declarations.name: CKSD.scalarWaldStatistic
declarations.doc: Wald statistic of a scalar simple null `θ = θ₀`, with information evaluated at the estimate: `n (T - θ₀)² I(T)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.scalarScoreStatistic
declarations.doc: Rao score statistic of a scalar simple null: `ℓₙ'(θ₀)² / (n I(θ₀))`, written with the derivative of the sample log likelihood.

declarations.name: CKSD.isIndependentIdenticallyDistributed_infinitePi_eval
declarations.doc: The coordinate process of the infinite product of a probability law is iid with that law.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_fin_eq_pi_of_iid
declarations.doc: The first `n` observations of an iid sequence have the `n`-fold product law.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_pi_of_iid
declarations.doc: Convergence in law of statistics of the first `n` observations of an iid sequence is convergence in law of the same statistics under the `n`-fold product measures.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInProbabilityZero_pi_iff_of_iid
declarations.doc: Convergence to zero in probability under the `n`-fold product measures is convergence to zero in probability of the same statistics of the first `n` observations of an iid sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_fisherInformation
declarations.doc: The Fisher information of a family with strictly positive densities, `C³` log likelihood, is a measurable function of the parameter.

declarations.name: CKSD.deriv_sampleLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: The derivative of the sample log likelihood is the sum of the likelihood scores.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_likelihoodScore_eq_zero_of_isMax
declarations.doc: At a global maximizer of a sample log likelihood that is differentiable in the parameter, the sum of the likelihood scores vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.pi_eq_withDensity_exp_sum_log_sub
declarations.doc: For a family with strictly positive densities, the `n`-fold product law at `θ` has density `exp (∑ᵢ (log f θ xᵢ - log f θ₀ xᵢ))` with respect to the product law at `θ₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianReal_map_sq_div_eq_noncentralChiSquared
declarations.doc: If `X ~ N(m, I)` with `I > 0`, then `X² / I` has the noncentral chi-squared law with one degree of freedom and noncentrality `m² / I`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianReal_withDensity_exp_eq
declarations.doc: Exponential tilting of a centred Gaussian law: the density `exp (h z - h² I / 2)` turns `N(0, I)` into `N(h I, I)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.noncentral_limit_of_tilt
declarations.doc: The joint limit law of the test statistic and the log likelihood ratio under the null, `(Z² / I, h Z - h² I / 2)` with `Z ~ N(0, I)`, tilted by the likelihood ratio, has the noncentral chi-squared first marginal of the local alternative, and the likelihood ratio has mean one.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_prodMk_zero
declarations.doc: Componentwise convergence to zero in probability gives convergence to zero of the pair.

declarations.name: CKSD.likelihood_test_expansions_of_iid
declarations.doc: Second-order expansions behind the likelihood-ratio, Wald, and score tests of a scalar simple null, on one probability space carrying an iid sample. Under the hypotheses of `mle_asymptotic_linearization_and_normality`, with `aₙ = √n (Tₙ - θ₀)` and the normalized score `Zₙ`, the likelihood-ratio statistic, the score statistic `Zₙ² / I`, and every plug-in Wald statistic `aₙ² J(Tₙ)` with `J` continuous at `θ₀` and `J θ₀ = I` differ from `I aₙ²` by `o_P(1)`, and the log likelihood ratio at `θ₀ + h / √n` equals `h Zₙ - h² I / 2 + o_P(1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.likelihood_tests_sub_score_sq_infinitePi
declarations.doc: Reduction of the scalar likelihood tests to the squared normalized score, on the coordinate process of the infinite product `P θ₀ ^ ℕ`. Under the hypotheses of `tendstoInDistribution_likelihoodRatio_wald_score_chiSquared`, the three statistics are measurable, the normalized score `Zₙ` of the first `n` coordinates converges in law to `N(0, I(θ₀))`, each of the three statistics of the first `n` coordinates differs from `Zₙ² / I(θ₀)` by `o_P(1)`, and the log likelihood ratio of `θ₀ + h / √n` against `θ₀` equals `h Zₙ - h² I(θ₀) / 2 + o_P(1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_likelihoodRatio_wald_score_chiSquared
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.11, null part, for a scalar parameter and the simple null `Θ₀ = {θ₀}` (so `q = k = 1`, `c(θ) = θ - θ₀`, and the restricted maximizer is `θ₀`). Under the hypotheses of 102.3 at `θ₀` with Fisher information continuous at `θ₀`, and for consistent global maximizers `T n` of the sample log likelihood, the likelihood-ratio, Wald, and score statistics each converge in law to `χ²₁` under `P θ₀`, and the Wald and score statistics differ from the likelihood-ratio statistic by `o_P(1)`. Composite nulls with `q < k` are outside this scope.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_likelihoodRatio_wald_score_noncentralChiSquared
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.11, local-alternative part, in the scalar simple-null scope of `tendstoInDistribution_likelihoodRatio_wald_score_chiSquared`. If in addition the model is DQM at `θ₀` with the likelihood score, then under `P (θ₀ + h / √n)` each of the three statistics converges in law to the noncentral `χ²₁` with noncentrality `h² I(θ₀)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.scalarWaldStatistic_self
declarations.doc: The Wald statistic vanishes at the null value.

declarations.name: CKSD.clipBCF
declarations.doc: Truncation `x ↦ max 0 (min x k)` as a bounded continuous function.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_mul_of_tendsto_of_integral_le_one
declarations.doc: Weighted weak convergence: if probability measures `μₙ` converge weakly to `ν` and a continuous nonnegative weight `w` is integrable with integral at most one under every `μₙ` and integral one under `ν`, then `∫ w f dμₙ → ∫ w f dν` for bounded continuous `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_mul_of_tendsto
declarations.doc: Weighted weak convergence: if probability measures `μₙ` converge weakly to `ν` and a continuous nonnegative weight `w` has integral one under every `μₙ` and under `ν`, then `∫ w f dμₙ → ∫ w f dν` for bounded continuous `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_cexp_ofReal_mul_I_sub_le
declarations.doc: The second-order Taylor remainder of `x ↦ exp (i x)`: `‖exp (i x) - (1 + i x - x² / 2)‖ ≤ min (|x|³ / 3) (2 x²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_cexp_ofReal_mul_I_sub_le_lindeberg
declarations.doc: The truncated form of the Taylor bound used in Lindeberg's argument: for `ε ≥ 0`, `‖exp (i t x) - (1 + i t x - (t x)² / 2)‖ ≤ |t|³ ε x² / 3 + 2 t² x² 1{|x| > ε}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_charFun_map_sub_one_sub_le
declarations.doc: Lindeberg's bound for one centred square-integrable variable `Y`: for every `ε ≥ 0`, `‖φ_Y(t) - (1 - 𝔼[Y²] t² / 2)‖ ≤ |t|³ ε 𝔼[Y²] / 3 + 2 t² 𝔼[Y² ; |Y| > ε]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_ite_lt_abs_sq
declarations.doc: The truncated second moment `ω ↦ Y² 1{|Y| > ε}` of a square-integrable variable is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_le_sq_add_integral_ite
declarations.doc: The second moment is at most `ε² + 𝔼[Y² ; |Y| > ε]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_prod_charFun_sub_exp_le
declarations.doc: Lindeberg's bound for one row of a triangular array: for centred square-integrable variables `Y j`, `j ∈ s`, with variances `σⱼ²`, every `ε ≥ 0` and every `t`, `‖∏ⱼ φ_{Yⱼ}(t) - exp (-(∑ⱼ σⱼ²) t² / 2)‖` is at most `|t|³ ε (∑ σⱼ²) / 3 + 2 t² Lₛ(ε) + t⁴ (∑ σⱼ²) (ε² + Lₛ(ε)) / 4`, where `Lₛ(ε) = ∑ⱼ 𝔼[Yⱼ² ; |Yⱼ| > ε]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sum_of_lindeberg
declarations.doc: **Lindeberg–Feller central limit theorem** for triangular arrays of real random variables. Let `X n 0, …, X n (k n - 1)` be independent, centred and square integrable for each `n`. If `∑ⱼ 𝔼[X_{n,j}²] → v` and the Lindeberg condition `∑ⱼ 𝔼[X_{n,j}² ; |X_{n,j}| > ε] → 0` holds for every `ε > 0`, then the row sums `∑ⱼ X_{n,j}` converge in distribution to `N(0, v)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sum_of_lindeberg_of_iIndepFun
declarations.doc: The Lindeberg–Feller central limit theorem for rows that are independent sequences: if each row `X n` is an independent family, the row sums over `j < k n` converge in distribution to `N(0, v)` under the hypotheses of `CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sum_of_lindeberg`.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalProcess
declarations.doc: The normalised centred empirical process `n^{-1/2} (∑_{i<n} f(Xᵢ) - n ∫ f dP)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalProcess_sub
declarations.doc: The empirical process is additive on integrable functions: `Gₙ (f - g) = Gₙ f - Gₙ g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalProcess_add
declarations.doc: The empirical process is additive on integrable functions: `Gₙ (f + g) = Gₙ f + Gₙ g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_empiricalProcess_le
declarations.doc: Deterministic bound: `|Gₙ f| ≤ n^{-1/2} (∑ |f|(Xᵢ) + n ∫ |f|)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_le_abs_empiricalProcess_le
declarations.doc: Bernstein's inequality for the empirical process of a bounded function: if `|g| ≤ b` and `∫ g² dP ≤ v` with `v > 0`, then `P(t ≤ |Gₙ g|) ≤ 2 exp(-t² / (2 (v + 2 b t / (3 √n))))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.halfOpenCube
declarations.doc: The half-open cube `∏ᵢ [aᵢ, aᵢ + w)` in Euclidean space.

declarations.name: CKSD.cubeGridPoint
declarations.doc: The point `a + (w / 2ᵏ) z` of the dyadic grid of level `k` in the cube anchored at `a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.cubeIndex
declarations.doc: The index of the dyadic cell of level `k` containing `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.cubeGridPoint_apply
declarations.doc: Coordinates of a grid point: `(a + (w / 2ᵏ) z)ᵢ = aᵢ + zᵢ w / 2ᵏ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_le_sqrt_card_mul_of_abs_le
declarations.doc: A vector whose coordinates are bounded by `c` has Euclidean norm at most `√d c`.

declarations.name: CKSD.cubeIndex_mem
declarations.doc: The cell indices of a point of the cube lie in `[0, 2ᵏ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.cubeGridPoint_mem
declarations.doc: Grid points with indices in `[0, 2ᵏ)` lie in the cube.

declarations.name: CKSD.sub_cubeGridPoint_cubeIndex_mem
declarations.doc: A point exceeds its grid point of level `k` coordinatewise by less than `w / 2ᵏ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_cubeGridPoint_cubeIndex_le
declarations.doc: A point of the cube is within `√d w / 2ᵏ` of its grid point of level `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.cubeIndex_eq_div_two
declarations.doc: The cell index of level `k` is the halved cell index of level `k + 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_cubeGridPoint_succ_sub_le
declarations.doc: Consecutive grid points of a chain are within `√d w / 2ᵏ⁺¹` of each other.

declarations.name: CKSD.cubeGridPoint_zero_cubeIndex
declarations.doc: The level-zero grid point of a point of the cube is the anchor.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_exists_cube_chain_le
declarations.doc: Dyadic chaining on a half-open cube. If every increment of a process `S` over the cube exceeds `‖u - v‖ ((j + 1) A + W)` with probability at most `2 pʲ⁺¹`, then the increment between the anchor and the grid point of level `K` of any point of the cube exceeds `√d w (2 A + W)` with probability at most `2 ∑_{k<K} (2ᵈ p)ᵏ⁺¹`.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalEnvelope
declarations.doc: The envelope `n^{-1/2} (∑_{i<n} F(Xᵢ) + n ∫ F dP)` bounding `|Gₙ f|` when `|f| ≤ F`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lipschitzChainRemainder
declarations.doc: The random remainder in the chaining bound for a Lipschitz family with envelope `L`: the envelope of the part of `L` above the truncation level `ε √n`, plus `2⁻ⁿ` times the envelope of `L`.

declarations.name: CKSD.bernsteinExponent
declarations.doc: The Bernstein exponent `t² / (2 (β + γ t))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.mul_bernsteinExponent_le
declarations.doc: The Bernstein exponent grows at least linearly under dilation by `c ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalEnvelope_nonneg
declarations.doc: The empirical envelope of a nonnegative function is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalEnvelope_const_mul
declarations.doc: The empirical envelope is homogeneous: `envₙ (c F) = c envₙ F`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_exists_abs_empiricalProcess_sub_gt_le
declarations.doc: **Maximal inequality for Lipschitz families.** Let `θ ↦ f θ` be a family of integrable functions on a half-open cube of width `w` anchored at `a`, Lipschitz in `θ` with a nonnegative square-integrable envelope `L`. For `n ≥ 1`, a truncation level `ε > 0` and `A ≥ 0`, the event that `|Gₙ f θ - Gₙ f a| > √d w (2A + Rₙ)` for some `θ` of the cube, where `Rₙ` is `lipschitzChainRemainder`, has probability at most `2 ∑_{k<n} (2ᵈ e^{-φ(A)})ᵏ⁺¹`, with `φ` the Bernstein exponent with `β = ∫ L² + 1` and `γ = 2ε/3`. The proof truncates the envelope at `ε √n`, applies Bernstein's inequality to the truncated increments, and chains over dyadic grids of levels `< n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_empiricalEnvelope
declarations.doc: The expectation of the empirical envelope of an integrable function is `2 √n ∫ F dP`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_lipschitzChainRemainder
declarations.doc: The chaining remainder `lipschitzChainRemainder` of a square-integrable envelope tends to zero in probability: its expectation is at most `(2/ε) ∫_{L > ε√n} L² + 2⁻ⁿ⁺¹ √n ∫ L`.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_piFinset_Ico_two_pow
declarations.doc: The number of grid indices of level `k` is `(2ᵏ)ᵈ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.add_smul_mem_halfOpenCube
declarations.doc: Scaling a half-open cube: if `h ∈ ∏ [uᵢ, uᵢ + w)` and `c > 0`, then `θ₀ + c h ∈ ∏ [θ₀ᵢ + c uᵢ, θ₀ᵢ + c uᵢ + c w)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.centredCube
declarations.doc: The half-open cube `∏ᵢ [θ₀ᵢ - ρ, θ₀ᵢ + ρ)` centred at `θ₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.mem_centredCube_of_norm_sub_lt
declarations.doc: Points within `ρ` of `θ₀` lie in the centred cube of half-width `ρ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_le_of_mem_centredCube
declarations.doc: Points of the centred cube of half-width `ρ` lie within `√d ρ` of the centre.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_two_pow_pow_mul_exp_neg
declarations.doc: `xᵈ e^{-a x}` along `x = 2ᵏ` tends to zero for `a > 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_sqrt_mul_sub_sub_inner
declarations.doc: If `φ` has derivative `⟪v, ·⟫` at `θ₀`, then `√n (φ(θ₀ + u/√n) - φ θ₀) → ⟪u, v⟫`.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalProcess_inner
declarations.doc: Linear functionals of a square-integrable centred vector: the empirical process of `⟪u, s⟫` is `⟪u, n^{-1/2} ∑ s(Xᵢ)⟫`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sqrt_mul_empiricalProcess_sub_sub_inner
declarations.doc: **Pointwise local expansion.** For a family `f θ` that is Lipschitz near `θ₀` with a square-integrable envelope and differentiable at `θ₀` with derivative `⟪s x, ·⟫` for a centred square-integrable `s`, and for a fixed local direction `u`, `√n (Gₙ f(θ₀ + u/√n) - Gₙ f θ₀) - ⟪u, n^{-1/2} ∑ s(Xᵢ)⟫ → 0` in probability. The proof is Chebyshev's inequality and dominated convergence for the second moment of the remainder.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_measureReal_exists_abs_sqrt_mul_empiricalProcess_sub_sub_inner
declarations.doc: **Uniform local expansion of the empirical process.** In the setting of `tendstoInMeasure_sqrt_mul_empiricalProcess_sub_sub_inner`, with `n^{-1/2} ∑ s(Xᵢ)` bounded in probability, for every `R > 0` the remainder `√n (Gₙ f(θ₀ + h/√n) - Gₙ f θ₀) - ⟪h, n^{-1/2} ∑ s(Xᵢ)⟫` tends to zero in outer probability uniformly over `‖h‖ ≤ R`. The proof covers the cube `[-2R, 2R)ᵈ` by `2ᵏᵈ` dyadic cells, applies the maximal inequality `measureReal_exists_abs_empiricalProcess_sub_gt_le` in each cell, and the pointwise expansion at the cell anchors.

declarations.name: CKSD.mEstimator_asymptotic_linearization_and_normality
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.24: local asymptotic linearity and normality of multivariate M-estimators. The negative-definite matrix `V` is the Hessian of the population criterion through its quadratic little-o expansion. The empirical optimization error is `o_P(1/n)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCriterion
declarations.doc: Empirical average of a real criterion evaluated at a parameter.

declarations.name: CKSD.populationCriterion
declarations.doc: Population criterion under a fixed data-generating law.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_log_lt_integral_log_of_withDensity_ne
declarations.doc: Strict Gibbs inequality for strictly positive densities: if two probability laws with strictly positive densities `f, g` differ, then `∫ log g dP_f < ∫ log f dP_f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_ball_measurable_dominating_integral_lt
declarations.doc: Wald's local bracketing step. For a criterion continuous in the parameter of a separable metric space and dominated by an integrable envelope, if `∫ m θ < c` then on some ball about `θ` the criterion is dominated by one measurable integrable function with integral below `c`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_mle_of_compact
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.2: Wald consistency with continuous positive densities on a compact parameter space. The log-likelihood envelope is integrable at the true law; identifiability concerns the laws, so no irrelevant distinction between density versions is required.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCriterion_add_const
declarations.doc: An empirical criterion is unchanged if its per-observation criterion is translated.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_ofReal_condExp
declarations.doc: Pulling a bounded `m`-measurable complex factor through a real conditional expectation: `∫ W g = ∫ W 𝔼[g | m]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condExp_sq_le_sq_add_condExp_ite
declarations.doc: A conditional variance is at most `ε²` plus the conditional truncated second moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_of_le_of_tendstoInMeasure
declarations.doc: Bounded convergence in probability: if `0 ≤ Yₙ ≤ B` and `Yₙ ≤ Lₙ` almost surely with `Lₙ → 0` in probability, then `𝔼 Yₙ → 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_of_ae_eq_of_measure_tendsto_zero
declarations.doc: Convergence in probability transfers to sequences that agree with the original one outside events whose probabilities tend to zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.nonneg_of_tendstoInMeasure_of_nonneg
declarations.doc: If `Vₙ ≥ 0` almost surely and `Vₙ → v` in probability, then `v ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sum_of_sum_condVar_le
declarations.doc: The martingale central limit theorem when the conditional variances of each row sum to at most a constant `B`: square-integrable martingale-difference rows whose summed conditional variances `V n ≤ B` converge in probability to `v ≥ 0`, and whose summed conditional truncated second moments tend to zero in mean, have row sums converging in distribution to `N(0, v)`. The proof compares `𝔼 exp (i t Sₙ)` with `exp (-t² v / 2)` through the telescoping estimate `norm_integral_mdsZ_sub_one_le`.

declarations.name: CKSD.mul_zero_or_one_martingaleDifference
declarations.doc: Multiplying a square-integrable martingale difference `Y` (for `𝓕 ≤ 𝓖`, `Y` being `𝓖`-measurable with `𝔼[Y | 𝓕] = 0`) by an `𝓕`-measurable `{0, 1}`-valued factor `ι` gives a square-integrable martingale difference whose conditional variance and conditional truncated second moments are those of `Y` multiplied by `ι`.

declarations.name: CKSD.mle_asymptotic_linearization_and_normality
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.3, scalar smooth likelihood-score roots and their efficient expansion. `ell` is the per-observation log likelihood; the score/information moment identities and the local third-derivative envelope are explicit hypotheses.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_inv_sqrt_smul_sum_sub_of_iid
declarations.doc: The multivariate central limit theorem for IID Euclidean random vectors with finite second moment, centered by their common expectation and scaled by the square root of the sample size. The limiting covariance may be singular.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sqrt_smul_sampleAverage
declarations.doc: The Euclidean sample-mean central limit theorem for an i.i.d. sequence with law `P`, with the population covariance matrix as the limiting Gaussian covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.rnDeriv_count_eq_zero_of_noAtoms
declarations.doc: Relative to counting measure, the chosen Radon–Nikodym derivative of an atomless law is zero, even though every law is absolutely continuous with respect to counting measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasQuadraticMeanDerivAt_of_rnDeriv_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A square-root Radon–Nikodym remainder is vacuous if all chosen reference densities vanish. Sigma-finite domination rules out this degeneracy for probability path laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCDF_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The empirical distribution function as a normalised sum of indicators.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCDF_mono
declarations.doc: The empirical distribution function is monotone.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCDF_extremes
declarations.doc: The empirical distribution function is `1` at `∑ |Xᵢ|` and `0` below `-∑ |Xᵢ|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_empiricalCDF_of_sampleQuantile_lt
declarations.doc: Order characterisation of the left sample quantile, for `n ≥ 1` and `p ∈ (0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_empiricalCDF
declarations.doc: Measurability of the empirical distribution function at a fixed point.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_sampleQuantile
declarations.doc: Measurability of the left sample quantile, for `p ∈ (0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_ite_le_eq_measureReal_Iic
declarations.doc: The integral of the indicator of `(-∞, a]` is the mass `P (-∞, a]`; for a probability measure this is the distribution function at `a` (`ProbabilityTheory.cdf_eq_real`).

declarations.name: CKSD.sqrt_mul_inv_natCast
declarations.doc: `√n / n = 1 / √n`, in the form used for normalised sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_sqrt_mul_cdf_sub
declarations.doc: Local increments of a distribution function differentiable at `q`: `√n (F(q + t/√n) - F(q)) → f t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sqrt_mul_empiricalCDF_sub
declarations.doc: The local empirical process at `q`: `√n (Fₙ(q + t/√n) - Fₙ(q)) → f t` in probability when the distribution function is differentiable at `q` with derivative `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sqrt_mul_sub_empiricalCDF
declarations.doc: Central limit theorem for the empirical distribution function at a point `q` with `F(q) = p`: `√n (p - Fₙ(q)) / f` converges in law to `N(0, p(1-p)/f²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sub_of_crossing
declarations.doc: Ghosh's crossing lemma: if `Wₙ` is bounded in probability and, for all `t` and `ε > 0`, the probabilities of the crossing events `{Vₙ ≤ t, Wₙ ≥ t + ε}` and `{Vₙ ≥ t + ε, Wₙ ≤ t}` tend to `0`, then `Vₙ - Wₙ → 0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_bahadur_remainder
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.7: the Bahadur representation of a sample quantile. If the distribution function `F` is differentiable at the `p`-quantile `q` with `F'(q) = f > 0`, then `√n (ξ̂ₙ,ₚ - q - (p - Fₙ(q)) / f) → 0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sampleQuantile
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.6: asymptotic normality of a sample quantile. If the distribution function is differentiable at the `p`-quantile `q` with positive derivative `f`, then `√n (ξ̂ₙ,ₚ - q)` converges in law to `N(0, p (1 - p) / f²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.centredCriterionModulus
declarations.doc: Local modulus of the centred criterion process `Mₙ - M` on the ball of radius `δ` about `θ₀`, as a nonnegative extended-real random quantity.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_le_outerExpectation_div
declarations.doc: Markov's inequality for outer expectations: a set on which `f ≥ t` has outer measure at most `E* f / t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isBoundedInProbability_rate_mEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.25: the rate theorem for `M`-estimators. Suppose the deterministic criterion has quadratic separation `M θ - M θ₀ ≤ -c d(θ,θ₀)²` near `θ₀`, and that for every `n ≥ 1` and all `δ` in a fixed interval `(0, δ₀)`, the outer expectation of the local modulus of `Mₙ - M` is at most `C φₙ(δ)/√n` with a constant `C ≥ 0`, where `δ ↦ φₙ(δ)/δ^a` is decreasing on `(0,∞)` for a fixed `a < 2`. If `rₙ² φₙ(1/rₙ) ≤ √n`, the estimator maximizes `Mₙ` up to `O_P(rₙ⁻²)`, and it is consistent in outer probability, then `rₙ d(Tₙ, θ₀) = O_P(1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.regressionMObjective
declarations.doc: Fixed-design convex regression objective.

declarations.name: CKSD.fixedDesignGramMatrix
declarations.doc: Empirical Gram matrix of the first `n` fixed-design rows.

declarations.name: CKSD.regression_mEstimator_asymptotic_linearization_and_normality
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.48: asymptotic linearization and normality of fixed-design convex M-estimators. The right derivative of `ρ` is `ψ`. The `L²` continuity of shifted scores is expressed by nonnegative extended integrals, so nonintegrable remainders cannot be assigned value zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.regressionMObjective_zero
declarations.doc: The zero-sample convex regression objective has value zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientScore_eq_self_of_inner_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A score orthogonal to every nuisance score is its own efficient score.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientInformationMatrix
declarations.doc: Efficient information matrix `Ĩ_ij = ⟨ℓ̃_i, ℓ̃_j⟩` of a vector of `L²` scores, where `ℓ̃` is the residual after projection on the nuisance tangent space generated by `scores`.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientInfluence
declarations.doc: Efficient influence function `Ĩ⁻¹ ℓ̃(x)`, evaluated at an observation through the chosen representatives of the efficient scores.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsRegularAlongPaths
declarations.doc: Regularity of an estimator sequence along a family of one-dimensional submodels `t ↦ Q i t` of probability measures whose parameter moves in direction `dir i`: under the product law at `t = 1/√n`, `√n (Tₙ - (θ + dir i / √n))` converges in law to the same `L` for every `i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_convolution_of_isRegularAlongPaths
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.34, convolution part. For every direction `a ∈ ℝᵏ` and nuisance score `g` in a linear space `G ⊆ L²(P)`, the submodel `t ↦ Q (a, g) t` passes through `P` at `t = 0`, has parameter `θ + t a`, is dominated by `ν`, and is QMD at `0` with score `a ⬝ ℓ̇ + g`. The nuisance tangent space is the closure of `G`. If the efficient information matrix is positive definite, the limit law of every estimator sequence regular along these submodels is the convolution of `N(0, Ĩ⁻¹)` with a probability measure. The common reference measure `ν` is sigma-finite, so its Radon–Nikodym densities represent every dominated path law.

declarations.name: CKSD.isRegularAlongPaths_gaussian_iff_asymptotically_linear
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.34, efficiency part, in the setting of `exists_convolution_of_isRegularAlongPaths`. A measurable estimator sequence is regular along all submodels with limit `N(0, Ĩ⁻¹)` if and only if it is asymptotically linear in the efficient influence function under `P`. The common dominating reference measure `ν` is sigma-finite.

declarations.name: CKSD.locationLaw
declarations.doc: Location law with density `η (x - θ)` with respect to Lebesgue measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.locationFisherInformation
declarations.doc: Fisher information for location, `∫ η'² / η`, with the convention `η'²/0 = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.locationScore
declarations.doc: Location score `-η'(x-θ)/η(x-θ)` of the location family at `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSymmetricFiniteInformationDensity
declarations.doc: A symmetric probability density on the line that is absolutely continuous with locally integrable derivative `η'`, chosen odd, and has finite Fisher information for location. Choosing an odd version of the derivative is no restriction: the odd part of any version of the derivative of an even absolutely continuous function is again a version.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSymmetricFiniteInformationDensity.isProbabilityMeasure_locationLaw
declarations.doc: The location laws of a symmetric finite-information density are probability measures.

declarations.name: CKSD.symmetricNuisanceScores
declarations.doc: Scores of symmetric nuisance perturbations at `P` about the centre `θ`: mean-zero `L²` functions that are even about `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurePreserving_reflect_locationLaw
declarations.doc: The reflection `x ↦ 2θ - x` preserves a symmetric location law centred at `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientScore_locationScore_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.41, efficient-score part: in the symmetric location model, with nuisance tangent space the closed span of the mean-zero `L²` functions that are even about `θ` (the scores of symmetric perturbations of `η`), the location score is orthogonal to the nuisance tangent space, so it is the efficient score, and the efficient information is the Fisher information `I_η`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_adaptive_estimator_center_of_symmetry
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.41, adaptation part: there are measurable estimators, not depending on the symmetric density, that are asymptotically normal with the efficient variance `I_η⁻¹` at every symmetric density of finite Fisher information, regularly along local location alternatives `θ + h/√n`. The location laws are probability measures by `IsSymmetricFiniteInformationDensity.isProbabilityMeasure_locationLaw`; the instance binder only makes them available to the statement. Regularity along symmetric nuisance perturbations is outside this scope.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasQuadraticMeanDerivAt
declarations.doc: Quadratic-mean differentiability at a parameter, without a domain restriction, using Statlib.

declarations.name: CKSD.nuisanceTangentSpace
declarations.doc: Closed nuisance tangent space generated by a specified class of `L²` nuisance scores.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientScore
declarations.doc: Efficient score as the residual after projecting out the nuisance tangent space.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientInformation
declarations.doc: Efficient information for a scalar score.

declarations.name: CKSD.contaminationLaw
declarations.doc: Contamination path for a probability law and one contaminating observation.

declarations.name: CKSD.influenceFunction
declarations.doc: Influence function as the right derivative of a statistical functional along contamination.

declarations.name: CKSD.missingMeanScore
declarations.doc: Missing-at-random augmented inverse-probability score.

declarations.name: CKSD.SampleSplit
declarations.doc: A finite partition of a sample into labeled folds. Empty folds are allowed in the definition.

declarations.name: CKSD.SampleSplit.trainingIndices
declarations.doc: Training indices for a fold are all indices outside that fold.

declarations.name: CKSD.crossFittedAverage
declarations.doc: Cross-fitted average with nuisance estimates trained exclusively on the other folds.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: Log likelihood of a finite iid sample with a given single-observation density.

declarations.name: CKSD.likelihoodRatioStatistic
declarations.doc: Likelihood-ratio statistic comparing two specified log-likelihood values.

declarations.name: CKSD.waldStatistic
declarations.doc: Wald quadratic statistic with the estimated covariance of the parameter estimate.

declarations.name: CKSD.scoreStatistic
declarations.doc: Score quadratic statistic with the information matrix of the whole sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.bootstrapLaw
declarations.doc: Conditional nonparametric bootstrap law of a statistic, given the observed sample. For `n=0` this uses the zero empirical measure convention of `empiricalMeasure`.

declarations.name: CKSD.studentizedStatistic
declarations.doc: Standardization using an estimated standard deviation, with division-by-zero value zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.edgeworthApproximation
declarations.doc: Finite-order Edgeworth distribution-function approximation for supplied correction polynomials.

declarations.name: CKSD.saddlepointDensity
declarations.doc: Saddlepoint approximation to the sample-mean density, for a chosen solution of `K'(s)=x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.efficientInformation_nonneg
declarations.doc: Efficient information is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.waldStatistic_self
declarations.doc: A zero displacement gives a zero Wald statistic.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_uStatistic_of_nondegenerate
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.8: the central limit theorem for U-statistics. For a symmetric square-integrable kernel `h` of order `m + 1` with mean `θ` and first projection `g(x) = E h(x, X₂, …) - θ`, `√n (Uₙ - θ)` converges in law to `N(0, (m + 1)² Var g)`. In the degenerate case `Var g = 0` the limit is the point mass at `0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.uStatistic_two_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The order-two ordered-injection sum is the sum over distinct ordered pairs.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_pair_ne_left
declarations.doc: The sum of a one-coordinate term over all distinct ordered pairs.

declarations.name: CKSD.uStatistic_two_sub_eq
declarations.doc: The order-two Hoeffding decomposition is a deterministic identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_pi_pair
declarations.doc: Distinct coordinates under a finite product law have the product of their laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_integral_kernel
declarations.doc: The conditional integral of a square-integrable real kernel is square integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_hoeffding_kernel_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A centered conditional kernel has zero first-coordinate integral.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_pair_mul_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A centered pair kernel is orthogonal to any square-integrable function not using its first coordinate.

declarations.name: CKSD.insertNth_eq_of_ne
declarations.doc: Inserting a different value at one coordinate leaves every other coordinate unchanged.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_pair_mul_pair
declarations.doc: Two centered symmetric pair kernels are orthogonal unless their unordered coordinate pairs coincide.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_pair_mul_single
declarations.doc: A centered symmetric pair kernel is orthogonal to each one-coordinate function.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_sum_pairs
declarations.doc: The sum of a square-integrable kernel over distinct coordinate pairs is square integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sum_pairs_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Degenerate pair sums have mean zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sum_pairs
declarations.doc: The second moment of a degenerate symmetric ordered-pair sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sum_pairs_mul_sum_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A degenerate pair sum is orthogonal to the sum of any square-integrable one-coordinate function.

declarations.name: CKSD.uStatistic_hoeffding_decomposition_and_variance
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.29: order-two Hoeffding decomposition, including the exact variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.uStatistic_two_finite_rank_eq
declarations.doc: The finite-rank quadratic U-statistic is a difference between squared sample sums and sample sums of squares. The identity includes sample sizes zero and one.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_uStatistic_finite_rank_of_scores
declarations.doc: A finite-rank quadratic kernel has the Gaussian-chaos limit whenever its vector of normalized scores has the standard Gaussian limit.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_uStatistic_of_finite_rank_degenerate
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.30: finite-rank degenerate quadratic kernels have Gaussian-chaos limits.

declarations.name: CKSD.uStatistic_projection_spec
declarations.doc: The first projection `g(a) = ∫ h(a, y) dPᵐ(y) - θ` of a square-integrable kernel is measurable, square integrable and centred, and `y ↦ h(a, y)` is integrable for almost every `a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.uStatistic_sub_projection_eq
declarations.doc: The remainder of the Hájek projection is the U-statistic of the kernel `h(z) - θ - ∑ⱼ g(zⱼ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_uStatistic_sub_projection
declarations.doc: The remainder `Uₙ - θ - ((m + 1)/n) ∑ᵢ g(xᵢ)` of the Hájek projection is square integrable for every sample size.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_integral_sq_uStatistic_sub_projection_le
declarations.doc: **The Hájek projection of a U-statistic.** For a symmetric square-integrable kernel `h` of order `m + 1` under `P`, with mean `θ` and first projection `g`, the remainder `Uₙ - θ - ((m + 1)/n) ∑ᵢ g(xᵢ)` has second moment at most `C / n²` under `Pⁿ` for `n ≥ 2 (m + 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_two_of_lipschitz_envelope
declarations.doc: Square integrability of a parameter family with a square-integrable Lipschitz envelope, at parameters within the Lipschitz radius.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_le_abs_centredSum_sub_le
declarations.doc: Chebyshev's inequality for the increments of the centred partial-sum process of a parameter family with a square-integrable Lipschitz envelope.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_centredSum_sub_le
declarations.doc: Deterministic Lipschitz bound for the increments of the centred partial-sum process.

declarations.name: CKSD.dyadicGridPoint
declarations.doc: The left endpoint of the dyadic cell of level `j`, of width `δ / 2 ^ j`, containing `t` in the grid anchored at `θ₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.dyadicGridPoint_index_mem
declarations.doc: The dyadic cell index of a point within `δ` of the anchor lies in `[-2 ^ j, 2 ^ j)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_dyadic_sub_le
declarations.doc: A dyadic grid point lies within `δ` of the anchor, as does the midpoint of its cell.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sub_dyadicGridPoint_le
declarations.doc: A point is within one cell width of its dyadic grid point.

declarations.name: CKSD.dyadicGridPoint_succ
declarations.doc: Consecutive dyadic levels: the finer grid point is the coarser one or the midpoint of its cell.

declarations.name: CKSD.dyadicGridPoint_zero
declarations.doc: The level-zero dyadic grid point of a point within `δ` of the anchor is `θ₀ - δ` or `θ₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_dyadic_chain_le
declarations.doc: Dyadic chaining bound: if the increments of a real process indexed by `[θ₀ - δ, θ₀ + δ]` satisfy the Chebyshev bound `P(c ≤ |S a - S b|) ≤ L (a - b)² / c²`, then for any random parameter `t` the process at the dyadic grid point of `t` of any level stays within `c` of its value at `θ₀`, except on an event of probability at most `300 L δ² / c²` or where `|t - θ₀| ≥ δ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_centredSum_sub_of_lipschitz
declarations.doc: Stochastic equicontinuity of the empirical process of a scalar parameter family with a square-integrable Lipschitz envelope: evaluated at a consistent random parameter `Tₙ`, the normalised centred partial-sum increment `n^{-1/2} ∑ᵢ (ψ_{Tₙ} - ψ_{θ₀})(Xᵢ) - √n (P ψ_{Tₙ} - P ψ_{θ₀})` tends to `0` in probability. The proof is a dyadic chaining argument with Chebyshev's inequality at each level.

declarations.name: CKSD.zEstimator_asymptotic_linearization_and_normality
declarations.doc: GAPS 102.4, the scalar Z-estimator theorem under a square-integrable Lipschitz envelope.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sq_mul_log_sq_mul_le
declarations.doc: Multiplication by a scalar in the unit interval preserves an integrable entropy bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_expanding_smooth_cutoffs
declarations.doc: Smooth expanding radial cutoffs can be chosen with a common Lipschitz bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.logSobolevInequality_of_hasCompactSupport
declarations.doc: A logarithmic Sobolev bound on smooth compactly supported tests extends to all admissible tests.

declarations.name: CKSD.logSobolevInequality_gibbsMeasure_of_stronglyMonotoneGradient
declarations.doc: Bakry–Émery: a strongly convex smooth potential has logarithmic Sobolev constant `1/m`.

declarations.name: CKSD.potential_add_inner_add_le
declarations.doc: A strongly monotone gradient gives a lower tangent paraboloid at every base point.

declarations.name: CKSD.potential_interpolation_le
declarations.doc: Tangent paraboloids imply the strong convexity interpolation inequality.

declarations.name: CKSD.two_mul_le_mul_sq_add_div
declarations.doc: A scalar Young inequality with an arbitrary positive quadratic coefficient.

declarations.name: CKSD.exponential_interpolation_exponent_le
declarations.doc: The pointwise exponential comparison used in the Prékopa–Leindler proof of LSI.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_exponential_interpolation_le
declarations.doc: The Prékopa–Leindler interpolation estimate for a smooth log-density perturbation.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_integral_exponential_perturbation
declarations.doc: Differentiate a bounded exponential perturbation under a finite-density integral.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_le_of_eventually_le_right
declarations.doc: Right-hand comparison of differentiable functions compares derivatives at a contact point.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropy_exponential_le_of_quadratic_upper_bound
declarations.doc: Sharp entropy-energy inequality for bounded log-density perturbations with bounded derivative and a global quadratic upper Taylor bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.quadratic_upper_bound_of_lipschitz_fderiv
declarations.doc: A Lipschitz derivative gives a global quadratic upper Taylor bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_gibbsMeasure
declarations.doc: Integration against the Gibbs law is normalized weighted Lebesgue integration.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropy_gibbs_exponential_le
declarations.doc: Bounded logarithmic perturbations satisfy the Gibbs entropy-energy bound with sharp constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_bounded_quadratic_upper_bound
declarations.doc: A smooth function constant off a compact set has bounded derivative and a quadratic upper bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_log_regularization_bounds
declarations.doc: The logarithm of a regularized smooth compactly supported square is an admissible bounded perturbation in the sharp entropy estimate.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_entropy_of_dominated_convergence
declarations.doc: Dominated convergence of both entropy moments gives convergence of entropy.

declarations.name: CKSD.regularized_log_gradient_energy_le
declarations.doc: Regularization of a square preserves the sharp gradient-energy upper bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropy_gibbs_regularized_sq_le
declarations.doc: A regularized compactly supported square satisfies the sharp logarithmic Sobolev bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_entropy_add_inv
declarations.doc: Adding positive constants tending to zero preserves the entropy of a bounded nonnegative function.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropy_gibbs_sq_le_of_hasCompactSupport
declarations.doc: Smooth compactly supported tests satisfy the sharp Bakry–Émery logarithmic Sobolev bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.poissonMass
declarations.doc: Poisson likelihood `e^{-θ} θ^x / x!` as a real number. For `θ ≥ 0` it is the Poisson mass of `x` (`poissonMass_coe`); it is defined for every real `θ`, so that it can be integrated against an arbitrary prior on `ℝ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.poissonMass_coe
declarations.doc: For a nonnegative intensity, `poissonMass` is the mass of Mathlib's Poisson law.

declarations.name: CKSD.metropolisAcceptance
declarations.doc: Metropolis–Hastings acceptance probability `min (1, π(y) q(y,x) / (π(x) q(x,y)))` of a move from `x` to `y`, with the convention that it is one when `π(x) q(x,y) = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.metropolisTransition
declarations.doc: Metropolis–Hastings transition matrix of a proposal matrix `q` and target weights `π`: the off-diagonal entries are `q(x,y)` times the acceptance probability, and the diagonal also carries the total probability of rejected proposals.

declarations.name: CKSD.leapfrogStep
declarations.doc: One leapfrog step `p ↦ p - (h/2) g(x)`, `x ↦ x + h p`, `p ↦ p - (h/2) g(x)` with identity mass matrix, step size `h` and force `g` (the gradient of the potential).

declarations.name: CKSD.momentumFlip
declarations.doc: Momentum reversal `(x, p) ↦ (x, -p)` on phase space.

declarations.name: CKSD.normalPosterior
declarations.doc: Posterior of a normal location with known variance `v` under a prior density `prior`, after `n` observations with sample mean `mean`: the prior density times `exp(-n (θ - mean)² / (2v))`, normalized. Likelihood factors that do not depend on the parameter cancel in the normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_comp_eq_sum_measureReal
declarations.doc: The integral of a function of a random variable with finitely many values is the sum of the values weighted by their probabilities.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_comp_of_finite
declarations.doc: A function of a random variable with finitely many values is integrable under a finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_div_of_summable_integral_sq_div
declarations.doc: If `∑ₖ 𝔼[Zₖ²] / bₖ² < ∞`, then `Zₖ / bₖ → 0` almost surely, by Chebyshev's inequality and the Borel–Cantelli lemma.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_empiricalMeasure_vector
declarations.doc: Integration of a vector-valued function against the empirical measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropyIntegrand
declarations.doc: The nonnegative integrand in the variational formula for entropy.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropyIntegrand_nonneg
declarations.doc: The entropy integrand is nonnegative for a nonnegative value and a positive reference.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_entropyIntegrand
declarations.doc: Integrability of the entropy integrand follows from integrability of its two moments.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_entropyIntegrand
declarations.doc: The integral of the entropy integrand differs from entropy by its value at the mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropy_le_integral_entropyIntegrand
declarations.doc: Every positive reference value gives an upper bound on entropy.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_entropyIntegrand_mean
declarations.doc: Choosing the mean as reference recovers entropy exactly.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropy_congr_ae
declarations.doc: Entropy respects almost-everywhere equality.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropy_le_mul_of_measure_le_smul
