declarations.doc: Domination of probability measures gives the same domination of nonnegative entropies.

declarations.name: CKSD.logSobolevInequality_of_measure_le_smul
declarations.doc: A logarithmic Sobolev inequality transfers between probability measures whose densities are bounded above and below. The constant is multiplied by the ratio of the bounds.

declarations.name: CKSD.gibbsMeasure_le_smul_of_sub_le
declarations.doc: A lower bound on a change of potential bounds the ratio of the corresponding Gibbs laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.logSobolevInequality_gibbsMeasure_add
declarations.doc: Holley–Stroock bounded perturbation: adding a bounded measurable potential multiplies a logarithmic Sobolev constant by at most the exponential of the potential's oscillation.

declarations.name: CKSD.bridgeIterate
declarations.doc: Iterative proportional fitting from `R`: odd iterates fit the law `ν` of `finish`, even iterates of positive index fit the law `μ` of `start`.

declarations.name: CKSD.bridgeIterate_zero
declarations.doc: The reference law is the zeroth iterate.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_bridgeIterate_step
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.77: the entropy Pythagorean identity for each step of the path-space iteration. It holds for every feasible competitor, without assuming it minimizes entropy.

declarations.name: CKSD.gibbsMeasure
declarations.doc: Gibbs law `e^{-V(x)} dx / Z` with partition integral `Z = ∫ e^{-V}`. It is a probability measure when `e^{-V}` is integrable (`isProbabilityMeasure_gibbsMeasure`); otherwise the Bochner integral `Z` is zero and the definition carries no meaning.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_gibbsMeasure
declarations.doc: If `e^{-V}` is integrable, the Gibbs law is a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.diffusionGenerator
declarations.doc: Generator `L f(x) = ⟨∇f(x), b(t,x)⟩ + ½ ∑ᵢⱼ A(t,x)ᵢⱼ ∂ᵢ∂ⱼ f(x)` of a diffusion with drift `b` and infinitesimal covariance `A`, in Euclidean coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsFokkerPlanckSolution
declarations.doc: Weak Fokker–Planck equation on `[0, T]`: every `μ t` is a probability measure and, for every smooth compactly supported test function `f`, `∫ f dμₜ = ∫ f dμ₀ + ∫₀ᵗ ∫ L f dμₛ ds`, with the integrability needed to make sense of the right side.

declarations.name: CKSD.eulerMaruyamaStep
declarations.doc: Euler–Maruyama step `x + h b(x) + √h σ z` with an already sampled standard Gaussian increment `z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.langevinStepLaw
declarations.doc: Law after one step `x ↦ x - h ∇V(x) + √(2h) Z` of the unadjusted Langevin algorithm started from the law `P`, with `Z` an independent standard Gaussian vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaAcceptance
declarations.doc: Acceptance probability of a move from `x` to `y` in the Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm with target `e^{-V}` and Gaussian proposal `N(x - h ∇V(x), 2h I)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ddpmStep
declarations.doc: Denoising (DDPM) update `x + h s(x) + √((t - h) h / t) z` for variance-exploding Brownian noising, with fitted score `s`, remaining time `t`, step `h`, and a standard Gaussian draw `z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.intervalIntegral_eq_zero_of_nonmeasurable_component
declarations.doc: A nonmeasurable time coefficient forces a vector-valued integral to vanish under the Bochner convention whenever one fixed scalar component recovers that coefficient.

declarations.name: CKSD.intervalIntegral_translating_rotation_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The planar translating/rotating drift has a scalar component that recovers its time coefficient whenever the second coordinate of the frozen state is nonzero.

declarations.name: CKSD.probabilityFlowVelocity
declarations.doc: Velocity `-f(T-t,x) + ½ g gᵀ(T-t) ∇ log p_{T-t}(x)` of the probability flow on `[0, T)`, and `0` outside.

declarations.name: CKSD.probabilityFlow_isContinuityEquation_and_map
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.63, probability-flow part: the time-reversed marginals `qₜ = p_{T-t}` of a diffusion with positive `C¹` densities solve the continuity equation with the probability-flow velocity on every `(0, T')`, `T' < T`, and when that velocity is Lipschitz the continuous flow started from `p_T` has law `p_{T-t}`. The forward marginals are a weak Fokker–Planck solution with a finite initial second moment; the reverse-time stochastic equation is not part of this statement.

declarations.name: CKSD.varianceExplodingLaw
declarations.doc: The law `π * N(0, tI)` of `Y + √t ξ` with `Y ∼ π` and independent standard normal `ξ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.varianceExplodingScore
declarations.doc: Score `∇ log (π * N(0, tI))(x)`, written by Tweedie's formula as the ratio `∫ (y - x)/t · e^{-‖x-y‖²/2t} π(dy) / ∫ e^{-‖x-y‖²/2t} π(dy)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ddpmLaw
declarations.doc: Law of the DDPM sampler after `n` steps along the times `τ`, started from `N(0, TI)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_ddpmLaw_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.75: relative-entropy bound for the DDPM sampler under only a finite second moment, for steps `hₙ ≤ h̄(T - τₙ)` with `h̄ ≤ 1/2`, early stopping `δ = T - τ_N`, and the accumulated score error `ε²_sc = ∑ hₙ 𝔼_{π_{T-τₙ}} ‖ŝ_{T-τₙ} - ∇ log π_{T-τₙ}‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_ddpm_geometric_schedule
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.75: the geometric step schedule. With `N` least such that `(1 - h̄)ᴺ T ≤ δ`, the times `τₙ = T - (1 - h̄)ⁿ T` for `n < N` and `τ_N = T - δ` satisfy the step hypothesis, and `N ≤ 1 + h̄⁻¹ log(T/δ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ddpmStepRatio
declarations.doc: Step ratio `h̄ = ε² / (2d(1 + log(T/δ)))` of the DDPM parameter choice of GAPS 104.75.

declarations.name: CKSD.ddpmStepRatio_pos
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.75: the parameter choice `h̄ = ε²/(2d(1 + log(T/δ)))` is positive for `0 < ε² ≤ d` and `0 < δ < T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ddpmStepRatio_le_half
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.75: the parameter choice `h̄ = ε²/(2d(1 + log(T/δ)))` is admissible, `h̄ ≤ 1/2`, for `0 < ε² ≤ d` and `0 < δ < T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.div_two_mul_add_two_mul_ddpmStepRatio_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.75: with `T = m₂²/ε²` and `h̄ = ε²/(2d(1 + log(T/δ)))`, the deterministic part `m₂²/(2T) + 2h̄d(1 + log(T/δ))` of the KL bound equals `3ε²/2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_add_inv_ddpmStepRatio_mul_log
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.75: with `h̄ = ε²/(2d(1 + log(T/δ)))`, the schedule bound `1 + h̄⁻¹ log(T/δ)` on the number of steps equals `1 + 2dε⁻²(1 + log(T/δ)) log(T/δ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.clm_apply_gradient_eq_sum
declarations.doc: A linear functional applied to a gradient, in Euclidean coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.gradient_log_eq_inv_smul
declarations.doc: The gradient of `log m` is `∇m / m` where `m` is differentiable and nonzero.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_fderiv_gradient_add_mul_laplacian_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Integration by parts on `ℝᵈ`: `∫ (∇f · ∇m + m Δf) = 0` for compactly supported `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isFokkerPlanckSolution_add_score_of_continuityEquation
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.76: smooth positive densities solving the continuity equation with velocity `v` also solve the Fokker–Planck equation of `dX = (v + ε∇ log μ)(X) dt + √(2ε) dW`, for every continuous `ε ≥ 0`. Both equations are taken in the weak integral form on `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_marginalPreservingDiffusion
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.76, constant noise level: if the jointly Borel drift `bₜ = vₜ + ε∇ log μₜ` is Lipschitz uniformly in `t ∈ [0, 1]` and `∫₀¹ ∫ ‖bₜ‖ dμₜ dt < ∞`, a continuous solution with interval-integrable pathwise drift of `Xₜ = X₀ + ∫₀ᵗ bₛ(Xₛ) ds + √(2ε) Wₜ` with `X₀ ∼ μ₀` independent of the Brownian motion has law `μₜ` for every `t ∈ [0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.stochasticInterpolant_score
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.76: the score of a stochastic interpolant. For `Xₜ = Iₜ(X₀, X₁) + γₜ Z` with standard normal `Z` independent of the coupling and `γₜ > 0`, the law of `Xₜ` has a smooth positive density `mₜ` and `∇ log mₜ(Xₜ) = -γₜ⁻¹ 𝔼[Z | Xₜ]` almost surely.

declarations.name: CKSD.stochasticInterpolant_integral_sub_eq_integral_velocity
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.76: the velocity of a stochastic interpolant, in the weak form of the continuity equation. Let `Xₜ = Iₜ(X₀, X₁) + γₜ Z` with `I` and `γ` continuously differentiable in `t`, and `∫₀¹ 𝔼‖∂ₜIₜ(X₀, X₁)‖² dt < ∞` (continuity of `γ̇` makes a bound on `∫₀¹ γ̇ₜ² dt` unnecessary), and let `vₜ(Xₜ)` be, for every `t ∈ (0, 1)`, a version of `𝔼[∂ₜIₜ + γ̇ₜ Z | Xₜ]`. Then for every smooth compactly supported `φ` and `0 < a ≤ b < 1`, `𝔼 φ(X_b) - 𝔼 φ(X_a) = ∫ₐᵇ 𝔼[∇φ(Xₜ) · vₜ(Xₜ)] dt`. The square-integrability in `t` does not make `∂ₜIₜ` integrable at every fixed `t`, so the identity is stated in integrated form.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivWithinAt_right_step
declarations.doc: A right-continuous step has zero right derivative everywhere, including at its jump.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_nonconstant_zero_right_derivative
declarations.doc: Zero right derivatives and an initial condition do not imply the constant ODE solution.

declarations.name: CKSD.cellCount
declarations.doc: The cell counts `#{l | jₗ = i}` of an assignment of `n` observations to cells, as reals.

declarations.name: CKSD.cellCount_nonneg
declarations.doc: Cell counts are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.cellCount_succ
declarations.doc: Splitting off the first observation adds one to the count of its cell.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_prod_mul_dirichletMeasure
declarations.doc: **Multinomial–Dirichlet conjugacy.** Weighting the Dirichlet law `Dir(a)` by the likelihood `∏ₗ y_{jₗ}` of an assignment `j` of `n` observations to cells gives, after normalization, the Dirichlet law `Dir(a + counts(j))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_cells_eq_dirichletMeasure
declarations.doc: The Dirichlet marginal of a Dirichlet process on a partition indexed by any finite type: `IsDirichletProcess` states it for partitions indexed by `Fin k`, and the Dirichlet laws are compatible with reindexing (TauCeti's aggregation law along a bijection).

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_toLp_measureReal
declarations.doc: The vector of cell masses of a measurable random measure is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_prod_measureReal_of_isDirichletProcess
declarations.doc: **Size-biased expansion over a partition.** For a Dirichlet process `P` with base `α`, a partition `R` into cells of positive mass, and an assignment `p` of `n` observations to cells, weighting by the likelihood `∏ₗ P(R (p l))` turns the law of the cell masses into the Dirichlet law with parameters `α(R k)` plus the counts of `p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_prod_measureReal_of_subset
declarations.doc: **Expansion over a refined partition.** For a Dirichlet process `P` with base `α`, a partition `A` into cells of positive mass, and sets `B l ⊆ A (c l)`, weighting by the likelihood `∏ₗ P(B l)` turns the law of the cell masses of `A` into the Dirichlet law with parameters `α(A i)` plus the counts of `c`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleCount
declarations.doc: The number of the observations `x l` lying in a set `A`, as a real number.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleCount_nonneg
declarations.doc: Sample counts are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_sampleCount
declarations.doc: The sample count of a measurable set is a measurable function of the sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleCount_eq_cellCount
declarations.doc: If each observation `x l` lies in the cell `A (c l)` of a disjoint family, the sample counts of the cells are the cell counts of `c`.

declarations.name: CKSD.subcellSets
declarations.doc: The measurable sets contained in a cell of `A` or in the complement of its union.

declarations.name: CKSD.isPiSystem_subcellSets
declarations.doc: The sets contained in a cell form a π-system.

declarations.name: CKSD.generateFrom_subcellSets
declarations.doc: The sets contained in a cell of a measurable family generate the σ-algebra.

declarations.name: CKSD.isCountablySpanning_subcellSets
declarations.doc: The sets contained in a cell of a finite family are countably spanning.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_map_posterior_eq_dirichletMeasure
declarations.doc: **Posterior cell masses of a Dirichlet process.** Let the prior be the law of a Dirichlet process with base `α`, let the data be an i.i.d. sample of size `n` from the random measure, and let `post` be a posterior kernel. For a partition `A` into cells of positive `α`-mass whose union has `α`-null complement, for almost every sample `x` the posterior law of the cell masses is the Dirichlet law with parameters `α(A i)` plus the number of observations in `A i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.memPartitionMasses
declarations.doc: The masses that a probability measure gives to the cells of the `m`-th finite partition generated by a sequence of sets `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.memPartitionMassesSpace
declarations.doc: The σ-algebra on probability measures generated by the cell masses of the `m`-th partition generated by `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_memPartitionMasses
declarations.doc: The cell masses of a finite partition into measurable cells depend measurably on the probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.ext_of_map_memPartitionMasses
declarations.doc: **Uniqueness of laws of random measures.** Two laws of random probability measures on a space whose σ-algebra is generated by a sequence of measurable sets `t` agree as soon as they give the same laws to the cell masses of every finite partition `memPartition t m`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_dirichletPosteriorBase
declarations.doc: The posterior base measure of a measurable set is its prior mass plus its sample count.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_isDirichletProcess_posterior
declarations.doc: **Conjugacy of the Dirichlet process.** Let the prior be the law of a Dirichlet process with base `α ≠ 0` on a countably generated space, let the data be an i.i.d. sample of size `n` from the random measure, and let `post` be a posterior kernel. If a Dirichlet process law exists for each posterior base measure `α + ∑ₗ δ_{x l}`, then for almost every sample the posterior is the Dirichlet process law with that base measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsDirichletProcessLaw
declarations.doc: A law on probability measures is the law of a Dirichlet process with base measure `α`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_measureReal_of_isDirichletProcess
declarations.doc: The mean of a cell of a Dirichlet process is its share of the base measure. TauCeti's Dirichlet mean is applied to the two-cell partition `{A, Aᶜ}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isDirichletProcess_stickBreaking
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.15: Sethuraman's stick-breaking representation. With independent `Beta(1, |α|)` fractions and independent atoms of law `α / |α|`, independent of each other, every measurable random probability measure agreeing a.s. with `∑ πₖ δ_{θₖ}` is a Dirichlet process.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isDirichletProcessLaw
declarations.doc: **Existence of the Dirichlet process.** For every finite nonzero base measure there is a law of a Dirichlet process: the law of Sethuraman's stick-breaking measure on the product of the i.i.d. fraction and atom spaces, where the stick-breaking measure is almost surely a probability measure (`CKSD.ae_tsum_stickBreakingWeight_eq_one`).

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_isDirichletProcessLaw_posterior
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.15: conjugacy of the Dirichlet process. For every version of the posterior given `n` conditionally independent observations, the posterior is a.s. a Dirichlet process with base `α + ∑ δ_{xᵢ}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_integral_posterior_eq_polyaPredictiveLaw
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.15: the Blackwell–MacQueen predictive law is the posterior mean of the random measure, granted posterior conjugacy (`ae_isDirichletProcessLaw_posterior`).

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_langevin_generator_eq_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.37: invariance of the Gibbs law for the scalar Langevin generator. For a `C¹` potential `V` and a compactly supported `C²` test function `f`, `∫ (f'' - V' f') e^{-V} / Z = 0` with `Z = ∫ e^{-V}`. The identity holds for the unnormalized weight `e^{-V}`, so it needs no integrability of `e^{-V}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.dist_synchronous_langevin_le_exp
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.38: synchronous coupling. If `x` and `y` solve `x t = x 0 - ∫₀ᵗ b(x s) ds + W t` with the same continuous forcing `W` (so that their difference solves the integral equation below) and `⟪b x - b y, x - y⟫ ≥ m ‖x - y‖²`, then `‖x t - y t‖ ≤ e^{-mt} ‖x 0 - y 0‖`. The coefficient `m` may be any real number; `m > 0` gives contraction.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_exp_neg_mul_of_hasDerivAt_neg_of_two_mul_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.41: the Grönwall step of exponential entropy decay. If `E` is continuous on `[0, ∞)` with `E' = -I` on `(0, ∞)` (dissipation of relative entropy by Fisher information) and `2m E ≤ I` (a logarithmic Sobolev inequality), then `E t ≤ e^{-2mt} E 0` for `t ≥ 0`. The coefficient `m` may be any real number.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sub_score_div_two_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.64: Hyvärinen's score-matching identity on `ℝ`. For a positive `C¹` density `p` with square-integrable score `p'/p` and a compactly supported `C¹` candidate score `g`, `𝔼[(g - p'/p)²/2] = 𝔼[g²/2 + g'] + 𝔼[(p'/p)²/2]`, so the score-matching risk is minimized without knowledge of `p'/p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condExp_prod_of_condExp_slices
declarations.doc: Slice conditional expectations give the conditional expectation on the product space: if `v t (X t ·)` is a version of `𝔼[W | X t]` for `ρ`-almost every `t`, then `(t, ω) ↦ v t (X t ω)` is a version of `𝔼[W | (t, X t)]` under `ρ ⊗ π`.

declarations.name: CKSD.wasserstein_le_barycentric_velocity_action
declarations.doc: SYNOPSIS 104.72: action bounds for the barycentric velocity of a straight coupling. For a coupling `π` with finite second moment and `X_t = (1 - t) X₀ + t X₁`, if `v t (X_t)` is a version of `𝔼[X₁ - X₀ | X_t]` for every `t ∈ [0, 1]`, then `W₂²(π₀, π₁) ≤ ∫₀¹ 𝔼‖v t (X_t)‖² dt ≤ 𝔼‖X₁ - X₀‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasDensity.measure_nonpos_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A law with real density `p` gives no mass to the set where `p ≤ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasDensity.ae_pos
declarations.doc: Under a law with density `p`, the density is almost surely positive.

declarations.name: CKSD.llr_ae_eq_log_sub_log
declarations.doc: For laws `P = p · μ` and `Q = q · μ` with `P ≪ Q`, the log-likelihood ratio `log (dP/dQ)` is `P`-almost surely `log p - log q`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_log_sub_log_eq_neg_toReal_klDiv
declarations.doc: For probability laws `P = p · μ`, `Q = q · μ` with finite Kullback–Leibler divergence `KL(P ‖ Q)`, the function `log q - log p` is `P`-integrable with integral `-KL(P ‖ Q)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.prod_mul_exp_le_prod
declarations.doc: If `a` and `b` are positive and `∑ (log bᵢ - log aᵢ) ≥ -γ n`, then `(∏ aᵢ) e^{-γ n} ≤ ∏ bᵢ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_infinitePi_evidence_lt
declarations.doc: **Evidence lower bound.** Let `P θ = f θ · μ` and let `B` be a measurable set of parameters with `KL(P θ₀ ‖ P θ) < γ` for `θ ∈ B`. Under the true i.i.d. law `P θ₀^∞`, the probability that the evidence `∫ ∏_{i<n} f θ (ωᵢ) dπ(θ)` is below `π(B)/2 · ∏_{i<n} f θ₀ (ωᵢ) · e^{-γ n}` tends to zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_sum_lt_neg_two_mul_le
declarations.doc: Chebyshev bound for the sum of independent copies of a real variable with mean at least `-δ` and second moment at most `δ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_log_sub_log_of_secondMoment
declarations.doc: The log-density ratio has a finite second moment when the likelihood-ratio second moment used in the posterior contraction hypotheses is finite.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_sum_log_ratio_lt_le
declarations.doc: The probability that the log likelihood of an alternative in a KL and second-moment ball falls below `-2 n δ` is at most `1/(n δ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_infinitePi_evidence_lt_le
declarations.doc: Quantitative evidence lower bound on a KL and log-likelihood second-moment ball. For `n > 0`, the evidence is at least half the prior mass of the ball times the true likelihood and `exp (-2 n δ)`, except on a set of probability at most `2/(n δ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_infinitePi_evidence_lt_of_secondMoment
declarations.doc: The evidence lower bound holds with probability tending to one for varying KL and second-moment balls of radius `δ n`, provided `n δ n → ∞`. The prior mass of each ball may vanish, and no lower bound on that mass is needed for this relative evidence estimate.

declarations.name: CKSD.infinitePi_map_fin_val
declarations.doc: The first `n` coordinates of an i.i.d. sequence with law `P` have the `n`-fold product law.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockSample
declarations.doc: The `j`-th block of length `k` of a sequence: the coordinates `j k, …, j k + k - 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_blockSample
declarations.doc: The block map is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.infinitePi_map_blockSample
declarations.doc: Each block of length `k` of an i.i.d. sequence has the `k`-fold product law.

declarations.name: CKSD.iIndepFun_blockSample
declarations.doc: The consecutive blocks of length `k` of an i.i.d. sequence are independent.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_sum_blockSample_ge_le
declarations.doc: Hoeffding's inequality for block statistics: if `g` takes values in an interval of length one, the centred sum of `g` over the first `m` blocks of length `k` of an i.i.d. sequence exceeds `m/4` with probability at most `exp (-m/8)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_exponentiallyConsistent_tests
declarations.doc: **Exponentially consistent tests.** If tests `φ n` of `P θ₀` against the alternatives `A` have type I error tending to zero and type II error tending to zero uniformly on `A`, then there are tests `ψ n` and `β > 0` whose type I error and uniform type II error are both at most `exp (1/8) exp (-β n)`. The tests `ψ n` reject when at least half of the block tests reject.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLangevinFlow
declarations.doc: The flow of laws of the overdamped Langevin diffusion: a weak Fokker–Planck solution with drift `-gradV` and covariance `2I` on `[0, T]` for every `T ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.chiSqDiv
declarations.doc: Chi-squared divergence `∫ (dμ/dν - 1)² dν` for `μ ≪ ν`, and `∞` otherwise.

declarations.name: CKSD.poincareInequality_iff_chiSqDiv_langevin_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.44: the Poincaré inequality with constant `C` is equivalent to exponential decay at rate `2/C` of the chi-squared divergence along every Langevin flow.

declarations.name: CKSD.logSobolevInequality_iff_klDiv_langevin_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.44: the logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant `C` is equivalent to exponential decay at rate `2/C` of the relative entropy along every Langevin flow.

declarations.name: CKSD.wasserstein_sq_langevin_le_of_logSobolev
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.44: under a logarithmic Sobolev inequality, the Otto–Villani inequality gives `W₂²(μₜ, π) ≤ 2C e^{-2t/C} KL(μ₀‖π)` along every Langevin flow.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_one_add_mul_log_one_add_sub_le
declarations.doc: Second-order Taylor bound for `y log y` at `y = 1`: `|(1+s) log(1+s) - s - s²/2| ≤ 4|s|³` for `|s| ≤ 1/2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_comp_of_abs_le
declarations.doc: A continuous function of a bounded continuous real function is integrable under a finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_le_of_logSobolevInequality_of_abs_le
declarations.doc: A logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant `C` gives the Poincaré bound with constant `C` for bounded smooth test functions: apply it to `1 + εg` and expand the entropy to second order in `ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_mul_arctan_inv_mul
declarations.doc: The truncations `R arctan(s/R)`, `R = n + 1`, converge to `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.poincareInequality_of_logSobolevInequality
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.44: a logarithmic Sobolev inequality implies the Poincaré inequality with the same constant, for every probability measure on a real normed space. Unbounded test functions are reduced to the bounded case `variance_le_of_logSobolevInequality_of_abs_le` through the truncations `R arctan(f/R)` and dominated convergence.

declarations.name: CKSD.add_inner_add_le_of_isStronglyMonotoneGradient
declarations.doc: Quadratic lower bound from a strongly monotone gradient: `V x ≥ V 0 + ⟪∇V(0), x⟫ + (α/2) ‖x‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_exp_neg_of_isStronglyMonotoneGradient
declarations.doc: For a potential with a strongly monotone gradient (`∇²V ⪰ αI` with `α > 0`), the Gibbs density `e^{-V}` is integrable, by the quadratic lower bound `add_inner_add_le_of_isStronglyMonotoneGradient` and Gaussian integrability.

declarations.name: CKSD.logSobolevInequality_gibbsMeasure_of_bounded_perturbation
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.44: Bakry–Émery and Holley–Stroock. If `V = V₀ + ψ` with `∇²V₀ ⪰ mI`, `m > 0`, and `a ≤ ψ ≤ b`, then the Gibbs law satisfies the logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant `e^{b-a}/m`.

declarations.name: CKSD.poincareInequality_gibbsMeasure_of_bounded_perturbation
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.44: under the hypotheses of the Bakry–Émery and Holley–Stroock theorem, the Gibbs law of `V₀ + ψ` satisfies the Poincaré inequality with constant `e^{b-a}/m`. It follows from the logarithmic Sobolev inequality `logSobolevInequality_gibbsMeasure_of_bounded_perturbation`.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_mem_moreauYosidaResolvent_jkoFreeEnergy
declarations.doc: Every positive JKO step has a unique minimizer for a continuous nonnegative potential and one finite-energy comparison law.

declarations.name: CKSD.jko_scheme_tendsto_fokkerPlanck
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.43: the Jordan–Kinderlehrer–Otto theorem. Every JKO step for the free energy has a unique minimizer, and the piecewise-constant interpolations converge, weakly in `L¹` at every time and strongly in `L¹((0,T) × ℝᵈ)`, to a weak solution of `∂ₜρ = Δρ + ∇·(ρ∇V)` with datum `ρ₀`. Uniqueness of the limiting weak solution is not part of this statement.

declarations.name: CKSD.gibbsMeasure_quadratic_eq_map_stdGaussian
declarations.doc: The Gibbs law of an isotropic quadratic potential is a scaled standard Gaussian.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_pos_gaussianReal_tail_eq_quarter
declarations.doc: A fixed positive threshold has standard Gaussian upper-tail mass exactly one quarter.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_quadraticGibbs_halfspace_warm_start
declarations.doc: Conditioning a scaled isotropic Gaussian on a fixed upper-quartile halfspace gives a four-warm probability law supported on that halfspace.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_schwartz_sub
declarations.doc: A translate of a Schwartz function is integrable under every finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasFDerivAt_integral_schwartz_sub
declarations.doc: Differentiation commutes with averaging translates of a Schwartz function under a finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.contDiff_integral_schwartz_sub_nat
declarations.doc: A finite-measure average of Schwartz translates has derivatives of every finite order.

declarations.name: CKSD.contDiff_integral_schwartz_sub
declarations.doc: A finite-measure average of translates of a Schwartz function is smooth.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSmoothingKernel
declarations.doc: The Lebesgue density of the centered isotropic Gaussian with standard deviation `σ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_schwartz_gaussianSmoothingKernel
declarations.doc: At positive scale the isotropic Gaussian density is a Schwartz function, using TauCeti's Gaussian.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_affine_stdGaussian_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: An affine image of the standard Gaussian has the translated isotropic Gaussian density. The change of variables uses TauCeti's `Measure.map_affine_withDensity`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSmoothingKernel_pos
declarations.doc: The isotropic Gaussian density is strictly positive at positive scale.

declarations.name: CKSD.contDiff_gaussianSmoothingKernel
declarations.doc: The isotropic Gaussian density is smooth at positive scale.

declarations.name: CKSD.smooth_positive_gaussianSmoothing
declarations.doc: Convolving any probability measure with a nondegenerate isotropic Gaussian gives a smooth strictly positive density.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_add_gaussian_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: The law of the sum of independent signals and Gaussian noise has the averaged Gaussian density.

declarations.name: CKSD.condExp_of_joint_density
declarations.doc: Conditional expectation from a joint density: divide the density-weighted numerator by the positive marginal density. The observation space needs no topological structure.

declarations.name: CKSD.fderiv_gaussianSmoothingKernel
declarations.doc: The derivative of the isotropic Gaussian density is its density times the linear score.

declarations.name: CKSD.gradient_gaussianSmoothing
declarations.doc: The gradient of a Gaussian convolution is the average of the Gaussian density gradients.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_pair_add_gaussian_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: The joint law of a signal and its sum with independent Gaussian noise has the Gaussian likelihood density relative to signal law times Lebesgue measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.det_fderiv_hamiltonianFlow
declarations.doc: Hamiltonian flow derivatives have determinant one.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurePreserving_hamiltonianFlow
declarations.doc: Hamiltonian time maps preserve any additive Haar measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurePreserving_withDensity_of_invariant
declarations.doc: An invariant measurable density preserves a measure-preserving transformation.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurePreserving_hamiltonianFlow_withDensity
declarations.doc: Any measurable density depending only on energy is invariant under Hamiltonian flow.

declarations.name: CKSD.gibbsMeasure_prod_stdGaussian_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: The Gibbs-Gaussian phase law has density depending only on mechanical energy.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurePreserving_mechanicalFlow_gibbsMeasure
declarations.doc: Ideal mechanical Hamiltonian flow preserves Gibbs positions and independent Gaussian momenta.

declarations.name: CKSD.mechanicalHamiltonian
declarations.doc: Mechanical energy on position-momentum phase space.

declarations.name: CKSD.mechanicalVelocity
declarations.doc: The position-momentum velocity of Hamilton's equations.

declarations.name: CKSD.lipschitzWith_mechanicalVelocity
declarations.doc: A Lipschitz force gives a globally Lipschitz Hamiltonian velocity.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasFDerivAt_mechanicalHamiltonian
declarations.doc: The derivative of mechanical energy consists of the potential gradient and momentum.

declarations.name: CKSD.hamiltonianVectorField_mechanicalHamiltonian
declarations.doc: Mechanical Hamilton's equations have velocity `(p,-gradV(q))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.contDiff_mechanicalHamiltonian
declarations.doc: Mechanical energy is twice continuously differentiable for a C2 potential.

declarations.name: CKSD.mechanicalFlow
declarations.doc: The canonical mechanical flow of a globally Lipschitz force.

declarations.name: CKSD.mechanicalFlow_eq_hamiltonianFlow
declarations.doc: The mechanical flow is the symplectic Hamiltonian flow of its energy.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_mechanicalFlow
declarations.doc: Mechanical-flow trajectories solve Hamilton's equations.

declarations.name: CKSD.mechanicalFlow_fst_eq
declarations.doc: Position along a mechanical orbit is the integral of momentum.

declarations.name: CKSD.mechanicalFlow_snd_eq
declarations.doc: Momentum along a mechanical orbit is the integral of the force.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_intervalIntegral_sq_le
declarations.doc: Squared norm of a continuous time integral is bounded by length times its squared energy.

declarations.name: CKSD.mechanical_position_error_sq_le
declarations.doc: The local position error of Hamiltonian flow against its frozen-force quadratic step is controlled only by the time integral of squared momentum.

declarations.name: CKSD.statisticalHellingerDistance
declarations.doc: Real Hellinger adapter in the convention `h² = integral (sqrt p - sqrt q)²` for probability measures. For arbitrary measures an infinite squared divergence is totalized to zero by `ENNReal.toReal`; distance interpretations require finite divergence.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sqrt_rnDeriv_eq_integral_sqrt_density_mul
declarations.doc: Hellinger affinity in terms of densities relative to a common dominating measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasDensity.memLp_sqrt
declarations.doc: The square root of an integrable nonnegative density belongs to `L²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.statisticalHellingerDistance_sq_eq_integral
declarations.doc: Hellinger distance is the `L²` distance between square roots of densities.

declarations.name: CKSD.hellingerScore
declarations.doc: Bounded Hellinger score separating a null density `p` from an alternative density `q`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_hellingerScore
declarations.doc: The Hellinger score is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_hellingerScore_le_one
declarations.doc: The Hellinger score takes values in `[-1,1]`, including points where both densities vanish.

declarations.name: CKSD.mul_hellingerScore_sq_le
declarations.doc: A density-weighted squared Hellinger score is at most the squared square-root difference.

declarations.name: CKSD.sub_mul_hellingerScore_eq
declarations.doc: The mean separation identity for the Hellinger score.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_mul_le_sqrt
declarations.doc: Cauchy–Schwarz for real `L²` functions, in square-root moment form.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_hellingerScore
declarations.doc: The bounded Hellinger score belongs to every `Lᵖ` under a finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_hellingerScore_sub_eq
declarations.doc: The difference between the alternative and null score means is the squared Hellinger distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_hellingerScore_sq_le
declarations.doc: The squared score has expectation at most the squared Hellinger distance under its alternative.

declarations.name: CKSD.hellingerScore_swap
declarations.doc: Exchanging the densities negates the Hellinger score.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_sub_le_hellinger
declarations.doc: Changing a law by Hellinger distance `ρ` changes the mean of a bounded score by at most `2 ρ a + ρ²`, when the score's second moment under the reference law is at most `a²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_le_of_hellinger
declarations.doc: A bounded score's second moment under a perturbed law is at most twice its reference second moment plus twice the squared Hellinger distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.statisticalHellingerDistance_triangle_of_hasDensity
declarations.doc: Triangle inequality for Hellinger distance among laws with a common dominating measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_centered_hellingerScore_sum_ge_le
declarations.doc: A Bernstein bound for an iid bounded score with second moment at most `3h²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_hellinger_ball_test
declarations.doc: Exponentially accurate tests of a law against a Hellinger ball around an alternative. The score test is uniform over all dominated laws in the ball of radius `h(P,Q)/8`.

declarations.name: CKSD.seqDistSq
declarations.doc: Squared `ℓ²` distance between real sequences, possibly infinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.inverseProblemSobolevBall
declarations.doc: The Sobolev ellipsoid `S^β(R) = {f : ∑ⱼ j^{2β} fⱼ² ≤ R²}`, with `j` running from `1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.inverseProblemLaw
declarations.doc: Law of the observations `Yⱼ = κⱼ fⱼ + ε Zⱼ` with independent standard normal `Zⱼ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.inverseProblemRisk
declarations.doc: Mean squared `ℓ²` risk of an estimator at the truth `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSeqPosterior
declarations.doc: Posterior under the prior with independent `fⱼ ∼ N(0, j^{-1-2β})`, in conjugate form: coordinate `j` is normal with mean `λⱼκⱼYⱼ / (κⱼ²λⱼ + ε²)` and variance `λⱼε² / (κⱼ²λⱼ + ε²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasPolynomialSingularValues
declarations.doc: Polynomially decaying singular values: `c₀⁻¹ j^{-a} ≤ κⱼ ≤ c₀ j^{-a}`, `j ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_ofReal_sq_add_gaussianReal
declarations.doc: Second moment of an affine function under a normal law, in `ℝ≥0∞`: `∫⁻ ((c X - d)² + s) = (cμ - d)² + c² v + s` for `X ∼ N(μ, v)` and `s ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.rpow_neg_add_mul_rpow_neg_sub_one_le
declarations.doc: Tangent-line estimate for `t ↦ t^{-m}`: `x^{-m} + m x^{-m-1} ≤ (x - 1)^{-m}` for `m > 0`, `x > 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tsum_ofReal_rpow_add_le
declarations.doc: Shifted `p`-series tail bound by telescoping: `∑_{n ≥ 1} (T + n)^{-q} ≤ T^{1-q}/(q-1)` for `T > 0`, `q > 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_lintegral_seqDistSq_gaussianSeqPosterior
declarations.doc: Expected posterior squared `ℓ²` distance from the truth in the Gaussian sequence model: the sum over coordinates of squared bias, variance of the posterior mean, and posterior variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSeqPosterior_term_le
declarations.doc: Coordinatewise bounds for the Gaussian sequence posterior with `x = ε²` and `n = j + 1`: the squared relative bias is at most `c₀² x^r n^{2β}`, the variance of the posterior mean is at most the posterior variance, and the posterior variance is at most `c₀² 2^{1+2β} (T + n)^{-(1+2β)}` with `T = x^{-1/(2β+2a+1)}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tsum_gaussianSeqPosterior_risk_le
declarations.doc: Uniform bound on the expected posterior squared distance over the Sobolev ellipsoid: at most `(c₀² R² + c₀² 2^{1+2β}/β) (ε²)^r` with `r = 2β/(2β+2a+1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_gaussianSeqPosterior_contraction
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.20: uniform posterior contraction at the minimax rate for the Gaussian prior `fⱼ ∼ N(0, j^{-1-2β})` matched to the Sobolev smoothness, for every `M_ε → ∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_minimax_rate_inverseProblem
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.20: the minimax `ℓ²` rate over a Sobolev ellipsoid in a mildly ill-posed linear inverse problem is `ε^r` with `r = 2β/(2β+2a+1)`. There are constants `0 < c ≤ C`, depending only on `a`, `β`, `R`, and `c₀`, such that for every operator with polynomially decaying singular values and every noise level `ε ∈ (0, 1]` some measurable estimator has worst-case squared risk at most `(C ε^r)²` and every measurable estimator has worst-case squared risk at least `(c ε^r)²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinLaw
declarations.doc: The underlying measure of a law in the Wasserstein space `P₂(ℝᵈ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.jkoFreeEnergy
declarations.doc: Free energy `∫ ρ log ρ + ∫ V dρ` on the Wasserstein space, with the entropy relative to Lebesgue measure; it is `⊤` for laws without a density.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinDensity
declarations.doc: Real Lebesgue density of the absolutely continuous part of a Wasserstein law. This represents the whole law when that law is absolutely continuous with respect to volume.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_exp_neg_mul_norm_sq
declarations.doc: Every centered Gaussian envelope on Euclidean space is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.jkoFreeEnergy_eq_klDiv_gaussian_add
declarations.doc: A quadratic change of reference identifies the free energy with Gaussian relative entropy plus potential energy and an explicit second-moment correction.

declarations.name: CKSD.jkoFreeEnergy_gaussian_lower_bound
declarations.doc: A nonnegative potential gives the usual quadratic Gaussian lower bound on the free energy.

declarations.name: CKSD.jkoFreeEnergy_ne_bot
declarations.doc: A nonnegative-potential free energy has no minus-infinite values on P2.

declarations.name: CKSD.ereal_le_liminf_of_positive_tilts
declarations.doc: Lower semicontinuity after every positive quadratic tilt implies lower semicontinuity along a sequence with bounded quadratic moments.

declarations.name: CKSD.jkoFreeEnergy_ne_top_iff_klDiv_gaussian_and_potential
declarations.doc: Finite free energy is equivalent to finite Gaussian relative entropy and potential energy.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_potential_of_jkoFreeEnergy_ne_top
declarations.doc: Finite free energy for a nonnegative continuous potential makes the potential integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_norm_sq_eq_wasserstein_dirac_sq
declarations.doc: The second moment is the square of the quadratic Wasserstein distance from the origin.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_integral_norm_sq_le_of_isBounded
declarations.doc: A Wasserstein-bounded sequence has uniformly bounded second moments.

declarations.name: CKSD.jkoFreeEnergy_add_quadratic_eq
declarations.doc: Adding the Gaussian quadratic correction leaves a narrowly lower-semicontinuous entropy and nonnegative potential, up to a finite normalization constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.jkoFreeEnergy_le_liminf_of_isBounded
declarations.doc: The free energy is narrowly lower semicontinuous along any Wasserstein-bounded sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_moreauYosida_jkoFreeEnergy_ne_bot
declarations.doc: Gaussian moment compensation bounds the JKO Moreau envelope below at a Dirac law for every positive step size.

declarations.name: CKSD.nonempty_moreauYosidaResolvent_jkoFreeEnergy
declarations.doc: Every positive JKO step for a continuous nonnegative potential has a minimizer.

declarations.name: CKSD.wasserstein_dist_sq_le_half_add_half
declarations.doc: The square of the Wasserstein distance is convex along ordinary mixtures.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_wasserstein_half_mixture
declarations.doc: Integration is affine along an ordinary half mixture.

declarations.name: CKSD.jkoFreeEnergy_toReal_half_mixture_lt
declarations.doc: The free energy is strictly convex along ordinary half mixtures of distinct finite-energy laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.subsingleton_moreauYosidaResolvent_jkoFreeEnergy
declarations.doc: A nonnegative continuous-potential JKO step has at most one minimizer, by ordinary-mixture strict entropy convexity. No convexity assumption on the potential is needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.kineticGenerator
declarations.doc: Generator `p·∇ₓf - (∇V(x) + γp)·∇ₚf + γΔₚf` of the kinetic Langevin diffusion.

declarations.name: CKSD.kineticGibbsMeasure
declarations.doc: The invariant law `π ⊗ N(0, I)` of the kinetic Langevin diffusion.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsKineticFokkerPlanckSolution
declarations.doc: Weak form of the kinetic Fokker–Planck equation on `[0, ∞)`, tested on smooth compactly supported functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.gradX
declarations.doc: Position gradient of a function on phase space.

declarations.name: CKSD.gradP
declarations.doc: Momentum gradient of a function on phase space.

declarations.name: CKSD.kineticCouplingNorm
declarations.doc: The twisted norm `|||(x,p)|||² = ‖x‖² + ‖x + 2p/γ‖²` of synchronous coupling.

declarations.name: CKSD.kineticH1Energy
declarations.doc: Weighted `H¹(𝛑)` energy `‖f‖² + β⁻¹‖∇ₓf‖² + ‖∇ₚf‖²` for `β > 0`, possibly infinite. Outside this temperature domain the integrand uses the totalized real inverse and `ENNReal.ofReal`, without an energy interpretation.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_hasDensity_kineticGibbsMeasure
declarations.doc: A smooth density and its logarithmic derivative for the kinetic Gibbs measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_kineticGenerator_eq_zero_of_fderiv_density
declarations.doc: Weighted divergence form of the kinetic generator has zero integral.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_kineticGenerator_eq_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.48: invariance of `π ⊗ N(0, I)`, in the weak form `∫ Lf d𝛑 = 0` for smooth compactly supported `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_kineticGenerator_not_symmetric
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.48: the kinetic Langevin diffusion is not reversible: its generator is not symmetric in `L²(𝛑)` on smooth compactly supported functions, in every positive dimension.

declarations.name: CKSD.kineticCouplingNorm_synchronous_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.48: contraction of synchronous coupling in the twisted norm at rate `α/γ`, for `αI ⪯ ∇²V ⪯ βI` and `γ ≥ √(2β)`. The differences of two copies driven by one Brownian motion solve the noiseless integral equations given as hypotheses.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_kinetic_hypocoercive_decay_of_poincare
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.48: `L²` hypocoercivity under a Poincaré inequality with constant `1/α` and `β`-smoothness, with friction `γ = c₀√β`. The relative density `fₜ = d𝛑ₜ/d𝛑 - 1` is assumed continuously differentiable; the constants depend only on `c₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_kinetic_entropic_hypocoercive_decay
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.48: entropic hypocoercivity under a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant `1/α`, with friction `γ = c₀√β`. The Lyapunov functional is the relative entropy plus a positive definite twisted Fisher information of the log-density `hₜ = log(d𝛑ₜ/d𝛑)`, assumed continuously differentiable. Here the rate constant `c'` may depend on `c₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSamplingPotential
declarations.doc: Standing sampling hypotheses on a potential: twice continuously differentiable, with gradient `gradV`, the gradient `β`-Lipschitz, and `e^{-V}` integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStronglyMonotoneGradient
declarations.doc: Strong monotonicity of the gradient, equivalent to `∇²V ⪰ αI` for a `C²` potential.

declarations.name: CKSD.ulaLaw
declarations.doc: Law of the unadjusted Langevin algorithm after `n` steps of size `h` from the initial law `μ₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_ula_iteration_complexity
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.39: iteration complexity of the unadjusted Langevin algorithm under `αI ⪯ ∇²V ⪯ βI`, both in `W₂` at the last iterate and in relative entropy for the average of the laws of iterates `N+1, …, 2N`. The initial law has a finite second moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_klDiv_ula_le_of_logSobolev
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.45: Vempala–Wibisono bound for the unadjusted Langevin algorithm. If the Gibbs law `π` satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant `1/α` and `V` is `β`-smooth (not necessarily convex), there is a universal `C` such that for `0 < h ≤ α / (4β²)` and all `N`, `KL(μ_N ‖ π) ≤ e^{-α N h} KL(μ₀ ‖ π) + C β² d h / α`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_wasserstein_ula_le_of_stronglyConvex
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.45: geometric `W₂` convergence of the unadjusted Langevin algorithm under `αI ⪯ ∇²V ⪯ βI`: there are universal `c, C` such that for `0 < h ≤ c / (βκ)` and all `N`, `W₂(μ_N, π) ≤ e^{-α N h / 2} W₂(μ₀, π) + C β √(d h) / α`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_mala_mixing_time_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.47: mixing-time upper bound for the `1/2`-lazy Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm from an `M`-warm start (`μ₀ ≤ Mπ`), with `Λ = log max {κ, d, M/ε, c₂}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isSamplingPotential_and_stronglyMonotone_gaussianPrecision
declarations.doc: Positive isotropic Gaussian precision gives the sampling hypotheses with every permitted curvature ratio at least one. The intrinsic Gaussian condition number remains one.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_mala_mixing_time_ge
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.47: a scale-adaptive lower bound for lazy MALA. For each step size `h` and accuracy `ε`, the target, curvature scale `α`, and warm initialization may be chosen afterwards. Here `κ` is the ratio of permitted upper and lower curvature bounds; the target need not attain that intrinsic condition number. A sufficiently concentrated isotropic Gaussian supplies the bound. This quantifier scope does not assert one fixed normalized target is hard for every step size.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaStepLaw
declarations.doc: One step of the `1/2`-lazy Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm acting on laws: the image of `μ ⊗ N(0, I) ⊗ U(0,1) ⊗ U(0,1)` under the lazy accept–reject map.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaStepLaw_def
declarations.doc: The explicit sampling representation of a lazy MALA step.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_malaStepMap
declarations.doc: The lazy MALA accept-reject update is measurable for measurable potential and gradient.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_malaStepLaw
declarations.doc: Lazy MALA maps probability laws to probability laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaStepLaw_apply_ge_of_acceptance_lt
declarations.doc: If proposals from an event have small acceptance on a noise event, the accept-reject update retains at least the corresponding rejected mass inside the original event.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_closedBall_real_ge
declarations.doc: A probability law on Euclidean space gives arbitrarily high mass to a bounded ball.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_large_gaussian_step
declarations.doc: A large effective step makes a prescribed noise ball typical and its acceptance bound small.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaStepLaw_real_apply_ge_of_acceptance_lt
declarations.doc: Uniform small acceptance on a high-probability noise event gives a real retained-mass bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaStepLaw_iterate_real_apply_ge
declarations.doc: The retained-mass bound iterates, and every lazy MALA iterate is a probability law.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaStepLaw_iterate_far_of_acceptance_lt
declarations.doc: A warm event retaining seven eighths of its mass stays far from a target giving it at most half.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_scaled_gaussian_mala_far
declarations.doc: For any finite budget and positive step, a scaled Gaussian admits a four-warm law whose lazy MALA iterates stay at total variation distance at least three eighths.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianPrecisionPotential
declarations.doc: The centered isotropic Gaussian potential with precision `a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianPrecisionPotential_def
declarations.doc: The potential as an explicit quadratic function.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianPrecisionPotential_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluation of the quadratic Gaussian potential.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianPrecisionGradient
declarations.doc: The gradient of the Gaussian potential with precision `a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianPrecisionGradient_def
declarations.doc: The gradient as an explicit scalar linear map.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianPrecisionGradient_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluation of the linear Gaussian gradient.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasGradientAt_gaussianPrecisionPotential
declarations.doc: The gradient identity for the isotropic Gaussian potential.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaAcceptance_gaussianPrecision
declarations.doc: The MALA log-acceptance ratio for an isotropic Gaussian is a difference of squared norms.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_gaussian_proposal_ge
declarations.doc: At large step size, typical Gaussian proposals from states away from zero have large norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaAcceptance_gaussian_one_le_exp
declarations.doc: Uniformly away from zero, large Gaussian MALA steps have exponentially small acceptance on the typical proposal-noise event.

declarations.name: CKSD.malaAcceptance_gaussian_rescale
declarations.doc: Rescaling a Gaussian target rescales the effective MALA step by inverse variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_proposal_rescale
declarations.doc: The Gaussian proposal commutes with simultaneous target and state rescaling.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_comp_pair_succ_eq
declarations.doc: One-step Markov property for a function of the last two states of a finite-state chain given by its path probabilities: for a function `F` of the prefix `(X 0, …, X n)`, `𝔼[F · φ(X n, X (n+1))] = 𝔼[F · ∑_y K(X n, y) φ(X n, y)]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_comp_eq_pow_mulVec
declarations.doc: `k`-step Markov property from the initial state of a finite-state chain given by its path probabilities: `𝔼[a(X 0) v(X k)] = 𝔼[a(X 0) (Kᵏ v)(X 0)]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.chainFiltration
declarations.doc: The natural filtration of a finite-state process: its `n`-th `σ`-algebra is generated by the prefix `(X 0, …, X n)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_chainFiltration
declarations.doc: A real function of the prefix `(X 0, …, X n)` is measurable for the `n`-th `σ`-algebra of the natural filtration.

declarations.name: CKSD.condExp_comp_pair_succ_ae_eq
declarations.doc: Markov property in conditional form: given the prefix `(X 0, …, X n)`, the conditional expectation of `φ(X n, X (n+1))` is `∑_y K(X n, y) φ(X n, y)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_abs_pow_mulVec_le_of_pos
declarations.doc: Geometric decay of `Kᵏ g` for a positive stochastic matrix `K` with invariant law `π` and a `π`-centred `g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_sub_mulVec_eq_of_pos
declarations.doc: Poisson equation for a positive stochastic matrix: `u = ∑ₖ Kᵏ g` solves `u - K u = g`, and `K u = ∑ₖ Kᵏ⁺¹ g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_finite_markov_chain_sum
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.24: central limit theorem for a stationary Markov chain on a finite space with a positive transition matrix `K` and invariant law `π`. The series of autocovariances of `f(Xₖ)` converges absolutely, and `√n (n⁻¹ ∑_{i<n} f(Xᵢ) - π f)` converges in law to the centred normal law with variance `σ² = Var f(X₀) + 2 ∑_{k ≥ 1} Cov(f(X₀), f(Xₖ))`. The proof solves the Poisson equation `u - K u = f - π f` by `u = ∑ₖ Kᵏ (f - π f)`, writes the centred sums as a martingale plus a bounded remainder, and identifies `σ²` with the martingale variance `∑ₓ π(x) ∑_y K(x,y) (u(y) - (K u)(x))²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_exists_tendsto_sum_martingaleDifference
declarations.doc: A real martingale-difference series converges almost surely when the expected squares of its increments are summable.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_unique_mcKeanVlasov_and_particleSystem
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.51: well-posedness. Under a Lipschitz drift, the McKean–Vlasov equation has a solution, unique up to indistinguishability among solutions with integrable marginals, and every particle system has a pathwise unique solution.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_particle_paths
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.51: propagation of chaos. For every horizon `T` and every `k`, the joint path law on `[0, T]` of the first `k` particles converges weakly to the `k`-fold product of the McKean–Vlasov path law. The hypotheses do not make the path maps measurable (particles of index at least `N` are unconstrained), so the statement is convergence of the image measures in the `ProbabilityMeasure` topology rather than `TendstoInDistribution`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution.ae_eq_of_interactionDrift
declarations.doc: With a bounded Lipschitz interaction, nonlinear solutions sharing the initial condition and Brownian forcing are indistinguishable; the Brownian property itself is not needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.lipschitzWith_integral_interaction
declarations.doc: Averaging a bounded Lipschitz interaction preserves its Lipschitz constant in position.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_iid_nonlinear_copies_on_Icc
declarations.doc: One nonlinear solution can be transported along the iid input forcings to iid continuous solution paths with the same marginal laws, on any fixed bounded time interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution.iIndepFun_interactionDrift
declarations.doc: For bounded Lipschitz interactions, separately given nonlinear solutions with iid initial conditions and Brownian drivers are independent and identically distributed at each time.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_integral_sq_interactionFluctuation_le_of_solutions
declarations.doc: Integrability and mean bound for time-integrated interaction fluctuations of nonlinear solutions driven by iid initial conditions and Brownian motions.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsParticleSystem.ae_residual_integral_eq
declarations.doc: Same-forcing particle and nonlinear solutions satisfy the residual coupling equation.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_lintegral_sup_particle_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.56: quantitative propagation of chaos for a bounded Lipschitz interaction, by synchronous coupling with independent nonlinear copies driven by the same initial values and Brownian motions. The constant depends only on `T`, the Lipschitz constants, and `sup |K|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.meanFieldV
declarations.doc: Correlation `V(θ) = 𝔼[Y φ(X, θ)]` of a feature with the response.

declarations.name: CKSD.meanFieldU
declarations.doc: Feature kernel `U(θ, θ') = 𝔼[φ(X, θ) φ(X, θ')]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.meanFieldRisk
declarations.doc: Population risk `½ 𝔼(Y - f_ρ(X))²` of the mean-field predictor `f_ρ = ∫ φ(·, θ) ρ(dθ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.meanFieldRisk_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.53: the elementary expansion `R(ρ) = ½𝔼Y² - ∫ V dρ + ½ ∫∫ U dρ dρ` for a bounded measurable feature map.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_meanField_limit
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.53: mean-field limit of two-layer network training. With bounded Lipschitz gradients of `V` and `U`, the nonlinear continuity equation `∂ₜρ = ∇·(ρ∇_θΨ(·; ρ))` has a unique narrowly continuous probability solution with datum `ρ₀`, and the empirical measures of the time-scaled gradient flow from independent `ρ₀`-distributed initial particles converge to it in `W₁`, almost surely and uniformly on bounded time intervals.

declarations.name: CKSD.globalSolution_fst_eq_add
declarations.doc: The time coordinate of an augmented flow increases at unit speed.

declarations.name: CKSD.backwardFlowTest
declarations.doc: Pull a terminal spatial test backward along an augmented flow.

declarations.name: CKSD.backwardFlowTest_globalSolution
declarations.doc: The backward-flow test is constant along every augmented trajectory.

declarations.name: CKSD.contDiff_backwardFlowTest
declarations.doc: A smooth vector field and smooth terminal test give a smooth backward-flow test.

declarations.name: CKSD.fderiv_backwardFlowTest_apply_field
declarations.doc: The backward-flow test solves the backward transport equation for the smooth field.

declarations.name: CKSD.backwardFlowTest_terminal
declarations.doc: The backward-flow test agrees with its prescribed terminal value.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_backwardFlowTest_le
declarations.doc: A uniform bound on the terminal test bounds the backward-flow test at every space-time point.

declarations.name: CKSD.lipschitzWith_globalSolution_time_of_bound
declarations.doc: A bounded vector field gives a uniform Lipschitz bound in flow time.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_smooth_bounded_clock
declarations.doc: A compactly supported smooth clock agrees with time on a neighbourhood of a bounded nonnegative interval. Its bounds do not depend on any vector field.

declarations.name: CKSD.boundedBackwardFlowTest
declarations.doc: A bounded smooth clock makes backward transport tests well-behaved on the whole time line.

declarations.name: CKSD.lipschitzWith_boundedBackwardFlowTest
declarations.doc: The global Lipschitz bound of a clocked backward test depends only on uniform bounds of the clock, field and terminal test.

declarations.name: CKSD.boundedBackwardFlowTest_eventuallyEq
declarations.doc: On an open interval where the clock is the identity, the clocked and ordinary tests agree on a neighbourhood of every space-time point.

declarations.name: CKSD.fderiv_boundedBackwardFlowTest_apply_field
declarations.doc: The clocked test satisfies the exact backward equation on intervals where the clock equals time.

declarations.name: CKSD.contDiff_boundedBackwardFlowTest
declarations.doc: A bounded clocked test inherits the smoothness of the field, clock and terminal data.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_approximate_backward_test
declarations.doc: Bounded Lipschitz velocity fields admit globally bounded smooth backward test functions whose transport residual tends uniformly to zero, with one derivative bound for all errors.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_stronglyMeasurable_version_of_ae_continuous
declarations.doc: An a.s. continuous process with a.e. strongly measurable sections on a separable first-countable time space has a sectionwise strongly measurable indistinguishable version.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBrownianReal.exists_integrable_uniform_bound
declarations.doc: A real Brownian motion has an integrable random bound uniform on a compact time interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_integrable_uniform_bound_brownianEuclidean
declarations.doc: Coordinatewise Brownian motion has an integrable random bound uniform on compact intervals.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_integrable_uniform_bound_add_brownianEuclidean
declarations.doc: An integrable initial vector plus Brownian motion admits a uniform integrable random bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_particle_path_sub_le_empirical_wasserstein
declarations.doc: A whole-path empirical Wasserstein discrepancy controls every particle path in a synchronous coupling, with a constant independent of the particle count.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsParticleSystem.ae_coupled_vector_integral_eq_on_Icc
declarations.doc: Same-input particle systems and identically distributed nonlinear paths satisfy the finite vector integral equations used by the synchronous propagation-of-chaos estimate.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_le_exp_mul_integral_of_forced_eq_on_path
declarations.doc: Common forcing stability needs the drift perturbation only along the reference solution.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_norm_empiricalMeasure
declarations.doc: Empirical laws have integrable norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_le_of_particle_integral_eq
declarations.doc: Common-forcing particle paths are controlled by the discrepancy of the reference empirical marginals from their prescribed law. The norm of a configuration is its maximum particle norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_empiricalMeasure
declarations.doc: Pushforward of an empirical law is the empirical law of the mapped atoms.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinEDist_one_IccExtend_map_le
declarations.doc: Evaluation at any projected time cannot increase first-Wasserstein distance of path laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinEDist_one_empirical_IccExtend_toReal_le
declarations.doc: Empirical marginal Wasserstein discrepancy is uniformly bounded by the discrepancy of path laws, whenever the latter is finite.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinEDist_one_nonneg_le_of_isContinuityEquation_of_bound
declarations.doc: Bounded velocity makes a narrowly continuous probability solution Lipschitz in first Wasserstein distance on nonnegative time, even before any moment condition is known.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsWassersteinLipschitzDrift.lipschitzWith_nonneg_marginalDrift_of_wasserstein_bound
declarations.doc: Wasserstein-Lipschitz marginal curves give globally Lipschitz nonlinear drifts after projecting time to the nonnegative half-line.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsWassersteinLipschitzDrift.lipschitzWith_nonneg_marginalDrift
declarations.doc: Along a bounded-velocity nonlinear continuity-equation solution, a Wasserstein-Lipschitz drift is globally Lipschitz in space and projected nonnegative time.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinEDist_one_ne_top_of_isContinuityEquation
declarations.doc: A narrowly continuous finite-measure continuity-equation solution is at finite first Wasserstein distance between its endpoint laws. No moment of the second endpoint is assumed.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_norm_end_of_isContinuityEquation
declarations.doc: Finite first moments propagate along narrowly continuous solutions of the continuity equation solely from the action integrability built into its definition.

declarations.name: CKSD.isContinuityEquation_congr_measure_on_Ioo
declarations.doc: Replacing time marginals only outside the equation interval preserves its weak identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteMeasureNonnegExtension
declarations.doc: Continue a nonnegative-time probability marginal family constantly to negative times.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteMeasureNonnegExtension_toMeasure
declarations.doc: The extended finite measure has the prescribed nonnegative-time marginal.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_finiteMeasure_nonneg_extension
declarations.doc: The nonnegative-time marginal family, continued constantly to negative times, is narrowly continuous whenever its bounded continuous tests are continuous on the nonnegative half-line.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_norm_of_isContinuityEquation_on_nonneg
declarations.doc: A narrowly continuous probability solution on nonnegative time has integrable norm at every time, provided the initial law has integrable norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinEDist_one_le_of_isContinuityEquation_of_bound
declarations.doc: Bounded velocity controls first-Wasserstein displacement without any endpoint moment hypotheses.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_eq_of_isContinuityEquation_of_bounded_lipschitz
declarations.doc: Two narrowly continuous probability solutions for a bounded globally Lipschitz velocity have the same terminal integrals against every smooth bounded Lipschitz scalar test.

declarations.name: CKSD.eq_of_isContinuityEquation_of_bounded_lipschitz
declarations.doc: Narrowly continuous probability solutions of a continuity equation with bounded globally Lipschitz space-time velocity are unique without moment hypotheses.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_iid_mcKeanVlasov_paths_on_Icc
declarations.doc: One nonlinear solution supplies iid nonlinear path copies driven by the original iid initial states and Brownian motions, for a general Wasserstein-Lipschitz drift.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBrownianEuclidean
declarations.doc: A standard Brownian motion in `ℝᵈ`: independent coordinates, each a real Brownian motion.

declarations.name: CKSD.pathOn
declarations.doc: The path of `x` on `[0, T]`, as a continuous map, or `0` if `x` is not continuous there.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsWassersteinLipschitzDrift
declarations.doc: Lipschitz continuity of a drift in position and in `W₁` of the measure, on probability measures with a finite first moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDInitialAndDrivers
declarations.doc: Independent identically distributed initial states and Brownian drivers, the initial states independent of the drivers.

declarations.name: CKSD.identDistrib_countable_evals_of_isPreBrownianReal
declarations.doc: Countable collections of evaluations of two real Brownian motions have the same law.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBrownianEuclidean.identDistrib_countable_evals
declarations.doc: Countable evaluations of Euclidean Brownian drivers have a law independent of the chosen Brownian realization.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDInitialAndDrivers.identDistrib_forcing_evals
declarations.doc: Countably many evaluations of the initial state plus its Brownian driver are identically distributed across the independent input particles.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDInitialAndDrivers.iIndepFun_forcing_evals
declarations.doc: Countably sampled additive forcings are independent across the input particles.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsParticleSystem
declarations.doc: The `N`-particle system: particles `i < N` solve `Xⁱₜ = X₀ⁱ + ∫₀ᵗ b(Xⁱₛ, μᴺₛ) ds + Wⁱₜ` with continuous paths, `μᴺₛ` the empirical measure of the first `N` particles.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution
declarations.doc: A solution of the McKean–Vlasov equation `Yₜ = ξ + ∫₀ᵗ b(Yₛ, Law(Yₛ)) ds + Bₜ` with continuous paths.

declarations.name: CKSD.interactionDrift
declarations.doc: Drift `b₀(x) + ∫ K(x, y) μ(dy)` of an interaction model.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBrownianEuclidean.ae_continuous_toNNReal
declarations.doc: Euclidean Brownian paths remain almost surely continuous after the nonnegative-time projection.

declarations.name: CKSD.pathOn_apply_of_continuousOn
declarations.doc: On a continuous path, the continuous-map path constructor agrees with evaluation.

declarations.name: CKSD.pathOn_IccExtend_of_continuousOn
declarations.doc: Extending a constructed continuous path agrees with the original path on its interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_integral_interaction
declarations.doc: Averaging a bounded continuous interaction against a continuous process gives a continuous time-position drift, with no moment condition on the process.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_integral_interaction_le
declarations.doc: The norm of the mean of a bounded interaction is bounded by the same constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_le_of_bounded_interactions_on_Icc
declarations.doc: Two integral equations with the same additive forcing and bounded interaction terms differ by a deterministic bound, independent of their initial data and the forcing.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_le_of_bounded_interactions
declarations.doc: Two integral equations with the same additive forcing and bounded interaction terms differ by a deterministic bound, independent of their initial data and the forcing.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_integral_interaction_sub_le
declarations.doc: Coupling the variables inside the interaction bounds the difference of their averaged interactions by their mean distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.aestronglyMeasurable_uncurry_of_ae_continuous
declarations.doc: A process with measurable time sections and almost surely continuous paths is jointly almost everywhere strongly measurable on every product with a time measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_zero_of_le_integral_add_integral_mean_of_integrable_bound
declarations.doc: An integrable random envelope suffices for the stochastic integral Grönwall zero criterion.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_zero_of_le_integral_add_integral_mean
declarations.doc: A nonnegative continuous process bounded on a time interval vanishes if its pathwise bound is an integral of itself plus an integral of its mean, both starting from zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_of_interaction_integral_eq_on_Icc
declarations.doc: Nonlinear same-forcing uniqueness for a bounded Lipschitz interaction. Neither independence nor any assumption on the law of the common forcing is needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_on_Icc_of_interaction_integral_eq
declarations.doc: Nonlinear same-forcing uniqueness for a bounded Lipschitz interaction. Neither independence nor any assumption on the law of the common forcing is needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalMeasure_succ_eq_tauCeti
declarations.doc: The finite-index empirical law agrees with TauCeti's offset sequence convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_probabilityMeasure_map_of_eventually_aemeasurable_of_ae_tendsto
declarations.doc: Eventual measurability suffices for weak convergence of image laws under almost sure pointwise convergence.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_empirical_wasserstein_one
declarations.doc: Iid integrable random paths have almost surely consistent empirical first-Wasserstein laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasFiniteMoment_one_empiricalMeasure
declarations.doc: Finite empirical laws have finite first moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinEDist_one_empirical_map_ne_top
declarations.doc: A finite empirical law and an integrable image law are at finite first-Wasserstein distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.aemeasurable_pathOn_of_ae_continuous

declarations.name: CKSD.IsWassersteinLipschitzDrift.lipschitzWith_position

declarations.name: CKSD.IsWassersteinLipschitzDrift.aestronglyMeasurable_drift_of_ae_continuous

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_integrable_uniform_bound_of_spatially_lipschitz_integral_eq

declarations.name: CKSD.IsWassersteinLipschitzDrift.lipschitzWith_particleDrift

declarations.name: CKSD.IsParticleSystem.ae_eq_of_wassersteinLipschitz

declarations.name: CKSD.meanPathDistance

declarations.name: CKSD.meanPathDistance_le_of_ae_bound

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_L1_le_of_ae_bound

declarations.name: CKSD.meanPathDistance_le_integral_of_ae_bound

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_L1_le_integral_of_ae_bound

declarations.name: CKSD.dist_L1_le_integral_of_ae_bound

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_IccExtend_eval

declarations.name: CKSD.injective_pathForcingMap

declarations.name: CKSD.pathOfRationalCoordinates_apply

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_pathOfRationalCoordinates

declarations.name: CKSD.forcedPicardMap

declarations.name: CKSD.forcedPicardMap_apply

declarations.name: CKSD.dist_iterate_forcedPicardMap_apply_le

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_contractingWith_iterate_forcedPicardMap

declarations.name: CKSD.surjective_pathForcingMap

declarations.name: CKSD.dist_le_exp_mul_dist_pathForcingMap

declarations.name: CKSD.pathForcingEquiv

declarations.name: CKSD.lipschitzWith_pathForcingEquiv_symm

declarations.name: CKSD.pathForcingEquiv_symm_apply_eq

declarations.name: CKSD.dist_pathMarginalLaw_le_meanPathDistance
declarations.doc: A common-source coupling bounds the distance between random-path marginal laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_nonlinearFrozenDrift_le

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_frozenPathSolutionMap_le

declarations.name: CKSD.nonlinearPathPicard_ae_norm_sub_le

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_nonlinear_path_solution

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_nonlinear_brownian_path_solution

declarations.name: CKSD.nonlinearFrozenDrift

declarations.name: CKSD.lipschitzWith_nonlinearFrozenDrift

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_frozenPathSolutionMap_comp

declarations.name: CKSD.finite_coupling_gronwall

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_intervalIntegral_le_length_mul_integral_sq

declarations.name: CKSD.finite_coupling_gronwall_sq

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_mean_interaction_sub_le
declarations.doc: The empirical interaction difference is bounded by a particle's error plus the mean error.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_sq_le_residual_energy
declarations.doc: Deterministic squared-error estimate for synchronously coupled interacting particles.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_le_of_individual_add_average_bound
declarations.doc: An individual plus an averaged residual bound integrates to twice the common mean bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_iSup_enorm_sq_le_of_individual_add_average_bound

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_le_exp_mul_integral_of_forced_eq

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_integral_sub_integral_le_mul_wassersteinEDist_one

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_meanFieldInteraction

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_unique_nonlinear_continuity_solution_of_bound

declarations.name: CKSD.particle_vector_integral_eq_of_hasDerivAt

declarations.name: CKSD.reference_vector_integral_eq_on_Icc

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution.exists_integrable_uniform_bound
declarations.doc: A solution with integrable initial state and Brownian forcing admits an integrable random bound uniform on each compact time interval, under exactly the pointwise moment solution predicate.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_intervalIntegrable_wasserstein_drift_of_bound
declarations.doc: A time-measurable Wasserstein-Lipschitz drift along an integrably bounded process is interval-integrable on compact time intervals, by comparison with the drift at the origin.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution.ae_intervalIntegrable_drift_of_bound
declarations.doc: A local integrable envelope makes a nonlinear solution drift interval-integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_of_wasserstein_integral_eq_on_Icc
declarations.doc: Two locally integrably bounded nonlinear integral equations with the same additive forcing and a Wasserstein-Lipschitz drift agree almost surely on their common compact time interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution.ae_eq_on_Icc
declarations.doc: Nonlinear solutions with the same integrable initial state and Brownian forcing agree almost surely on every compact nonnegative time interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution.ae_eq
declarations.doc: Nonlinear solutions with the same integrable initial state and Brownian forcing are indistinguishable on nonnegative times.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_norm_sum_centeredInteraction_sq_le
declarations.doc: For a frozen location and independent samples, the expected squared centered interaction sum is at most `4κ²` times the number of samples.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_norm_empiricalInteraction_sub_sq_le
declarations.doc: In an iid sample, the interaction average seen by one sampled particle differs from its population counterpart in mean square by at most `16κ²/N`, including the self-interaction term.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinEDist_one_map_toReal_le_integral_norm_sub
declarations.doc: The common-source coupling bounds first Wasserstein distance by mean pointwise distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinEDist_one_empirical_toReal_le_norm_sub
declarations.doc: Pairing equal-index atoms controls empirical first Wasserstein distance in the uniform configuration norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution.wassersteinEDist_toReal_le_of_zero_forcing_of_bound

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution.ae_norm_le_of_zero_forcing_of_bound

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution.ae_eq_on_Icc_of_zero_forcing_of_bound

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMcKeanVlasovSolution.ae_eq_of_zero_forcing_of_bound

declarations.name: CKSD.metropolisAcceptance_le_one
declarations.doc: The Metropolis–Hastings acceptance probability is at most one.

declarations.name: CKSD.metropolisAcceptance_nonneg
declarations.doc: The Metropolis–Hastings acceptance probability is nonnegative for nonnegative weights and proposals.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_metropolisTransition
declarations.doc: Each row of the Metropolis–Hastings matrix sums to one, for arbitrary `π` and `q`, because the diagonal carries the rejected mass.

declarations.name: CKSD.metropolisTransition_mem_rowStochastic
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.22: for nonnegative target weights and a row-stochastic proposal, the Metropolis–Hastings matrix is row stochastic.

declarations.name: CKSD.metropolisTransition_detailedBalance
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.22: detailed balance `π(x) P(x,y) = π(y) P(y,x)` of the Metropolis–Hastings matrix `P`, for nonnegative target weights (not necessarily normalized) and nonnegative proposals.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_metropolisTransition
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.22: the target weights are invariant for the Metropolis–Hastings matrix, `∑ₓ π(x) P(x,y) = π(y)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_pow_eq_of_stationary
declarations.doc: An invariant law of a square matrix is invariant for all of its powers.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sum_pow_sub_le_of_minorization
declarations.doc: Doeblin's bound: a minorization `K x y ≥ ε π y` by an invariant probability vector `π` of a matrix with unit row sums gives geometric convergence of every row of `K ^ n` to `π`, uniformly over events.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sum_independenceSampler_pow_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.32: uniform convergence rate of the independence sampler. For a positive target `π` and a positive proposal density `g` with `π ≤ M g`, every row of the `n`-step Metropolis–Hastings matrix with proposal `q(x, y) = g(y)` is within `(1 - 1/M)ⁿ` of `π`, uniformly over events. The condition `π ≤ M g` forces `M ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurePreserving_leapfrogStep
declarations.doc: A single leapfrog step preserves Lebesgue measure on phase space: it is the composition of two momentum kicks and a position drift, each a shear.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurePreserving_leapfrogStep_iterate
declarations.doc: GAPS 104.35: repeated leapfrog steps preserve Lebesgue measure on phase space.

declarations.name: CKSD.leapfrogStep_momentumFlip_leapfrogStep
declarations.doc: A single leapfrog step is reversible: flipping the momentum after a step and stepping again returns the flipped initial point.

declarations.name: CKSD.leapfrogStep_iterate_reversible
