Then `√n (MMD_u² - ‖δ‖²)` converges in distribution to the centered normal law with variance `4 Var_P ⟨φ, δ⟩ + 4 Var_Q ⟨φ, δ⟩`.

declarations.name: CKSD.energy_distance_nonneg_eq_zero_iff_and_eq_squaredMMD
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.62: for laws `P, Q` on `ℝ^d` with finite first moments, the energy distance `D = 2 E‖X - Y‖ - E‖X - X'‖ - E‖Y - Y'‖` is nonnegative, vanishes exactly when `P = Q`, and equals twice the squared MMD of the distance kernel `CKSD.distanceKernel`.

declarations.name: CKSD.distance_covariance_nonneg_eq_zero_iff_and_eq_squaredMMD
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.62: for a law `P` on `ℝ^d × ℝ^e` with finite second moments and marginals `μ, ν`, the squared distance covariance `V = E[A(X, X') B(Y, Y')]` of the doubly centered distances is nonnegative, vanishes exactly when `P = μ ⊗ ν`, and equals four times the squared MMD (the HSIC) of the product of the two distance kernels between `P` and `μ ⊗ ν`.

declarations.name: CKSD.squaredMMD_joint_prod_eq_zero_iff_indepFun
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.63, independence criterion for a characteristic product-space kernel: for a bounded measurable characteristic kernel `k` on `X × Y` and a law `P` of a pair, the HSIC `MMD²(P, P_X ⊗ P_Y)` vanishes exactly when the two coordinates are independent under `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isCharacteristicKernel_iff_spectral_measure_full_support
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.68(c), characteristicness iff the symmetric spectral measure has full support: for a symmetric finite measure `L` on `ℝ^d`, `d ≥ 1`, the translation-invariant kernel `k(x, y) = ∫ cos ⟨w, x - y⟩ dL(w)` is characteristic exactly when every open ball has positive `L`-measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_coord_mul_coord
declarations.doc: Products of two coordinates are integrable under a law with finite second moments.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_coord
declarations.doc: Coordinates are integrable under a law with integrable identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_coord
declarations.doc: The coordinates of the mean are the means of the coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_quadratic_kernel_prod
declarations.doc: The product-measure integral of the quadratic polynomial kernel `(1 + ⟨x, y⟩)²` in terms of first and second moments.

declarations.name: CKSD.squaredMMD_quadratic_polynomial_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.68(d), quadratic-polynomial MMD depends only on the first two moments: for laws with finite second moments, the squared MMD of the kernel `(1 + ⟨x, y⟩)²` is `2 ‖m_P - m_Q‖² + ∑_{i,j} (E_P[x_i x_j] - E_Q[x_i x_j])²`. In particular this kernel is not characteristic.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_squaredMMD_probabilityMeasure
declarations.doc: For a bounded continuous kernel, squared MMD is continuous in its first probability law.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_probabilityMeasure_iff_tendsto_squaredMMD_of_tight
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.70, MMD metrizes weak convergence along uniformly tight sequences: for a bounded continuous characteristic kernel on a separable metric space and a uniformly tight sequence of probability laws `P n`, `P n → Q` weakly (in Mathlib's `ProbabilityMeasure` topology) exactly when `MMD²(P n, Q) → 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_langevin_stein_operator_eq_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.71, scalar Langevin Stein identity for bounded continuously differentiable tests: if `P` has a positive `C¹` density `p` with integrable score `p'/p`, then `E_P[g (p'/p) + g'] = 0` for every bounded `C¹` function `g` with integrable derivative.

declarations.name: CKSD.landscapeMeasure
declarations.doc: Measure used for the `Lp` persistence landscape representation.

declarations.name: CKSD.LandscapeLp
declarations.doc: The Banach-space representation of persistence landscapes at exponent `p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.LandscapeLp.ae_tendsto_sampleAverage
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.23: strong law for integrable independent identically distributed landscapes: the sample averages of pairwise independent, identically distributed, integrable random elements of `LandscapeLp p` converge almost surely to the mean. Pairwise independence is sufficient, as in Mathlib's Etemadi strong law.

declarations.name: CKSD.intrinsicEDist
declarations.doc: The intrinsic (path-length) distance of a set: the infimum of the lengths of paths from `x` to `y` that stay in `M`, `∞` when there is none.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSampleWalk
declarations.doc: A walk from `x` through the sample `S` with steps of length at most `ε`, ending at `y`; the list records the vertices after `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.walkLength
declarations.doc: Euclidean length of the walk from `x` along `l`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleGraphEDist
declarations.doc: Shortest-path distance in the `ε`-neighbourhood graph on `S` with Euclidean edge lengths, `∞` between different components. Its graph interpretation applies to endpoints in `S`; the definition also permits an ambient starting point outside `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eventually_sampleGraphEDist_intrinsicEDist_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.4, convergence of graph geodesics. Let `M = j(N) ⊂ ℝ^D` be a compact connected smooth submanifold of positive reach, and let the samples `S n ⊆ M` be `δ n`-nets of `M` in its intrinsic distance. If `ε n → 0` and `δ n / ε n → 0`, then the shortest-path distances of the `ε n`-neighbourhood graphs converge to the intrinsic distances uniformly over pairs of sample points: for every `η > 0`, eventually `|d_{G_n}(x, y) - d_M(x, y)| ≤ η` for all `x, y ∈ S n` (stated as two one-sided bounds in `ℝ≥0∞`).

declarations.name: CKSD.intrinsicEDist_eq_edist_of_lengthPreserving
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.4, flat case. Let `φ` map `M` into a real normed space with convex image `Ω`, have a left inverse `ψ` on `M` that is continuous on `Ω`, and preserve the lengths of paths in `M` (an isometry for the intrinsic length structure). Then `d_M(x, y) = ‖φ x - φ y‖` on `M`. Remark, not part of the statement: for `Ω ⊆ ℝ^d`, classical multidimensional scaling of the squared intrinsic distances of a finite sample then returns the points `φ(x_i)` up to a Euclidean isometry, by the Schoenberg criterion of Section 108.8.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_finset_net_of_le_measure_ball
declarations.doc: A packing bound for nets: if every open ball of radius `s > 0` centered in `K` has `P`-mass at least `a > 0` under a probability measure `P`, then a finite subset `F ⊆ K` with `|F| a ≤ 1` is a `2s`-net of `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_sub_le_measureReal_pi_hausdorffDist_le
declarations.doc: Hausdorff sampling bound from a small-ball lower bound: let `μ` be a probability measure carried by a measurable set `K` such that every ball `B(x, s)` with `x ∈ K` and `0 < s ≤ ε/2` has mass at least `β s^d`. Then an independent sample of size `n` from `μ` is `ε`-close to `K` in Hausdorff distance with probability at least `1 - (β (ε/4)^d)⁻¹ exp(-β (ε/2)^d n)`. The proof is a union bound over the balls of radius `ε/2` around a maximal `ε/2`-packing of `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_hausdorffMeasure_ball_inter_range_ge_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc: Uniform small-ball bound on a compact immersed manifold: if `N` is a compact smooth manifold modeled on `ℝ^d` and `j : N → ℝ^D` a smooth immersion, there are `a, r₀ > 0` such that `μH[d] (B(j x, r) ∩ j(N)) ≥ a r^d` for every `x ∈ N` and every `r ∈ (0, r₀)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsColumnLow
declarations.doc: Row `i` carries the lowest nonzero entry of column `j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsReducedMatrix
declarations.doc: A matrix is reduced when distinct nonzero columns have distinct lows.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMatrixReduction
declarations.doc: `R = D V` is a column reduction of `D`: `V` is upper triangular with nonzero diagonal (hence invertible) and `R` is reduced.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftPart
declarations.doc: The lower-left part of `D`: rows with index at least `a`, columns with index below `b`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank
declarations.doc: Rank of the lower-left submatrix of rows `a, a+1, …` and columns `0, …, b-1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsColumnLow.unique
declarations.doc: A column has at most one low.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isColumnLow_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc: A nonzero column has a low.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftPart_eq_mul
declarations.doc: Masking is multiplication by diagonal projections on both sides.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank_mul_le
declarations.doc: Right multiplication by an upper triangular matrix does not raise lower-left ranks.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank_eq_of_isMatrixReduction
declarations.doc: Lower-left ranks are invariant under a column reduction.

declarations.name: CKSD.rank_eq_card_of_isReducedMatrix
declarations.doc: The rank of a reduced matrix is the number of its nonzero columns.

declarations.name: CKSD.isColumnLow_lowerLeftPart_iff
declarations.doc: Lows of the masked matrix are the lows of the original in the masked region.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsReducedMatrix.lowerLeftPart
declarations.doc: A masked reduced matrix is reduced.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank_eq_card_of_isReducedMatrix
declarations.doc: Lower-left ranks of a reduced matrix count the columns with low in the region.

declarations.name: CKSD.pairingRankCombination
declarations.doc: The alternating rank combination of the pairing lemma, in the `0`-based indexing of `Fin m`: with `D^i_j` the submatrix of rows `i, …, m-1` and columns `0, …, j`, it is `rank D^i_j - rank D^{i+1}_j + rank D^{i+1}_{j-1} - rank D^i_{j-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.pairingRankCombination_eq_ite
declarations.doc: The pairing combination of ranks is the indicator of the lows of any column reduction.

declarations.name: CKSD.isColumnLow_iff_pairingRankCombination_eq_one
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.32, the pairing lemma: for every column reduction `R = D V` of a square matrix over a field, row `i` is the low of column `j` of `R` exactly when the alternating combination of ranks of lower-left submatrices of `D` equals `1`. In particular the pairing does not depend on the reduction (`isColumnLow_iff_of_isMatrixReduction`). The statement holds for every square matrix, so it covers boundary matrices over `ℤ/2` and signed boundary matrices over any field. Indices start at `0`; the homological reading of the pairs is `CKSD.IsColumnLow.dim_eq_and_persistentBettiOfMatrix_eq` and `CKSD.persistentBettiOfMatrix_eq_card`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isColumnLow_iff_of_isMatrixReduction
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.32: the pairing is independent of the chosen reduction: for two column reductions `R = D V` and `R' = D V'` of the same matrix, `R` and `R'` have the same column lows.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsFilteredBoundaryMatrix
declarations.doc: A graded filtered chain-complex boundary matrix whose `k`th basis vector has degree `dim k`: nonzero entries lower degree by one and precede the column in filtration order, and `D * D = 0`. Signed simplicial incidence matrices are examples; the axioms do not require incidence entries.

declarations.name: CKSD.filteredChains
declarations.doc: Chains of dimension `p` of the subcomplex formed by the first `a` simplices.

declarations.name: CKSD.filteredCycles
declarations.doc: Cycles of dimension `p` of the subcomplex formed by the first `a` simplices.

declarations.name: CKSD.filteredBoundaries
declarations.doc: Boundaries of dimension `p` of the subcomplex formed by the first `b` simplices.

declarations.name: CKSD.persistentBettiOfMatrix
declarations.doc: Persistent Betti number of the simplexwise filtration: the rank of the map in degree-`p` homology induced by the inclusion of the first `a` simplices into the first `b`, computed as `dim Z_p(K_a) - dim (Z_p(K_a) ∩ B_p(K_b))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Matrix.rank_add_of_disjoint_supports
declarations.doc: Matrices with disjoint row supports and disjoint column supports have additive rank.

declarations.name: CKSD.dimColumnPart
declarations.doc: The part of `D` in the columns of dimension `q`.

declarations.name: CKSD.dimColumnPartCompl
declarations.doc: The part of `D` in the columns of dimension other than `q`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank_eq_add_dimColumnPart
declarations.doc: Lower-left ranks split along column dimensions for a matrix whose nonzero entries raise the dimension by one.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank_succ_of_col_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Adding a zero column does not change lower-left ranks.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank_of_row_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Adding a zero row does not change lower-left ranks.

declarations.name: CKSD.pairingRankCombination_eq_zero_of_col
declarations.doc: The pairing combination vanishes at a zero column.

declarations.name: CKSD.pairingRankCombination_eq_zero_of_row
declarations.doc: The pairing combination vanishes at a zero row.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsColumnLow.dim_eq
declarations.doc: In a column reduction of a matrix whose nonzero entries raise the dimension by one, the low of column `j` has dimension one less than `j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsColumnLow.lt
declarations.doc: In a column reduction of a strictly upper triangular matrix, the low of a column lies strictly above the diagonal.

declarations.name: CKSD.dimReducedPart
declarations.doc: The matrix obtained from a column reduction `R` by keeping the columns of dimension `q` and, in them, the rows of dimension `q - 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.dimTransformPart
declarations.doc: The transformation matrix of `dimReducedPart`: the columns of `V` of dimension `q`, and standard basis vectors in the other columns.

declarations.name: CKSD.isColumnLow_dimReducedPart_iff
declarations.doc: Lows of the restricted reduction are the lows of `R` in columns of dimension `q`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMatrixReduction_dimColumnPart
declarations.doc: Keeping the columns of dimension `q` of a column reduction gives a column reduction of the part of `D` in the columns of dimension `q`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerLeftRank_dimColumnPart_eq_card
declarations.doc: Lower-left ranks of the part of `D` in the columns of dimension `q` count the columns of dimension `q` whose low lies in the region.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsColumnLow.col_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A row that is the low of some column of a column reduction of `D`, with `D * D = 0`, indexes a zero column: positive simplices have zero reduced columns.

declarations.name: CKSD.Submodule.finrank_map_add_finrank_inf_ker
declarations.doc: Rank–nullity for the restriction of a linear map to a subspace.

declarations.name: CKSD.filteredChains_eq_range
declarations.doc: Chains of the subcomplex are the range of a diagonal projection.

declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_filteredChains
declarations.doc: The dimension of the chains of the subcomplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_filteredChains_eq_range
declarations.doc: The boundary of the chains of the subcomplex is the range of a masked part of `D`.

declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_filteredCycles_add
declarations.doc: Dimension of the cycles of the subcomplex formed by the first `a` simplices.

declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_filteredCycles_inf_filteredBoundaries_add
declarations.doc: Dimension of the cycles of `K_a` that bound in `K_b`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsColumnLow.exists_and_iff
declarations.doc: A statement about the low of a column can be read off at any low of that column.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isColumnLow_iff
declarations.doc: A column has a low exactly when it is nonzero.

declarations.name: CKSD.persistentBettiOfMatrix_eq_card
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.32, the persistent Betti numbers of a reduced filtered boundary matrix count the bars `[i, j)` with `low_R(j) = i`, `i < a ≤ b ≤ j`, and the essential bars born before `a`. The inequality `a ≤ b` is not needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsColumnLow.dim_eq_and_persistentBettiOfMatrix_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.32, homological meaning of the pairing (indices from `0`; the subcomplex `K_a` consists of the first `a` simplices). If `low_R(j) = i`, then `σ_j` has dimension one more than `σ_i`, adding `σ_i` raises the Betti number in its dimension (`σ_i` is positive) and adding `σ_j` lowers the Betti number one dimension below its own (`σ_j` is negative). The bars are the pairs `[i, j)` with `low_R(j) = i` and the essential intervals `[j, ∞)` for zero columns `j` that are the low of no column; the count of bars by persistent Betti numbers is `CKSD.persistentBettiOfMatrix_eq_card`. The restatement for monotone functions on simplices, with bars `[f(σ_i), f(σ_j))`, is a relabelling and is not stated separately.

declarations.name: CKSD.unifIntegrable_of_eventually_small_tails
declarations.doc: Eventually uniformly small quadratic tails, together with finite individual moments, give uniform integrability; the finite initial segment causes no obstruction.

declarations.name: CKSD.unifIntegrable_of_tendsto_wasserstein_law
declarations.doc: Maps whose laws converge in quadratic Wasserstein distance are uniformly integrable in quadratic mean. The maps may be defined on any probability space.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_norm_sq_sub_of_tendstoInMeasure_of_tendsto_wasserstein_law
declarations.doc: Convergence in measure and quadratic Wasserstein convergence of the laws imply convergence in mean square.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_graphPlan_of_isOptimalCoupling
declarations.doc: Optimal graph plans from a fixed absolutely continuous Euclidean source converge weakly when their target laws converge in quadratic Wasserstein distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.isOptimalCoupling_graphPlan_of_integral_norm_sq_eq
declarations.doc: The real squared-displacement identity identifies an optimal quadratic graph coupling between finite-second-moment probability laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_sq_optimal_map_sub
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.42: L2 stability of optimal maps with a fixed absolutely continuous source. Let `μ` be an absolutely continuous law with finite second moment, `T` and `Tₙ` measurable optimal maps from `μ` to laws `ν` and `νₙ` with finite second moments. If `W₂(νₙ, ν) → 0`, then `∫ ‖Tₙ - T‖² dμ → 0`. The laws `νₙ = (Tₙ)_# μ` are probability measures automatically.

declarations.name: CKSD.PersistenceModule
declarations.doc: A real-indexed persistence module over a field is a functor to vector spaces.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPointwiseFiniteDimensional
declarations.doc: A persistence module is pointwise finite-dimensional when every vector space is finite- dimensional.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsQTame
declarations.doc: A persistence module is q-tame when its structure maps across strict intervals have finite rank.

declarations.name: CKSD.PersistenceInterleaving
declarations.doc: An interleaving, including naturality and both composition identities.

declarations.name: CKSD.interleavingEDist
declarations.doc: Extended interleaving distance, with value infinity when no interleaving exists.

declarations.name: CKSD.FiniteDeathDiagram
declarations.doc: A persistence diagram's finite-death component, with multiplicity recorded by its index set.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching
declarations.doc: A partial matching: every point is matched to at most one point on the other side.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.cost
declarations.doc: Cost of a partial matching, including the distance of unmatched points to the diagonal.

declarations.name: CKSD.bottleneckEDist
declarations.doc: Bottleneck distance on finite-death diagrams, allowing unmatched points on the diagonal.

declarations.name: CKSD.persistenceTent
declarations.doc: Tent function associated to one finite persistence interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.persistenceLandscape
declarations.doc: Persistence landscape: level `k` is the `(k+1)`st largest tent height. The supremum over finite subsets avoids choosing an ordering of diagram points.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCechSimplex
declarations.doc: A Čech simplex in an ambient metric space, with closed balls of radius `r`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsRipsSimplex
declarations.doc: A Rips simplex in the diameter-`2r` parameter convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCechSimplex.isRipsSimplex
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.21, the first Čech/Rips inclusion in every pseudometric space: a Čech simplex of radius `r` is a Rips simplex of parameter `r`, since points within `r` of a common center are within `2r` of each other.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCechSimplex.mono
declarations.doc: Čech simplices are closed under taking faces.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsRipsSimplex.mono
declarations.doc: Rips simplices are closed under taking faces.

declarations.name: CKSD.persistenceTent_nonneg
declarations.doc: Persistence tents are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis
declarations.doc: An interval basis of a persistence module over a preorder: a decomposition of `V` as a direct sum of interval modules, with supports `support j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_intervalBasis_of_isPointwiseFiniteDimensional
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.18, existence (Crawley-Boevey's theorem): every pointwise finite-dimensional persistence module over `ℝ` with coefficients in a field is a direct sum of interval modules. The finite totally ordered case is Gabriel's theorem in type `A_n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.repr_map_apply
declarations.doc: Coordinates of the image of a vector under a structure map, in an interval basis: the coordinate of a bar alive at `u` is its coordinate at `t` if it is alive at `t`, and zero otherwise.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.range_map
declarations.doc: In an interval basis, the image of a structure map `V_s → V_t` is spanned by the bars alive at `s` and at `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.ker_map
declarations.doc: In an interval basis, the kernel of a structure map `V_t → V_u` is spanned by the bars alive at `t` and dead at `u`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.exists_equiv_support_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.18, uniqueness: the multiset of intervals of an interval decomposition of a persistence module over `ℝ` is unique, that is, any two interval bases are related by a support-preserving bijection of their index sets. Pointwise finite dimensionality is not needed: interval modules have local endomorphism rings, so the Krull–Remak–Schmidt–Azumaya theorem applies to arbitrary direct sums of them.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap
declarations.doc: The comparison map `U_t → V_{t+ε}` attached to a partial matching `R` of the bars of two interval bases: a bar is sent to its partner when the partner is alive at `t + ε`, and to zero otherwise.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap_basis
declarations.doc: Value of the comparison map on a basis vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap_basis_of_rel
declarations.doc: The comparison map sends a matched bar to its partner, or to zero once the partner is dead.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap_basis_of_not
declarations.doc: The comparison map kills unmatched bars.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.map_basis_apply
declarations.doc: Structure maps on basis vectors of an interval basis.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap_natural
declarations.doc: Naturality of the comparison maps, under the compatibility condition `h1` on supports.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.barMap_comp_barMap
declarations.doc: Composite of the comparison maps for a matching and its transpose.

declarations.name: CKSD.IntervalBasis.nonempty_interleaving_of_matching
declarations.doc: An `ε`-interleaving from an `ε`-compatible partial matching of the bars of two interval bases.

declarations.name: CKSD.DiagramMatching.sumRel
declarations.doc: The partial matching of the bars of two full diagrams that combines a matching of finite parts with a bijection of essential parts.

declarations.name: CKSD.interleavingEDist_le_fullBottleneckEDist
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.20, the easy half of the isometry theorem: for persistence modules with finite closed-open interval bases, the interleaving distance is at most the bottleneck distance of the diagrams. A matching of cost `ε` gives an `ε`-interleaving bar by bar.

declarations.name: CKSD.interleavingEDist_eq_fullBottleneckEDist
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.20, the isometry theorem, for persistence modules of finite type with closed-open bars: if `U` and `V` decompose into finitely many interval modules over `[b, d)` and `[b, ∞)`, their interleaving distance equals the bottleneck distance of their diagrams (both are `∞` exactly when the numbers of essential bars differ). The general `q`-tame case, with diagrams defined from rank functions and intervals with arbitrary endpoint types, is not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_cos_add_two_mul_uniformPhase
declarations.doc: Over a uniformly distributed phase on `[0, 2π]`, `cos (c + 2b)` has mean zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_randomFourierFeatureTerm
declarations.doc: The random-feature summand is continuous in the frequency and phase.

declarations.name: CKSD.randomFourierFeatureTerm_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: The random-feature summand takes values in `[-2, 2]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_randomFourierFeatureTerm
declarations.doc: The random-feature summand is unbiased for the translation-invariant kernel.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_pi_sum_sub_integral_ge_le
declarations.doc: Hoeffding's inequality for a sample of `D` independent copies of a variable with values in `[a, b]`: the sum of the centered copies exceeds `D ε` with probability at most `exp (-2 D ε² / (b - a)²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_randomFourierFeatureKernel
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.74: random Fourier features are unbiased. The random Fourier feature kernel of an independent sample of frequencies `w_j ∼ L` and uniform phases `b_j ∈ [0, 2π]` has mean `k(x, y) = ∫ cos ⟨w, x - y⟩ dL(w)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_abs_randomFourierFeatureKernel_sub_ge_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.74: the pointwise Hoeffding bound for random Fourier features. For an independent sample of `D ≥ 1` frequencies `w_j ∼ L` and uniform phases, the random-feature kernel deviates from `k(x, y) = ∫ cos ⟨w, x - y⟩ dL(w)` by at least `ε > 0` with probability at most `2 exp(-D ε² / 8)`. Its unbiasedness is `CKSD.integral_randomFourierFeatureKernel`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_randomFourierFeatureTerm_sub_le
declarations.doc: The random-feature summand is Lipschitz in the pair of points: at the frequency-phase pair `(w, b)` it moves by at most `2 ‖w‖ (‖x - x'‖ + ‖y - y'‖)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_cos_inner_sub_le
declarations.doc: The shift-invariant kernel `k(x, y) = ∫ cos ⟨w, x - y⟩ dL(w)` is Lipschitz in the pair of points, with constant `σ = √(E ‖w‖²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_randomFourierFeatureError_sub_le
declarations.doc: The random-feature error `D⁻¹ ∑ⱼ 2 cos(⟨wⱼ, x⟩ + bⱼ) cos(⟨wⱼ, y⟩ + bⱼ) - k(x, y)` is Lipschitz in the pair of points with the random constant `2 D⁻¹ ∑ⱼ ‖wⱼ‖ + σ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_uniform_randomFourierFeatureKernel_error_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.74: the uniform compact-set random-feature bound. For a compact set `M ⊆ ℝ^d`, a frequency law `L` with finite second moment `σ² = E ‖w‖²`, and `ε ≤ σ diam M`, the probability that the random-feature kernel of `D` features deviates from `k` by at least `ε` somewhere on `M × M` is at most `98 (σ diam M / ε)² exp(-D ε² / (32 (d + 1)))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_of_continuousOn_compact_prod
declarations.doc: A function continuous on `M × M`, for a compact `M`, is integrable for every finite measure concentrated on `M × M`. No second countability of the ambient space is needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_squaredMMD_sub_le_of_uniform_kernel_error
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.74, deterministic transfer of a uniform kernel error to squared MMD: if two continuous kernels differ by at most `ε` on `M × M` for a compact `M` carrying both laws, their squared MMDs differ by at most `4 ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_of_subset
declarations.doc: Faces of simplices of a simplicial complex are simplices.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary_apply
declarations.doc: The simplicial boundary, evaluated at a simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary_mem_sublevelChains
declarations.doc: The boundary maps chains of the sublevel complex to chains of the sublevel complex.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence_insert_mul_self
declarations.doc: The incidence number of a codimension-one face is a sign.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence_insert_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The incidence number of a codimension-one face is nonzero.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialTwinHomotopy
declarations.doc: The chain homotopy of a twin pair `(v, w)`: it sends a simplex `σ` containing `w` but not `v` to `± (σ ∪ {v})`, with the sign of `σ` in the boundary of `σ ∪ {v}`, and the other simplices to zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialTwinHomotopy_mem_sublevelChains
declarations.doc: The twin homotopy raises the dimension by one and preserves sublevel complexes.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary_apply_of_twin
declarations.doc: The boundary of a chain vanishing on the simplices that contain `w` but not `v`, evaluated at such a simplex `σ`, only sees the simplex `σ ∪ {v}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary_simplicialTwinHomotopy_apply
declarations.doc: The boundary of the twin homotopy restores the coefficients on simplices containing `w` but not `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eq_zero_of_twin
declarations.doc: A chain vanishing on the simplices containing `w` but not `v`, whose boundary vanishes on those simplices as well, vanishes on all simplices containing `w`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti_eq_of_twin
declarations.doc: Removing a twin: let `v ≠ w` be vertices such that adding `v` to a simplex containing `w` gives a simplex with the same filtration value. Then deleting all simplices containing `w` does not change the persistent Betti numbers of the sublevel filtration.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence_map
declarations.doc: Incidence numbers are invariant under an order embedding of the vertices.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialChainMap
declarations.doc: Transport of chains along an order embedding of the vertices.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialChainMap_apply_map
declarations.doc: Transported chains take the original coefficient on the image of a simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialChainMap_apply_of_notMem
declarations.doc: Transported chains vanish off the image of the vertex embedding.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialChainMap_injective
declarations.doc: Transport of chains is injective.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_map_eq_of_subset_map
declarations.doc: A subset of the image of an order embedding is the image of a subset.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary_simplicialChainMap
declarations.doc: Transport of chains commutes with the boundary.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelChains_map
declarations.doc: Sublevel chains of the transported complex are the transported sublevel chains.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti_map
declarations.doc: Persistent Betti numbers are invariant under an order embedding of the vertices.

declarations.name: CKSD.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.simplexOn
declarations.doc: The full simplex on a finite set `T` of vertices: all nonempty subsets of `T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_simplexOn
declarations.doc: Membership in the full simplex on a finite set of vertices.

declarations.name: CKSD.PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_top
declarations.doc: Membership in the full simplex: all nonempty vertex sets.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti_pullback
declarations.doc: Pullback invariance: for a map `π` of vertices with an order-embedded section `s`, the sublevel filtration `σ ↦ Φ (π σ)` of the full simplex on `V` has the same persistent Betti numbers as the sublevel filtration of `Φ` on the full simplex on `X`. The vertices outside the image of `s` are twins of vertices in the image and are removed one at a time.

declarations.name: CKSD.diam_image_le_diam_image_add
declarations.doc: Diameters of the two projections of a set of pairs in a correspondence of distortion at most `2 d` differ by at most `2 d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMonotoneOnFaces_ripsFiltrationValue_image
declarations.doc: The Rips filtration value of the image of a simplex under a vertex map is monotone along faces.

declarations.name: CKSD.fullBottleneckEDist_rips_le_ghDist
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.36, for finite metric spaces: the degree-`p` persistence diagrams of the Rips filtrations of two nonempty finite metric spaces, in the diameter-`2r` parameter, are within bottleneck distance `d_GH(X, Y)`. In the maximum-edge parameter the filtration values double, and the bound becomes `2 d_GH(X, Y)`. The linear orders on the points only orient simplices. Totally bounded spaces (where `q`-tameness is needed) and the Čech variants are not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscretePotential
declarations.doc: The semidiscrete potential `φ_g(x) = min_j (‖x - y_j‖² - g_j)`, the integrand of `CKSD.semidiscreteTransportDual`.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscreteTransportDual_eq
declarations.doc: The dual functional is the integral of the potential plus the linear term.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscretePotential_le
declarations.doc: The potential is at most each of the shifted costs.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_semidiscretePotential_eq
declarations.doc: For at least one site the potential is attained.

declarations.name: CKSD.mem_laguerreCell_iff
declarations.doc: A point lies in the Laguerre cell of `y_j` exactly when the potential is attained at `j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_mem_laguerreCell
declarations.doc: Every point lies in some Laguerre cell.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_semidiscretePotential_sub_le
declarations.doc: The potential is `1`-Lipschitz in the weights for the sup norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_semidiscretePotential
declarations.doc: The potential is measurable in the point.

declarations.name: CKSD.neg_norm_le_semidiscretePotential
declarations.doc: The potential is bounded below by `-‖g‖`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_norm_sub_sq
declarations.doc: For a law with finite second moment, the squared distance to a site is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_semidiscretePotential
declarations.doc: For a law with finite second moment, the potential is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_sq_sub_norm_sub_sq
declarations.doc: The cost difference of two sites is affine: `‖x - a‖² - ‖x - c‖² = 2 ⟨x, c - a⟩ + ‖a‖² - ‖c‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_forall_ne_of_absolutelyContinuous
declarations.doc: For an absolutely continuous law and distinct sites, almost every point has no ties.

declarations.name: CKSD.isClosed_laguerreCell
declarations.doc: Laguerre cells are closed.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_laguerreCell
declarations.doc: Laguerre cells are measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.eventually_mem_laguerreCell
declarations.doc: A point of a Laguerre cell with no ties stays in the cell for all nearby weights.

declarations.name: CKSD.eventually_notMem_laguerreCell
declarations.doc: A point outside a Laguerre cell stays outside for all nearby weights.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasFDerivAt_semidiscretePotential
declarations.doc: Off the ties, the potential is differentiable in the weights, with derivative `-e_j` on the cell of `y_j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indicator_laguerreCell_eq
declarations.doc: At a point without ties, the indicator of the Laguerre cell of `y_j` is the Kronecker delta of the unique minimizing site.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasFDerivAt_integral_semidiscretePotential
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56, differentiation under the integral: for an absolutely continuous law with finite second moment and distinct sites, `g ↦ ∫ φ_g dP` has derivative `-∑ P(L_j(g)) e_j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_measureReal_laguerreCell
declarations.doc: The mass of a Laguerre cell depends continuously on the weights, for an absolutely continuous law and distinct sites.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasFDerivAt_semidiscreteTransportDual
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56, the gradient formula: the dual functional has derivative `∑ (b_j - P(L_j(g))) e_j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.contDiff_semidiscreteTransportDual
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56: the dual functional is continuously differentiable.

declarations.name: CKSD.concaveOn_semidiscreteTransportDual
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56: the dual functional is concave.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscretePotential_add_const
declarations.doc: Adding a constant to all weights lowers the potential by that constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscreteTransportDual_add_const
declarations.doc: For target masses summing to one, the dual functional is invariant under adding a constant to the weights.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscreteTransportDual_le
declarations.doc: An upper bound for the dual functional: with `C = ∑ⱼ ∫ ‖x - y_j‖² dP`, `E(g) ≤ C - b_i (max g - g_i)` for every site `i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscreteTransportDual_isMax_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56: the maximizers of the dual functional are exactly the weights whose Laguerre cells have the target masses.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isMax_semidiscreteTransportDual
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56: the dual functional attains its maximum.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_indicator_laguerreCell_eq
declarations.doc: At a point without ties lying in the Laguerre cell of `y_j`, a sum of indicators of the cells picks out the `j`-th value.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_smul_dirac_singleton
declarations.doc: A discrete measure `∑ b_j δ_{y_j}` with distinct sites gives the site `y_j` the mass `b_j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_smul_dirac_compl_range
declarations.doc: A discrete measure `∑ b_j δ_{y_j}` is carried by the sites.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscreteTransportMap
declarations.doc: The semidiscrete transport map sends each Laguerre cell `L_j(g)` to its site `y_j` (on the null set of ties the value is a sum of sites).

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_semidiscreteTransportMap
declarations.doc: The semidiscrete transport map is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_exists_mem_laguerreCell
declarations.doc: For an absolutely continuous law and distinct sites, almost every point lies in a Laguerre cell and has no ties.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_semidiscreteTransportMap
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56: when the Laguerre cells have the masses `b_j`, the semidiscrete transport map pushes `P` forward to the discrete law `∑ b_j δ_{y_j}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_norm_sub_semidiscreteTransportMap_sq
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56: when the Laguerre cells have the masses `b_j`, the quadratic cost of the semidiscrete transport map is the value of the dual functional.

declarations.name: CKSD.ofReal_semidiscreteTransportDual_le_lintegral
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56, weak duality: for every coupling `π` of `P` and `∑ b_j δ_{y_j}` with distinct sites, the dual functional is at most the quadratic cost of `π`.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscreteTransportDual_eq_wassersteinEDist_sq
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56, the value: when the Laguerre cells have the masses `b_j` (equivalently, at a maximizer), the dual functional equals the squared Wasserstein distance `W₂(P, ∑ b_j δ_{y_j})²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_inf_add_finrank_inf_le
declarations.doc: The rank inequality behind the nonnegativity of persistence multiplicities: for `Y ≤ X` and `U ≤ V`, `dim (Y ⊓ V) + dim (X ⊓ U) ≤ dim (X ⊓ V) + dim (Y ⊓ U)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_add_finrank_inf_le
declarations.doc: For `Y ≤ X`: `dim Y + dim (X ⊓ U) ≤ dim X + dim (Y ⊓ U)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eq_sum_sum_add_sum_of_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Two-variable telescoping of a function vanishing at the first index `0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_filter_sigma_fin
declarations.doc: Counting the elements of a sigma type over the fibres where a predicate holds.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_fin_ite_lt_eq_sum_range
declarations.doc: A sum over `Fin n` of the indices below `k ≤ n` is a sum over `range k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_fin_ite_le_eq_sum_range
declarations.doc: A sum over `Fin n` of the indices at least `k ≤ n` is a sum over `range (n - k)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence
declarations.doc: Signed incidence number of the face `τ` in the simplex `σ`: nonzero exactly when `τ` is a nonempty codimension-one face, with sign `(-1)^k` where the deleted vertex is the `k`th vertex of `σ` in increasing order (counting from `0`).

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary
declarations.doc: The simplicial boundary on chains, which are functions on finite vertex sets. Vertices have zero boundary (no augmentation).

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMonotoneOnFaces
declarations.doc: A function on simplices is monotone along faces of `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelChains
declarations.doc: Chains of dimension `p` of the sublevel subcomplex `K_a = {σ ∈ K : f σ ≤ a}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelCycles
declarations.doc: Cycles of dimension `p` of `K_a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelBoundaries
declarations.doc: Boundaries of dimension `p` of `K_b`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti
declarations.doc: Persistent Betti number `dim Z_p(K_a) - dim (Z_p(K_a) ∩ B_p(K_b))`, where `Z_p(K_a)` and `B_p(K_b)` are the cycles and boundaries of the chains spanned by simplices of value at most `a`, respectively `b`. Monotonicity of `f` is not assumed; when `f` is `IsMonotoneOnFaces`, the sets `K_a` are subcomplexes and this is the rank of `H_p(K_a) → H_p(K_b)` for `a ≤ b`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentHomology
declarations.doc: The persistent homology group `Z_p(K_a) / (Z_p(K_a) ∩ B_p(K_b))` in degree `p`. When `f` is `IsMonotoneOnFaces` and `a ≤ b`, it is the image of `H_p(K_a) → H_p(K_b)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSublevelDiagram
declarations.doc: `(D, e)` is the degree-`p` persistence diagram of the sublevel filtration of `f`: finite bars `[D.birth i, D.death i)` and essential bars `[e k, ∞)`, such that for `a ≤ b` the persistent Betti number counts the bars containing `[a, b]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelChains_mono
declarations.doc: Sublevel chains grow with the level.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelChains_congr_fun
declarations.doc: Sublevel chains of two functions agree when the sublevel sets agree on `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti_congr_fun
declarations.doc: Persistent Betti numbers of two functions agree when the two pairs of sublevel sets agree.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelPersistentBetti_cast
declarations.doc: The persistent Betti number as an integer difference of dimensions.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSublevelDiagram.exists_fin
declarations.doc: A sublevel diagram indexed by arbitrary finite types can be reindexed by `Fin`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isSublevelDiagram_and_values
declarations.doc: Strengthened existence of sublevel diagrams: the bars can be chosen with endpoints that are values of `f` at simplices of `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isSublevelDiagram
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.18, finite sublevel form: persistence diagrams of sublevel filtrations of finite simplicial complexes exist. Monotonicity of `f` is not assumed: the proof uses only that the chain spaces of `K_a` grow with `a`, and the bars are read off from the rank function at the critical values by inclusion–exclusion. For `f` monotone on faces this is the interval decomposition of the finite-type persistence module `a ↦ H_p(K_a)`, read through its rank invariant.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence_erase
declarations.doc: The incidence number of the face obtained by deleting the vertex `x`: the sign `(-1)^k` where `x` is the `k`th vertex of `σ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Incidence numbers vanish unless the first set is obtained by deleting one vertex.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplexIncidence_empty_left
declarations.doc: Incidence numbers vanish when the face is empty.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_simplexIncidence_mul_simplexIncidence
declarations.doc: The boundary of a boundary vanishes: `∑_τ [ρ : τ] [τ : σ] = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.simplicialBoundary_apply_simplicialBoundary
declarations.doc: The boundary of a boundary vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_forall_le_iff_le_of_ordered
declarations.doc: If `f` is ordered by `h` on `K` (`h σ ≤ h τ → f σ ≤ f τ`), every sublevel set of `f` on `K` is a sublevel set of `h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_le_forall_le_iff_le_of_ordered
declarations.doc: Two-level version of `exists_forall_le_iff_le_of_ordered`, with ordered levels.

declarations.name: CKSD.relabelDiagram
declarations.doc: The finite part of the relabelling of a diagram along simplices `sb`, `sd`: the bar `i` becomes `[f (sb i), f (sd i))`, and bars of length zero are discarded.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSublevelDiagram.relabel
declarations.doc: Relabelling: let `f` be ordered by `h` on `K`. If the bars of a diagram of `h` have endpoints `h (sb i)`, `h (sd i)` and `h (se k)` at simplices of `K`, then the relabelled bars `[f (sb i), f (sd i))` (without those of length zero) and `[f (se k), ∞)` form a diagram of `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fullBottleneckEDist_le_of_ordered
declarations.doc: Bottleneck stability when the two functions are ordered by a common monotone function `h`. The diagrams of `f` and `g` are both relabellings of one diagram of `h`, and matching the bars with the same label costs at most `δ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.discordantPairs
declarations.doc: Pairs of simplices of `K` ordered oppositely by `f` and `g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMonotoneOnFaces.convexComb
declarations.doc: A convex combination of functions monotone along faces is monotone along faces.

declarations.name: CKSD.fullBottleneckEDist_le_of_card_discordantPairs_le
declarations.doc: Bottleneck stability for `Fin`-indexed diagrams, by strong induction on the number of discordant pairs: without discordant pairs, `f` and `g` are both ordered by `f + g`; otherwise an intermediate convex combination `m` resolves one discordant pair and has fewer discordant pairs with both `f` and `g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fullBottleneckEDist_le_of_isSublevelDiagram
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.19, simplicial form: for monotone functions `f, g` on the simplices of a finite simplicial complex, the degree-`p` persistence diagrams of the sublevel filtrations (finite and essential parts) are within bottleneck distance `‖f - g‖_∞ = max_{σ ∈ K} |f σ - g σ|`. The statement for tame functions on triangulable spaces, with singular homology of sublevel sets, is not formalized; for piecewise-linear functions it reduces to this case.

declarations.name: CKSD.finrank_map_sublevelChains_le
declarations.doc: For `h` injective on `K`, passing from the level just below `h σ` to `h σ` adds at most the simplex `σ`, and only in dimension `σ.card - 1`; so the image of the chains under any linear map grows in dimension by at most one, and not at all in other dimensions.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelCycles_mono
declarations.doc: Sublevel cycles grow with the level.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelBoundaries_mono
declarations.doc: Boundaries grow with the level.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_birth_add_card_essential_le
declarations.doc: For `h` injective on `K`, a diagram of `h` in degree `p` has at most one bar (finite or essential) born at `h σ`, and none unless `σ` is a `p`-simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_death_le
declarations.doc: For `h` injective on `K`, a diagram of `h` in degree `p` has at most one finite bar dying at `h σ`, and none unless `σ` is a `(p + 1)`-simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist_eq_zero_of_equiv
declarations.doc: Diagrams related by bijections preserving all points are at `q`-Wasserstein distance zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist_eq_zero_of_isSublevelDiagram
declarations.doc: Diagrams of the same function are at `q`-Wasserstein distance zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist_le_of_ordered
declarations.doc: `q`-Wasserstein stability when the two functions are ordered by a common function `h` that is injective on `K`. The bars of the diagram of `h` have distinct endpoint simplices, and matching the relabelled bars with the same label costs at most `∑_{σ ∈ K} |f σ - g σ|^q`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_injective_ordered
declarations.doc: Every function on simplices is ordered by a function injective on `K`: break ties by an enumeration of the simplices and take ranks.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist_le_of_card_discordantPairs_le
declarations.doc: `q`-Wasserstein stability for `Fin`-indexed diagrams, by strong induction on the number of discordant pairs, as for the bottleneck distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.diagramWassersteinEDist_le_of_isSublevelDiagram
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.35, the finite-complex clause: for monotone functions `f, g` on the simplices of a finite simplicial complex `K` and `1 ≤ q < ∞`, the `q`-Wasserstein distance between the full degree-`p` diagrams is at most `(∑_{σ ∈ K} |f σ - g σ|^q)^{1/q}`. The clauses for tame Lipschitz functions on triangulable spaces with polynomially growing triangulations are not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.ripsFiltrationValue
declarations.doc: The Rips filtration value of a simplex in the diameter-`2r` convention: `σ ∈ Rips(r)` exactly when `diam σ ≤ 2r`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMonotoneOnFaces_ripsFiltrationValue
declarations.doc: Diameters are monotone, so the Rips filtration is a monotone filtration of the full simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.ripsFiltrationValue_le_iff
declarations.doc: A nonempty simplex has Rips filtration value at most `r` exactly when it is a Rips simplex of parameter `r`, that is, when all its pairwise distances are at most `2r`.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateGaussianPDFReal_zero_smul_one
declarations.doc: The density of `N(0, s I)` is `c_s exp(-‖z‖² / (2 s))` with `c_s` its value at the origin.

declarations.name: CKSD.isoGaussianPDF
declarations.doc: The density of `N(0, s I)` on `ℝ^d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isoGaussianPDF_eq
declarations.doc: The density of `N(0, s I)` in the form `c_s exp(-‖z‖² / (2 s))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isoGaussianPDF_pos
declarations.doc: The density of `N(0, s I)` is positive.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_isoGaussianPDF
declarations.doc: The density of `N(0, s I)` is continuous.

declarations.name: CKSD.isoGaussianPDF_le_isoGaussianPDF_zero
declarations.doc: The density of `N(0, s I)` is maximal at the origin.

declarations.name: CKSD.isoGaussianPDF_sub_le
declarations.doc: Gaussian domination: if `‖y‖² ≤ R`, then the density of `N(0, s I)` at `x - y` is at most a constant times the density of `N(0, 2 s I)` at `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_isoGaussianPDF
declarations.doc: The density of `N(0, s I)` is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateGaussian_smul_one_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: `N(0, s I)` has density `isoGaussianPDF d s` with respect to Lebesgue measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_multivariateGaussian_smul_one
declarations.doc: Integrals against `N(0, s I)` as Lebesgue integrals against its density.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_norm_mul_isoGaussianPDF
declarations.doc: `‖x‖` times the density of `N(0, s I)` is Lebesgue integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_gaussianSmoothing
declarations.doc: The Gaussian smoothing of a probability measure is a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_norm_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: The norm is integrable under a centred multivariate Gaussian law.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasFiniteMoment_gaussianSmoothing
declarations.doc: The Gaussian smoothing of a law with finite first moment has finite first moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_gaussianSmoothing_eq
declarations.doc: Integrals against a Gaussian smoothing: for `f` continuous with `|f x| ≤ ‖x‖` and `ν` with finite first moment, `∫ f d(ν * N(0, σ² I)) = ∫ (∫ f(x) φ(x - y) dx) dν(y)` with `φ` the Gaussian density.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_abs_sampleMean_sub_le
declarations.doc: Mean absolute deviation of a sample mean: for `g` with `|g| ≤ B` almost surely and an i.i.d. sample of size `n ≥ 1`, `E |n⁻¹ ∑ g(X_i) - E g| ≤ B / √n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.unitCube
declarations.doc: The cube `[-1, 1]^d` in `ℝ^d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_unitCube
declarations.doc: The cube `[-1, 1]^d` is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sq_le_of_mem_unitCube
declarations.doc: Points of the cube `[-1, 1]^d` have squared norm at most `d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_empiricalMeasure
declarations.doc: Every real function is integrable for an empirical measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_empiricalMeasure
declarations.doc: The integral against an empirical measure is the sample average.

declarations.name: CKSD.smoothingConst
declarations.doc: The constant `K` of the Gaussian domination bound `φ_{σ²}(x - y) ≤ K φ_{2σ²}(x)` for `y` in the cube `[-1, 1]^d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.smoothingConst_pos
declarations.doc: The Gaussian domination constant is positive.

declarations.name: CKSD.isoGaussianPDF_sub_le_of_mem_unitCube
declarations.doc: Gaussian domination on the cube: for `y ∈ [-1, 1]^d`, `φ_{σ²}(x - y) ≤ K φ_{2σ²}(x)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.smoothedDensity
declarations.doc: The Lebesgue density `x ↦ ∫ φ_{σ²}(x - y) dP(y)` of the Gaussian smoothing of `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_smoothedDensity
declarations.doc: The smoothed density is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.smoothedDensity_nonneg
declarations.doc: The smoothed density is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.smoothedDensity_le
declarations.doc: For a law on the cube, the smoothed density is dominated by `K φ_{2σ²}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinEDist_one_gaussianSmoothing_le
declarations.doc: Weighted total variation bound: for a sample in the cube, `W₁` between the Gaussian smoothings of its empirical measure and of `P` is at most `∫ ‖x‖ |p_n(x) - p(x)| dx`, by Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality.

declarations.name: CKSD.smoothingMoment
declarations.doc: The constant `∫ ‖x‖ K φ_{2σ²}(x) dx` of the smoothed empirical `W₁` rate.

declarations.name: CKSD.smoothingMoment_nonneg
declarations.doc: The constant `smoothingMoment` is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_lintegral_smoothedDensity_le
declarations.doc: The expected weighted total variation between smoothed empirical and population densities is at most `smoothingMoment d σ / √n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_wassersteinEDist_gaussianSmoothing_le
declarations.doc: The parametric rate of Gaussian-smoothed empirical `W₁` with an explicit constant: for a law `P` on `[-1, 1]^d` and `n ≥ 1`, `E W₁(μ_n * N_σ, P * N_σ) ≤ smoothingMoment d σ / √n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_cos_inner_eq_re_charFun
declarations.doc: The cosine moment is the real part of the characteristic function.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sin_inner_eq_im_charFun
declarations.doc: The sine moment is the imaginary part of the characteristic function.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_cos_inner_sub_prod
declarations.doc: The cosine of a projected difference is integrable under every finite product law.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_cos_inner_sub_prod
declarations.doc: The product-law cosine moment is the Euclidean pairing of characteristic functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_spectralKernel_prod
declarations.doc: Integrating a translation-invariant spectral kernel against a product law interchanges its spectral and observation integrals.

declarations.name: CKSD.squaredMMD_spectralKernel_eq_integral
declarations.doc: The spectral expression for squared MMD is the weighted squared distance between characteristic functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.isCharacteristicKernel_spectral_of_full_support
declarations.doc: A spectral measure charging every ball produces a characteristic translation-invariant kernel, by uniqueness of characteristic functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_probabilityMeasures_charFun_sub_eq_of_even_bump
declarations.doc: A nonzero even smooth Fourier perturbation vanishing at the origin is the difference of two probability characteristic functions up to a positive normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_even_smooth_bump_of_spectral_gap
declarations.doc: A ball missing from a symmetric spectral measure contains the support of a nonzero even smooth Fourier perturbation which vanishes at the origin.

declarations.name: CKSD.isCharacteristicKernel_spectral_iff
declarations.doc: A translation-invariant kernel with a finite symmetric spectral measure is characteristic exactly when the spectral measure charges every open ball.

declarations.name: CKSD.quadraticEntropicCost
declarations.doc: Squared Euclidean cost in TauCeti's nonnegative extended-real convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.quadraticEntropicTransport
declarations.doc: Real entropic quadratic transport cost, used where the bounded-support cost is finite.

declarations.name: CKSD.entropicBarycentricMap
declarations.doc: Barycentric projection of a quadratic Gibbs coupling represented by a target dual potential. The denominator is explicit; applications supply a positive finite normalization integral.

declarations.name: CKSD.quadraticEntropicTransport_empirical_bounds
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.55: dimension-free mean-square and bias bounds for empirical entropic costs. For `ε > 0` there is `C > 0`, independent of the dimension, such that for laws `P, Q` on the ball of radius `1/2` and `n ≥ 1` samples the empirical entropic cost `S_n` satisfies `E (S_n - S)² ≤ C / n` and `|E S_n - S| ≤ C / n`. The entropic-map estimation bound is not asserted here. Constants may depend on `ε` only.

declarations.name: CKSD.SatisfiesWassersteinKarcherEquation
declarations.doc: Karcher equation for a specified collection of optimal transport maps.

declarations.name: CKSD.displacementLaw
declarations.doc: Displacing a law by the vector field `v` for time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.barycenter_derivative_of_component_derivatives
declarations.doc: Finite sums of quadratic transport first variations give the equal - weight barycenter derivative.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_wassersteinBarycenterEnergy_displacement
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.58, directional first variation of the equal-weight barycenter energy. For an absolutely continuous law `P` with finite second moment and square-integrable maps `T_i` that are optimal from `P` to the targets, the energy along the displacement `x ↦ x + t v(x)` has derivative `∫ ⟨x - k⁻¹ ∑ T_i x, v x⟩ dP` at `t = 0`. The targets are probability laws with finite second moment because they are the images `(T_i)_# P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.satisfiesWassersteinKarcherEquation_of_minimizer
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.58: a minimizing barycenter with the supplied optimal maps satisfies the Karcher equation.

declarations.name: CKSD.satisfiesWassersteinKarcherEquation_iff
declarations.doc: The Karcher equation says exactly that the average optimal map is the identity almost surely.

declarations.name: CKSD.mixedKernelDivergence
declarations.doc: The mixed divergence `⟨∇_x, ∇_y⟩ k(x, y) = ∑_j ∂_{x_j} ∂_{y_j} k(x, y)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.langevinSteinKernel
declarations.doc: The Langevin Stein kernel of a score `b` and a kernel `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.kernelSteinDiscrepancySq
declarations.doc: Squared kernel Stein discrepancy of `μ`, in closed form.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsDistantlyDissipative
declarations.doc: Distant dissipativity of a score: `⟨b x - b y, x - y⟩ ≤ -κ ‖x - y‖²` once `‖x - y‖ ≥ R`.

declarations.name: CKSD.inverseMultiquadricKernel
declarations.doc: The inverse multiquadric kernel `(c² + ‖x - y‖²)^β`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_of_kernelSteinDiscrepancySq_inverseMultiquadric_tendsto_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.72(b): let `P` have a positive continuously differentiable density `p` with score `b = ∇ log p` that is Lipschitz and distantly dissipative. For the inverse multiquadric kernel with `c > 0` and `β ∈ (-1, 0)`, every sequence of laws with square-integrable score whose kernel Stein discrepancy tends to zero converges weakly to `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_not_tendsto_of_kernelSteinDiscrepancySq_tendsto_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.72(d): for `d ≥ 3` and the standard Gaussian target (score `b x = -x`), let `k` be a `C²` kernel which, together with `∇_x k`, `∇_y k` and `⟨∇_x, ∇_y⟩ k`, is bounded, and whose decay function `γ(r)` (the supremum of `|k|`, `‖∇_x k‖` and `|⟨∇_x, ∇_y⟩ k|` over `‖x - y‖ ≥ r`) is `o(r^{-α})` with `α = (1/2 - 1/d)⁻¹`. Then some sequence of laws with finite second moments has kernel Stein discrepancy tending to zero without converging weakly to the standard Gaussian. This covers the Gaussian, Matérn and Wendland kernels. The `C²` hypothesis strengthens the source's continuity requirement on the listed derivatives. Clauses (a) and (c) are not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.singularHomologyModule
declarations.doc: Degree-`n` singular homology of a topological space with coefficients in `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelSetFunctor
declarations.doc: The filtration of a space by the sublevel sets `{f ≤ t}` of a real function, as a functor from `ℝ` to topological spaces.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelHomologyModule
declarations.doc: The sublevel persistence module `t ↦ H_n({f ≤ t}; k)` of a real function.

declarations.name: CKSD.reach
declarations.doc: The reach of a set: the supremum of the radii `r` such that every point at distance less than `r` from the set has a unique nearest point in it.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsDistanceCriticalPoint
declarations.doc: A point outside `K` is critical for the distance function to `K` when it lies in the convex hull of its nearest points in `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.weakFeatureSize
declarations.doc: The weak feature size: the infimum of the positive critical values of the distance function, `∞` when there are none.

declarations.name: CKSD.offsetInclusion
declarations.doc: Inclusion of offsets of a set.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_deformationRetraction_offset_of_hausdorffDist_lt
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.22, deformation retraction of offsets. Let `M = j(N) ⊂ ℝ^D` be a compact smooth `d`-dimensional submanifold without boundary with reach at least `τ > 0`, and `P ⊆ M` finite and nonempty with `d_H(P, M) = ε < √(3/20) τ`. For `r ∈ (2ε, √(3/5) τ)` the offset `P^r` contains `M` and strongly deformation retracts onto it. By the nerve theorem the Čech complex of radius `r` then has the homotopy type of `M`; the nerve theorem is not part of this statement.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_sample_size_hausdorffDist_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.22, the sampling bound. Let `M = j(N) ⊂ ℝ^D` be a compact smooth `d`-dimensional submanifold without boundary and `c > 0`. There are `C, ε₀ > 0` such that for every law `μ` concentrated on `M` with density at least `c` with respect to the `d`-dimensional Hausdorff measure on `M` (the Riemannian volume), all `ε ∈ (0, ε₀)`, `δ ∈ (0, 1)` and `n ≥ C ε^{-d} (log(1/ε) + log(1/δ))`, an independent sample of size `n` is `ε`-close to `M` in Hausdorff distance with probability at least `1 - δ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.nonempty_range_offsetHomology_equiv_of_weakFeatureSize
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.37, offsets: let `K ⊂ ℝ^D` be compact and nonempty with weak feature size at least `τ > 0`, and `P` finite and nonempty with `d_H(K, P) = ε`. If `ε < i` and `i + 2ε ≤ j < τ - ε` (which forces `ε < τ/4`), the image of `H_n(P^i) → H_n(P^j)` is isomorphic to `H_n(K^r)` for every `r ∈ (0, τ)`, in every degree `n` and over every field. Taking `τ = wfs(K)` when it is finite gives the source statement. Offsets are closed thickenings; since `P` is finite and `K` compact, `d_H(K, P) = ε` gives the closed interleavings `K^a ⊆ P^{a+ε}` and `P^a ⊆ K^{a+ε}` used by the argument. The Čech-complex form follows by the nerve theorem and is not stated separately.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleRipsFiltrationValue
declarations.doc: The Rips filtration of a finite indexed sample, in the diameter-`2r` convention: the Rips filtration value `diam (x '' σ) / 2` of the image of the index simplex `σ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.nonempty_ripsPersistentHomology_equiv_of_weakFeatureSize
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.37, Rips complexes: let `K ⊂ ℝ^D` be compact and nonempty with weak feature size at least `τ > 0`, and `x` a finite sample with `d_H(K, {x_i}) < ε` for some `ε < τ/9`. If `2ε ≤ α ≤ (τ - ε)/4`, the image of `H_n(Rips(α/2)) → H_n(Rips(2α))` (diameter-`2r` parameter, simplicial homology over a field) is isomorphic to `H_n(K^r)` for every `r ∈ (0, τ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.manifoldCriticalPoints
declarations.doc: Critical points of a real function on a manifold modeled on `ℝ^m`: the points where the manifold derivative vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.manifoldCriticalCount
declarations.doc: The number of critical points of Morse index `q`, in `ℕ∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sublevelHomologyModule_bars_of_isMorse
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.34, diagrams of the sublevel persistence of a Morse function. Let `f` be a Morse function with distinct critical values on a closed smooth `m`-manifold and `k` a field, and for each degree `q` let `B q` be an interval decomposition of `t ↦ H_q({f ≤ t}; k)` into finitely many closed-open bars, finite ones `[(D q).birth i, (D q).death i)` and essential ones `[e q i, ∞)`. Then every endpoint is a critical value; the number `c_q` of index-`q` critical points is the number of degree-`q` bars plus the number of finite degree-`(q-1)` bars; there are exactly `β_q(M)` essential degree-`q` bars; and each critical value is an endpoint of exactly one bar. The homotopy-theoretic description (cell attachment at critical values) is not restated.

declarations.name: CKSD.mem_convexHull_farthest_of_isMin
declarations.doc: At a point `c` minimizing the largest squared distance to a nonempty finite set `S`, the point `c` lies in the convex hull of the farthest points of `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_dist_le_sqrt_two_mul_of_dist_le
declarations.doc: A finite set of diameter at most `2r` in a finite-dimensional real inner product space lies in a closed ball of radius `√2 r`, centered at a point minimizing the largest distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.cech_rips_inclusions
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.21, the Euclidean Čech/Rips inclusions, in the diameter-`2r` convention: for a finite set `S` in a finite-dimensional real inner product space, if `S` lies in a closed ball of radius `r` then all pairwise distances are at most `2r`, and if all pairwise distances are at most `2r` then `S` lies in a closed ball of radius `√2 r`.

declarations.name: CKSD.massRadius_eq_quantile_map_dist
declarations.doc: On a probability space, the mass radius `δ_{P,u}(x)` at a level `u ≥ 0` is the quantile at level `u` of the law of the distance `y ↦ d(x, y)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_distanceToMeasure_sub_le_wasserstein
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.24: stability of distance to a measure. For laws `P, Q` on `ℝ^d` with finite second moments and a mass parameter `m ∈ (0, 1]`, the distance functions satisfy `|d_{P,m}(x) - d_{Q,m}(x)| ≤ W₂(P, Q) / √m` at every point `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_empirical_wasserstein_rpow_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.40, all three bounded-support regimes on a unit ball: for `p ≥ 1` there is `C > 0` such that for every law `P` on the closed unit ball of `ℝ^d` and `n ≥ 1`, the expected `W_p^p` distance between `P` and its empirical measure is at most `C n^{-1/2}` if `d < 2p`, `C log(1 + n) n^{-1/2}` if `d = 2p`, and `C n^{-p/d}` if `d > 2p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_mem_support_preimage_of_support_eq_univ
declarations.doc: A continuous map from a compact space onto a law with full support takes the support of the source law onto the target space.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_measure_preserving_isometryEquiv_of_zero_distortion
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.43, the upgrade from a zero-distortion coupling to an isometry: let `μ, ν` be laws on compact metric spaces that charge every open ball, and `π` a coupling of them with `d(x, x') = d(y, y')` for `π ⊗ π`-almost every pair of pairs. Then some isometry `f : X ≃ᵢ Y` pushes `μ` to `ν`. The full-support assumption realizes the source's restriction to the supports.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_unique_gaussian_wasserstein_barycenter
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.46: the covariance equation and unique Gaussian barycenter of finitely many laws. For weights `w` summing to one and Gaussian laws `N(m_i, A_i)` with positive definite covariances, there is a positive definite `S` solving the fixed-point equation `S = ∑ w_i (S^{1/2} A_i S^{1/2})^{1/2}`, and `N(∑ w_i m_i, S)` is the unique minimizer of `P ↦ ∑ w_i W₂²(P, N(m_i, A_i))` among the laws with finite second moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.rpow_div_le_wassersteinEDist_volume_cube
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.50, quantization lower bound for the uniform unit cube: for `d ≥ 3`, every law `Q` carried by at most `n` points is at `W₁`-distance at least `n^{-1/d} / (108 d)` from the uniform law on `[0, 1]^d`. (`n ≥ 1` is implied by `Q (range x) = 1`.)

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_wasserstein_gaussianSmoothing_empiricalMeasure_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.51, the parametric rate of Gaussian-smoothed empirical W1 on a bounded cube: for `σ > 0` there is `C > 0` such that for every law `P` on `[-1, 1]^d` and `n ≥ 1`, the expected `W₁` distance between the Gaussian smoothings of the empirical measure and of `P` is at most `C / √n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidiscreteTransportDual_concave_differentiable_and_attains_max
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.56: smooth semidiscrete dual, cell-mass equations and dual attainment. For an absolutely continuous law `P` with finite second moment and a discrete target with positive masses `b_j` at distinct sites `y_j`, the dual functional `E(g)` is concave and `C¹` with gradient `b_j - P(Laguerre cell j)`; its maximizers are exactly the weights whose Laguerre cells have masses `b_j`; and a maximizer exists, with value `W₂²(P, ∑ b_j δ_{y_j})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.commute_cfcSqrt_right
declarations.doc: A matrix commuting with `B` commutes with its square root `CFC.sqrt B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.optimalMap_eq_cfcSqrt_mul_inv_iff_commute
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.57, the covariance-commutation criterion for compatibility with the standard Gaussian. For `A` positive definite and `B` positive semidefinite, the optimal map `A^{-1/2} (A^{1/2} B A^{1/2})^{1/2} A^{-1/2}` from `N(0, A)` to `N(0, B)` equals the composite `B^{1/2} A^{-1/2}` of the optimal maps through the standard Gaussian exactly when `A` and `B` commute.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinBarycenterEnergy
declarations.doc: The equal-weight Wasserstein barycenter energy `(2k)⁻¹ ∑_i W₂²(P, target_i)`, with the factor `1/2` normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinBarycenterGradient
declarations.doc: The candidate barycenter gradient `x - k⁻¹ ∑_i T_i x` represented by transport maps `T_i` (optimal maps from the current law to the targets).

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinEDist_two_map_toReal_sq_le
declarations.doc: The squared `2`-Wasserstein distance between the laws of `S` and `T` under `P` is at most the mean squared distance `∫ ‖S x - T x‖² dP`, by the coupling `(S, T)_# P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_norm_sub_smul_sub_sq
declarations.doc: Pointwise form of the descent identity: with `g = x - k⁻¹ ∑ Tᵢ`, moving `x` by `-τ g` changes the sum of squared distances to the `Tᵢ` by `-k (2τ - τ²) ‖g‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.wassersteinBarycenterEnergy_map_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.59, the energy-descent inequality for the averaged-transport update. Let `P` have finite second moment, let `T_i` be square-integrable maps that are optimal from `P` to `P_i = (T_i)_# P`, and let `g = x - k⁻¹ ∑ T_i x` be the barycenter gradient. Then for every step size `τ` the update `x ↦ x - τ g(x)` lowers the barycenter energy by at least `(τ - τ²/2) ∫ ‖g‖² dP`. The usual descent interpretation uses `τ ∈ [0, 1]`; no convergence of the iteration is asserted.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_displacement_cost_eq_wasserstein_of_minimizer
declarations.doc: A least-cost coupling for the displaced quadratic cost realizes the squared Wasserstein distance of the displaced source to the target.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_wasserstein_sq_displacement
declarations.doc: First variation of the squared quadratic Wasserstein distance along an arbitrary measurable square-integrable displacement, at an absolutely continuous source law.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_mul_wasserstein_sq_empiricalMeasure
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.47: let `μ` be concentrated on `[a, b]` with a density `f` continuous on `[a, b]` and bounded there between positive constants (the upper bound is automatic by continuity on the compact interval, and `a < b` follows because `μ` has a density and total mass one). For an i.i.d. sample of law `μ`, `n W₂²(μ_n, μ)` converges in distribution to `∫₀¹ B⁰(u)² / f(F⁻¹(u))² du`, where `B⁰(u) = W(u) - u W(1)` is the Brownian bridge built from any Brownian motion `W`; consequently `√n W₂(μ_n, μ)` is bounded in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.ballLegendreConjugate
declarations.doc: Legendre conjugate of a potential, with the supremum over the closed unit ball.

declarations.name: CKSD.semidualFunctional
declarations.doc: Semidual functional `∫ φ dμ + ∫ φ* dν`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ballSupCoveringNumber
declarations.doc: Covering number of a class of potentials in the supremum norm over the closed unit ball.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsRegularPotentialClass
declarations.doc: Regularity class for transport-map estimation (Section 108.53): potentials bounded by `B` on the closed unit ball, ambient twice continuously differentiable at each point of that ball, with `½ I ≤ ∇²φ ≤ 2 I` there, and with sup-norm metric entropy `log N(ε, Φ) ≤ A ε^{-γ} log(1 + 1/ε)` for `0 < ε ≤ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSemidualEstimator
declarations.doc: A semidual estimator: a map from paired samples to potentials in `Φ` minimizing the empirical semidual functional.

declarations.name: CKSD.transportMapRisk
declarations.doc: Squared `L²(μ)` error of the estimated transport map `∇φ̂`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_transportMapRisk_semidualEstimator_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.53, the parametric-rate bound for semidual estimators. Let `μ` be carried by a closed ball of radius `r ∈ [0, 1)` and `ν` by the closed unit ball, with `ν = (∇φ₀)_# μ` for `φ₀ ∈ Φ`. The regular class `Φ` has entropy exponent `γ ∈ [0, 1)`. Every semidual estimator from `n` independent pairs satisfies `E ‖∇φ̂ - ∇φ₀‖²_{L²(μ)} ≤ K n^{-1/2}`, where `K` is independent of `n` and may depend on `r`. The expectation is the lower Lebesgue integral of the measurable risk.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_transportMapRisk_semidualEstimator_le_of_poincare
declarations.doc: GAPS 108.53, the fast rate: if moreover `Φ` is convex and `μ` satisfies the Poincaré inequality `Var_μ(h) ≤ C_P ∫ ‖∇h‖² dμ` for continuously differentiable `h`, the risk of every semidual estimator is at most `K (log n / n)^{2/(2+γ)}`. The source is carried by a closed ball of radius `r ∈ [0, 1)`; the constant may depend on this interior margin. The minimax rate for Hölder maps and its wavelet estimator are not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isCoupling_map_prodMap_eq
declarations.doc: A coupling out of a measurable pushforward lifts to a coupling out of the original law.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerSemicontinuous_of_ennreal_ofReal
declarations.doc: Lower semicontinuity of the nonnegative extended-real coercion implies real lower semicontinuity.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerSemicontinuous_lintegral_coupling_displacement
declarations.doc: The nonnegative displacement cost is weakly lower semicontinuous on a family of plans with fixed first marginal, even when the vector field is merely measurable. Lusin sets for the fixed marginal provide the uniform continuity sets required by the portmanteau theorem.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_norm_displacement_coupling_sq
declarations.doc: Finite second moments make the displaced quadratic cost integrable against every coupling.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_norm_displacement_coupling_sq
declarations.doc: Exact quadratic expansion of a coupling cost along a square-integrable displacement.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_inner_displacement_coupling_le
declarations.doc: The linear displacement coefficient is uniformly bounded by the marginal second moments.

declarations.name: CKSD.lowerSemicontinuous_integral_coupling_displacement_sq
declarations.doc: The real quadratic displacement cost is lower semicontinuous on fixed-marginal couplings with finite second moments, for any measurable square-integrable displacement field.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_of_map_eq
declarations.doc: Convergence in distribution depends on the limit random variable only through its law.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_id_iff
declarations.doc: Convergence in distribution to a law `ν`, with the identity as limit random variable, is convergence of the laws to `ν` in Mathlib's `ProbabilityMeasure` topology.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBoundedInProbability
declarations.doc: Boundedness in probability (uniform tightness) of a real sequence: for every `ε > 0` there is `C > 0` with `μ {C < |X n|} ≤ ε` for all large `n`. The sets `{C < |X n|}` are measured by the outer measure, so no measurability of `X n` is required; this serves the stochastic `O_P` algebra of possibly nonmeasurable sequences. For almost everywhere measurable `X n` and finite `μ` it is tightness of the laws, Mathlib's `IsTightMeasureSet (range fun n ↦ μ.map (X n))` (`CKSD.isBoundedInProbability_iff_isTightMeasureSet`).

declarations.name: CKSD.isBoundedInProbability_iff_isTightMeasureSet
declarations.doc: For almost everywhere measurable real random variables under a finite measure, boundedness in probability is tightness of the set of their laws (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.IsTightMeasureSet`). Eventual bounds suffice for tightness of the whole sequence since each finite measure on `ℝ` is tight.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalMeasure
declarations.doc: The empirical measure; the empty sample gives the zero measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_empiricalMeasure
declarations.doc: The empirical measure of a nonempty sample is a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleAverage
declarations.doc: The empirical average of the first `n` observations of a sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIndependentIdenticallyDistributed
declarations.doc: A measurable independent sequence with common law `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasDensity
declarations.doc: `f` is a real density of `P` with respect to `μ`: `f` is measurable, `μ`-almost everywhere nonnegative, and `P = μ.withDensity (ofReal ∘ f)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_of_hasDensity
declarations.doc: A density of a probability law on `ℝ` is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest
declarations.doc: A randomized test: a measurable function `φ : X → [0, 1]`, the probability of rejection at each observation.

declarations.name: CKSD.thresholdTest
declarations.doc: The one-sided randomized test in a statistic `T`: reject when `c < T x`, reject with probability `γ` when `T x = c`, and accept otherwise.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsUnbiasedEstimator
