declarations.doc: An unbiased estimator of `g`: a measurable `δ` that is integrable under every `P θ` with mean `g θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSufficientStatistic
declarations.doc: Sufficiency of a measurable statistic `T`: one Markov kernel `K` (the conditional law of the observation given `T`) disintegrates every joint law of `(T, X)`, i.e. `(P θ).map (T, id) = (P θ).map T ⊗ₘ K` for all `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCompleteStatistic
declarations.doc: Completeness of a statistic `T`: every measurable `g` with `g ∘ T` integrable and of mean zero under every `P θ` vanishes `P θ`-almost everywhere on the range of `T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBoundedlyCompleteStatistic
declarations.doc: Bounded completeness of a statistic `T`: completeness restricted to bounded measurable `g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsUniformlyMostPowerfulTest
declarations.doc: A uniformly most powerful level-`α` test of `H₀` against `H₁`: `φ` has level `α` on `H₀` and at every `θ ∈ H₁` its power is at least that of every level-`α` test.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsUniformlyMostPowerfulUnbiasedTest
declarations.doc: A uniformly most powerful unbiased level-`α` test: `φ` has level `α` on `H₀`, power at least `α` on `H₁`, and maximal power on `H₁` among all such unbiased level-`α` tests.

declarations.name: CKSD.RandomizedDecisionRule
declarations.doc: A randomized decision rule: a Markov kernel from observations to actions.

declarations.name: CKSD.risk
declarations.doc: The risk `R(θ, δ) = ∫∫ L(θ, a) dδ(x)(a) dP θ(x)` of a randomized decision rule. It is a Bochner integral, used for integrable (typically bounded) losses.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_iff_measureReal_lt_dist
declarations.doc: For a finite measure, convergence in measure is the vanishing of the real-valued measures of the sets `{ε < dist (f i) (g)}`, with strict inequality; compare Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.tendstoInMeasure_iff_measureReal_dist`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest.nonneg
declarations.doc: A test takes nonnegative values.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest.le_one
declarations.doc: A test takes values at most one.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest.abs_le_one
declarations.doc: A test is bounded by one in absolute value.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest.const
declarations.doc: A constant in `[0, 1]` is a test.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest.one_sub
declarations.doc: The complementary test `1 - φ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest.integrable
declarations.doc: A test is integrable for every finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest.integrable_mul
declarations.doc: The product of a test with an integrable function is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest.integral_nonneg
declarations.doc: The mean of a test is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest.integral_le_one
declarations.doc: The mean of a test under a probability measure is at most one.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest.integral_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: The mean of a test under a probability measure lies in `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStatisticalTest.integral_one_sub
declarations.doc: The mean of the complementary test `1 - φ` under a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.isStatisticalTest_thresholdTest
declarations.doc: A threshold test with randomization `γ ∈ [0, 1]` in a measurable statistic is a test.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_measurable_finite_quantizations
declarations.doc: Every nonempty separable metric space has measurable finite quantizations converging pointwise to the identity. The action set at stage `n` has `n + 1` elements.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_finiteMeasure_subsequence_limit_of_mass_eq
declarations.doc: Finite measures of fixed mass on a compact metric space admit a weakly convergent subsequence. Normalization reduces this to compactness of probability measures.

declarations.name: CKSD.snd_withDensity_map_compProd
declarations.doc: Weighting the first coordinate of a mapped composition product commutes with mixing the correspondingly weighted input law.

declarations.name: CKSD.fst_map_compProd
declarations.doc: Mapping both coordinates of a Markov composition product preserves the pushed-forward first marginal.

declarations.name: CKSD.snd_withDensity_eq_of_finiteMeasure_tendsto
declarations.doc: Bounded continuous weighting and taking the second marginal preserve finite weak limits.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteMeasure_tendsto_map_of_pointwise
declarations.doc: Pointwise convergent measurable quantizations give weak convergence of every finite push-forward law.

declarations.name: CKSD.risk_eq_sum_actionLaw
declarations.doc: Risk with finite actions is the loss paired with the randomized action-law masses.

declarations.name: CKSD.isCompact_convex_range_actionLaw
declarations.doc: A finite experiment's attainable action-probability matrices form a compact convex set.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_finite_randomization_of_risk_dominance
declarations.doc: Finite-action risk comparison forces exact simulation of any finite-action rule.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_joint_of_finite_randomizations
declarations.doc: Exact finite randomizations produce a joint likelihood-vector law with every required coordinate-weighted marginal. Compactness chooses one joint subsequence for all parameters.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteLikelihoodCube
declarations.doc: The compact cube of bounded likelihood vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteLikelihoodCube_def
declarations.doc: The likelihood cube is the order interval from zero to one.

declarations.name: CKSD.mem_finiteLikelihoodCube_iff
declarations.doc: A likelihood vector belongs to the cube exactly when its coordinates lie in `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteDominatingMeasure
declarations.doc: The sum of a finite family of probability laws dominates every family member.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteDominatingMeasure_def
declarations.doc: The dominating measure is the finite sum of the experiment laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_finiteDominatingMeasure
declarations.doc: A finite family member is bounded above by the dominating sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteLikelihoodMap
declarations.doc: Finite likelihood vectors use bounded versions of the Radon–Nikodym densities.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteLikelihoodMap_def
declarations.doc: The likelihood vector consists of the Radon–Nikodym densities clamped above at one.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteLikelihoodMap_apply
declarations.doc: Each likelihood coordinate is the corresponding clamped density.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_finiteLikelihoodMap
declarations.doc: The bounded likelihood vector is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDensity_finiteLikelihoodMap
declarations.doc: A coordinate of the bounded likelihood vector is a density relative to the dominating sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.isSufficientStatistic_finiteLikelihoodMap
declarations.doc: In a standard Borel sample space, the finite likelihood vector is sufficient.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_finiteLikelihood_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: Pushing a finite experiment to its likelihood cube expresses each law as a coordinate tilt of the pushed-forward dominating sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.isGarbling_of_finiteLikelihoodMap
declarations.doc: A standard Borel finite experiment can be reconstructed by one Markov kernel from its bounded likelihood vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.splitLogPartition
declarations.doc: Log partition function of a natural exponential family whose natural statistic is the pair `(T, S)`, with natural parameter `(η, ζ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.splitExponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: The natural exponential law with density `exp(η·T + ζ·S - A(η, ζ))` with respect to the base measure `ν`; it is a probability measure on the natural parameter space when `ν ≠ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.conditionalExponentialKernel
declarations.doc: The exponential tilt of a family of measures `ν_s` by the parameter `η`, normalized in each fibre: the kernel `s ↦ exp(η·t - A_s(η)) ν_s(dt)` with `A_s(η) = log ∫ exp(η·t) ν_s(dt)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.withDensity_exp_compProd_eq_fst_compProd
declarations.doc: Exponential tilting of a composition product. If `μ` is a finite measure and `κ` a Markov kernel, and the tilt of `μ ⊗ₘ κ` by `exp (a t + b s)` is finite, then this tilt is its first marginal composed with the fibrewise normalized tilt `s ↦ exp (a t - log ∫ exp (a t') κ s) κ s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.conditionalExponentialKernel_withDensity_exp_neg
declarations.doc: Tilting a kernel by `exp (-η₁ · t)` and then forming the conditional exponential kernel at `η` is the conditional exponential kernel of the untilted kernel at `η - η₁`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isFiniteMeasure_splitExponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: The split exponential law has finite total mass where its density is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.splitExponentialFamilyMeasure_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: Two split exponential laws differ by an exponential tilt in `(S, T)`; here `c` is the difference of the two log partition functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_kernel_conditional_exponential_family
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.43: conditional exponential families. For a natural exponential family with natural statistic `(T, S)` with values in Euclidean spaces, there is one s-finite kernel `s ↦ ν_s`, free of the parameter, such that at every natural parameter `(η, ζ)` the joint law of `(S, T)` is the law of `S` composed with the kernel `s ↦ exp(η·t - A_s(η)) ν_s(dt)`; that is, the conditional law of `T` given `S = s` has this density for almost every `s`, and it is free of `ζ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMinimalSplitStatistic
declarations.doc: Minimality of a split natural statistic `(T, S)` with real `T`: no nontrivial affine function `a T + b·S` is almost everywhere constant under the base measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUniformlyMostPowerfulUnbiasedTest_conditional_two_sided
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.46, two-sided part: conditional tests with a nuisance parameter. In a minimal exponential family with real natural statistic `T`, nuisance statistic `S`, and natural parameter `(η, ζ)` ranging over an open convex set `U` on which the family is defined and which meets the hyperplane `η = η₀`, a test that rejects for values of `T` outside the conditional interval `[c₁(S), c₂(S)]`, accepts inside it, and has conditional size `α` and conditional first-moment constraint `E[Tφ | S] = α E[T | S]` at one point of the hyperplane, is UMPU of level `α` for `η = η₀` against `η ≠ η₀`. The randomization at the conditional critical points is unrestricted.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUniformlyMostPowerfulUnbiasedTest_conditional_one_sided
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.46, one-sided part: in the setting of `isUniformlyMostPowerfulUnbiasedTest_conditional_two_sided`, a test that rejects for `T > c(S)`, accepts for `T < c(S)`, and has conditional size `α` at one point of the hyperplane `η = η₀` is UMPU of level `α` for `η ≤ η₀` against `η > η₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_compact_convex_game_saddle_point
declarations.doc: A compact convex family of finite risk vectors has a least-favourable probability vector and a risk vector forming a saddle point for weighted risk.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_statistical_game_saddle_point
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.32: the minimax theorem for statistical games with finitely many parameters and actions. There are a randomized rule `δ` and a prior `π` such that `δ` is a Bayes rule for `π` and the risk of `δ` at every parameter is at most its Bayes risk; hence `δ` is minimax, `π` is least favorable, and the minimax and maximin values agree.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_admissible_bayes_risk_le_of_closed_convex
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.37: the complete class theorem for a finite parameter set, in risk-set form. Let `C` be a closed convex set of risk vectors in `ℝ^d`, `d > 0`, bounded below. Every `x ∈ C` is dominated by an admissible point `y ∈ C` (no point of `C` is at most `y` coordinatewise and strictly smaller somewhere) that is Bayes for some prior `w` on the `d` parameter values.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_equivariant_rule_risk_eq_average
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.39: the averaging (Hunt–Stein) construction for a finite group with its uniform Haar measure. In an invariant decision problem with bounded measurable invariant loss, every randomized rule `δ` has an equivariant rule `bar` whose risk at `θ` is the average of the risks of `δ` over the orbit of `θ`. The minimax consequences are not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_analytic_inverse_exponential_family_mean
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.42: the mean parametrization of a regular minimal natural exponential family. For a nonzero σ-finite base measure `ν` on a finite-dimensional real inner product space `E` whose natural parameter space `N` is open and nonempty, the mean map `η ↦ ∫ x d(P η)(x)` is real analytic on `N` and is a bijection of `N` onto the interior `K` of the convex hull of the support of `ν`, with real analytic inverse on `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isAdmissibleRisk_of_blyth
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.58: Blyth's method. Let `Θ` be a convex subset of Euclidean space with nonempty interior and let the rules `δ` in a class `D` have continuous risk functions `R δ`. Suppose there are finite measures `π n` on `Θ` with Bayes rules `δ n`, giving uniformly positive mass to every convex subset with nonempty interior for large `n`, such that the Bayes risk excess `∫ R δ₀ dπ n - ∫ R (δ n) dπ n` of `δ₀` tends to zero. Then `δ₀` is admissible.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMoreInformative
declarations.doc: The experiment `P` is more informative than `Q` (Blackwell): for every finite decision problem with bounded loss, every randomized rule based on `Q` is matched, at every parameter, by a rule based on `P` with risk at most its risk.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMoreInformative_of_isGarbling
declarations.doc: Garbling cannot improve any finite-action bounded-loss decision problem.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMoreInformative_iff_isGarbling
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.62: Blackwell's comparison theorem for a finite parameter set. A family of probability laws `P` is more informative than `Q`, whose sample space is standard Borel, if and only if `Q` is a garbling of `P`. Both families are dominated, by `∑ θ, P θ` and `∑ θ, Q θ`, since the parameter set is finite.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_withDensity_comp
declarations.doc: Pushing forward a measure with a density that factors through `φ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasDensity.integral_eq
declarations.doc: Integrals against a law with a density are density-weighted integrals.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasDensity.integrable
declarations.doc: The density of a finite law is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasDensity.integrable_iff
declarations.doc: For a law with a density, integrability of `g` is integrability of `f · g` for the reference measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasDensity.integral_eq_one
declarations.doc: The density of a probability law has integral one.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDensity_withDensity_ofReal
declarations.doc: A measurable everywhere nonnegative `h` is a density of `ν.withDensity (ofReal ∘ h)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_withDensity_ofReal
declarations.doc: Integrals against a measure with a nonnegative real density `h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_withDensity_ofReal_iff
declarations.doc: Integrability against a measure with a nonnegative real density `h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_map_withDensity_ofReal
declarations.doc: Integrals against the image under `T` of a measure with a nonnegative real density `h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_map_withDensity_ofReal_iff
declarations.doc: Integrability against the image under `T` of a measure with a nonnegative real density.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_rao_blackwell_estimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.7: one parameter-independent Rao–Blackwell rule, with convex risk reduction at each parameter value, so the loss may depend on the parameter. The rule is `s ↦ ∫ δ dK(s)` for the kernel `K` witnessing sufficiency.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_of_isCompleteStatistic_of_isUnbiasedEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.8, uniqueness part: unbiased functions of a complete statistic agree.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_of_isSufficientStatistic_of_isBoundedlyCompleteStatistic
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.9: Basu's theorem. A boundedly complete sufficient statistic `T` is independent of every ancillary statistic `A` under every `P θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_div_information_le_variance
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.10, scalar score-moment form of the information inequality. The derivative-under-integral assumptions give the displayed cross-moment identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMinimumVarianceUnbiasedEstimator_iff_covariance_eq_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.12: the covariance characterization of uniformly minimum variance unbiased estimators. A square-integrable unbiased estimator `W` of `g` is UMVU if and only if it is uncorrelated, under every `P θ`, with every square-integrable unbiased estimator of zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.isSufficientStatistic_iff_exists_factorization
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.1: factorization on a standard Borel sample space and an arbitrary measurable statistic space.

declarations.name: CKSD.convex_naturalParameterSpace
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.4, convexity part: the natural parameter space `{η | ∫ exp ⟪η, t⟫ dν(t) < ∞}` of a measure `ν` on a real inner product space is convex (Hölder's inequality, here through the convexity of `exp`).

declarations.name: CKSD.isCompleteStatistic_withDensity_exp_inner
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.5: completeness of the natural statistic. For the laws `exp ⟪η, T⟫ / Z(η) · ν` with `η` ranging over a nonempty open set `U`, where `Z(η)` is the (finite, positive) normalizer, the statistic `T` is complete.

declarations.name: CKSD.isSufficientStatistic_likelihoodRatio_and_ae_eq_comp
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.2: for a countable family with everywhere positive densities `f θ`, the likelihood ratio `R(x) = (f θ x / f θ₀ x)_θ` is sufficient, and it is minimal: for every sufficient statistic `T` there is a measurable `φ` with `R = φ ∘ T` almost surely under every `P θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_exponential_family_of_monotone_sufficient_statistics
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.6: a Pitman–Koopman–Darmois theorem. Let the laws `P θ` be mutually absolutely continuous with a reference probability `P₀`, and suppose that for infinitely many sample sizes `n` (including `n = 1`) the product densities are nondecreasing functions of a real statistic `Tₙ`. Then the family is a one-parameter exponential family: `dP θ / dP₀ = C(θ) exp (a(θ) T)` for a real statistic `T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.analyticOnNhd_logPartition_and_fderiv_eq_moments
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.4: in the natural exponential family with base measure `ν` on a finite-dimensional real inner product space `E` and statistic the identity, the log partition function `A` is real analytic on the interior of the natural parameter space `N`; at every `η ∈ interior N` its gradient is the mean of the law `P η` at `η` and its Hessian is the covariance of `P η`.

declarations.name: CKSD.RealExponentialFamily
declarations.doc: A regular scalar natural exponential family: laws `exp (η T - A(η)) · base` for natural parameters `η` in an open interval `domain` on which `exp (η T)` is `base`-integrable, with a nonzero σ-finite base measure and a statistic `T` that is not almost everywhere constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.RealExponentialFamily.cumulant
declarations.doc: The log normalizer `A(η) = log ∫ exp (η T) d base` of a scalar exponential family.

declarations.name: CKSD.RealExponentialFamily.law
declarations.doc: The law `exp (η T - A(η)) · base` of the family at a natural parameter `η ∈ domain`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_ne_zero_forall_inner_le_of_notMem_interior
declarations.doc: A point outside the interior of a convex set `C` of a finite-dimensional inner product space is weakly separated from `C`: some `u ≠ 0` has `⟪u, x⟫ ≤ ⟪u, t⟫` for all `x ∈ C`. If `C` has empty interior it lies in a hyperplane `⟪u, ·⟫ = c`, and `±u` works.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_isMaxOn_logLikelihood_iff_mem_interior_convexHull_support
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.69: existence of the maximum likelihood estimator in a regular minimal natural exponential family. For the family with base measure `ν` on `E` and statistic the identity, whose natural parameter space `N` is nonempty, the log likelihood `η ↦ ⟪η, t⟫ - logPartition ν id η` of an observation `t` attains its maximum on `N` if and only if `t` lies in the interior of the convex hull of the support of `ν`. Openness of `N` (regularity) is not needed: the shifted partition function `η ↦ ∫⁻ exp ⟪η, x - t⟫ dν` is lower semicontinuous and coercive on all of `E`, and is infinite off `N`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasFDerivAt_logPartition_and_eq_of_isMaxOn
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.69: in a regular minimal natural exponential family with open natural parameter space `N`, a maximizer `η ∈ N` of the log likelihood `ζ ↦ ⟪ζ, t⟫ - logPartition ν id ζ` solves the likelihood equation `∇ logPartition ν id η = t` (the mean of the law at `η` is `t`), and it is the unique maximizer on `N`.

declarations.name: CKSD.mixtureWeight
declarations.doc: The weights `2^{-(n+1)}` used for countable mixtures.

declarations.name: CKSD.mixtureWeight_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The mixture weights are nonzero.

declarations.name: CKSD.tsum_mixtureWeight
declarations.doc: The mixture weights sum to one.

declarations.name: CKSD.countableMixture
declarations.doc: The countable mixture `∑ 2^{-(n+1)} P (θs n)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.countableMixture_univ
declarations.doc: A countable mixture of probability measures has total mass one.

declarations.name: CKSD.countableMixture_apply_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A measurable set is null for a countable mixture iff it is null for every component.

declarations.name: CKSD.absolutelyContinuous_countableMixture
declarations.doc: Each component of a countable mixture is absolutely continuous with respect to it.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_absolutelyContinuous_countableMixture
declarations.doc: Halmos–Savage lemma, density form: a family of laws with densities with respect to a σ-finite measure is dominated by one of its countable mixtures.

declarations.name: CKSD.countableMixture_map_prodMk_eq_compProd
declarations.doc: A countable mixture of laws sharing a disintegrating kernel is disintegrated by that kernel.

declarations.name: CKSD.countableMixture_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: The density of a countable mixture with respect to a dominating measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_prodMk_eq_compProd_of_withDensity_comp
declarations.doc: If `P = L.withDensity (r ∘ T)` and the joint law of `(T, X)` under `L` is disintegrated by `K`, then the joint law under `P` is also disintegrated by `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eq_withDensity_rnDeriv_comp_of_compProd
declarations.doc: If two finite laws `P ≪ L` have joint laws of `(T, X)` disintegrated by the same kernel, then `P` has a density with respect to `L` that is a function of `T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_factorization_of_isSufficientStatistic
declarations.doc: Sufficiency implies a factorization of the densities (necessity half of GAPS 101.1).

declarations.name: CKSD.isSufficientStatistic_of_factorization
declarations.doc: A factorization of the densities implies sufficiency (sufficiency half of GAPS 101.1). The common kernel is the conditional distribution of the sample given `T` under a dominating countable mixture of the family.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSymmetricStatistic
declarations.doc: A statistic on a finite sample is symmetric under all coordinate permutations.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSymmetricallyComplete
declarations.doc: Completeness restricted to the symmetric sample statistics.

declarations.name: CKSD.isSymmetricallyComplete_of_complete_convex_family
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.13: completeness of permutation-invariant statistics in a convex complete model.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_orderStatistics_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.21: joint order-statistic density for an absolutely continuous law. The proof combines TauCeti's chamber formula `TauCeti.Probability.map_orderStatistics_pi` with TauCeti's product-density identity `TauCeti.pi_withDensity`.

declarations.name: CKSD.betaMeasure_nat_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: On the unit interval the beta density with integer shapes `j + 1` and `n - j` is the polynomial `n! / (j! (n - j - 1)!) u ^ j (1 - u) ^ (n - j - 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_orderStatistic_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.21: the marginal density of the zero-indexed `j`th order statistic. The proof compares distribution functions: TauCeti's `TauCeti.Probability.cdf_map_orderStatistic_pi_eq_regularizedIncompleteBeta` and `TauCeti.Probability.cdf_betaMeasure_eq` give the beta law of `F(X₍ⱼ₎)`, and TauCeti's probability integral transform `MeasureTheory.Measure.cdf_map_eq_volume_restrict` moves the beta density back along `F`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_setOf_sort_eq
declarations.doc: The set of samples with a prescribed sorting permutation is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_sort_eq_and_indepFun_orderStatistics
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.21: for an i.i.d. sample from an atomless law on `ℝ`, the sorting permutation (the ranks) is uniformly distributed on the `n!` permutations and independent of the vector of order statistics. The permutation group carries its discrete σ-algebra. The proof refines the chamber decomposition of TauCeti's `TauCeti.Probability.map_orderStatistics_pi`: ties are null (`TauCeti.Probability.ae_eval_ne_eval_infinitePi`), and coordinate permutations preserve the product law and the order statistics (`TauCeti.orderStatistic_comp_perm`).

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLocationEquivariant
declarations.doc: Location-equivariance of a real estimator on a finite sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.pitmanEstimator
declarations.doc: The Pitman location estimator, using an improper Lebesgue prior.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_eq_lintegral_indicator_mul_lintegral_sub_const
declarations.doc: Orbit decomposition of Lebesgue integrals on `Fin n → ℝ` along the diagonal direction: the integral of `H` is the integral over `z`, weighted by the indicator of `z i₀ ∈ [0, 1]`, of the integral of `H` along the line `u ↦ z - u • 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_ofReal_sq_sub_mul_le
declarations.doc: Minimization of a weighted quadratic: for an integrable weight `w ≥ 0` with integrable first moment and positive mass, the weighted second moment `∫ (c - u)² w(u) du` is minimal at the weighted mean `c = ∫ u w / ∫ w`.

declarations.name: CKSD.pitmanGoodSet
declarations.doc: The samples at which the Pitman estimator is well defined: the normalizing and first-moment integrals exist and the normalizing integral is positive.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_prod_sub
declarations.doc: Joint measurability of the location likelihood `(x, u) ↦ ∏ f (x i - u)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_pitmanEstimator
declarations.doc: The Pitman estimator is measurable for a measurable density.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_pitmanGoodSet
declarations.doc: The Pitman good set is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.sub_const_mem_pitmanGoodSet
declarations.doc: The Pitman good set is invariant under diagonal translations.

declarations.name: CKSD.sub_const_mem_pitmanGoodSet_iff
declarations.doc: Membership in the Pitman good set is invariant under diagonal translations.

declarations.name: CKSD.pitmanEstimator_sub_const
declarations.doc: On the good set, the Pitman estimator is location-equivariant.

declarations.name: CKSD.pitmanEstimator_minimum_equivariant_risk_of_nonneg
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.40 for a nonnegative density: on the good set the Pitman estimator minimizes the equivariant squared-error risk.

declarations.name: CKSD.pitmanEstimator_minimum_equivariant_risk
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.40: the Pitman estimator minimizes equivariant squared-error risk. The normalizing and first-moment integrals are assumed to exist almost surely explicitly.

declarations.name: CKSD.convex_l2OrderInterval
declarations.doc: The nonnegative order interval in real `L²` is convex.

declarations.name: CKSD.isCompact_weak_l2OrderInterval
declarations.doc: Nonnegative order intervals in real `L²` are weakly compact, by reflexivity.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_weak_l2Inner
declarations.doc: Evaluation of an `L²` inner product is weakly continuous in its second argument.

declarations.name: CKSD.l2Const_one_nonneg
declarations.doc: The constant-one element of real `L²` is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.weakDecisionSimplex
declarations.doc: A probability decision rule represented in weak `L²` coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.isCompact_weakDecisionSimplex
declarations.doc: Weak compactness of finite randomized action probabilities.

declarations.name: CKSD.convex_weakDecisionSimplex
declarations.doc: The finite decision simplex is convex in the product weak topology.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_decision_weight
declarations.doc: Each action probability of a decision rule is square integrable under a finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.decisionWeights
declarations.doc: The weak `L²` coordinates of the action probabilities of a randomized decision rule.

declarations.name: CKSD.decisionWeights_mem_weakDecisionSimplex
declarations.doc: A decision rule has weak `L²` action probabilities in the simplex.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_decisionRule_of_weakDecisionSimplex
declarations.doc: Every weak `L²` point of the decision simplex is represented by a Markov kernel.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_rnDeriv_of_le
declarations.doc: The density of a measure bounded by a finite measure is in `L²`, with values in `[0,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.l2DominatedDensity
declarations.doc: The `L²` Radon–Nikodym density of a measure dominated by a finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.risk_eq_sum_l2Inner
declarations.doc: Risk for a finite action space is a finite sum of `L²` pairings with model densities.

declarations.name: CKSD.isCompact_convex_range_risk
declarations.doc: Finite-action risk vectors form a compact convex set when a finite measure dominates all model laws with bounded densities. The compactness uses weak `L²` randomizations.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateGaussianPDFReal_smul_one
declarations.doc: The isotropic Gaussian density `N(θ, v I)` in closed form: its value at `θ` times `exp (-‖x - θ‖² / (2v))`. Stated for TauCeti's `multivariateGaussianPDFReal`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_integration_by_parts
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.64: Gaussian integration by parts (Stein's identity) for `X ~ N(θ, v I)` and a continuously differentiable `g` with `g ∈ L²` and integrable partial derivatives: `E[(Xᵢ - θᵢ) gᵢ(X)] = v E[∂ᵢ gᵢ(X)]`. The proof writes the law as a density against Lebesgue measure (TauCeti's `multivariateGaussian_eq_withDensity`) and applies Mathlib's `integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable`.

declarations.name: CKSD.james_stein_risk_eq_and_lt
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.57: the James–Stein estimator `δ(x) = (1 - (p - 2) / ‖x‖²) x` for `X ~ N(θ, I)` in dimension `p ≥ 3` has risk `p - (p - 2)² E‖X‖⁻²`, strictly smaller than the risk `p` of `X`.

declarations.name: CKSD.scheffe_contrast_supremum
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.60: the simultaneous-contrast supremum underlying Scheffé's method: for `v` in a subspace `S`, `sup_{u ∈ S, u ≠ 0} ⟪u, v⟫² / (s² ‖u‖²) = ‖v‖² / s²` (the supremum is attained at `u = v`; for `v = 0` it is `0`). The Gaussian pivot of the method is not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_intervalWeight_integral_eq_setIntegral_quantile
declarations.doc: **Window tests.** For a probability law `μ` on `ℝ` and levels `0 < a < b < 1`, there is an interval weight `w` (equal to `1` strictly between `c₁ ≤ c₂`, to `γᵢ ∈ [0, 1]` at `cᵢ`, and to `0` elsewhere) with `∫ w ψ dμ = ∫_{(a, b)} ψ (Q v) dv` for every `μ`-integrable `ψ`, where `Q` is the quantile function of `μ`. The endpoints are `cᵢ = Q a, Q b`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_setIntegral_comp_quantile_eq_mul
declarations.doc: **Two-point size selection.** For a probability law `μ` on `ℝ`, a nondecreasing `μ`-integrable `f` that is not `μ`-almost everywhere constant, and `α ∈ (0, 1)`, some window `(a, a + α)` of levels inside `(0, 1)` satisfies `∫_{(a, a + α)} f (Q v) dv = α ∫ f dμ`, where `Q` is the quantile function of `μ`. The proof is the intermediate value theorem: the window integral is continuous in `a`, below `α ∫ f dμ` at `a = 0` and above it at `a = 1 - α`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_mul_exp_add_mul_exp_le_one_iff
declarations.doc: **Two-sided exponential thresholds.** For exponents `β₁ < 0 < β₂` and `c₁ ≤ c₂` there are `A, B > 0` such that `g t = A e^{β₁ t} + B e^{β₂ t}` satisfies `g ≤ 1` on `[c₁, c₂]` and `g ≥ 1` off `(c₁, c₂)`. For `c₁ < c₂` the constants solve `g c₁ = g c₂ = 1`; for `c₁ = c₂ = c` they make `g` tangent to `1` at `c`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_mul_exp_le_of_abs_sub_lt
declarations.doc: On `|η - η₀| < ε`, the derivative factor `|t| e^{η t}` is dominated by the two exponentials at `η₀ ± 2ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_integral_mul_exp
declarations.doc: Differentiation under the integral sign for a bounded multiple of an exponential family integrand, at an interior point of the Laplace-integrability set.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_chord_of_const_mul_exp
declarations.doc: A nonnegative multiple of `t ↦ exp (d t)` lies below its chord over `[c₁, c₂]` and above the extension of that chord outside the open interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUniformlyMostPowerfulUnbiasedTest_of_two_tail_moment_constraints
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.45: the two-tail exponential-family test satisfying the two moment constraints is UMPU. The proof applies `integral_le_of_generalized_neyman_pearson` with the chord of the likelihood ratio through the critical points; for a competing unbiased test, the two moment constraints follow from the vanishing derivative of its power function at `η₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condExp_eq_const_of_isSimilarTest
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.49: similar tests have Neyman structure. If `T` is sufficient and boundedly complete, every test `φ` that is similar of size `α` (its power is `α` at every parameter) has conditional rejection probability `E_θ[φ | T] = α` almost surely for every `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.invariant_iff_factors_through_maximal_invariant
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.55, algebraic part: if `M` is a maximal invariant for a group action (invariant, and `M x = M y` only when `y` is in the orbit of `x`), a function is invariant if and only if it factors through `M`. No measurability of the factor is asserted.

declarations.name: CKSD.mean_scale_ratio_eq_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.56: under the scale group `(x, s) ↦ (c x, c s)`, `c > 0`, acting on pairs of a mean and a positive scale, the ratio `x / s` is a maximal invariant: `x / s = y / t` if and only if `(y, t) = (c x, c s)` for some `c > 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condKernel_comp_withDensity_eq_snd
declarations.doc: A tilt depending only on the conditioning coordinate preserves the conditional kernel.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_markovKernel_of_tilted_joint_laws
declarations.doc: A family obtained by tilting one joint law in its first coordinate has one common Markov randomization for all its second marginal laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_markovKernel_of_tilted_event_probabilities
declarations.doc: Equality of tilted event probabilities suffices to construct a common randomization kernel. This form applies directly to the limiting likelihood-ratio identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_markovKernel_of_map_eq_tilted_joint_laws
declarations.doc: A measurable change of observation coordinates pulls the common randomization back to the original observation laws, without needing an inverse coordinate map.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_kernel_real_apply
declarations.doc: Integrating the real-valued mass of a kernel row gives the mass of the mixture law.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_eq_of_integral_exp_inner_eq
declarations.doc: Multivariate Laplace determinacy: two finite measures on a finite-dimensional real inner product space whose Laplace transforms `u ↦ ∫ exp ⟪u, t⟫` are finite and agree on a ball around the origin are equal.

declarations.name: CKSD.analyticOnNhd_logPartition
declarations.doc: The log partition function `η ↦ log ∫ e^{⟪η, x⟫} dν` of a nonzero measure on a finite-dimensional real inner product space is real analytic on the interior of the natural parameter space.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasFDerivAt_logPartition
declarations.doc: At an interior point `η` of the natural parameter space, the derivative of the log partition function is `⟪m, ·⟫`, where `m = ∫ x dP_η` is the mean of the law `P_η`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fderiv_fderiv_logPartition_apply
declarations.doc: At an interior point `η` of the natural parameter space, the second derivative of the log partition function is the covariance form `(u, v) ↦ Cov_{P_η}(⟪u, X⟫, ⟪v, X⟫)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_exponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: At an interior point `η` of the natural parameter space, `P_η` is a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_id_exponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: At an interior point `η` of the natural parameter space, `P_η` has a first moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_inner_exponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: At an interior point `η` of the natural parameter space, every linear functional `⟪w, ·⟫` is square integrable under `P_η`.

declarations.name: CKSD.analyticOnNhd_mean_exponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: The mean map of a natural exponential family with open natural parameter space `N` is real analytic on `N`.

declarations.name: CKSD.injOn_mean_exponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: The mean map of a minimal natural exponential family with open natural parameter space `N` is injective on `N`.

declarations.name: CKSD.mean_exponentialFamilyMeasure_mem_interior_convexHull_support
declarations.doc: For a minimal natural exponential family with open natural parameter space, the mean of every law of the family lies in the interior of the convex hull of the support of the base measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_hasStrictFDerivAt_mean_exponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: For a minimal natural exponential family with open natural parameter space `N`, the mean map has at every point of `N` a strict derivative that is a continuous linear equivalence.

declarations.name: CKSD.StatisticalModel
declarations.doc: A measurably parametrized statistical model: a Markov kernel from the parameter space to the sample space.

declarations.name: CKSD.StatisticalExperiment
declarations.doc: A statistical experiment: a probability law on the sample space for each parameter, with no measurable structure on the parameter space.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsAncillaryStatistic
declarations.doc: An ancillary statistic: a measurable `T` whose law `(P θ).map T` does not depend on `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMinimumVarianceUnbiasedEstimator
declarations.doc: A uniformly minimum variance unbiased estimator of `g`: `W` is a square-integrable unbiased estimator of `g` and, at every `θ`, its variance is at most that of every square-integrable unbiased estimator of `g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.testPower
declarations.doc: The power `θ ↦ ∫ φ dP θ` of a randomized test `φ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasTestLevel
declarations.doc: `φ` is a test of level `α` for the null hypothesis `H₀`: its power is at most `α` at every `θ ∈ H₀`. This is stated pointwise, so no supremum over a possibly empty `H₀` is taken.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsSimilarTest
declarations.doc: `φ` is similar of size `α` on `B`: its power equals `α` at every `θ ∈ B` (typically the boundary of the null hypothesis).

declarations.name: CKSD.HasConfidenceCoverage
declarations.doc: The confidence set `C` has coverage at least `1 - α`: for every `θ`, the event `θ ∈ C x` is measurable and has `P θ`-probability at least `1 - α`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsAdmissibleRisk
declarations.doc: `δ` is admissible in the class `D` of rules with risk functions `R`: no `δ'` has risk at most that of `δ` everywhere and strictly smaller somewhere.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBayesRule
declarations.doc: `δ` is a Bayes rule for the prior (or weight measure) `π` in the class `D` of rules with risk functions `R`: the risk of `δ` is `π`-integrable, and its integrated risk `∫ R δ dπ` is at most that of every rule whose risk is `π`-integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMinimaxRule
declarations.doc: `δ` is a minimax rule in the class `D` of rules with risk functions `R`: the risk of `δ` is bounded above, and its maximal risk `⨆ θ, R δ θ` is at most that of every rule with risk bounded above. Rules with unbounded risk have infinite maximal risk and are never better.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsGarbling
declarations.doc: The experiment `Q` is a garbling of `P`: one Markov kernel `K` maps every `P θ` to `Q θ`, `Q θ = K ∘ₘ P θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.likelihoodScore
declarations.doc: The score `∂/∂θ log f(θ, x)` of a likelihood `f` in a real parameter `θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fisherInformation
declarations.doc: The Fisher information `I(θ) = ∫ (∂/∂θ log f(θ, x)) ^ 2 dP θ(x)` of a real-parameter model, as the second moment of the score; regularity hypotheses belong to the theorems using it.

declarations.name: CKSD.fisherInformationMatrix
declarations.doc: The information matrix `(∫ sᵢ sⱼ dP)ᵢⱼ` of a vector score `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.naturalParameterSpace
declarations.doc: The natural parameter space `{η | ∫ exp ⟪η, T⟫ dν < ∞}` of the natural exponential family with base measure `ν` and statistic `T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.logPartition
declarations.doc: The log partition function `η ↦ log ∫ exp ⟪η, T⟫ dν` of a natural exponential family.

declarations.name: CKSD.exponentialFamilyMeasure
declarations.doc: The law `exp (⟪η, T⟫ - logPartition ν T η) · ν` of the natural exponential family at `η`; it is a probability measure for `η` in `naturalParameterSpace ν T` when `ν ≠ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsMinimalExponentialFamily
declarations.doc: A minimal natural exponential family: no nonzero linear functional `⟪u, T⟫` of the statistic is `ν`-almost everywhere constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.confidenceSetOfTests
declarations.doc: The confidence set obtained by inverting tests: `θ` is in the set at `x` iff the test of the point null hypothesis `θ` does not reject at `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasConfidenceCoverage_confidenceSetOfTests
declarations.doc: Test/confidence-set duality: inverting level-`α` tests with measurable rejection regions gives confidence sets with coverage at least `1 - α`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fisherInformation_nonneg
declarations.doc: The Fisher information is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsUniformlyMostPowerfulTest.hasTestLevel
declarations.doc: A uniformly most powerful level-`α` test has level `α`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsGarbling.refl
declarations.doc: Every experiment is a garbling of itself, by the identity kernel.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_le_of_generalized_neyman_pearson
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.47: the generalized Neyman–Pearson lemma, sufficiency part, with signed multipliers. If the test `φ` rejects where `f₀ > ∑ kᵢ fᵢ` and accepts where `f₀ < ∑ kᵢ fᵢ`, and a test `ψ` satisfies the side conditions `kᵢ ∫ ψ fᵢ ≤ kᵢ ∫ φ fᵢ`, then `∫ ψ f₀ ≤ ∫ φ f₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_neyman_pearson_test
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.14: the Neyman–Pearson lemma, existence and sufficiency. For laws `P₀`, `P₁` with densities `f₀`, `f₁` with respect to `μ` and a size `α ∈ (0, 1)`, there are `k ≥ 0` and a test `φ` of exact size `α` under `P₀` with `φ = 1` on `{f₁ > k f₀}` and `φ = 0` on `{f₁ < k f₀}`; it is most powerful at level `α`. The almost-everywhere uniqueness of most powerful tests is not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_le_integral_thresholdTest_of_monotone_likelihood_ratio
declarations.doc: The Neyman–Pearson step of the Karlin–Rubin theorem: for laws `Pa`, `Pb` with positive densities whose ratio `fb / fa` is a nondecreasing function of `T`, the threshold test in `T` is at least as powerful under `Pb` as every test whose size under `Pa` does not exceed its own.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_eq_zero_of_integral_eq_zero_of_pos_density
declarations.doc: If `Pa` has an everywhere positive density and `Pb` has a density with respect to the same measure, then a measurable `g : X → [0, 1]` with `∫ g dPa = 0` also has `∫ g dPb = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_thresholdTest_le_of_monotone_likelihood_ratio
declarations.doc: The reversed Neyman–Pearson step of the Karlin–Rubin theorem: if the density ratio `fb / fa` of positive densities is a nondecreasing function of `T`, a threshold test in `T` whose power under `Pb` is at most that of a test `ψ` also has size at most that of `ψ` under `Pa`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_thresholdTest
declarations.doc: The size `P {c < T} + γ P {T = c}` of a threshold test in a real statistic.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_integral_thresholdTest_eq
declarations.doc: Every size `β ∈ (0, 1)` is attained by a threshold test in a real statistic `T`, with the threshold the `(1 - β)`-quantile of the law of `T` (TauCeti's `Measure.quantile`).

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_of_measurable_of_abs_le
declarations.doc: A bounded measurable real function is integrable for a finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_comp_mul_eq_integral_comp_mul_integral_kernel
declarations.doc: If the joint law of `(T, X)` under `μ` is the law of `T` composed with the Markov kernel `K`, then `∫ g(T) φ dμ = ∫ g(T) (∫ φ dK(T)) dμ` for bounded measurable `g` and `φ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_comp_eq_integral_integral
declarations.doc: Integration against a mixture `P ∘ₘ Λ` of a Markov kernel: the integral is the average of the component integrals.

declarations.name: CKSD.comp_map_eq_of_map_prodMk_eq_compProd
declarations.doc: If the joint law of `(T, X)` under `μ` is `μ.map T ⊗ₘ K`, then `μ` is the mixture of `K` over the law of `T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_sub_mul_abs_le_of_convexOn
declarations.doc: A real convex function on the line is bounded below by `L 0 - c |t|` for some constant `c`.

declarations.name: CKSD.setIntegral_preimage_eq_integral_indicator_mul
declarations.doc: A set integral over a preimage `T⁻¹ B` as an integral against the indicator of `B` at `T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_indicator_one_le_one
declarations.doc: The indicator of a set is bounded by one in absolute value.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_indicator_comp_mul_eq
declarations.doc: The bounded-function case of `integral_comp_mul_eq_integral_comp_mul_integral_kernel` with the indicator of a measurable set of statistic values.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_integral_kernel_eq_of_isBoundedlyCompleteStatistic
declarations.doc: For a boundedly complete sufficient statistic `T` with disintegrating kernel `K`, a bounded measurable `φ` whose expectation is `α` under every parameter satisfies `∫ φ dK(T) = α` almost surely under every parameter.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_zero_of_setIntegral_pi_eq_zero
declarations.doc: An integrable function on a finite product of measurable spaces whose integrals over all measurable boxes `∏ᵢ Aᵢ` vanish is zero almost everywhere.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_pi_comp_equiv_of_symmetric
declarations.doc: A permutation-invariant function has the same integral under the product measure `Measure.pi μ` and under its permuted version `Measure.pi (fun j ↦ μ (σ j))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_pi_eq_integral_integral_insertNth
declarations.doc: Fubini at the coordinate `j`: integrate the `j`-th coordinate last.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_zero_pi_of_isCompleteStatistic_of_convex
declarations.doc: **Completeness of symmetric statistics.** In a convex complete set `C` of probability laws, a measurable symmetric function of a sample of size `n` that has mean zero under every `Pⁿ`, `P ∈ C`, vanishes `Pⁿ`-almost everywhere for every `P ∈ C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUniformlyMostPowerfulTest_of_monotone_likelihood_ratio
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.15: the Karlin–Rubin theorem. In a family with everywhere positive densities whose likelihood ratios `f b / f a` (`a < b`) are nondecreasing functions of `T`, the threshold test `thresholdTest T c γ` of size `α` at `θ₀` is uniformly most powerful of level `α` for `θ ≤ θ₀` against `θ > θ₀`. Positivity of the densities avoids the convention for ratios with zero denominator. The monotonicity of the power function is not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_standardize_pi_gaussianReal
declarations.doc: Standardization of a Gaussian sample: the coordinates `(xᵢ - m) / √v` of an i.i.d. `N(m, v)` sample form a standard Gaussian vector in Euclidean space.

declarations.name: CKSD.stdGaussian_map_inner_of_norm_eq_one
declarations.doc: A unit linear functional of a standard Gaussian vector is standard Gaussian, from Mathlib's `variance_dual_stdGaussian` and `integral_strongDual_stdGaussian`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_sample_mean_residual_laws
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.17: chi-squared residual law and independence from the sample mean. The proof projects the standardized sample onto the constants and their orthogonal complement, using TauCeti's `HasLaw.iIndepFun_orthogonalProjectionOnto_stdGaussian`, `HasLaw.norm_sq_orthogonalProjectionOnto_stdGaussian`, and `TauCeti.Probability.hasLaw_studentT_of_gaussian_chiSquared`.

declarations.name: CKSD.intervalTest
declarations.doc: The two-sided interval test in a real statistic value `T`: reject when `c₁ < T < c₂`, reject with probability `γ₁` at `T = c₁` and `γ₂` at `T = c₂`, and accept otherwise.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_ump_interval_test
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.50: in a regular scalar natural exponential family, for `η₁ < η₂` and `α ∈ (0, 1)` there is an interval test in the natural statistic with size exactly `α` at `η₁` and at `η₂`; it is uniformly most powerful of level `α` for `η ≤ η₁ or η ≥ η₂` against `η₁ < η < η₂`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_one_sided_test_risk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.53: one-sided tests form an essentially complete class for two-decision problems in a family with monotone likelihood ratio. The densities are everywhere positive (so the laws are mutually absolutely continuous), the loss `L θ` of rejecting (`true`) minus accepting (`false`) is positive below `θ₀` and negative above it, and the threshold may be infinite. For every test `φ` there is a threshold test in `T` whose risk `L θ false + (L θ true - L θ false) · power` is at most that of `φ` at every `θ`. The threshold test matches the size of `φ` at `θ₀` (`exists_integral_thresholdTest_eq`); the two Neyman–Pearson steps of the Karlin–Rubin argument then compare powers below and above `θ₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.most_powerful_of_mixture_null
declarations.doc: GAPS 101.54: least favorable distributions, sufficiency part. Let `Λ` be a prior on the parameter space of a composite null hypothesis `P`. If `φ` has level `α` at every null parameter and is most powerful at level `α` for the simple null `P ∘ₘ Λ` against the alternative `Q`, then `φ` is most powerful at level `α` for the composite null against `Q`. The least-favorability of `Λ` and the concentration of `Λ` on the set where the power equals `α` are not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalRisk
declarations.doc: Empirical risk on a finite sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsEmpiricalRiskMinimizer
declarations.doc: An empirical risk minimizer; existence is a separate assertion.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginLoss
declarations.doc: Ramp margin loss at a positive margin scale.

declarations.name: CKSD.exponentialLoss
declarations.doc: Exponential loss of a signed binary margin.

declarations.name: CKSD.boostingScore
declarations.doc: AdaBoost's accumulated score from a sequence of weak binary predictors.

declarations.name: CKSD.boostingWeight
declarations.doc: AdaBoost's normalized observation weights before round `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.boostingWeightedError
declarations.doc: Weighted misclassification error of a weak predictor.

declarations.name: CKSD.relu
declarations.doc: Scalar ReLU activation `x ↦ max 0 x` (the scalar form of TauCeti's vector-valued `reluActivation`).

declarations.name: CKSD.twoLayerPredictor
declarations.doc: A one-hidden-layer real predictor `x ↦ ∑ⱼ aⱼ σ(⟪wⱼ, x⟫ + bⱼ)` with `N` hidden units on a real inner product space.

declarations.name: CKSD.kmeansRisk
declarations.doc: Population `k`-means distortion `∫ minⱼ d(x, cⱼ)² dP` for an ordered list of `k` centers. The minimum is the real `sInf` of a finite set; for `k = 0` it is `sInf ∅ = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasQuerySensitivity
declarations.doc: A query has sensitivity at most `c` for the supplied neighboring-data relation.

declarations.name: CKSD.aboveThresholdTime
declarations.doc: AboveThreshold's first crossing, for fixed threshold noise and a noise stream.

declarations.name: CKSD.training_error_le_exponential_loss
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.24, exponential loss dominates empirical training error, including zero margins.

declarations.name: CKSD.sub_le_of_threshold_add_le_add
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.74, deterministic accuracy on the simultaneous bounded-noise event, crossing case: if the threshold noise `z` and the query noise are at most `α / 2` in absolute value, a noisy query value at or above the noisy threshold `T + z` has true value at least `T - α`.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_add_of_add_lt_threshold_add
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.74, deterministic accuracy on the simultaneous bounded-noise event, non-crossing case: if the threshold noise `z` and the query noise are at most `α / 2` in absolute value, a noisy query value below the noisy threshold `T + z` has true value at most `T + α`.

declarations.name: CKSD.relu_nonneg
declarations.doc: The ReLU activation is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.relu_of_nonneg
declarations.doc: ReLU is the identity on the nonnegative half-line.

declarations.name: CKSD.barronFourierMoment
declarations.doc: First absolute Fourier moment in Mathlib's `exp(-2πi⟨x,ω⟩)` normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.logisticNetwork
declarations.doc: One-hidden-layer logistic network with a separate output bias.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_logisticNetwork_sq_error_le_barron_moment
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.28: Barron's `N⁻¹/²` logistic approximation rate on the unit ball. The squared-error form uses a universal constant and the first absolute Fourier moment. The target is continuous on the whole space, which fixes its representative on singular laws. (For `d = 0` the space is a point and constants are exact.)

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_norm_sub_integral_sq_le
declarations.doc: Centering a square-integrable Hilbert-space function reduces its second moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_feature_average_sq_error_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.28, Hilbert-space sampling step: an integral feature mean admits a finite average with squared error bounded by its second moment divided by the number of features.

declarations.name: CKSD.uniformGridSlope
declarations.doc: Slope between consecutive points of the uniform grid on `[0,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.reluLinearInterpolant
declarations.doc: Uniform-grid piecewise linear interpolant in its affine-plus-ReLU representation.

declarations.name: CKSD.sub_chord_le_of_deriv2_ge
declarations.doc: One-sided chord bound: if `f` is `C²` with `f'' ≥ -B` on `[u, v]`, then on `[u, v]` the function exceeds its chord by at most `B (x - u)(v - x) / 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_chord_sub_le
declarations.doc: Linear interpolation error on an interval `[u, v]` for a `C²` function with `|f''| ≤ B` there: `|chord(x) - f(x)| ≤ B (v - u)² / 8`.

declarations.name: CKSD.affine_add_sum_hinge_eq
declarations.doc: Telescoping form of the ReLU interpolant's affine pieces: the affine term plus the first `j` hinge corrections is the line through `(j/N, f(j/N))` with slope `s_j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.reluLinearInterpolant_eq_of_mem
declarations.doc: On the grid cell `[j/N, (j+1)/N]`, `j < N`, the ReLU interpolant is the chord of `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_reluLinearInterpolant_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.36, one-dimensional `C²` scope: a fixed-grid ReLU network has uniform `N⁻²` error. The architecture has `N-1` hinges plus an affine term. General Sobolev spaces, dimensions, and fractional target smoothness require additional approximation theory.

declarations.name: CKSD.barronFourierMoment_nonneg
declarations.doc: Fourier moment integrands are nonnegative, independently of integrability.

declarations.name: CKSD.reluLinearInterpolant_zero
declarations.doc: The ReLU interpolant agrees with the target at the left endpoint of the grid.

declarations.name: CKSD.SeededBanditPolicy
declarations.doc: A seeded bandit policy: the arm at time `t` from the history of length `t` and a seed.

declarations.name: CKSD.historyPlayCount
declarations.doc: Number of plays of arm `k` in a finite history.

declarations.name: CKSD.historyRewardSum
declarations.doc: Total reward collected from arm `k` in a finite history.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditHistory
declarations.doc: The history of the first `t` arms and rewards of a policy run on a reward table.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditArm
declarations.doc: The arm played at time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditReward
declarations.doc: The reward received at time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.rewardTableLaw
declarations.doc: Law of the reward table: independent entries, with `R (k, j)` of law `ν k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armMean
declarations.doc: Mean reward of an arm.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditRegret
declarations.doc: Regret after `n` plays: `n` times the optimal mean minus the expected total reward.

declarations.name: CKSD.SeededBanditPolicy.IsMeasurable
declarations.doc: Measurability of a seeded policy in the history and the seed.

declarations.name: CKSD.expFamilyLogPartition
declarations.doc: Log-partition function of the natural exponential family generated by `λ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.expFamilyLaw
declarations.doc: The member `exp(θx - b(θ)) λ(dx)` of the natural exponential family generated by `λ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lai_robbins_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.49: the Lai–Robbins lower bound for exponential-family bandits. The base measure `λ` is σ-finite and not concentrated at one point, the natural parameters range over the open interval `(l, r)` on which `exp(θx)` is `λ`-integrable, and the policy is uniformly good: its regret is `o(n^α)` for every `α > 0` at every configuration. An optimal arm has the largest natural parameter `θ⋆`, and `liminf regret(n) / log n` is at least the Lai–Robbins sum, stated as eventual domination of every smaller constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditFirstArgmax
declarations.doc: The first maximizing coordinate of a finite real vector (the arm `0` is never needed).

declarations.name: CKSD.thompsonPolicy
declarations.doc: Thompson sampling with independent uniform priors for Bernoulli rewards: at time `t` each arm draws from its Beta posterior `Beta(1 + successes, 1 + failures)` by inverse transform of the uniform seed `u (t, k)`, and the largest draw is played (ties to the smallest index).

declarations.name: CKSD.thompsonSeedLaw
declarations.doc: Law of the Thompson seeds: independent uniform variables on `[0,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_thompson_regret_div_log
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.51, Thompson sampling: for Bernoulli arms with means in `(0,1)` and a unique optimal arm, Thompson sampling with uniform priors attains the Lai–Robbins constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.ucb1Policy
declarations.doc: The UCB1 policy: each arm once, then a maximizer of `x̄ⱼ + √(2 log t / nⱼ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_bernoulli_banditRegret_ge
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.62, lower bound: for `K ≥ 2` and `n > K / (4 log(4/3))`, every seeded (hence every randomized) strategy has regret at least `(√2 - 1)√(nK)/√(32 log(4/3))` on some instance with independent Bernoulli rewards.

declarations.name: CKSD.historyPlayCount_snoc
declarations.doc: Appending a pair to a history increases the count of its arm by one.

declarations.name: CKSD.historyRewardSum_snoc
declarations.doc: Appending a pair to a history adds its reward to the total of its arm.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditArmProcess
declarations.doc: The arm process of a seeded policy on a reward table, as a function of the table.

declarations.name: CKSD.historyPlayCount_banditHistory
declarations.doc: The count of an arm in the history equals the number of its plays.

declarations.name: CKSD.historyRewardSum_banditHistory
declarations.doc: The reward total of an arm in the history is the sum of its first table entries.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditHistory_update
declarations.doc: Changing a table entry `(k, j)` that has not been reached leaves the history unchanged.

declarations.name: CKSD.SeededBanditPolicy.IsMeasurableAt
declarations.doc: A seeded policy that is measurable in the history for a fixed seed.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_historyPlayCount
declarations.doc: The count of an arm is a measurable function of the history.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_historyRewardSum
declarations.doc: The reward total of an arm is a measurable function of the history.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_banditHistory
declarations.doc: The history is a measurable function of the reward table.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_banditArmProcess
declarations.doc: The arm process of a measurable policy is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_banditFirstArgmax
declarations.doc: The first maximizing coordinate is a maximizer.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_banditFirstArgmax
declarations.doc: The first maximizing coordinate is a measurable function of the vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.ucb1Policy_isMeasurableAt
declarations.doc: The UCB1 policy is measurable in the history.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_eval_mul_eq_of_update_invariant
declarations.doc: Under a product law on `ι → ℝ`, a coordinate is independent of every measurable function that does not depend on that coordinate, so their product integrates to the product of the integrals. The independence comes from Mathlib's `iIndepFun_infinitePi` and `indep_iSup_of_disjoint`.

declarations.name: CKSD.rewardTableLaw_map_eval
declarations.doc: The law of a table entry is the law of its arm.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_rewardTableLaw
declarations.doc: The table law is a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_eval_rewardTableLaw
declarations.doc: The mean of a table entry is the mean of its arm.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eval_mem_Icc_rewardTableLaw
declarations.doc: Table entries lie in `[0,1]` almost surely when the reward laws do.

declarations.name: CKSD.armMean_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: The mean of a law on `[0,1]` lies in `[0,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditPlayIndicator
declarations.doc: The indicator that at time `t` the policy plays arm `k` for the `(j+1)`-st time.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditPlayIndicator_update
declarations.doc: Whether arm `k` is played for the `(j+1)`-st time at time `t` does not depend on the table entry `(k, j)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_banditPlayIndicator
declarations.doc: The play indicator is measurable in the table.

declarations.name: CKSD.historyPlayCount_le
declarations.doc: The count of an arm in a history of length `t` is at most `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eq_sum_sum_mul_banditPlayIndicator
declarations.doc: A function of the arm played and of its count, written with play indicators.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_banditReward_eq
declarations.doc: The expected reward at time `t` is the expected mean of the arm played (Wald's identity in the reward-table model): the play of arm `k` for the `(j+1)`-st time is decided before the entry `(k, j)` is revealed, hence independently of it.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_integral_armPlayCount_eq
declarations.doc: The expected play counts add up to the number of rounds.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditRegret_dirac_eq
declarations.doc: The regret of a policy with a fixed seed is the gap-weighted sum of the expected play counts.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_gap_mul_le_sqrt
declarations.doc: Splitting the arms at the gap `√(K L / n)` bounds the gap-weighted play counts by `14 √(K n L)`, given the per-arm bound `8 L / Δ² + 3` on the counts of arms with positive gap.

declarations.name: CKSD.ucb1Policy_of_le
declarations.doc: For `t ≥ K` the UCB1 policy plays the first maximizer of the UCB1 index.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_ucb1_banditRegret_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.62, upper bound: UCB1 has regret at most `C √(K n log n)` for all `n ≥ max(K, 2)` and all reward laws on `[0,1]`, with a universal constant `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.selfNormalizedDesign
declarations.doc: The regularized design matrix `V₀ + ∑_{1 ≤ i ≤ t} Xᵢ Xᵢᵀ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_exists_selfNormalized_gt_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.63, self-normalized bound (Abbasi-Yadkori–Pál–Szepesvári): with probability at least `1 - δ`, simultaneously for all `t ≥ 1`, `‖∑ᵢ Xᵢ εᵢ‖²_{Vₜ⁻¹} ≤ 2σ² log(det(Vₜ)^{1/2} det(V₀)^{-1/2} / δ)`. The noise `εₜ` is `𝓕ₜ`-measurable and conditionally `σ`-sub-Gaussian given `𝓕ₜ₋₁`, and `Xₜ` is `𝓕ₜ₋₁`-measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_linUCB_regret_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.63, LinUCB regret for a finite decision set. Actions `xₜ ∈ 𝒟` are `𝓕ₜ`-measurable and maximize `⟨μ̂ₜ, x⟩ + √βₜ ‖x‖_{Σₜ⁻¹}` for the ridge estimate `μ̂ₜ` with `Σₜ = λ I + ∑_{τ<t} x_τ x_τᵀ`, `λ = σ²/W²`; observations are `⟨μ⋆, xₜ⟩ + ηₜ` with `ηₜ` `𝓕ₜ₊₁`-measurable and conditionally `σ`-sub-Gaussian given `𝓕ₜ`. With probability at least `1 - δ`, for all `T`, the regret is at most `c max(σ, BW) √T (d log(1 + T B² W² / (d σ²)) + log(4/δ))`. The scale `max(σ, BW)` accounts for initial leverage when `λ = σ²/W²`. The minimax lower bound `d√T/2500` is not formalized here.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalRademacherComplexityOfSet
declarations.doc: Empirical Rademacher complexity of a class `F` of real functions at the sample `x`: the average over the `2ⁿ` sign vectors `σ` of `sup_{f ∈ F} n⁻¹ ∑ᵢ σᵢ f(xᵢ)`, with `true` coding `+1`. The supremum is the real `sSup` (so it is `0` for an empty class or a class whose signed averages are unbounded above).

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalRademacherComplexity
declarations.doc: Empirical Rademacher complexity of the indexed class `{f h | h ∈ H}` at the sample `x`; it is `empiricalRademacherComplexityOfSet` of the range of `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalRademacherComplexity_eq
declarations.doc: The empirical Rademacher complexity of an indexed class as an average of suprema over the index set.

declarations.name: CKSD.classificationRisk
declarations.doc: Binary classification risk `𝔼[g(X) ≠ Y]` of the classifier `g` (with `true` coding the label `1`), for the feature law `P` and the regression function `η(x) = P(Y = 1 | X = x)`: `∫ (1 - η) 1{g = 1} + η 1{g = 0} dP`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hedgeWeight
declarations.doc: Exponential-weights (Hedge) probabilities after `t` rounds with learning rate `η`: `pₜ(i) ∝ exp(-η ∑_{s<t} ℓₛ(i))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsDifferentiallyPrivate
declarations.doc: `(ε, δ)`-differential privacy of a kernel `M` for the neighbouring relation `R`: `M d A ≤ e^ε M d' A + δ` for all neighbouring `d, d'` and measurable events `A`. Local privacy is the case of the total relation.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount
declarations.doc: Number of plays of arm `i` before time `t` by the arm process `A`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armSampleAverage
declarations.doc: Average `n⁻¹ ∑_{j<n} R i j` of the first `n` rewards of arm `i` in the reward table `R` (equal to `0` for `n = 0`).

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_beliefPropagation_exact_on_tree
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.23: positive tree models have BP fixed points giving the exact node and edge marginals. The leaf-to-root implementation and the reconstruction theorem for arbitrary boundary beliefs are separate parts of the catalogue entry.

declarations.name: CKSD.beliefPropagation_tree_unique_up_to_scale
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.23: each directed-edge message in a positive tree model is unique up to positive scale. The proof is by strong induction on the size of the branch behind the sending vertex.

declarations.name: CKSD.chordal_of_junctionTree
declarations.doc: **Graphs with junction trees are chordal.** If the cliques `c i` enumerate the maximal cliques of `G` and a tree `T` on them has the running-intersection property, then every cycle of `G` of length at least four has a chord.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_junctionTree_of_chordal
declarations.doc: **Chordal graphs have junction trees.** A finite graph in which every cycle of length at least four has a chord admits an injective enumeration `c` of its maximal cliques and a tree `T` on the indices in which every clique on the path between two cliques contains their intersection.

declarations.name: CKSD.coordSum
declarations.doc: Sum of a function of configurations over the coordinates in `D`, the coordinates outside `D` being frozen at their values in `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.coordSum_empty
declarations.doc: Summing over no coordinates is evaluation.

declarations.name: CKSD.coordSum_congr
declarations.doc: `coordSum D f x` only sees values of `f` at configurations agreeing with `x` off `D`.

declarations.name: CKSD.coordSum_union
declarations.doc: Summing over disjoint coordinate sets in two stages (Fubini for finite sums).

declarations.name: CKSD.coordSum_singleton
declarations.doc: Summing over one coordinate.

declarations.name: CKSD.dependsOn_coordSum
declarations.doc: If `f` depends only on the coordinates in `s`, then its partial sum over `D` depends only on the coordinates in `s \ D`.

declarations.name: CKSD.coordSum_mul_left
declarations.doc: A factor that does not depend on the coordinates in `D` comes out of `coordSum D` on the left.

declarations.name: CKSD.coordSum_mul_right
declarations.doc: A factor that does not depend on the coordinates in `D` comes out of `coordSum D` on the right.

declarations.name: CKSD.coordSum_biUnion_prod
declarations.doc: Summing a product of factors over a disjoint union of coordinate blocks, each factor not depending on the blocks of the other factors, factorizes into the product of the blockwise sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_flip_ne
declarations.doc: Flipping one label is an involution, so a label-blind guess at that coordinate is wrong for exactly half of all labellings.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_labelling_le_average_error
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.7, finite-support no-free-lunch bound; taking arbitrarily large `m` gives the infinite-feature-space assertion. For any learning rule trained on `n` labelled points drawn uniformly from `m` features, some labelling makes its expected error (averaged over samples and test points) at least `(1 - n / m) / 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_classificationLoss
declarations.doc: Binary conditional classification loss is integrable under a probability law.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_decide_half_le
declarations.doc: The plug-in rule `x ↦ (1/2 ≤ a x)` of a measurable function is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.classificationRisk_sub_bayes_risk_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.8: the exact excess Bayes classification risk identity. For a regression function `η` with values in `[0,1]` and any measurable classifier `g`, the excess risk of `g` over the Bayes classifier `g⋆(x) = (1/2 ≤ η x)` is `∫_{g ≠ g⋆} |2η - 1| dP`.

declarations.name: CKSD.classificationRisk_plugin_sub_bayes_risk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.8: the plugin classification risk bound. The plug-in classifier `x ↦ (1/2 ≤ a x)` built from an integrable estimate `a` of the regression function `η` has excess risk at most `2 ∫ |a - η| dP`.

declarations.name: CKSD.surrogate_minimizer_sign_of_convex
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.11, pointwise classification calibration of a convex surrogate. If `φ` is convex and differentiable at `0` with `φ'(0) > 0`, then for `η ∈ [0,1]`, `η ≠ 1/2`, every minimizer `u` of the conditional surrogate risk `η φ(-u) + (1 - η) φ(u)` has the sign of `η - 1/2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_uniform_empirical_risk_deviation_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.1, finite-class uniform risk concentration (a scoped PAC upper bound): for a finite class of `[0,1]`-valued functions and an i.i.d. sample of size `n`, the probability that some empirical mean deviates from its expectation by more than `ε` is at most `2 |H| exp(-2 n ε²)`. (For `n = 0` the bound is at least `2 |H|`, and trivial.)

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sSup_range_sub_sSup_range_le
declarations.doc: Suprema over a finite nonempty index of pointwise `c`-close families are `c`-close.

declarations.name: CKSD.sSup_range_add_le
declarations.doc: The supremum over a finite nonempty index of a sum is at most the sum of the suprema.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalRademacherComplexity_neg
declarations.doc: The empirical Rademacher complexity is unchanged when the class is negated.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurePreserving_ghostSwap
declarations.doc: Measure preservation of the coordinatewise swap of a ghost sample: for a sign pattern `σ`, coordinates with `σ i = false` are exchanged between the two samples.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sSup_range_le
declarations.doc: A supremum over a finite nonempty index of values bounded by `C` is bounded by `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_of_abs_le
declarations.doc: A measurable function bounded in absolute value is integrable for a finite measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_sum_mul_div_le
declarations.doc: An average `(∑ᵢ aᵢ uᵢ)/n` with `|aᵢ| ≤ 1` and `|uᵢ| ≤ C`, `C ≥ 0`, lies in `[-C,C]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_empiricalRademacherComplexity
declarations.doc: Measurability of the empirical Rademacher complexity of a measurable finite class.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_empiricalRademacherComplexity_le
declarations.doc: The empirical Rademacher complexity of a nonempty finite class bounded by `C` is bounded by `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sSup_sub_le_two_mul_rademacher
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.2, symmetrization: the expected supremum of the centered empirical means of a finite class with values in `[-1,1]` is at most twice the expected empirical Rademacher complexity.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_integral_add_le_sSup_le
declarations.doc: McDiarmid tail for the supremum of the centered empirical means of a finite class whose members oscillate by at most `1`: the supremum exceeds its mean by `t ≥ 0` with probability at most `exp(-2 n t²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_two_mul_rademacher_add_lt_sSup_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.2, high-probability Rademacher bound for a finite class of `[0,1]`-valued functions: with probability at least `1 - δ`, the uniform deviation `sup_h |n⁻¹ ∑ᵢ f h (xᵢ) - ∫ f h dP|` is at most `2 𝔼 R̂ₙ + √(log(2/δ) / (2n))`, where `𝔼 R̂ₙ` is the expected empirical Rademacher complexity. The expectation bound of GAPS 107.2 is `integral_sSup_sub_le_two_mul_rademacher`.

declarations.name: CKSD.conformalRank
declarations.doc: Strict rank of a coordinate: the number of coordinates with a strictly smaller value.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_card_conformalRank_lt
declarations.doc: At least `k` coordinates have strict rank below `k`, whatever the ties.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_conformalRank_lt_of_injective
declarations.doc: For distinct values exactly `k` coordinates have strict rank below `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.conformalRank_comp_swap
declarations.doc: Swapping two coordinates transports the strict rank.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_conformalRank_cast
declarations.doc: The strict rank is a measurable function of the vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_card_conformalRank_lt
declarations.doc: The number of coordinates of strict rank below `k` is a measurable function of the vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.conformalEvent
declarations.doc: The conformal event `{ω | #{i < n : Sᵢ(ω) < Sₙ(ω)} < k}` for the last of `n + 1` scores `S₀, …, Sₙ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.natCast_add_one_mul_measureReal_conformalEvent
declarations.doc: Under exchangeability of the scores, `(n + 1)` times the probability of the conformal event is the expected number of coordinates of strict rank below `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.div_le_measureReal_conformalEvent
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.6, the exchangeable-rank coverage assertion, with ties allowed: for exchangeable scores `S₀, …, Sₙ` and `k ≤ n + 1`, the last score has fewer than `k` strictly smaller scores among the others with probability at least `k / (n + 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_conformalEvent_eq_div
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.6, the exchangeable-rank coverage assertion, without ties: if the scores are almost surely distinct, the coverage probability is exactly `k / (n + 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sSup_add_sSup_le_of_lipschitz
declarations.doc: One-coordinate contraction step: for an `L`-Lipschitz `φ` and `c ≥ 0`, `sup(a + cφ(u)) + sup(a - cφ(u)) ≤ sup(a + cLu) + sup(a - cLu)` over a finite index.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_sSup_rademacher_comp_le
declarations.doc: Ledoux–Talagrand contraction for a finite class: composing the coordinates with an `L`-Lipschitz function multiplies the summed Rademacher suprema by at most `L`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_finiteDiracSum
declarations.doc: Integrals against a finite weighted sum of Dirac masses on `Fin K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_exp_le
declarations.doc: Hoeffding's lemma for a finite probability vector and values in `[0,1]`, from Mathlib's `hasSubgaussianMGF_of_mem_Icc`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hedge_regret_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.5: the exponential-weights regret bound, for any positive learning rate. For losses `ℓₜ(i) ∈ [0,1]` on `K ≥ 1` experts, the Hedge forecaster with learning rate `η > 0` has cumulative expected loss at most that of any fixed expert `i` plus `log K / η + η T / 8`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_sum_mul_sub_le_of_exponential_weights
declarations.doc: Deterministic exponential-weights bound with nonnegative estimated losses `ℓ̂`: if `p t i ∝ exp(-η ∑_{s<t} ℓ̂ s i)`, then `∑_{t<T} ∑ᵢ p t i ℓ̂ t i - ∑_{t<T} ℓ̂ t i⋆ ≤ log K / η + (η/2) ∑_{t<T} ∑ᵢ p t i ℓ̂ t i²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exponentialWeights_succ
declarations.doc: Multiplicative update form of exponential weights: `p (t+1) i = p t i exp(-η ℓ̂ t i) / ∑ⱼ p t j exp(-η ℓ̂ t j)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_integral_loss_le
declarations.doc: Exchange step for replace-one stable algorithms: the expected risk of the output is at most the expected loss on the `i`-th training point plus the stability constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_sub_sum_div_sub_le_of_stable
declarations.doc: Bounded differences of the generalization defect `∫ ℓ(x, ·) dP - n⁻¹ ∑ⱼ ℓ(x, xⱼ)` of a `β`-uniformly stable algorithm with losses in `[0, M]`: changing one training point changes it by at most `2β + M / n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_sum_div_add_lt_integral_le_of_stable
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.12: generalization of a measurable uniformly stable algorithm.
