If replacing one training point changes every loss by at most `β` and losses lie in `[0, M]`, then with probability at least `1 - δ` the risk is at most the empirical risk plus `β + (2 n β + M) √(log(1/δ) / (2n))` (Bousquet–Elisseeff).

declarations.name: CKSD.PairwiseGraphicalModel
declarations.doc: A positive pairwise model on a finite graph with a common finite state alphabet.

declarations.name: CKSD.PairwiseGraphicalModel.orderedEdges
declarations.doc: The oriented edge set with the smaller vertex listed first.

declarations.name: CKSD.PairwiseGraphicalModel.weight
declarations.doc: Unnormalized configuration weight.

declarations.name: CKSD.PairwiseGraphicalModel.partitionFunction
declarations.doc: Partition function of a finite pairwise model.

declarations.name: CKSD.PairwiseGraphicalModel.mass
declarations.doc: Normalized configuration mass.

declarations.name: CKSD.LocalBeliefTables
declarations.doc: Arrays of node and oriented-edge beliefs. Nonedges are unused coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLocallyConsistentBelief
declarations.doc: The local polytope of a finite pairwise model.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsInteriorLocalBelief
declarations.doc: Strict positivity in the coordinates constrained by the local polytope.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLocalBeliefDirection
declarations.doc: Homogeneous local-polytope constraints describing its tangent directions.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteTableEntropy
declarations.doc: Shannon entropy `∑ᵢ -pᵢ log pᵢ` of a real table, with `0 log 0 = 0` (Mathlib's `Real.negMulLog`).

declarations.name: CKSD.betheEntropy
declarations.doc: Bethe entropy of local node and edge tables.

declarations.name: CKSD.betheFreeEnergy
declarations.doc: Bethe free energy, including the vertex and edge potential terms.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBetheStationary
declarations.doc: Stationarity of the Bethe energy along every direction preserving the local constraints.

declarations.name: CKSD.incomingMessageProduct
declarations.doc: Product of incoming messages at `i`, omitting the possible recipient `j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBeliefPropagationFixedPoint
declarations.doc: Belief-propagation fixed-point equations, allowing one positive scale for each message.

declarations.name: CKSD.beliefPropagationNode
declarations.doc: Normalized node belief induced by incoming messages.

declarations.name: CKSD.beliefPropagationEdge
declarations.doc: Normalized edge belief induced by messages entering its endpoints.

declarations.name: CKSD.isBetheStationary_iff_exists_beliefPropagationFixedPoint
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.19: Bethe stationary points in the positive local polytope are exactly BP beliefs.

declarations.name: CKSD.PairwiseGraphicalModel.weight_pos
declarations.doc: Every finite positive graphical-model configuration has positive weight.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsTriangulatedGraph
declarations.doc: A graph is triangulated: every cycle of length at least four has a chord, an edge of the graph between two of its vertices that is not an edge of the cycle.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsJunctionTree
declarations.doc: `T` on the enumeration `c` of cliques is a junction tree of `G`: `c` lists every maximal clique exactly once, `T` is a tree, and every clique on the path between two cliques contains their intersection. Maximal cliques are the finite vertex sets that are maximal (Mathlib's `Maximal`) among the cliques.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasJunctionTree
declarations.doc: A graph has a junction tree.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasJunctionTree_iff_isTriangulated
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.27: a finite graph has a junction tree if and only if it is triangulated.

declarations.name: CKSD.jointMarginal
declarations.doc: Marginal table of a joint configuration mass on a finite set of vertices.

declarations.name: CKSD.tableMarginal
declarations.doc: Marginal of a table on `C` to the subset `D`, given by its membership proof.

declarations.name: CKSD.junctionTreeProduct
declarations.doc: Junction-tree product formula: clique tables divided by separator tables, one separator factor per tree edge, the separator table being the marginal of the lower-indexed clique.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_jointMarginal
declarations.doc: A marginal table has the total mass of the joint table.

declarations.name: CKSD.tableMarginal_jointMarginal
declarations.doc: Marginalizing the marginal on `C` to `D ⊆ C` gives the marginal on `D`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_eq_one_and_tableMarginal_eq_of_jointMarginal
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.27, necessity in the marginal problem: the clique marginals of a joint probability table are normalized and agree on separators. No junction-tree hypothesis is needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.junctionTreeProduct_isJointLaw
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.27, sufficiency in the marginal problem: on a junction tree, normalized nonnegative clique tables that agree on separators are the clique marginals of the junction-tree product, which is a probability table.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_joint_with_clique_marginals_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.27, marginal problem on a junction tree: nonnegative clique tables are the clique marginals of a joint probability law exactly when every table is normalized and adjacent tables agree on their separator; in that case the junction-tree product formula is such a law. The uniqueness of the Markov law is not formalized here.

declarations.name: CKSD.ridgeSmoother
declarations.doc: Fixed-design ridge smoother for the objective `‖y - Aβ‖²/(2n) + λ‖β‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ridgePrediction
declarations.doc: Predicted values of a fixed-design ridge fit.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasKernelCriticalRadius
declarations.doc: Empirical kernel critical-radius inequality in terms of normalized Gram eigenvalues.

declarations.name: CKSD.ridgePrediction_oracle_bounds
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.13: fixed-design kernel-ridge oracle bounds for a finite feature representation. The constants are universal. Both the expected bound and the Gaussian tail bound use the same critical radius. The eigenvalues `mu j` of the normalized Gram matrix `A Aᵀ / n` are automatically nonnegative. This does not formalize the eigenvalue-decay calculation for infinite RKHSs.

declarations.name: CKSD.kmeansSampleRisk
declarations.doc: Empirical `k`-means distortion of a finite sample, using an ordered center representation.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_kmeans_centers_of_compact
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.16: almost-sure consistency of compactly constrained empirical `k`-means minimizers. This scope assumes a fixed compact support containing all centers. The unbounded-support theorem under only a second moment requires an additional localization argument. (For `k = 0` all center sets are empty and the statement is trivial.)

declarations.name: CKSD.kmeansRisk_comp_perm
declarations.doc: Permuting center labels leaves the population distortion unchanged.

declarations.name: CKSD.ridgePrediction_zero
declarations.doc: A ridge smoother sends zero observations to zero predicted values.

declarations.name: CKSD.labelUniform
declarations.doc: The uniform law on `[0,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.labelledSample
declarations.doc: Labelled sample from features, label variables, and tie-breaking variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.knnRule
declarations.doc: The `k`-nearest-neighbour rule on a labelled sample with tie-breaking variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.knnExpectedError
declarations.doc: Expected error `𝔼 Lₙ` of the `k`-nearest-neighbour rule built from `n` observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.bayesClassificationRisk
declarations.doc: Bayes risk `R* = 𝔼 min(η(X), 1 - η(X))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.nearestNeighborAsymptoticRisk
declarations.doc: Asymptotic `1`-nearest-neighbour risk `L_NN = 𝔼[2η(X)(1 - η(X))]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_oneNN_expectedError
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.14 (Cover–Hart): for every distribution on `ℝ^d × {0,1}`, the expected error of the `1`-nearest-neighbour rule converges to `L_NN = 𝔼[2η(X)(1 - η(X))]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.bayesRisk_le_nnRisk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.14, Cover–Hart inequalities `R* ≤ L_NN ≤ 2R*(1 - R*)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_tendsto_knn_expectedError
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.14, fixed odd `k`: the limits `L_kNN` of the expected errors exist, are nonincreasing over odd `k`, and satisfy `R* ≤ L_kNN ≤ R* + 1/√(k e)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_knn_expectedError_bayesRisk
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.14, universal consistency (Stone): if `kₙ → ∞` and `kₙ / n → 0`, the expected error of the `kₙ`-nearest-neighbour rule tends to the Bayes risk for every distribution.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_localAveraging_sq_error
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.20, Stone's theorem for response-independent local averaging (forests). The weights `w n i x xs u` are nonnegative, sum to one, and are jointly measurable functions of the query point `x`, the sample features `xs`, and independent randomness `u ∼ ν`, but not of the responses. Under the domination, localization, and vanishing-maximum conditions the estimate `mₙ(x) = ∑ᵢ wₙᵢ(x) Yᵢ` is consistent in `L²(P_X)` for the regression function `m`, characterized by `∫_{X ∈ s} Y = ∫_s m dP_X`.

declarations.name: CKSD.signedMargin
declarations.doc: Signed classification margin for Boolean labels, with `true` representing `+1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_marginLoss_sub_le
declarations.doc: The ramp margin loss `min(1, max(0, 1 - u/ρ))` is `1/ρ`-Lipschitz.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginLoss_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: The ramp margin loss takes values in `[0,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginLoss_eq_one_of_nonpos
declarations.doc: The ramp margin loss dominates the zero-one loss of a nonpositive margin.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_margin_generalization_error_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.10: uniform expected-Rademacher margin bound for a finite class. For real scores `f h` bounded by `B`, margin scale `ρ > 0` and `δ ∈ (0,1)`, with probability at least `1 - δ` every `h` has misclassification probability at most its empirical ramp margin risk plus `2/ρ` times the expected Rademacher complexity of the margins plus `√(log(1/δ) / (2n))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_indicator_mul_eq_of_condExp
declarations.doc: Conditional-probability identity: if `P[1_{A = j} | 𝓕] = p` and `g` is bounded and `𝓕`-measurable, then `∫ 1_{A = j} g = ∫ p g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exp3EstimatedCumulativeLoss
declarations.doc: Exp3 importance-weighted cumulative estimated loss.

declarations.name: CKSD.exp3WeightLowerBound
declarations.doc: The deterministic lower bound for Exp3 probabilities: `c₀ = 1/K` and `c_{t+1} = c_t exp(-η / c_t)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exp3WeightLowerBound_pos
declarations.doc: The Exp3 lower-bound sequence is positive.

declarations.name: CKSD.exp3WeightLowerBound_le
declarations.doc: Exponential weights with nonnegative estimated losses `ℓ̂ t j ≤ 1 / p t j` stay above the positive sequence `exp3WeightLowerBound K η`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_regret_le_of_exp3
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.52: expected Exp3 regret against an oblivious loss sequence. The arm `A t` is drawn with conditional probabilities `p t` given the past `F t`, and `p t` is the exponential- weights distribution, with learning rate `η = √(2 log K / (T K))`, of the importance-weighted cumulative estimated losses. Then the expected regret against every fixed arm over `T` rounds is at most `√(2 T K log K)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FiniteMarkovDecisionProcess
declarations.doc: A finite discounted Markov decision process on the finite state space `S` with actions `A`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FiniteMarkovDecisionProcess.discount_mem_Ioo
declarations.doc: The discount of a finite model lies in the open unit interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.bellmanOperator
declarations.doc: The Bellman optimality operator `(TV)(i) = ⨆_b (r(i,b) + γ ∑ⱼ P(j | i,b) V(j))`. The real supremum is a maximum for a nonempty finite action set (and `0` for an empty one).

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_le_of_sum_eq_one
declarations.doc: A probability average of values bounded by `c` is bounded by `c`.

declarations.name: CKSD.bellmanOperator_contractingWith
declarations.doc: The Bellman optimality operator is a `γ`-contraction for the sup norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.optimalStateValue
declarations.doc: The optimal value function: the unique fixed point of the Bellman optimality operator.

declarations.name: CKSD.bellmanOperator_optimalStateValue
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.58, Bellman optimality: the optimal value function is a fixed point of the Bellman optimality operator (and it is the only one, by the contraction property).

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_greedy_optimalStateValue
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.58, greedy policy: some stationary deterministic policy `π` attains the maximum in the Bellman equation at every state, `V⋆(i) = r(i,π i) + γ ∑ⱼ P(j | i,π i) V⋆(j)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.optimalStateValue_le_of_forall_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.58, primal linear program: every superharmonic `U`, that is `r(i,b) + γ ∑ⱼ P(j | i,b) U(j) ≤ U(i)` for all `i, b`, dominates the optimal value.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_optimalStateValue_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.58, primal linear program: for nonnegative weights `ρ`, the optimal value minimizes `∑ ρ U` over superharmonic `U`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_optimalStateValue_eq_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.58, primal linear program: for positive weights `ρ`, the optimal value is the unique minimizer of `∑ ρ U` over superharmonic `U`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_mulVec_le_of_mem_rowStochastic
declarations.doc: A row-stochastic matrix does not increase the sup norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_le_norm_one_sub_smul_mulVec_div
declarations.doc: Resolvent bound `‖x‖ ≤ ‖(I - γH)x‖ / (1 - γ)` for a row-stochastic `H` and `0 ≤ γ < 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUnit_one_sub_smul_of_mem_rowStochastic
declarations.doc: `I - γH` is invertible for a row-stochastic `H` and `0 ≤ γ < 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_sub_smul_mulVec_inv_mulVec
declarations.doc: The resolvent `(I - γH)⁻¹` is a right inverse on vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.inv_one_sub_smul_mulVec_mulVec
declarations.doc: The resolvent `(I - γH)⁻¹` is a left inverse on vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_inv_one_sub_smul_mulVec
declarations.doc: For a row-stochastic `H`, the resolvent `(I - γH)⁻¹` dominates the identity on nonnegative vectors: `v ≤ (I - γH)⁻¹ v`; in particular the resolvent is positive.

declarations.name: CKSD.inv_one_sub_smul_mulVec_mono
declarations.doc: The resolvent `(I - γH)⁻¹` is monotone on vectors for a row-stochastic `H`.

declarations.name: CKSD.inv_one_sub_smul_mulVec_const
declarations.doc: The resolvent `(I - γH)⁻¹` maps the constant `c` to the constant `c / (1 - γ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.inv_one_sub_smul_mulVec_sub_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.59, resolvent identity: for row-stochastic `P, H` and `0 ≤ γ < 1`, the values `V = (I - γP)⁻¹ r` and `W = (I - γH)⁻¹ r` satisfy `V - W = γ (I - γH)⁻¹ (P - H) V`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_inv_one_sub_smul_mulVec_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.59, sup-norm error bound: with `V = (I - γP)⁻¹ r` and `W = (I - γH)⁻¹ r` for row-stochastic `P, H` and `0 ≤ γ < 1`, `‖V - W‖ ≤ γ/(1-γ) ‖(P - H) V‖`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_projected_fixed_point_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.60, the deterministic error bound underlying TD(λ): if `P` is a norm contraction, `T` is Lipschitz with constant `γ(1-λ)/(1-γλ)` for `γ ∈ (0,1)` and `λ ≤ 1`, `V` is the fixed point of `T` and `w` the fixed point of `P ∘ T`, then `‖w - V‖ ≤ (1-γλ)/(1-γ) ‖PV - V‖`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_asynchronous_stochastic_approximation
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.54, asynchronous stochastic approximation (Tsitsiklis; Jaakkola–Jordan–Singh): let `T` be a `γ`-contraction of `ℝ^ι` in the sup norm with fixed point `x⋆`, and let `Qₙ₊₁(i) = (1 - αₙ(i)) Qₙ(i) + αₙ(i) (T(Qₙ)(i) + Eₙ(i))` with `𝓕ₙ`-measurable steps `αₙ(i) ∈ [0,1]`, `∑ₙ αₙ(i) = ∞`, `∑ₙ αₙ(i)² < ∞` almost surely, and martingale-difference noise `Eₙ` with bounded conditional second moments. Then `Qₙ → x⋆` almost surely. Tabular Q-learning is the case of the Bellman operator on state-action pairs, with steps only on the visited pair.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_sub_mul_log_le_log_sum_exp
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.26, finite-state entropy variational formula for the log partition function, upper bound: for every probability vector `w`, `∑ᵢ wᵢ aᵢ + H(w) ≤ log ∑ᵢ exp aᵢ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_softmax_mul_sub_mul_log_eq_log_sum_exp
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.26, finite-state entropy variational formula for the log partition function, attainment: the Gibbs (softmax) vector `exp aᵢ / Z` attains `log Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_log_sum_exp_div_atTop
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.26, the zero-temperature limit of a finite log partition function: `β⁻¹ log ∑ᵢ exp(β aᵢ) → maxᵢ aᵢ` as `β → ∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_predictions_of_gradient_flow
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.30, finite-width tangent-kernel training dynamics for a differentiable model: along the gradient flow `θ' = -n⁻¹ Dfᵀ (f(θ) - y)` of the empirical squared loss on `n` outputs, the predictions evolve by `(f ∘ θ)' = -n⁻¹ Df Dfᵀ (f(θ) - y)`, with tangent kernel `Df Dfᵀ`. The parameter and output spaces are arbitrary real Hilbert spaces.

declarations.name: CKSD.ridgeless_gaussian_risk_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.31, the underparameterized ridgeless risk with Gaussian noise.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_least_squares_gradient_descent
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.40, least-squares gradient descent and the preserved nullspace component: for a step `0 < η < 2 / ‖A‖²`, the iterates `θ ↦ θ - η Aᵀ(Aθ - y)` converge to a solution `θ*` of the normal equations with `θ* - θ₀ ∈ range Aᵀ`, i.e. the component of `θ₀` in `ker A` is preserved. The parameter space is a finite-dimensional real inner product space and the output space a real Hilbert space.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurePreserving_uncurry_pi
declarations.doc: The product measure `μ^{κ × U}` is the image of the iterated product measure `(μ^U)^κ` under uncurrying `z ↦ ((k, u) ↦ z k u)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_cexp_wideLayer
declarations.doc: **Characteristic function of a wide random layer.** Under independent standard normal parameters indexed by `(Fin N × U) ⊕ (Fin N ⊕ Unit)` (hidden-unit parameters `uₖ ∈ ℝ^U`, output weights `vₖ`, bias `b`), the scalar output `a b + c ∑ₖ vₖ g(uₖ)` has characteristic function at `1` equal to `exp(-a²/2) · (𝔼 exp(-c² g(u)²/2))^N`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_exp_neg_div_pow
declarations.doc: **Poisson-type limit of a mixture.** For an integrable `h ≥ 0` under a probability measure, `(𝔼 exp(-h/N))^N → exp(-𝔼 h)` as `N → ∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.DenseNetParams
declarations.doc: Parameters of a dense network with hidden widths `w 1, …, w H` and scalar output.

declarations.name: CKSD.denseActivation
declarations.doc: Hidden activations of a dense network.

declarations.name: CKSD.denseNetOutput
declarations.doc: Scalar output of a dense network.

declarations.name: CKSD.denseParamCount
declarations.doc: Number of scalar parameters of the architecture, including biases.

declarations.name: CKSD.denseHiddenNeurons
declarations.doc: Number of hidden neurons of the architecture.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPiecewisePolynomial
declarations.doc: A real activation is piecewise polynomial: on each of the finitely many half-open pieces cut out by a finite set of breakpoints it agrees with a polynomial.

declarations.name: CKSD.BooleanClassShatters
declarations.doc: A class of Boolean functions shatters a finite set if it realizes every labelling of it.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_le_of_shatters_denseSignClass
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.35, VC dimension of network sign classifiers: for a fixed piecewise-polynomial activation there is `c` such that every finite set shattered by the sign classifiers of one dense architecture with `P ≥ 2` parameters and depth `L = H + 1` has at most `c (P L log P + P L²)` points. Architectures are layered and fully connected.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalRademacherComplexity_biasFree_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.35, norm-based capacity: bias-free networks of depth `L = H + 1` on the unit ball, with a `1`-Lipschitz positively homogeneous activation and all weight matrices of Frobenius norm at most `C` (the squared Frobenius norm `∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ Wᵢⱼ²` being at most `C²`), have empirical Rademacher complexity at most `2^{L-1} C^L / √n`, independently of the widths. (For `n = 0` both sides vanish.)

declarations.name: CKSD.holderUnitCube
declarations.doc: The unit cube `[0,1]^d` in `Fin d → ℝ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.relu_depth_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.37, depth lower bound (Yarotsky): a `C²` function on `[0,1]^d` that is not affine there cannot be approximated uniformly within `ε` by ReLU networks with `H ≥ 1` hidden layers and at most `c ε^{-1/(2H)}` hidden neurons, for all small `ε`. The restriction to small `ε` is necessary, since constants approximate within any large `ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.relu_eldan_shamir_separation
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.37, depth separation (Eldan–Shamir) for the ReLU: for `d ≥ C` there are a probability measure on `ℝ^d` and a function bounded by `2` computed by a two-hidden-layer ReLU network of width at most `C d⁵` and parameters at most `C d^C` in absolute value, at squared `L²` distance at least `c` from every one-hidden-layer ReLU network of width at most `c e^{cd}` (the squared distance is an extended nonnegative integral, so no integrability is presupposed). The logistic and Heaviside cases are not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsInHolderBall
declarations.doc: Membership in the Hölder ball of smoothness `β ∈ (0,1]` and radius `K` on a domain `D`: `sup_D |g| + sup_{x ≠ y} |g x - g y| / ‖x - y‖^β ≤ K`, with the sup norm on `S → ℝ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.chainComp
declarations.doc: Composition `g (k-1) ∘ ⋯ ∘ g 0` of a chain of maps between coordinate spaces.

declarations.name: CKSD.compositionalHolderClass
declarations.doc: The compositional Hölder class of Schmidt-Hieber with smoothness indices in `(0,1]`: compositions `g q ∘ ⋯ ∘ g 0` with `g i : [a i, b i]^{d i} → [a (i+1), b (i+1)]^{d (i+1)}`, `[a 0, b 0] = [0,1]`, `|a i|, |b i| ≤ K`, each coordinate of `g i` depending on at most `t i` arguments and lying, as a function of those, in the Hölder ball of smoothness `β i` and radius `K`. The scalar output is the unique coordinate of `d (q+1) = 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.uniformDesignRegressionLaw
declarations.doc: Law of one observation `(X, f X + ε)` with `X` uniform on `[0,1]^d` and standard normal noise.

declarations.name: CKSD.compositionalHolder_minimax_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.29, minimax lower bound for compositional Hölder classes (Schmidt-Hieber), for smoothness indices in `(0,1]` and the uniform design on `[0,1]^d` (a density bounded above and below). With `β*ᵢ = βᵢ ∏_{j > i} βⱼ` and `φₙ = maxᵢ n^{-2β*ᵢ/(2β*ᵢ + tᵢ)}`, if `tᵢ ≤ min(d₀, …, dᵢ₋₁)`, then for all large `K` every measurable estimator has risk at least `c φₙ` at some member of the class. Risk is an extended nonnegative integral, allowing infinite risk for unrestricted estimators. The upper bound by sparse ReLU least squares is not formalized here.

declarations.name: CKSD.gpFirstLayerPreactivation
declarations.doc: Preactivation of one first-layer unit with parameters `θ = (weights, bias)` at input `y`, for `N(0, C_W/d)` weights and `N(0, C_b)` bias written as scaled standard normals.

declarations.name: CKSD.gpSecondLayerPreactivation
declarations.doc: Scalar output preactivation of a one-hidden-layer network of width `N` with independent standard normal parameters scaled to `N(0, C_b)` biases and `N(0, C_W / N)` output weights.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_wide_network_gaussian
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.39, Gaussian-process limit at initialization for one hidden layer: at finitely many inputs the output preactivations converge jointly in distribution, as the width tends to infinity, to the centered Gaussian vector with covariance `K²(x,x') = C_b + C_W 𝔼[σ(U)σ(U')]`, where `(U,U')` is the pair of preactivations of one first-layer unit at `x, x'`, centered Gaussian with covariance `K¹(x,x') = C_b + C_W ⟨x,x'⟩/d`. Deeper networks iterate this step.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStationaryPolicy
declarations.doc: A stationary randomized policy: each row is a probability vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyTransition
declarations.doc: State transition matrix under a stationary randomized policy.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyReward
declarations.doc: Expected one-step reward under a stationary randomized policy.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyValue
declarations.doc: Discounted value `V^π = (I - γ P^π)⁻¹ r^π` of a stationary randomized policy.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyActionValue
declarations.doc: State-action value of a stationary randomized policy.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyAdvantage
declarations.doc: Advantage `A^π(i,b) = Q^π(i,b) - V^π(i)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyObjective
declarations.doc: Expected value `J(π) = ∑ᵢ ρ i V^π(i)` under an initial law.

declarations.name: CKSD.optimalObjective
declarations.doc: Optimal objective over stationary randomized policies.

declarations.name: CKSD.naturalPolicyGradientIterate
declarations.doc: Natural policy gradient iterates for the softmax parameterization started at `θ = 0`: `π⁽ᵗ⁺¹⁾(b | i) ∝ π⁽ᵗ⁾(b | i) exp(η A⁽ᵗ⁾(i,b) / (1 - γ))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyTransition_nonneg
declarations.doc: The state transition matrix of a stationary policy has nonnegative entries.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_policyTransition
declarations.doc: The state transition matrix of a stationary policy is row-stochastic.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyTransition_mem_rowStochastic
declarations.doc: The state transition matrix of a stationary policy is row-stochastic.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyValue_eq_add
declarations.doc: Bellman equation `V^π = r^π + γ P^π V^π` of a stationary policy.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_policyAdvantage
declarations.doc: Averaging the advantage of `π` under the action law of a policy `π'`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_policyAdvantage_self
declarations.doc: The advantage of a stationary policy averages to zero under its own action law.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyValue_sub_eq
declarations.doc: Performance difference identity: `V^{π'} - V^π = (I - γ P^{π'})⁻¹ ā`, where `ā(i) = ∑_b π'(b | i) A^π(i,b)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyValue_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: Values of stationary policies with rewards in `[0,1]` lie in `[0, 1/(1-γ)]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_log_sub_log_nonneg
declarations.doc: Gibbs' inequality for positive probability vectors: `∑ p (log p - log q) ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_le_sum_mul_exp_policyAdvantage
declarations.doc: The normalizer `Z(i) = ∑_b π(b | i) exp(η A^π(i,b) / (1-γ))` of a natural policy gradient step from a stationary policy is at least `1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.naturalPolicyGradientIterate_pos
declarations.doc: Natural policy gradient iterates are stationary policies with positive entries.

declarations.name: CKSD.isStationaryPolicy_naturalPolicyGradientIterate
declarations.doc: Natural policy gradient iterates are stationary policies.

declarations.name: CKSD.log_naturalPolicyGradientIterate_succ
declarations.doc: Logarithmic form of the natural policy gradient step: `log π⁽ᵗ⁺¹⁾(b | i) = log π⁽ᵗ⁾(b | i) + η A⁽ᵗ⁾(i,b) / (1-γ) - log Z⁽ᵗ⁾(i)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.mul_log_le_policyValue_sub_of_log_update
declarations.doc: One step of the logarithmic update improves the value: if positive stationary policies `π, π'` satisfy `A^π(i,b) = (1-γ)/η (log π'(b | i) - log π(b | i) + log Z(i))` with `Z ≥ 1`, then `V^{π'}(i) - V^π(i) ≥ (1-γ)/η · log Z(i)` for every state `i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.policyObjective_sub_le_of_log_update
declarations.doc: Mirror-descent bound behind natural policy gradient: if positive stationary policies `π⁽ᵗ⁾`, started from the uniform policy, satisfy the logarithmic update `A⁽ᵗ⁾(i,b) = (1-γ)/η (log π⁽ᵗ⁺¹⁾(b | i) - log π⁽ᵗ⁾(b | i) + log Z⁽ᵗ⁾(i))` with normalizers `Z⁽ᵗ⁾ ≥ 1`, then for rewards in `[0,1]` and every stationary comparator `π⋆`, `J(π⋆) - J(π⁽ᵀ⁾) ≤ log |A| / (η T) + 1 / ((1 - γ)² T)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.optimalObjective_sub_npg_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.61: convergence of natural policy gradient with softmax policies from `θ = 0`, for rewards in `[0,1]`, any initial law `ρ`, and any step `η > 0` (Agarwal–Kakade–Lee–Mahajan): `J⋆(ρ) - J(π⁽ᵀ⁾) ≤ log |A| / (η T) + 1 / ((1 - γ)² T)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.FiniteMarkovBandit
declarations.doc: A finite Markov bandit: arms indexed by `ι` on a common finite state space `X`, each with a stochastic transition matrix and a reward function, and a discount `β ∈ (0,1)`. Only the played arm moves.

declarations.name: CKSD.gittinsRewardAndTime
declarations.doc: Expected discounted reward and discounted time until the first exit time `τ ≥ 1` from the continuation set `C`, for arm `k` started in each state.

declarations.name: CKSD.gittinsIndex
declarations.doc: The Gittins index of arm `k` in state `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditJointTransition
declarations.doc: Joint transition when arm `k` is played: only its coordinate moves.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditPolicyValue
declarations.doc: Discounted value of a stationary deterministic arm-selection rule on joint states.

declarations.name: CKSD.banditPolicyValue_le_of_gittins
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.51, Gittins index theorem for finite Markov bandits: always playing an arm of largest current Gittins index maximizes the expected discounted reward from every joint state. The comparison class is the stationary deterministic rules on joint states, which attain the optimum over all policies of this finite discounted model (GAPS 107.58). Countable state spaces are not covered.

declarations.name: CKSD.isDifferentiallyPrivate_compProd
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.65, basic composition of two adaptive private releases. The proof bounds the first release through the layer-cake formula for the truncated second-stage probability. The relation `R` is arbitrary, the exponential parameters are real, and the additive errors are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_sub_integral_le_mul_totalVariationDistance
declarations.doc: A measurable function with values in `[0, c]` has expectations under two probability measures differing by at most `c` times their total variation distance.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_le_exp_of_local_privacy
declarations.doc: A pure `ε`-locally private Markov kernel on a nonempty space has `e^ε ≥ 1`: apply the privacy inequality to the whole output space.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_measureReal_comp_sub_le_of_local_privacy
declarations.doc: For a pure `ε`-locally private Markov kernel `Q`, the output laws `Q ∘ₘ P₁` and `Q ∘ₘ P₂` differ on each event by at most `(e^ε - 1) · TV(P₁, P₂)` times the mass of that event under either output law.

declarations.name: CKSD.klFun_le_sq_sub_one
declarations.doc: The Kullback–Leibler function is dominated by the `χ²` integrand on `[0, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_le_ofReal_sq_of_abs_measureReal_sub_le
declarations.doc: If two probability measures satisfy `|μ A - ν A| ≤ δ ν A` for every event, then `KL(μ ‖ ν) ≤ δ²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_comp_le_of_local_differential_privacy
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.75, the single-release KL contraction under local privacy: for a pure `ε`-locally differentially private Markov kernel `Q`, the symmetrized Kullback–Leibler divergence of the output laws is at most `4 (e^ε - 1)² TV(P₁, P₂)²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_bernoulliMeasure_one_zero
declarations.doc: Integrals against the Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` on the real line.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_id_bernoulliMeasure_one_zero
declarations.doc: The Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` has mean `p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.bernoulliMeasure_one_zero_compl_Icc
declarations.doc: The Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` is supported by `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.kernel_apply_le_exp_mul_card
declarations.doc: Group privacy: a mechanism that is `ε`-differentially private for Hamming neighbours changes the probability of an event by at most the factor `exp(ε k)` between data sets that differ in at most `k` coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.ofReal_mul_comp_le_centralMeanRisk
declarations.doc: A lower bound for the central mean risk on a set of releases far from the mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.centralMeanRisk_add_centralMeanRisk_ge
declarations.doc: Le Cam's two-point bound for Bernoulli laws `Ber(1, 0, a)` and `Ber(1, 0, b)` with `a < b`: the sum of the two risks is at least `((b - a)/2)²` times the sum of the error probabilities of the test that rejects `a` when the release exceeds `(a + b)/2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.klBerReal_le_sq_div
declarations.doc: The binary Kullback–Leibler divergence is at most the χ² divergence `(p - q)² / (q (1 - q))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ofReal_half_le_or_of_ofReal_le_add
declarations.doc: If a sum is at least `r`, one of the two terms is at least `r / 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.two_mul_measureReal_sub_le_tvDist
declarations.doc: The event bound from the total variation distance: `2 (Q A - Q' A) ≤ tvDist Q Q'`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_div_six_le_measureReal_add_measureReal_compl
declarations.doc: The testing step of Le Cam's method after the Bretagnolle–Huber inequality: if `e⁻¹ ≤ 2 - tvDist Q' Q`, then every test errs with total probability at least `1/6`, that is, `1/6 ≤ Q A + Q' Aᶜ` for every event `A`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_bernoulli_centralMeanRisk_ge_inv
declarations.doc: The non-private part of the central lower bound: for every mechanism some Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` has mean squared error at least `1 / (192 n)`. The two laws `Ber(1/2)` and `Ber(1/2 + δ)` with `δ = 1/(2√n)` have product laws at Kullback–Leibler divergence at most `1` (Statlib's `klDiv_pi_const` and `klDiv_bernoulliMeasure_eq_klBerReal`), so by the Bretagnolle–Huber inequality (Statlib's `exp_neg_klDiv_le_two_sub_tvDist`) and data processing (`tvDist_comp_le`) no test separates them well.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_exp_mul_card_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The exponential moment of the number of nonzero coordinates under the product of Bernoulli laws: `∫ exp(ε #{i | dᵢ ≠ 0}) = (1 + q (e^ε - 1))ⁿ`, written as a lower integral.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_add_mul_exp_sub_one_pow_le_nine
declarations.doc: The exponential moment bound `(1 + q (e^ε - 1))ⁿ ≤ 9` when `q ε ≤ 1/n` and `ε ≤ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_bernoulli_centralMeanRisk_ge_private
declarations.doc: The private part of the central lower bound: for an `ε`-differentially private mechanism some Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` has mean squared error at least `min(1, 1/(nε))² / 72`. The two laws are `Ber(1, 0, 0) = δ₀` and `Ber(1, 0, q)` with `q = min(1, 1/(nε))`; by group privacy the release law under the second is at most `(1 + q(e^ε - 1))ⁿ ≤ 9` times the release law under the first.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_centralMeanRisk_ge
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66, central minimax lower bound: there is an absolute `c > 0` such that for `0 < ε ≤ 1` every `ε`-differentially private mechanism has mean squared error at least `c min(1, 1/n + 1/(nε)²)` for the mean of some law on `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.totalVariationDistance_bernoulliMeasure_le
declarations.doc: The total variation distance between `Ber(1, 0, a)` and `Ber(1, 0, b)` is at most `|a - b|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ofReal_mul_map_le_localMeanRisk
declarations.doc: A lower bound for the local mean risk on a set of estimates far from the mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_bernoulli_localMeanRisk_ge
declarations.doc: The lower half of the local minimax rate: for `ε`-locally private release kernels and a measurable estimator, some Bernoulli law `Ber(1, 0, p)` has mean squared error at least `min(1, 1/(nε²)) / 768`. The two laws are `Ber(1/2)` and `Ber(1/2 + δ)` with `δ = min(1/2, 1/(4ε√n))`; the release laws of one individual are at Kullback–Leibler divergence at most `16 ε² δ²` by the contraction under local privacy (GAPS 107.75, `klDiv_comp_le_of_local_differential_privacy`), and Le Cam's method concludes as in the central case.

declarations.name: CKSD.localLaplaceKernel
declarations.doc: The local Laplace release kernel: clip to `[-1,1]` and add Laplace noise of scale `2/ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMarkovKernel_localLaplaceKernel
declarations.doc: The local Laplace release kernel is a Markov kernel for positive `ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isDifferentiallyPrivate_localLaplaceKernel
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66: the local Laplace release kernel is `ε`-locally differentially private.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_sq_sub_localLaplace_le
declarations.doc: Under a law supported by `[-1,1]`, the squared deviation of a local Laplace release from the mean has lower integral at most `4 + 8/ε²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_id_localLaplace
declarations.doc: Under a law supported by `[-1,1]`, a local Laplace release has mean equal to the mean of the law.

declarations.name: CKSD.localMeanRisk_localLaplace_mean_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66: on laws supported by `[-1,1]`, the sample mean of local Laplace releases has mean squared error at most `(4 + 8/ε²)/n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.localMeanRisk_minimax_order
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66, local minimax rate: there are absolute `c, C > 0` such that for `0 < ε ≤ 1` every noninteractive protocol with `ε`-locally private release kernels and every measurable estimator has mean squared error at least `c min(1, 1/(nε²))` for some law on `[-1,1]`, and some such protocol has error at most `C min(1, 1/(nε²))` for every law on `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsHammingNeighbor
declarations.doc: Data sets in `ℝⁿ` are neighbouring when they differ in at most one coordinate, that is, when their Hamming distance is at most `1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.clipUnit
declarations.doc: Clipping to `[-1,1]`: the projection `Set.projIcc` onto the interval, as a real number.

declarations.name: CKSD.clipUnit_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: Clipped values lie in `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.clipUnit_of_mem
declarations.doc: Clipping is the identity on `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_clipUnit
declarations.doc: Clipping is continuous.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_clipUnit
declarations.doc: Clipping is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.clippedMean
declarations.doc: Mean of a data set clipped to `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.laplaceMeanMechanism
declarations.doc: The clipped Laplace mean mechanism with noise scale `2 / (n ε)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.centralMeanRisk
declarations.doc: Mean squared error of a central mechanism for the mean of `P`, from `n` observations. It is a lower Lebesgue integral in `ℝ≥0∞`, so a mechanism with infinite error has risk `∞` rather than the junk value `0` of a non-integrable Bochner integral.

declarations.name: CKSD.localMeanRisk
declarations.doc: Mean squared error of a noninteractive local protocol with release kernels `Q` and estimator `est`, for the mean of `P`, as a lower Lebesgue integral in `ℝ≥0∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_clippedMean_sub_le
declarations.doc: Changing one coordinate moves the clipped mean by at most `2 / n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.laplacePDF_le_exp_mul
declarations.doc: Shifting the location of a Laplace density by `δ` changes it by at most `e^{|δ|/b}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isDifferentiallyPrivate_of_eq_laplaceMeasure
declarations.doc: A Laplace mechanism `d ↦ Laplace(f d, b)` is `ε`-differentially private for a relation `R` along which `f` moves by at most `ε b`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isDifferentiallyPrivate_laplaceMeanMechanism
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66: the clipped Laplace mean mechanism is `ε`-differentially private.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sub_laplaceMeasure
declarations.doc: Mean squared deviation of a Laplace law from a point: squared bias plus variance `2b²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_sq_sub_laplaceMeasure
declarations.doc: The squared deviation from a point is integrable under a Laplace law.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_clippedMean_sub_sq_le
declarations.doc: On laws supported by `[-1,1]` the clipped sample mean has mean squared error at most `1/n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.centralMeanRisk_laplaceMeanMechanism_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66: on laws supported by `[-1,1]`, the clipped Laplace mean mechanism has mean squared error at most `1/n + 8/(n ε)²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isMarkovKernel_laplaceMeanMechanism
declarations.doc: The clipped Laplace mean mechanism is a Markov kernel for positive `n` and `ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_integral_le_one_of_support
declarations.doc: The mean of a law supported by `[-1,1]` lies in `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_centralMeanRisk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.66, central minimax upper bound: for every `ε > 0` (in particular `0 < ε ≤ 1`) some `ε`-differentially private mechanism (the clipped Laplace mean, or the constant release `0` when `1` is the smaller rate) has mean squared error at most `8 min(1, 1/n + 1/(nε)²)` for every law on `[-1,1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_real_edges
declarations.doc: In the binomial random graph `G(V, p)`, a set `A` of prescribed edges is present and a disjoint set `B` of prescribed edges is absent with probability `p ^ |A| (1 - p) ^ |B|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isolatedVertices
declarations.doc: The set of isolated vertices of a graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.incidentEdges
declarations.doc: The non-loop pairs incident to a vertex set `J`.

declarations.name: CKSD.subset_isolatedVertices_iff
declarations.doc: A vertex set `J` consists of isolated vertices exactly when no pair incident to `J` is an edge.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_real_subset_isolatedVertices
declarations.doc: A vertex set `J` consists of isolated vertices with probability `(1 - p) ^ |incidentEdges J|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_incidentEdges_le
declarations.doc: The number of pairs incident to `J` is at most `|J| |V|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_card_incidentEdges
declarations.doc: The number of pairs incident to `J` is at least `|J| (|V| - |J|)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isolatedMoment
declarations.doc: The `j`-th factorial moment of the number of isolated vertices of `G(V, p)`: `Sⱼ = ∑_{|J| = j} P(J consists of isolated vertices)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_choose_card_isolatedVertices
declarations.doc: The `j`-th binomial moment of the number of isolated vertices is `isolatedMoment p j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.bonferroni_isolatedVertices
declarations.doc: Bonferroni inequalities for the absence of isolated vertices: the alternating partial sums of the factorial moments bound `P(no isolated vertex)` alternately from above and below.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_real_isolatedVertices_eq_empty_mul_le
declarations.doc: Second-moment inequality for isolated vertices: `P(no isolated vertex) S₁² ≤ S₁ + 2 S₂ - S₁²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.internalPairs
declarations.doc: The non-loop pairs with both ends in `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.boundaryPairs
declarations.doc: The pairs joining `S` to its complement.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_internalPairs_le
declarations.doc: There are at most `|S|²` internal pairs.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_boundaryPairs
declarations.doc: There are exactly `|S| (|V| - |S|)` boundary pairs.

declarations.name: CKSD.not_isDiag_of_mem_boundaryPairs
declarations.doc: Boundary pairs are not loops.

declarations.name: CKSD.disjoint_internalPairs_boundaryPairs
declarations.doc: Internal and boundary pairs of the same set are disjoint.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_closed_set_of_not_connected
declarations.doc: A disconnected graph without isolated vertices on a nonempty vertex set has a vertex set `S` with `2 ≤ |S| ≤ |V| / 2`, no edge leaving `S`, and `|S| - 1` edges inside `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_real_not_connected_le
declarations.doc: Union bound for disconnected graphs without isolated vertices: `P(no isolated vertex, not connected) ≤ ∑_{k=2}^{|V|/2} C(|V|, k) C(k², k-1) p^{k-1} (1-p)^{k(|V|-k)}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_sub_pow_le_exp
declarations.doc: The real power `(1 - p) ^ m` is at most `exp (-p m)` for `p ≤ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_disconnSum
declarations.doc: The union bound for disconnected graphs without isolated vertices tends to zero as soon as `n pₙ ≥ log n - M` eventually.

declarations.name: CKSD.isolatedMoment_zero
declarations.doc: The zeroth factorial moment is one.

declarations.name: CKSD.isolatedMoment_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: Two-sided bounds `C(|V|, j) (1-p)^{j|V|} ≤ Sⱼ ≤ C(|V|, j) (1-p)^{j(|V|-j)}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isolatedVertices_eq_empty_of_connected
declarations.doc: In a connected graph on at least two vertices no vertex is isolated.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_real_connected_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: Connectivity and the absence of isolated vertices differ by at most the union bound: `P(no isolated vertex) - T ≤ P(connected) ≤ P(no isolated vertex)` on at least two vertices.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_isolatedMoment_threshold
declarations.doc: For fixed `x`, the `j`-th factorial moment of the number of isolated vertices of `G(n, (log n + x)/n)` tends to `e^{-jx} / j!`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_binomialRandom_connected_threshold
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.47, connectivity at `p = (log n + x)/n`: the probability that `G(n, p)` is connected tends to `exp (-e^{-x})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_sub_isolatedMoment_one_le
declarations.doc: First-moment bound: `P(no isolated vertex) ≥ 1 - S₁`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_binomialRandom_connected_of_tendsto_atTop
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.47: if `xₙ → ∞`, then `G(n, (log n + xₙ)/n)` is connected with probability tending to one.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_binomialRandom_exists_isolated_of_tendsto_atBot
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.47: if `xₙ → -∞`, then `G(n, (log n + xₙ)/n)` has an isolated vertex with probability tending to one (second-moment method).

declarations.name: CKSD.exploreStep
declarations.doc: One step of the exploration process. A state is a pair `(D, P)` of discovered and processed vertices; the least discovered unprocessed vertex is processed and the set `a` is added to the discovered vertices. If every discovered vertex is processed, the state does not change.

declarations.name: CKSD.ExploreValid
declarations.doc: Admissible histories of `m` exploration steps from the state `s`: at every step some discovered vertex is unprocessed and the newly discovered set is undiscovered so far.

declarations.name: CKSD.exploreFound
declarations.doc: The pairs revealed as edges along a history: the processed vertex joined to the newly discovered vertices.

declarations.name: CKSD.exploreMissed
declarations.doc: The pairs revealed as non-edges along a history: the processed vertex joined to the undiscovered vertices that are not discovered at this step.

declarations.name: CKSD.subset_exploreStep
declarations.doc: The exploration step is monotone in both coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.exploreFound_union_exploreMissed_spec
declarations.doc: Every revealed pair of a valid history from `s` joins an unprocessed vertex `x` to a different, undiscovered vertex `y`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exploreFound_exploreMissed_props
declarations.doc: Found and missed pairs of a valid history are disjoint.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_exploreFound_succ
declarations.doc: Cardinality recursion for found pairs.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_exploreMissed_succ
declarations.doc: Cardinality recursion for missed pairs.

declarations.name: CKSD.exploreWeight
declarations.doc: The weight of a history, `x^{#found} y^{#missed}`, restricted to admissible histories.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_exploreWeight_le
declarations.doc: The total weight of admissible histories of length `m` is at most `((x + y)^{|V|})^m` when `x, y ≥ 0` and `x + y ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exploreEvent
declarations.doc: The event that a history is realized: its found pairs are edges and its missed pairs are not.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_real_exploreEvent
declarations.doc: An admissible history is realized with probability `p^{#found} (1-p)^{#missed}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exploreNew
declarations.doc: The set discovered from the state `s` in a graph `G`: the undiscovered neighbours of the next processed vertex.

declarations.name: CKSD.exploreHistory
declarations.doc: The history of the exploration of `G` from the state `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.reachableSet
declarations.doc: The vertices reachable from `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ExploreInv
declarations.doc: The invariant of the exploration of the component of `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exploreHistory_spec
declarations.doc: The exploration of `G` from a state satisfying the invariant is an admissible realized history, and it discovers enough vertices as long as the component is large.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_real_reachableSet_card_le
declarations.doc: The component of `v` has more than `m` vertices with probability at most `λ^{-m} (1 - p + pλ)^{m|V|}` for every `λ ≥ 1` (exploration and the exponential moment bound).

declarations.name: CKSD.ncard_supp_connectedComponentMk
declarations.doc: The connected component of `v` has as many vertices as are reachable from `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_real_exists_large_component_le
declarations.doc: Union bound over the vertices: some component has more than `m` vertices with probability at most `|V| λ^{-m} (1 - p + pλ)^{m|V|}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_tendsto_binomialRandom_components_le_log'
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.47, subcritical phase: for `p = c/n` with `0 ≤ c < 1`, all components of `G(n, p)` have at most `C log n` vertices with probability tending to one.

declarations.name: CKSD.clampUnitInterval
declarations.doc: A real number clamped to the unit interval (Mathlib's projection `Set.projIcc`), used as an edge probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.balancedLabelings
declarations.doc: Labellings of `Fin n` with exactly `n / 2` vertices in the group `true`.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockModelGraphProb
declarations.doc: Probability of the graph `G` under the two-group block model given the labelling `σ`: independent edges with probability `p` within and `q` between groups (both clamped).

declarations.name: CKSD.blockModelMass
declarations.doc: Joint mass of a labelling and a graph under the symmetric two-group block model.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockModelGraphLaw
declarations.doc: Law of the observed graph of the symmetric two-group block model.

declarations.name: CKSD.exactRecoveryProbability
declarations.doc: Probability that an estimator recovers the labelling exactly, up to a global flip.

declarations.name: CKSD.labelingOverlap
declarations.doc: Normalized overlap `|∑ᵢ σᵢ τᵢ| / n` of two labellings in `±1` coding.

declarations.name: CKSD.weakRecoveryProbability
declarations.doc: Probability that an estimator has overlap at least `ε` with the planted labelling.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_exactRecovery_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.41: the exact-recovery threshold of the logarithmic-degree two-group block model, for `a, b > 0`. Recovery up to a global flip with probability tending to one is possible exactly when `(√a - √b)² ≥ 2`. The polynomial-time achievability claim is not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_exactRecovery_iff_of_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.41, the case `b = 0`: exact recovery is possible exactly when `a > 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_weakRecovery_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.42: the Kesten–Stigum threshold for weak recovery in the sparse two-group block model with `p = a/n`, `q = b/n`, `a, b > 0`. The efficiency claim is not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockModel_binomialRandom_mutually_contiguous
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.42: below the Kesten–Stigum threshold the sparse block model and the binomial random graph with the same average degree are mutually contiguous, stated directly on sequences of events (every set of graphs on `Fin n` is measurable).

declarations.name: CKSD.componentSize
declarations.doc: Number of vertices in the connected component of `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.largestComponentSize
declarations.doc: Number of vertices of a largest connected component (zero for the empty vertex set).

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_tendsto_binomial_random_components_le_log
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.47, subcritical phase: for `p = c/n` with `0 ≤ c < 1`, all components have at most `C log n` vertices with probability tending to one.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_giant_component
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.47, supercritical phase: for `p = c/n` with `c > 1`, the largest component has size `ζ n + o(n)` in probability, with `ζ ∈ (0,1)` the root of `1 - ζ = e^{-cζ}`, and any two distinct components have the smaller one of size at most `C log n` with probability tending to one.

declarations.name: CKSD.binomialRandom_connectivity_threshold
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.47, connectivity threshold: for `p = (log n + xₙ)/n`, connectivity has probability tending to one if `xₙ → ∞`, isolated vertices have probability tending to one if `xₙ → -∞`, and for constant `xₙ = x` the probability of connectivity tends to `exp(-e^{-x})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.finitePermOfFin
declarations.doc: The permutation of `ℕ` acting as `σ` on the first `n` labels and fixing all others.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_finitePermOfFin_eq_on
declarations.doc: Every permutation of `ℕ` agrees on the first `n` labels with a permutation moving only finitely many labels.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_comap_eq_of_finitePerm_invariant
declarations.doc: A law on graphs on `ℕ` invariant under every permutation of finitely many labels is invariant under every permutation of `ℕ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_graphonMixture_of_finitePerm_invariant
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.43: a law on graphs on `ℕ` invariant under permutations of finitely many labels is a mixture of graphon models, with a unique mixing measure on TauCeti's unit-interval graphon space (graphons modulo cut distance zero). The all-permutations case is TauCeti's `InfiniteExchangeableGraphLaw.existsUnique_bind_infiniteSampleLawOnSpace`.

declarations.name: CKSD.infiniteSampleLaw_eq_iff_exists_measurePreserving
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.43, uniqueness in the attained form (Borgs–Chayes–Lovász): two graphons on the unit interval have the same joint sampling law exactly when they have almost everywhere equal pullbacks under two measure-preserving self-maps of the unit interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_sum_sub_of_add_le_armSampleAverage
declarations.doc: The prefix sum of the centred rewards of one arm, rewritten from the prefix average.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_sum_sub_of_armSampleAverage_le
declarations.doc: The prefix sum of the centred losses of one arm, rewritten from the prefix average.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_mul_le_sum_sub_le
declarations.doc: Hoeffding's inequality for prefix sums of independent `[0,1]`-valued variables with common mean `μ`: `P(s c ≤ ∑_{j<s} (X j - μ)) ≤ exp(-2 s c²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.iIndepFun_reward
declarations.doc: The rewards of one arm, as a sequence, are independent.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_add_le_armSampleAverage_le
declarations.doc: Hoeffding's inequality for an upper deviation of the prefix average of one arm.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_armSampleAverage_le_sub_le
declarations.doc: Hoeffding's inequality for a lower deviation of the prefix average of one arm, obtained from the upper deviation bound for the losses `1 - R i j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_armSampleAverage
declarations.doc: Prefix averages of measurable rewards are measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount_succ
declarations.doc: The play count increases by one exactly at a play of the arm.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount_mono
declarations.doc: Play counts are monotone in time.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount_le
declarations.doc: The play count after `t` rounds is at most `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount_lt_of_play
declarations.doc: A play of the arm at time `t` makes its count strictly larger at every later time.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_filter_play_count_lt_le
declarations.doc: At most `ℓ` plays of an arm happen while its count is below `ℓ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_le_armPlayCount
declarations.doc: If the first `K` rounds play each arm once, then every arm has been played at least once by any time `t ≥ K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount_le_add_card
declarations.doc: Plays during the initialization rounds: the count of an arm before its initial play is zero, so with `1 ≤ ℓ` all plays with count at least `ℓ` happen at times `t ≥ K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ucb_deviation_of_play
declarations.doc: The deterministic step of the UCB1 analysis: if a suboptimal arm `i` with gap `Δ` is played at a time `t ≥ K` after at least `ℓ` earlier plays, where `8 log t ≤ Δ² ℓ`, then either the average of the optimal arm lies below its mean by the confidence radius, or the average of arm `i` lies above its mean by the confidence radius.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_armPlayCount
declarations.doc: Play counts of a measurable arm process are measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.exp_neg_two_mul_sqrt_sq_eq
declarations.doc: The Hoeffding bound at the UCB1 confidence radius: `exp(-2 s c²) = t⁻⁴` for `c = √(2 log t / s)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.natCast_mul_inv_pow_four_le
declarations.doc: `t · t⁻⁴ ≤ t⁻²` for `t ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armPlayCount_le_add_sum_indicator
declarations.doc: Pointwise domination of the play count of a suboptimal arm `i` under UCB1: after `ℓ` plays, every further play at a time `t ∈ [K, T)` is witnessed by a deviation of the prefix average of the optimal arm or of arm `i` at the confidence radius `√(2 log t / s)`, for some count `s ∈ [1, t]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_measureReal_ucb_deviation_le
declarations.doc: The probabilities of the UCB1 deviation events at time `t ≥ 1`, summed over the possible counts `s ∈ [1, t]` of the optimal arm and of arm `i`, are at most `2 t⁻²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_armPlayCount_le_of_ucb
declarations.doc: Expected play count of a suboptimal arm under UCB1 (Auer, Cesa-Bianchi and Fischer): for an arm `i` whose mean is below that of an arm `star` by `Δ > 0`, the expected number of plays of `i` during the first `T` rounds is at most `8 log T / Δ² + 3`. The reward table has independent entries in `[0,1]` almost surely, with a common mean along each arm; the arm process plays each arm once during the first `K` rounds and afterwards an arm of maximal UCB1 index.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_armPlayCount
declarations.doc: Play counts of a measurable arm process are integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_range_comp_eq_sum_mul_armPlayCount
declarations.doc: A sum over rounds of a function of the arm played, regrouped by arms.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_regret_le_of_ucb
declarations.doc: GAPS 107.50: UCB1 regret, with prefix rewards and all tie choices explicit. For a reward table with independent entries in `[0,1]` almost surely and mean `μ i` along arm `i`, an arm process that plays each arm once during the first `K` rounds and afterwards an arm of maximal UCB1 index has expected regret against an optimal arm `star` at most `8 ∑_{μ i < μ star} log T / Δᵢ + (1 + π²/3) ∑ᵢ Δᵢ`, where `Δᵢ = μ star - μ i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.matrixQuadraticForm
declarations.doc: Quadratic form of a real matrix on Euclidean space.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_matrixQuadraticForm
declarations.doc: A quadratic form `x ↦ xᵀ P x` is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleMean
declarations.doc: Mean of a finite Euclidean sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.scatterMatrix
declarations.doc: Centered scatter matrix of a finite Euclidean sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianNegLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: Negative Gaussian log-likelihood up to its constant term.

declarations.name: CKSD.simpleRandomSampleDesign
declarations.doc: Simple random sampling without replacement: the uniform law on the subsets of size `n` of a population of `N` units. It is a probability measure when `n ≤ N`.

declarations.name: CKSD.populationMean
declarations.doc: Finite-population mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.populationVariance
declarations.doc: Finite-population variance with divisor `N-1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLatinSquare
declarations.doc: A Latin square of order `s`: every symbol occurs exactly once in each row and in each column.

declarations.name: CKSD.OrthogonalLatinSquares
declarations.doc: Two Latin squares are orthogonal when superposing them gives every ordered pair of symbols exactly once.

declarations.name: CKSD.matrix_inv_smul_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc: Inversion commutes with nonzero real scalar multiplication, `(c • A)⁻¹ = c⁻¹ • A⁻¹`, for invertible and singular matrices alike.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_rpow_betaMeasure
declarations.doc: The positive real-power moment of a Beta variable.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_beta_rpow_pow
declarations.doc: A growing-shape Beta variable raised to its first shape has the moments of an exponentiated negative Gamma variable in the limit.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_beta_rpow
declarations.doc: The transformed growing-shape Beta variables converge weakly to an exponentiated Gamma law.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_of_exp_neg_gamma
declarations.doc: Convergence of exponentiated negative variables to an exponentiated Gamma law implies convergence of the variables themselves; positive closed tails handle the logarithmic endpoint.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_neg_mul_log_beta
declarations.doc: Growing-shape Beta logarithms have a Gamma limit with the exact unit rate.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_beta_rpow_pow_of_ratio
declarations.doc: The growing-shape Beta power moment limit permits any asymptotically equal power scale.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_pi_beta
declarations.doc: Positive Beta factors give a probability measure on their finite product.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_beta_product_rpow
declarations.doc: Finite products of asymptotically equal-scale Beta powers have an exponentiated Gamma limit.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_neg_mul_log_beta_product
declarations.doc: The logarithm of a finite independent Beta product converges to a Gamma law when the first shapes share a growing common scale; the limiting shape is the sum of second shapes.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockIndependenceRatio
declarations.doc: The determinant ratio for independence of two consecutive coordinate blocks.

declarations.name: CKSD.submatrix_finSumFinEquiv_eq_fromBlocks
declarations.doc: A Hermitian matrix reindexed as a sum is the matrix of its two principal blocks.

declarations.name: CKSD.det_eq_mul_det_principalBlocks_of_zero
declarations.doc: The determinant of a Hermitian block-diagonal matrix factors into its block determinants.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockIndependenceRatio_mem_Ioc
declarations.doc: The positive-definite block determinant ratio lies in the unit interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockIndependenceRatio_smul
declarations.doc: Nonzero rescaling leaves the block determinant ratio invariant.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_blockIndependenceRatio
declarations.doc: The block determinant ratio is a Borel measurable matrix statistic.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_blockIndependenceRatio_sampleCovarianceMatrix_eq_wishart
declarations.doc: The block determinant ratio of Gaussian sample covariance has its scatter Wishart law.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_blockIndependenceRatio_wishart_eq_beta_product
declarations.doc: The block-independence Wishart determinant ratio has a finite independent Beta-product law.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_block_independence_of_beta_product_laws
declarations.doc: A block determinant-ratio Beta law gives its chi-squared likelihood-ratio limit.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_blockIndependenceRatio_pow_wishartGramMeasure
declarations.doc: A block-ratio moment is a product of inverse block moments after a determinant tilt.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_negative_natCast_det_shift_wishartGramMeasure
declarations.doc: The shifted inverse determinant moment is valid for every natural tilt order.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_blockIndependenceRatio_pow_wishartGramMeasure_eq_gamma
declarations.doc: The natural moments of the block determinant ratio are the shifted Wilks Gamma quotient.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_blockIndependence_beta_product_pow_eq_gamma
declarations.doc: The Beta product with block-independence shapes has the same Gamma quotient.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_pair_symmetricCongruenceLinearMap_wishartGramMeasure
declarations.doc: Orthogonal Gaussian coordinate groups give independent Wishart congruence images.

declarations.name: CKSD.coe_symmetricCongruenceLinearMap_submatrix_one
declarations.doc: Congruence by selected identity rows reads off the corresponding principal submatrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_pair_principalBlocks_wishartGramMeasure
declarations.doc: Distinct uncorrelated groups of coordinates have independent principal Wishart blocks.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateGamma_block_ratio
declarations.doc: The Gamma quotient for a block determinant ratio reduces to a shifted Wilks quotient.

declarations.name: CKSD.wishartNormalizer_shift_ratio
declarations.doc: The determinant tilt normalizer separates into its scalar, scale and Gamma factors.

declarations.name: CKSD.wishartNormalizer_block_ratio_mul_negative_moments
declarations.doc: Block-diagonal scale factors cancel against the shifted inverse determinant moments.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearCombinationCorrelation
declarations.doc: The correlation of `aᵀU` and `bᵀV` for covariance blocks `Suu`, `Suv`, `Svv`.

declarations.name: CKSD.canonicalCorrelationMatrix
declarations.doc: The whitened cross-covariance `Σ_UU^{-1/2} Σ_UV Σ_VV^{-1/2}`, whose singular values are the canonical correlations.

declarations.name: CKSD.transpose_inv_sqrt_of_posSemidef
declarations.doc: For a real positive semidefinite matrix `S`, the inverse `(S^{1/2})⁻¹` of its square root is symmetric.

declarations.name: CKSD.inv_sqrt_mul_inv_sqrt_of_posSemidef
declarations.doc: For a real positive semidefinite matrix `S`, `(S^{1/2})⁻¹ (S^{1/2})⁻¹ = S⁻¹`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUnit_det_inv_sqrt_of_posDef
declarations.doc: The inverse square root of a real positive definite matrix is invertible.

declarations.name: CKSD.inv_sqrt_mul_mul_inv_sqrt_of_posDef
declarations.doc: The whitening identity `Σ^{-1/2} Σ Σ^{-1/2} = 1` for a real positive definite `Σ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.charpoly_canonicalCorrelationMatrix_mul_transpose
declarations.doc: The squared canonical correlations are the roots of the characteristic polynomial of `Σ_UU⁻¹ Σ_UV Σ_VV⁻¹ Σ_VU`.

declarations.name: CKSD.charpoly_canonicalCorrelationMatrix_transform
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.29: canonical correlations are unchanged by nonsingular linear transformations `U ↦ P U` and `V ↦ Q V`; the characteristic polynomial of `M Mᵀ`, whose roots are the squared canonical correlations, is invariant.

declarations.name: CKSD.canonicalCorrelationMatrix_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc: The whitened cross-covariance vanishes exactly when the cross-covariance does.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_elim_dotProduct_fromBlocks_mulVec
declarations.doc: The quadratic form of a block matrix on a block vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_dotProduct_mulVec_le_of_posSemidef_fromBlocks
declarations.doc: Cauchy–Schwarz for the cross block of a positive semidefinite block matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_euclideanSpace_eq_sqrt_dotProduct
declarations.doc: The Euclidean norm as the square root of the dot product.

declarations.name: CKSD.dotProduct_mulVec_self_le
declarations.doc: The squared L2 operator-norm bound for a real matrix, in dot-product form.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_dotProduct_self_eq_one_and_mulVec_eq_norm
declarations.doc: The L2 operator norm of a real matrix with a nonempty column index is attained on a unit vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.canonicalCorrelationMatrix_whitening
declarations.doc: Whitening identities for canonical correlations: with `a = Σ_UU^{-1/2} x` and `b = Σ_VV^{-1/2} y`, the cross form becomes `xᵀ K y` and the variances become `‖x‖²`, `‖y‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_canonicalCorrelationMatrix_le_one
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.29: for a positive semidefinite joint covariance with positive definite diagonal blocks, the canonical correlations lie in `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isGreatest_linearCombinationCorrelation
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.29: the largest correlation between linear combinations `aᵀU` and `bᵀV` is the largest singular value (the L2 operator norm) of `Σ_UU^{-1/2} Σ_UV Σ_VV^{-1/2}`, and it is attained. The characterization of the subsequent canonical correlations under successive uncorrelatedness constraints is not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.firstBlockSelection
declarations.doc: Selection of the first `p` coordinates of `ℝ^{p+q}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.secondBlockSelection
declarations.doc: Selection of the last `q` coordinates of `ℝ^{p+q}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_gaussian_blocks_iff_canonicalCorrelationMatrix_eq_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.29: for a jointly Gaussian pair `(U, V)` with positive definite marginal covariances, `U` and `V` are independent exactly when all canonical correlations vanish.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_potentialOutcome_eq_sum_stratumOutcomeMean
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.47, finite-stratum potential-outcome identification under mean ignorability: if every covariate stratum and every treatment stratum `{X = x, A = a}` has positive probability and `E[Y(a) | X = x, A = a] = E[Y(a) | X = x]` (written without division), then `E[Y(a)] = ∑ₓ P(X = x) E[Y(a) | X = x, A = a]` (the adjustment formula).

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_potentialOutcome_eq_integral_div_propensity
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.47, inverse-propensity weighting: under the hypotheses of `integral_potentialOutcome_eq_sum_stratumOutcomeMean`, `E[Y(a)] = E[1{A = a} Y / e_a(X)]` with the observed outcome `Y = Y(A)` and the stratum propensity `e_a(x) = P(A = a | X = x)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_treatmentEffectInfluence_sub_eq_sum_mul
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.49, finite-stratum double-robustness bias identity. The causal identification and cross-fitting conclusions require the additional frameworks described in the source; this is the observable-moment identity. For working outcome regressions `a₁`, `a₀` and a working propensity `e` with values in `(0, 1)`, true stratum outcome means `m₁`, `m₀` and true propensity `e₀ = stratumPropensity P X A`, the bias of the augmented inverse-probability-weighted functional is `∑ₓ P(X = x) (e(x) - e₀(x)) ((a₁ - m₁)(x) / e(x) + (a₀ - m₀)(x) / (1 - e(x)))`; it vanishes when either the outcome regressions or the propensity are correct.

declarations.name: CKSD.instrumentStratumMean
declarations.doc: The mean of `f` on the instrument stratum `{Z = z}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.wald_ratio_eq_complier_average_effect
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.50: the Wald ratio identifies the complier average effect. For a binary instrument `Z` independent of the potential treatments `A z` and potential outcomes `Y a`, with monotonicity `A 0 ≤ A 1` and both instrument values of positive probability, the ratio of the instrument-stratum contrasts of the observed outcome `Y(A(Z))` and of the observed treatment `A(Z)` equals `E[Y 1 - Y 0 | A 0 = 0, A 1 = 1]`, the average effect on compliers. When the first-stage contrast vanishes both sides are zero, by the convention `x / 0 = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.treatmentEffectInfluence
declarations.doc: The efficient influence function of the average treatment effect at the observation `(x, a, y)`, for outcome regressions `m₀`, `m₁`, propensity score `e`, and effect `ate`: `m₁(x) - m₀(x) - ate + a (y - m₁(x)) / e(x) - (1 - a) (y - m₀(x)) / (1 - e(x))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.propensityScore
declarations.doc: The propensity score `e(X) = P(A = 1 | X)`, as a conditional expectation on the original sample space with respect to the σ-algebra generated by `X`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_propensityScore
declarations.doc: The propensity score of a measurable covariate is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.condIndepFun_propensityScore
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.48: the propensity score is a balancing score, `A ⫫ X | e(X)`, in the standard Borel setting.

declarations.name: CKSD.condIndepFun_of_propensityScore
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.48: ignorability descends from the covariates to their propensity score: if `Y ⫫ A | X`, then `Y ⫫ A | e(X)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.treatmentStratum
declarations.doc: The joint covariate-stratum and treatment event `{X = x, A = a}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.stratumOutcomeMean
declarations.doc: The observed conditional outcome mean `E[Y | X = x, A = a]` in a treatment stratum.

declarations.name: CKSD.stratumOutcomeVariance
declarations.doc: The observed conditional outcome variance `Var(Y | X = x, A = a)` in a treatment stratum.

declarations.name: CKSD.stratumPropensity
declarations.doc: The propensity `P(A = 1 | X = x)` in a covariate stratum.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteStrataTreatmentEffect
declarations.doc: The identified average treatment effect `E[m₁(X) - m₀(X)]` of an observed law with finitely many covariate strata.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteStrataTreatmentInfluence
declarations.doc: The treatment-effect influence function evaluated at the observed stratum nuisances.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_treatmentStratum
declarations.doc: Treatment strata are measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_eq_sum_treatmentStratum
declarations.doc: An integral splits over the finite partition into treatment strata.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_comp_treatmentStratum
declarations.doc: Integral of a function of the stratum labels.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_covariateStratum_eq_add
declarations.doc: The covariate stratum splits into its two treatment strata.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_finiteStrataTreatmentInfluence
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.56: the treatment-effect influence function in finite strata has mean zero. Positive joint stratum masses express overlap explicitly.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_finiteStrataTreatmentInfluence
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.56: the variance of the treatment-effect influence function in finite strata (the semiparametric efficiency bound) is `Var(m₁(X) - m₀(X)) + E[σ₁²(X) / e(X) + σ₀²(X) / (1 - e(X))]`, with `mₐ`, `σₐ²` the stratum outcome means and variances and `e` the stratum propensity. Positive joint stratum masses express overlap explicitly.

declarations.name: CKSD.setIntegral_withDensity_score_tilt
declarations.doc: Set integrals against a nonnegative linear score tilt of a measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteStrataTreatmentInfluence_eqOn
declarations.doc: On each treatment stratum the influence function is affine in the outcome.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasDerivAt_finiteStrataTreatmentEffect_score_tilt
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.56: the treatment-effect influence function represents derivatives along bounded mean-zero score tilts of the observed law: for a bounded measurable score `s` with `E[s] = 0` and the tilted laws `dP_t = (1 + t s) dP`, the functional `t ↦ τ(P_t)` has derivative `E[φ s]` at `t = 0`. The semiparametric convolution bound is not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_eval_of_uniform_on_balls
declarations.doc: Uniform convergence in probability on every norm ball may be evaluated at random points whose norms are bounded in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_convex_minValue
declarations.doc: For random convex functions with identity quadratic limit and tight random linear score, their minimum values are asymptotically minus one half of the squared score norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_convex_deviance
declarations.doc: A convex likelihood process with an identity quadratic approximation and asymptotically standard Gaussian score has chi-squared deviance between its full and subspace-constrained minima, with degrees of freedom equal to the codimension of the subspace.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_glm_whitening
declarations.doc: A positive definite information matrix and positive dispersion admit an invertible linear whitening change of coordinates, with the corresponding score and quadratic identities.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_simple_matrix_eigenvalue_sub_rayleigh_le
declarations.doc: Matrix form of the simple-eigenvalue quadratic remainder.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_matrix_le_card_mul_entrySum
declarations.doc: The Euclidean operator norm is bounded by the dimension times the entrywise sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.simple_empirical_covariance_eigenvalue_asymptotics
declarations.doc: A simple ordered empirical covariance eigenvalue has the scalar Rayleigh central limit law.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_sq_inner_gaussian_eigenvector
declarations.doc: Variance of the squared centered Gaussian eigenvector coordinate.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsChordalGraph
declarations.doc: A chordal (decomposable) graph: every cycle of length at least four has a chord, an edge between two vertices of the cycle that are not consecutive on it.

declarations.name: CKSD.GraphSeparates
declarations.doc: `S` separates `A` from `B` in an undirected graph: every walk from `A` to `B` meets `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.cliqueSeparator
declarations.doc: The separator `C_j ∩ (C₀ ∪ ⋯ ∪ C_{j-1})` of a sequence of cliques.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPerfectCliqueSequence
declarations.doc: A perfect sequence of the maximal cliques of `G`: every maximal clique occurs exactly once, and each separator is contained in an earlier clique.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsUndirectedGlobalMarkovMass
declarations.doc: The undirected global Markov property for a probability mass function: separation of disjoint sets implies conditional independence.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_maximal_isClique_superset
declarations.doc: In a finite graph every clique lies in a maximal clique.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUndirectedGlobalMarkovMass_of_factorization
declarations.doc: The undirected global Markov property follows from a factorization of the mass function into factors each depending only on the coordinates in a clique.

declarations.name: CKSD.cliqueHistory
declarations.doc: The union `C₀ ∪ ⋯ ∪ C_{m-1}` of the first `m` cliques of a sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.graphSeparates_cliqueSeparator
declarations.doc: For a perfect sequence of the maximal cliques, the separator `S_j` separates the new vertices `C_j \ S_j` from the earlier vertices `(C₀ ∪ ⋯ ∪ C_{j-1}) \ S_j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.clique_factorization_of_isUndirectedGlobalMarkovMass
declarations.doc: For a perfect sequence of the maximal cliques, the global Markov property implies the clique factorization of the marginal masses.

declarations.name: CKSD.isUndirectedGlobalMarkovMass_iff_clique_factorization
