declarations.doc: GAPS 105.36, discrete form: for a decomposable graph with a perfect sequence of its maximal cliques, a positive probability mass function is globally Markov exactly when `p(x) = ∏_C p_C(x_C) / ∏_S p_S(x_S)^{ν(S)}`, written here without division.

declarations.name: CKSD.principalBlock
declarations.doc: The block `B_{CC}` of a square matrix indexed by a finite set `C` of coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.padBlock
declarations.doc: `[B]^V`: a matrix indexed by `C`, padded with zeros to a square matrix indexed by `ι`.

declarations.name: CKSD.decomposableConcentrationMLE
declarations.doc: The explicit maximum likelihood estimate of the concentration matrix in a decomposable Gaussian graphical model with perfect sequence of cliques `C`: `n (∑_C [(ssd_C)⁻¹]^V - ∑_S ν(S) [(ssd_S)⁻¹]^V)`, the separators being counted with multiplicity.

declarations.name: CKSD.log_det_add_card_lt_log_det_add_trace_mul_inv
declarations.doc: Strict form of the Gaussian covariance criterion on a general finite index type: for positive definite `S ≠ C`, `log det S + dim < log det C + tr(S C⁻¹)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isConcentrationMLE_inv_of_apply_eq
declarations.doc: Sufficiency of the likelihood equations: if `Σ` is positive definite, agrees with `ssd / n` on the diagonal and on the edges of `G`, and `Σ⁻¹` vanishes off the edges, then `Σ⁻¹` is the maximum likelihood estimate of the concentration matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_pos_posSemidef_sub_smul_one
declarations.doc: A positive definite matrix dominates a positive multiple of the identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_isConcentrationMLE_inv
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.36, general graph: if `ssd` is positive definite and `n > 0`, there is a unique positive definite `Σ̂` that agrees with `ssd / n` on the diagonal and on the edges and whose inverse is the maximum likelihood estimate of the concentration matrix (in particular `Σ̂⁻¹` vanishes off the edges). Convergence of iterative proportional scaling is not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.isConcentrationMLE_decomposableConcentrationMLE
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.36, Gaussian decomposable model: for a perfect sequence `C` of the maximal cliques of `G` (so that `G` is decomposable) and `n > 0` observations, if every clique block of the sum-of-squares matrix `ssd` is positive definite (which holds almost surely when `n > max_C |C|` for a Gaussian sample), the maximum likelihood estimate of the concentration matrix exists, is unique, and equals `n (∑_C [(ssd_C)⁻¹]^V - ∑_S ν(S) [(ssd_S)⁻¹]^V)`. The likelihood involves `ssd` only through its clique blocks, so no condition on `ssd` outside them is needed. The almost-sure existence criterion `n > max_C |C|` as a necessary condition is not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.designInformationMatrix
declarations.doc: The information matrix `M(a) = ∑ᵢ aᵢ fᵢ fᵢᵀ` of a design with weights `a` on a finite design space whose points have regression vectors `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.designInformationMatrix_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The information matrix is the weighted sum `∑ᵢ aᵢ fᵢ fᵢᵀ` of rank-one matrices.

declarations.name: CKSD.trace_designInformationMatrix_mul
declarations.doc: `tr(M(a) N) = ∑ᵢ aᵢ fᵢᵀ N fᵢ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.posSemidef_designInformationMatrix
declarations.doc: The information matrix of a design with nonnegative weights is positive semidefinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.kiefer_wolfowitz_equivalence
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.37, Kiefer–Wolfowitz equivalence for a finite design space: a probability design `w` with nonsingular information matrix maximizes `det M(a)` over all probability designs if and only if `fᵢᵀ M(w)⁻¹ fᵢ ≤ p` at every design point, with equality at the points of positive weight.

declarations.name: CKSD.randomizationPValue
declarations.doc: The randomization p-value of arrangement `i`: the total randomization weight of the arrangements `j` whose statistic `T j` is at least `T i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_ite_randomizationPValue_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.38, conservative finite randomization p-values, including ties: for nonnegative randomization weights `w` (of total mass at most one, in applications) and `0 ≤ α`, the total weight of the arrangements whose randomization p-value is at most `α` is at most `α`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fisher_inequality
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.42, Fisher's inequality: in a balanced incomplete block design on `v` points with `b` blocks of size `k < v`, every point in `r > 0` blocks and every pair of distinct points in `ell` blocks, there are at least as many blocks as points, `v ≤ b`.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_le_sub_one_of_orthogonalLatinSquares
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.44, the upper bound on a family of mutually orthogonal Latin squares: there are at most `s - 1` pairwise orthogonal Latin squares of order `s ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_orthogonalLatinSquares_of_equiv
declarations.doc: Over a finite field `F` identified with `Fin s`, the squares `(x, y) ↦ a x + y` for the nonzero elements `a` form a complete family of mutually orthogonal Latin squares.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_orthogonalLatinSquares_of_isPrimePow
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.44, existence of a complete family at prime-power orders: for a prime power `s` there are `s - 1` pairwise orthogonal Latin squares of order `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.TripleStatus
declarations.doc: Status of the middle vertex `b` of consecutive trail vertices `a, b, c`: if `b` is a collider (`a → b ← c`) it must satisfy `P`, otherwise it must satisfy `N`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith
declarations.doc: A trail `q 0, …, q n` whose interior colliders satisfy `P` and whose interior noncolliders satisfy `N`. Repeated vertices are allowed.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.MemAncestorClosure
declarations.doc: A vertex lies in `C` or is an ancestor of a vertex of `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.ForwardReach
declarations.doc: A directed path from `v` to a vertex of `T` whose vertices after `v` avoid `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.trailAppend
declarations.doc: Concatenation of a trail `q₁` of length `n₁` with a trail `q₂`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_edge_self
declarations.doc: A directed acyclic graph has no loops.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_edge_of_edge
declarations.doc: A directed acyclic graph has no two-cycles.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.tripleStatus_of_edge_right
declarations.doc: The middle vertex of a triple is a noncollider when it has an arrow towards its right neighbour.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.tripleStatus_of_edge_left
declarations.doc: The middle vertex of a triple is a noncollider when it has an arrow towards its left neighbour.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.tripleStatus_comm
declarations.doc: The status of a triple does not depend on its orientation.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.trailAppend_of_le
declarations.doc: `trailAppend` agrees with the first trail up to its length.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.trailAppend_of_ge
declarations.doc: `trailAppend` agrees with the shifted second trail from the junction on.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith.rev
declarations.doc: The reverse of a trail is a trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith.shift
declarations.doc: A suffix of a trail, shifted to start at `0`, is a trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith.trunc
declarations.doc: A prefix of a trail is a trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith.append
declarations.doc: Concatenation of two trails meeting at a vertex with admissible status is a trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsTrailWith.snoc
declarations.doc: Extending a trail by one adjacent vertex, with an admissible status at the old endpoint, gives a trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isTrailWith_of_forward
declarations.doc: A forward directed chain is a trail whose interior vertices are all noncolliders.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isDescendant_of_forward
declarations.doc: Along a forward directed chain every later vertex is a descendant of the first.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_forward_of_isDescendant
declarations.doc: A nonempty directed path is a forward chain.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.forwardReach_of_not_memAncestorClosure
declarations.doc: If `v` lies outside the ancestral closure of `C` and is `t ∈ T` or an ancestor of some `t ∈ T`, then a directed path from `v` reaches `T` avoiding `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.tripleStatus_of_loop
declarations.doc: Junction step of the shortening argument: cutting a loop `q i = q j` out of an active trail leaves an admissible status at the junction.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_injective_activeTrail
declarations.doc: An active trail can be shortened to an injective active trail with the same endpoints.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isActivePath_of_isTrailWith
declarations.doc: An injective active trail is an active path.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_collider_of_forward_backward
declarations.doc: On a trail that leaves `q i` along an outgoing arrow and arrives at `q j` against an arrow out of `q j`, some interior vertex `q m` with `i < m < j` is a collider descending from `q i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isTrailWith_of_isActivePath
declarations.doc: An active path, read as a function on `ℕ`, is an injective active trail.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_activeTrail_of_semiActive
declarations.doc: A trail between `A` and `B` whose noncolliders avoid `C` and whose colliders lie in a set `D` all of whose vertices outside the ancestral closure of `C` are ancestors of `A ∪ B` (or lie in it) can be modified into an active trail between `A` and `B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.DSeparated.false_of_isTrailWith
declarations.doc: If `A` and `B` are d-separated by `C`, there is no active trail (repetitions allowed) from a vertex of `A` to a vertex of `B`: such a trail can be shortened to an active path. This is the bridge between trails on `ℕ` and the paths on `Fin (n + 1)` of `CausalGraph.IsActivePath`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.false_of_dSeparated_of_semiActiveTrail
declarations.doc: If `A` and `B` are d-separated by `C`, there is no trail between `A` and `B` whose noncolliders avoid `C` and whose colliders lie in a set `D` all of whose vertices outside the ancestral closure of `C` are ancestors of `A ∪ B` or lie in it.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph
declarations.doc: Finite directed acyclic causal graph; acyclicity excludes every nonempty directed cycle.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.parents
declarations.doc: Parents of a vertex in a causal graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsDescendant
declarations.doc: Proper descendant relation in a causal graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsActivePath
declarations.doc: A path `p 0, …, p n` (pairwise distinct vertices, consecutive ones adjacent) is active given `Z` when every interior collider `p (i-1) → p i ← p (i+1)` lies in `Z` or has a descendant in `Z`, and every interior noncollider lies outside `Z`. The endpoints are not constrained.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.DSeparated
declarations.doc: `Z` d-separates `A` from `B` when no path from a vertex of `A` to a vertex of `B` is active given `Z`. The sets need not be disjoint; see the module docstring for the resulting conventions (`A ∩ B ≠ ∅` excludes d-separation, endpoints in `Z` do not block).

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.MarkovEquivalent
declarations.doc: Two causal graphs are Markov equivalent if all their d-separation statements agree. The quantification is over all triples of vertex sets; by the reduction described in the module docstring this is equivalent to agreement on pairwise disjoint triples.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.Adjacent
declarations.doc: Undirected skeleton adjacency.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsUnshieldedCollider
declarations.doc: An unshielded collider is an inward-facing triple with nonadjacent endpoints.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.RespectsParents
declarations.doc: Local mass functions respect the parents of `G`: the local mass of `v` depends on the configuration only through its values at the parents of `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.directedFactorizationMass
declarations.doc: Recursive product mass `∏_v k_v(x_v | x)` from local conditional masses `k_v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass
declarations.doc: Truncated factorization for the intervention `do(X_A = a_A)`: zero unless `x` agrees with `a` on `A`, and otherwise the product of the local masses over the vertices outside `A`.

declarations.name: CKSD.markovEquivalent_iff_skeleton_and_colliders
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.67 (Verma–Pearl): two directed acyclic graphs on a finite vertex set are Markov equivalent if and only if they have the same skeleton (adjacency relation) and the same unshielded colliders.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.markovEquivalent_refl
declarations.doc: Graphical Markov equivalence is reflexive.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.parentFinset
declarations.doc: Parents of a vertex, as a finite set.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.nonDescendantFinset
declarations.doc: Nondescendants of a vertex other than the vertex itself and its parents.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.removeIncoming
declarations.doc: The graph with all arrows into `X` removed (`G_{\bar X}`).

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.removeOutgoing
declarations.doc: The graph with all arrows out of `Z` removed (`G_{\underline Z}`).

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.InterceptsDirectedPaths
declarations.doc: A directed path from a vertex of `X` to a vertex of `Y` has some vertex in `Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.BlocksBackdoorPaths
declarations.doc: Every back-door path from `X` to `Y`, that is, every path whose first arrow points into its initial vertex in `X`, is blocked by `W`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsBackdoorSet
declarations.doc: The back-door criterion for `Z` relative to `(X, Y)`: no vertex of `Z` is a descendant of a vertex of `X`, and `Z` blocks every back-door path from `X` to `Y`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsFrontdoorSet
declarations.doc: The front-door criterion for `Z` relative to `(X, Y)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsProbabilityMass
declarations.doc: A probability mass function on configurations.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLocalMassFamily
declarations.doc: Local conditional mass functions: each is a probability mass function in the state of its vertex, for every configuration of the other variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass
declarations.doc: Probability that the variables in `B` take the values of `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condMass
declarations.doc: Conditional probability that the variables in `B` take the values of `x`, given that the variables in `C` take the values of `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CondIndepMass
declarations.doc: Conditional independence of `X_A` and `X_B` given `X_C` for a mass function, in product form (no division).

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.RecursivelyFactorizes
declarations.doc: Recursive factorization `p(x) = ∏_v p(x_v | x_{pa(v)})`, with the conditional masses of `p` itself.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsLocalDirectedMarkov
declarations.doc: The local directed Markov property: each variable is conditionally independent of its nondescendants given its parents.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsGlobalDirectedMarkov
declarations.doc: The global directed Markov property: d-separation of disjoint sets implies conditional independence.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsFaithful
declarations.doc: A mass function is faithful to `G` when its conditional independences among disjoint sets are exactly the d-separations of `G`.

declarations.name: CKSD.overwriteOn
declarations.doc: Overwrite a configuration on `B` by values indexed by `B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.doMarginalMass
declarations.doc: Interventional probability that the variables in `B` take the values of `y`, under `do(X = x)` given by the truncated factorization.

declarations.name: CKSD.condDoMass
declarations.doc: Interventional conditional probability `P(y | do(x), w)`, all values read from `b`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_adjacent_self
declarations.doc: No vertex is adjacent to itself in a directed acyclic graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.Adjacent.ne
declarations.doc: Adjacent vertices are distinct.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.Adjacent.symm
declarations.doc: Adjacency is symmetric.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.Adjacent.not_dSeparated
declarations.doc: Adjacent vertices are joined by an active path of length one, whatever is conditioned on.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsActivePath.rev
declarations.doc: The reverse of an active path is active.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.DSeparated.symm
declarations.doc: d-separation is symmetric.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isDescendant_of_isActivePath_parents
declarations.doc: A path leaving `u` along an outgoing arrow and active given the parents of `u` is a directed path out of `u`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.dSeparated_parents_of_not_isDescendant
declarations.doc: A vertex `u` is d-separated by its parents from every other vertex that is neither a parent nor a descendant of `u`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_ite_prod_eq_sum_ite_prod_compl
declarations.doc: Summing out the coordinates of a set closed under children: the factors of the summed vertices disappear, the coordinates are frozen at those of `x`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_ite_mul_sum_ite_of_factor
declarations.doc: Conditional independence from a factorization `g = F * H` with `F` depending only on the coordinates in `R ∪ C` and `H` only on those outside `R`.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_directedFactorizationMass_eq_of_isAncestral
declarations.doc: Marginalizing a recursive product onto a set `E` inside an ancestral set `D` (closed under parents): the coordinates outside `D` may be frozen at those of `x` and their factors dropped.

declarations.name: CKSD.condIndepMass_directedFactorizationMass_of_dSeparated
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.62 (core step): a mass function that factorizes recursively along a directed acyclic graph, with local masses respecting the parents, satisfies the global directed Markov property: d-separation of disjoint sets implies conditional independence.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.dSeparated_parents_of_not_adjacent
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.70: two nonadjacent distinct vertices of a directed acyclic graph are d-separated by the parents of one of them.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.adjacent_iff_forall_not_dSeparated
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.70: two distinct vertices are adjacent if and only if no set of other vertices d-separates them.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isCollider_iff_notMem_of_dSeparated
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.70: in a skeleton path `u - v - w` with distinct endpoints, if `S` d-separates `u` and `w`, then `u → v ← w` exactly when `v ∉ S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.dSeparated_singleton_iff_of_isFaithful
declarations.doc: For a mass function faithful to `G` and to `H`, d-separation of two distinct vertices by a set avoiding them is the same in both graphs.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.adjacent_iff_of_isFaithful
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.70: the conditional independences of a mass function faithful to two directed acyclic graphs determine the skeleton: the two graphs have the same adjacencies.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsUnshieldedCollider.of_isFaithful
declarations.doc: An unshielded collider of `G` is an unshielded collider of `H` when the mass function is faithful to both graphs.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isUnshieldedCollider_iff_of_isFaithful
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.70: the conditional independences of a mass function faithful to two directed acyclic graphs determine the unshielded colliders; together with `CKSD.CausalGraph.adjacent_iff_of_isFaithful` and the Verma–Pearl theorem (GAPS 105.67) they determine the Markov equivalence class. The statement on the PC algorithm is not formalized.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.nonAncestorPart
declarations.doc: The vertices of `Z` that are not ancestors of any vertex of `W` in `G_{\bar X}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.augment
declarations.doc: The graph augmented by an intervention indicator `none` with an arrow into each vertex of `Z`; the original vertices are `some v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.augment_edge_some
declarations.doc: Arrows between original vertices of the augmented graph are the arrows of the graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.augment_edge_none
declarations.doc: The intervention indicator points exactly into the vertices of `Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.augment_not_edge_to_none
declarations.doc: No arrow points into the intervention indicator.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.isDescendant_of_augment
declarations.doc: Descendants among the original vertices of the augmented graph are descendants in the graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.augmentedLocalMass
declarations.doc: Local masses on the augmented graph: the indicator `none` is uniform on `{s₀, s₁}`; when it equals `s₁` the vertices of `Z` are set to the values of `b`, otherwise all vertices follow the local masses after `do(X = b)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isLocalMassFamily_augmentedLocalMass
declarations.doc: The augmented local masses form a local mass family.

declarations.name: CKSD.respectsParents_augmentedLocalMass
declarations.doc: The augmented local masses respect the parents of the augmented graph of `G_{\bar X}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.directedFactorizationMass_augmentedLocalMass
declarations.doc: The recursive product of the augmented local masses: the indicator mass times the law under `do(X ∪ Z)` (indicator `s₁`) or under `do(X)` (any other value).

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_augmented
declarations.doc: Marginal masses of the augmented mass, at a point with indicator value `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.transGen_removeIncoming_nonAncestorPart
declarations.doc: A directed path of `G_{\bar X}` ending in `W` survives the removal of the arrows into the vertices of `Z` that are not ancestors of `W` in `G_{\bar X}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_isDescendant_removeIncoming_mem
declarations.doc: In `G_{\bar X}` no vertex is a proper ancestor of a vertex of `X`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.dSeparated_augment_of_rule_three
declarations.doc: The graph-theoretic step of rule 3: if `Y` and `Z` are d-separated by `X ∪ W` in `G_{\bar X, \overline{Z(W)}}`, then `Y` and the intervention indicator are d-separated by `X ∪ W` in the augmented graph of `G_{\bar X}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condDoMass_rule_three
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.64, rule 3 of the do-calculus (insertion and deletion of actions): if `Y` and `Z` are d-separated by `X ∪ W` in `G_{\bar X, \overline{Z(W)}}`, then `P(y | do(x), do(z), w) = P(y | do(x), w)`. The conditioning events have positive interventional probability. The completeness of the three rules for identifiability is not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_congr_point
declarations.doc: A marginal mass depends only on the values of the point at the fixed coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_nonneg
declarations.doc: Marginal masses of a nonnegative mass function are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_anti
declarations.doc: Marginal masses decrease when more coordinates are fixed.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_union_of_support
declarations.doc: Fixing coordinates on which the mass is concentrated does not change a marginal mass.

declarations.name: CKSD.overwriteOn_of_notMem
declarations.doc: `overwriteOn` leaves the coordinates outside the overwritten set unchanged.

declarations.name: CKSD.overwriteOn_self
declarations.doc: `overwriteOn` with the values of the configuration itself does nothing.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_eq_sum_overwriteOn
declarations.doc: The law of total probability: a marginal mass is the sum, over the values of a disjoint set `Z` of variables, of the marginal masses with `Z` fixed as well.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass_congr
declarations.doc: Interventional masses depend only on the intervention values on the intervened set.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass_empty
declarations.doc: The empty intervention leaves the recursive product mass unchanged.

declarations.name: CKSD.intervenedLocalMass
declarations.doc: Local masses after the intervention `do(X = b)`: point masses at the values of `b` on `X`, the original local masses elsewhere.

declarations.name: CKSD.isLocalMassFamily_intervenedLocalMass
declarations.doc: Intervened local masses form a local mass family.

declarations.name: CKSD.respectsParents_intervenedLocalMass
declarations.doc: Intervened local masses respect the parents in the graph with the arrows into `X` removed.

declarations.name: CKSD.directedFactorizationMass_intervenedLocalMass
declarations.doc: The truncated factorization is the recursive product of the intervened local masses.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass_intervenedLocalMass
declarations.doc: Intervening on `X` after intervening on `Z` is intervening on `X ∪ Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass_nonneg
declarations.doc: Interventional masses are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.interventionMass_support
declarations.doc: The interventional mass under `do(X = a)` is concentrated on the configurations that agree with `a` on `X`.

declarations.name: CKSD.directedFactorizationMass_nonneg
declarations.doc: Recursive product masses are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_empty_directedFactorizationMass
declarations.doc: A recursive product of local masses has total mass one.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_empty_interventionMass
declarations.doc: An interventional mass has total mass one.

declarations.name: CKSD.div_eq_div_of_condIndepMass
declarations.doc: Conditional independence `Y ⊥ Z | X ∪ W`, for a mass concentrated on one value of `X`, in quotient form: `P(y | z, w) = P(y | w)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.doMarginalMass_eq_marginalMass_of_nonDescendant
declarations.doc: The interventional marginal of variables that are neither in `X` nor descendants of `X` equals their observational marginal.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsActivePath.mono
declarations.doc: An active path in a subgraph is active in the graph.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.dSeparated_removeOutgoing_of_blocksBackdoorPaths
declarations.doc: If every back-door path from `X` to `Y` is blocked by `W`, then in any subgraph with the arrows out of `X` removed, `Y` and `X` are d-separated by `W`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_isDescendant_of_blocksBackdoorPaths
declarations.doc: If every back-door path from `X` to `Z` is blocked by the empty set, then no vertex of `X` is a descendant of a vertex of `Z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.not_isDescendant_removeIncoming_of_intercepts
declarations.doc: If `Z` intercepts all directed paths from `X` to `Y`, then in the graph with the arrows into `Z` removed no vertex of `Y` is a descendant of a vertex of `X`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condDoMass_rule_one
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.64, rule 1 of the do-calculus (insertion and deletion of observations): if `Y` and `Z` are d-separated by `X ∪ W` in `G_{\bar X}`, then `P(y | do(x), z, w) = P(y | do(x), w)`. The conditioning event `{Z = z, W = w}` has positive interventional probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.condDoMass_rule_two
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.64, rule 2 of the do-calculus (action/observation exchange): if `Y` and `Z` are d-separated by `X ∪ W` in `G_{\bar X \underline Z}`, then `P(y | do(x), do(z), w) = P(y | do(x), z, w)`. The event `(z,w)` has positive probability under `do(x)`. The proof compares both sides with the mass in which the children of `Z` read the fixed values of `b` on `Z`; that mass factorizes along `G_{\bar X \underline Z}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.marginalMass_univ
declarations.doc: The marginal mass on all variables is the mass itself.

declarations.name: CKSD.CondIndepMass.mono_right
declarations.doc: The decomposition property of conditional independence: `A ⊥ B | C` implies `A ⊥ B' | C` for `B' ⊆ B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_marginalMass_insert_update
declarations.doc: Summing the marginal mass of `insert v C` over the values of `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.marginalMass_eq_prod_condMass_of_isLocalDirectedMarkov
declarations.doc: Under the local directed Markov property, the marginal mass of an ancestral set is the product of the conditional masses of its vertices given their parents.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.recursivelyFactorizes_of_isLocalDirectedMarkov
declarations.doc: The local directed Markov property implies recursive factorization.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_localMass_of_recursivelyFactorizes
declarations.doc: A recursively factorizing probability mass function is the recursive product of a local mass family respecting the parents.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.recursivelyFactorizes_tfae
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.62: for a probability mass function on finitely many finite-valued variables, recursive factorization along a directed acyclic graph, the local directed Markov property, and the global (d-separation) Markov property are equivalent. Discrete-variable form: densities with respect to counting measure on a finite product.

declarations.name: CKSD.doMarginalMass_eq_backdoor
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.63, back-door formula for discrete variables: if `Z` satisfies the back-door criterion relative to `(X, Y)`, then `P(y | do(x)) = ∑_z P(y | x, z) P(z)` for the law factorizing recursively along `G` with local masses `localMass`. The conditioning events `{X = x, Z = z}` are assumed to have positive probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.doMarginalMass_eq_frontdoor
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.63, front-door formula for discrete variables: if `Z` satisfies the front-door criterion relative to `(X, Y)`, then `P(y | do(x)) = ∑_z P(z | x) ∑_{x'} P(y | x', z) P(x')`. The conditioning events `{X = x}` and `{X = x', Z = z}` are assumed to have positive probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.symmetricMatrixEigenvalues
declarations.doc: Ordered Hermitian eigenvalues, with an explicit zero convention outside the Hermitian locus.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_simple_eigenvalue_sub_rayleigh_le
declarations.doc: A population spectral gap gives a quadratic remainder for a simple ordered eigenvalue.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_norm_sq_add_stdGaussian
declarations.doc: The squared length of a shifted finite-dimensional standard Gaussian has noncentral chi-squared law.

declarations.name: CKSD.nestedFStatistic
declarations.doc: The F statistic of the nested projection models `P₀ ≤ P₁`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNestedModelInvariantTest
declarations.doc: A test is invariant under rescaling, translation within the smaller model space, and the orthogonal maps that commute with both projections.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_nestedFStatistic_eq_noncentralF
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.16: under the larger model the F statistic has the noncentral F law with `r₁ - r₀` and `n - r₁` degrees of freedom and noncentrality `δ² = ‖(P₁ - P₀) μ‖² / σ²`; hence the power of any test based on it depends on `(μ, σ²)` only through `δ²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_nestedFStatistic_eq_fisherSnedecor
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.10, exact null F law for nested Gaussian projection models: for `Y ∼ N(m, v I_n)` with `v > 0` and `m` in the range of the smaller star projection `P₀`, where `P₁ P₀ = P₀` and `rank P₀ < rank P₁ < n`, the F statistic `(‖P₁ Y - P₀ Y‖² / (r₁ - r₀)) / (‖Y - P₁ Y‖² / (n - r₁))` has Fisher's F law with `r₁ - r₀` and `n - r₁` degrees of freedom. This is the case of zero noncentrality of `map_nestedFStatistic_eq_noncentralF`.

declarations.name: CKSD.strictMono_noncentralF_upper_tail
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.16: the power `P(F > c)` of the F test with critical value `c > 0` is strictly increasing in the noncentrality `δ²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fTest_isUniformlyMostPowerful_invariant
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.16: among level-`α` tests invariant under rescaling, translation within the smaller model space, and orthogonal maps of the hypothesis and residual spaces, the F test with critical value `c` (the upper `α` point of the central F law) is uniformly most powerful. The parameter is `(μ, σ²)` with `P₁ μ = μ` and `σ² > 0`; the null hypothesis is `P₀ μ = μ`. The level `α` is defined by the critical value `c`; for `c ≤ 0` it equals `1` and the statement is trivial, so no restriction `0 < α < 1` is imposed. The average-power optimality among similar tests is not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.factorCovariance
declarations.doc: Covariance `L Lᵀ + diag ψ` of an orthogonal factor model with loadings `L` and unique variances `ψ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.factorLikelihoodCriterion
declarations.doc: The Gaussian covariance criterion `log det Σ + tr(C Σ⁻¹)` at `Σ = L Lᵀ + diag ψ`, for a sample covariance `C`; it is the negative log-likelihood up to a constant and the factor `n / 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNormalizedFactorLoading
declarations.doc: Normalized loadings: `Lᵀ (diag ψ)⁻¹ L` is a diagonal matrix with distinct positive entries in decreasing order.

declarations.name: CKSD.factorColumnSigns
declarations.doc: The diagonal sign matrix changing the signs of the factor columns `j` with `s j = false`.

declarations.name: CKSD.loadingSignDistance
declarations.doc: Distance between two loading matrices modulo factor-column signs: the least operator norm of `L S - M` over the sign matrices `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.factorCovariance_mul_orthogonal
declarations.doc: Orthogonal rotations of factors do not change their implied covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNormalizedFactorLoading.exists_eq_mul_factorColumnSigns
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.35: normalized loadings are identified up to column signs once both their common covariance `L Lᵀ` and the diagonal unique covariance `diag ψ` are specified: if `L` and `M` are normalized for `ψ` and `L Lᵀ = M Mᵀ`, then `M = L S` for a diagonal sign matrix `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_factor_mle_of_compact
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.35: consistency of factor maximum likelihood on a compact identified parameter set: if the sample covariances `Cₙ` converge in probability to `Σ₀ = L₀ L₀ᵀ + diag ψ₀`, the parameter `(L₀, ψ₀)` lies in a compact set `K` on which the unique variances are bounded below by `a > 0` and on which `Σ₀` determines `ψ₀` and `L₀` up to column signs, then every minimizer `Tₙ` of the criterion over `K` has `ψ̂ₙ → ψ₀` and `L̂ₙ → L₀` modulo column signs, in probability. Compactness and the uniform lower bound on the unique variances are restrictions of this formulation; the unrestricted parameter space and asymptotic normality are not included.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent
declarations.doc: The observed-history event `{L̄_k = l̄_k, Ā_{k-1} = ā_{k-1}}` for a covariate record `l`: the covariates up to time `k` take the recorded values and the treatments before time `k` follow the regime `a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gRegimeEvent
declarations.doc: The regime-adherent past `{L̄_{k-1} = l̄_{k-1}, Ā_{k-1} = ā_{k-1}}` before time `k`; it is the whole space for `k = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent_congr
declarations.doc: History events depend only on the recorded covariates up to the current time.

declarations.name: CKSD.gRegimeEvent_congr
declarations.doc: Regime-adherent pasts depend only on the recorded covariates before the current time.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent_subset_gRegimeEvent
declarations.doc: The history event at time `k` is contained in the regime-adherent past before `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gHistoryEvent_snoc
declarations.doc: Appending the next covariate value splits the regime-adherent past.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_gHistoryEvent
declarations.doc: History events are measurable when the coordinate events are.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurableSet_gRegimeEvent
declarations.doc: Regime-adherent pasts are measurable when the coordinate events are.

declarations.name: CKSD.prod_div_succ_mul_eq_prod_div
declarations.doc: Telescoping of sequential weights: for real weights with the zero pattern of probabilities of nested events, the inverse treatment weights times the final probability equal the product of the conditional covariate probabilities.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_eq_sum_gInverseWeight
declarations.doc: Inverse-probability-weighted representation over the first `n` time points. If at each time `k < N` the potential outcome is mean-exchangeable with the treatment given the observed history, and regime-adherent continuations of histories of positive probability have positive probability, then for `n ≤ N` the mean of `Ya` is the sum over covariate records of the inverse treatment weights times the integral of `Ya` over the regime-adherent event.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_potentialOutcome_eq_gFormula
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.65: the longitudinal g-formula for discrete covariates. Covariates `L t` take values in a finite type and treatments `A t` in any type, at times `t = 0, …, T`; `l` ranges over covariate records `(l_0, …, l_T)`, `Ya` is the potential outcome under the regime `a` and `Y` the observed outcome. Consistency is `Y = Ya` whenever the observed treatments follow the regime. Sequential exchangeability is used in its mean form, `E[Ya 1{A_t = a_t} | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1}] = E[Ya | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1}] P(A_t = a_t | …)`, written without division; it is implied by `Ya ⊥ A_t | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1}`. Sequential positivity is `P(A_t = a_t | H_t, Ā_{t-1} = ā_{t-1}) > 0` for every observed history of positive probability, written as: a regime-adherent continuation of probability zero comes from a history of probability zero (it follows from any uniform lower bound on these conditional probabilities). The `t = 0` factor of the product is `P(L_0 = l_0)`, since the regime-adherent past before time `0` is the whole space. The iterated-conditional-expectation form and the general kernel form are not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.exponentialDispersionLaw
declarations.doc: The exponential dispersion law with cumulant `b`, dispersion `φ`, and natural parameter `θ`, relative to the dominating measure `ν`.

declarations.name: CKSD.canonicalGLMInformation
declarations.doc: The canonical-link information matrix `J = E[x xᵀ b''(⟪x, β⟫)]` of one covariate draw.

declarations.name: CKSD.canonicalGLMLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: The canonical-link log likelihood of the first `n` observations, up to terms free of `β`, with the dispersion kept.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCanonicalGLMRoot
declarations.doc: `β` solves the canonical-link likelihood equations for the first `n` observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_in_distribution_canonical_glm_root
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.3, canonical-link form: for independent and identically distributed pairs `(xᵢ, Yᵢ)` whose response given the covariate is exponential-dispersion with natural parameter `⟪x, β⟫`, with covariates bounded by `R`, smooth cumulant function, natural parameter space all of `ℝ`, and nonsingular `J = E[x xᵀ b''(⟪x, β⟫)]`, every measurable root `β̂` of the likelihood equations satisfies `√n (β̂ - β) ⇒ N(0, φ J⁻¹)`, and `φ̂^{-1/2} J^{1/2} √n (β̂ - β) ⇒ N(0, I_p)` for every consistent `φ̂`. Restrictions of scope: canonical link (`g = (b')⁻¹`), bounded covariates, and natural parameter space `ℝ`; the general twice-differentiable link is not covered. Consistency of `β̂` is not assumed: the log likelihood is concave, so every root is a maximizer, and the argument goes through the convexity lemma `CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sub_of_convexOn_of_isMinOn`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_in_distribution_canonical_glm_deviance
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.3, deviance test for nested canonical-link models with known dispersion: if the true coefficient lies in a subspace `L`, `β̂` is a consistent root of the full likelihood equations and `β̃` a consistent maximizer of the likelihood over `L`, then the scaled deviance difference `2 (ℓₙ(β̂) - ℓₙ(β̃))` converges in distribution to chi-squared on `p - dim L` degrees of freedom. Hypotheses as in `tendstoInDistribution_canonicalGLM_root`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gamma_add_nat_div_eq_prod_fin
declarations.doc: Positive Gamma quotients with natural shift are finite products.

declarations.name: CKSD.gamma_mul_add_nat_mul_div
declarations.doc: The integer multiplication identity for Gamma quotients with natural shifts.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_log_Gamma_add_sub_log_Gamma_sub_mul_log
declarations.doc: The logarithmic Gamma increment is asymptotic to the shift times the logarithm.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_Gamma_add_div_mul_rpow
declarations.doc: The Gamma ratio has its standard power asymptotic along arbitrary positive real arguments.

declarations.name: CKSD.condIndepFun_iff_ae_eq_prod_of_condDistrib_ae_eq
declarations.doc: Conditional independence through a conditional law: if the conditional distribution of `(f, g)` given `k` is a.e. the Markov kernel `κ`, then `f` and `g` are conditionally independent given `k` exactly when `κ` is a.e. the product of its two marginal kernels.

declarations.name: CKSD.condIndepFun_iff_indepFun_of_eq_add
declarations.doc: Conditional independence given `Y` of `f = R₁ + a₁ ∘ Y` and `g = R₂ + a₂ ∘ Y`, where the residual pair `(R₁, R₂)` is independent of `Y`, is equivalent to independence of `R₁` and `R₂`.

declarations.name: CKSD.otherCoordinates
declarations.doc: The coordinates of `x` other than the `i`-th and the `j`-th.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_otherCoordinates
declarations.doc: The map to the coordinates other than `i` and `j` is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.concentrationModel
declarations.doc: The concentration matrices of the Gaussian graphical model of `G`: positive definite matrices with zero entries off the edges of `G`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasGaussianPairwiseMarkovProperty
declarations.doc: The Gaussian pairwise Markov property of `N(m, Σ)` relative to an undirected graph: for nonadjacent `i ≠ j`, the coordinates `xᵢ` and `xⱼ` are conditionally independent given the remaining coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.condIndepFun_multivariateGaussian_iff_inv_apply_eq_zero
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.26: for a positive definite covariance `Σ` and `i ≠ j`, the coordinates `xᵢ` and `xⱼ` of `N(m, Σ)` are conditionally independent given the remaining coordinates exactly when the `(i, j)` entry of the concentration matrix `Σ⁻¹` vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasGaussianPairwiseMarkovProperty_iff_inv_mem_concentrationModel
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.26: for a positive definite covariance `Σ`, the law `N(m, Σ)` has the pairwise Markov property relative to `G` exactly when its concentration matrix `Σ⁻¹` lies in the concentration model of `G`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianConcentrationLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: The Gaussian log likelihood of a concentration matrix `K` for `n` observations with centred sum-of-squares matrix `ssd`, up to an additive constant and the factor `n / 2`: `log det K - tr(K ssd) / n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsConcentrationMLE
declarations.doc: `K` is the maximum likelihood estimate of the concentration matrix in the Gaussian graphical model of `G`: it lies in the concentration model and has strictly larger likelihood than every other concentration matrix of the model.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_exp_quadratic_atTop_zero
declarations.doc: A quadratic exponential tends to zero when its coefficient pair is lexicographically negative.

declarations.name: CKSD.coefficients_eq_zero_of_sum_exp_quadratic_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Distinct quadratic exponentials are linearly independent: normalize by the largest lexicographic exponent among the nonzero coefficients and take the limit at infinity.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianParameterPolynomial
declarations.doc: The polynomial recording the linear mean term and the quadratic covariance term.

declarations.name: CKSD.eval_gaussianParameterPolynomial
declarations.doc: Evaluating the Gaussian parameter polynomial gives its mean and covariance quadratic form.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianParameterPolynomial_injective
declarations.doc: The parameter polynomial determines the mean and every Hermitian covariance matrix. The odd part determines the mean, and polarization determines the covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_injective_eval_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc: A finite family of distinct real multivariate polynomials has an evaluation at which all values are distinct, since the product of their nonzero pairwise differences is nonzero.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearIndependent_gaussianExponents
declarations.doc: Distinct means and Hermitian covariance matrices give linearly independent Gaussian exponentials. A polynomial evaluation selects a separating line, and quadratic exponential growth proves linear independence on that line.

declarations.name: CKSD.InstrumentalVariableObservation
declarations.doc: Structural observation in an instrumental-variable model: regressor, instrument, error.

declarations.name: CKSD.instrumentSecondMoment
declarations.doc: Second moment of the instruments.

declarations.name: CKSD.instrumentRegressorMoment
declarations.doc: Cross second moment between instruments and regressors.

declarations.name: CKSD.instrumentErrorMoment
declarations.doc: Instrument-score covariance in the correctly specified structural model.

declarations.name: CKSD.instrumentalVariableSampleEstimator
declarations.doc: Two-stage least-squares sample estimator under the structural equation.

declarations.name: CKSD.instrumentalVariableCovariance
declarations.doc: Asymptotic two-stage least-squares covariance from the population instrument moments.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_twoStageLeastSquares
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.55: consistency of two-stage least squares. For independent identically distributed observations `(xᵢ, zᵢ, εᵢ)` with finite second moments, instruments orthogonal to the error (`E[z ε] = 0`), `E[z zᵀ]` positive definite, and the rank condition that `Dᵀ E[z zᵀ]⁻¹ D` with `D = E[z xᵀ]` is positive definite, the estimator computed from `yᵢ = ⟪xᵢ, β⟫ + εᵢ` converges in probability to `β`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_twoStageLeastSquares
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.55: heteroscedasticity-robust two-stage least-squares central limit theorem. Under the hypotheses of `tendstoInMeasure_twoStageLeastSquares` and square integrability of the score `ε z`, `√n (β̂ - β) ⇒ N(0, H⁻¹ Dᵀ Σ_Z⁻¹ Ω Σ_Z⁻¹ D H⁻¹)` with `Ω = E[ε² z zᵀ]`. No fourth moments are needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel
declarations.doc: Parameters of a reduced finite Gaussian mixture: all components are nondegenerate, distinct, and have positive weight. Laws and densities use the upstream TauCeti construction.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.law
declarations.doc: Probability law of a reduced Gaussian mixture, using TauCeti's finite mixture.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.density
declarations.doc: Real Gaussian-mixture density, using TauCeti's canonical continuous density.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.logLikelihood
declarations.doc: Log likelihood of a reduced Gaussian mixture at a finite observed sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.density_nonneg
declarations.doc: The canonical mixture density is nonnegative, by TauCeti.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.hasDensity
declarations.doc: The mixture's real density agrees with its law in CKSD's density interface, using TauCeti.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.exists_equiv_of_law_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.6: finite nondegenerate Gaussian mixtures are identifiable up to relabeling: two reduced mixtures with the same law have the same number of components, and a bijection of the components matches their weights, means and covariances.

declarations.name: CKSD.GaussianMixtureModel.not_bddAbove_logLikelihood
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.6: two Gaussian components already give an unbounded likelihood when their covariances are unconstrained: on a nonempty sample in positive dimension, the log-likelihoods of the two-component reduced mixtures are not bounded above.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_sampleMean_scatterMatrix_wishart_and_hotelling
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.22: for `n ≥ p + 1` independent observations from `N_p(m, Σ)` with `Σ` positive definite, the sample mean and the scatter matrix `A = ∑ᵢ (xᵢ - x̄)(xᵢ - x̄)ᵀ` are independent, `A` has the Wishart law `W_p(n - 1, Σ)`, and with `S = A / (n - 1)` the scaled Hotelling statistic `(n - p) / ((n - 1) p) · n (x̄ - m)ᵀ S⁻¹ (x̄ - m)` has the F law with `p` and `n - p` degrees of freedom.

declarations.name: CKSD.log_det_le_trace_sub_card
declarations.doc: The spectral inequality `log det A ≤ tr A - dim` for a positive-definite real matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.log_det_eq_trace_sub_card_iff
declarations.doc: Equality holds in `log det A ≤ tr A - dim` for a positive-definite real matrix exactly at the identity.

declarations.name: CKSD.log_det_add_card_le_log_det_add_trace_mul_inv
declarations.doc: The Gaussian covariance criterion `log det C + tr(S C⁻¹)` is at least its value `log det S + p` at `C = S`, for positive definite `S` and `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.log_det_add_card_eq_log_det_add_trace_mul_inv_iff
declarations.doc: The Gaussian covariance criterion `log det C + tr(S C⁻¹)` attains its minimum `log det S + p` only at `C = S`, for positive definite `S` and `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.matrixQuadraticForm_eq_dotProduct
declarations.doc: The Euclidean quadratic form agrees with the coordinate dot product.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_sub_sampleMean_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A nonempty finite sample has zero sum of deviations from its sample mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_matrixQuadraticForm_sub_eq
declarations.doc: Centering a quadratic sum at the sample mean separates its location error.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_matrixQuadraticForm_sub_sampleMean_eq_trace
declarations.doc: A centered quadratic sum is the trace pairing of the scatter matrix and its coefficient.

declarations.name: CKSD.matrixQuadraticForm_pos
declarations.doc: A positive-definite real matrix has a positive quadratic form on every nonzero vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianNegLogLikelihood_sampleMean_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.28: the Gaussian negative log-likelihood of a sample whose sample covariance `S = n⁻¹ ∑ᵢ (xᵢ - x̄)(xᵢ - x̄)ᵀ` is positive definite is minimized, over all means `m` and positive definite covariances `C`, at `(x̄, S)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianNegLogLikelihood_eq_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.28: the minimizer of the Gaussian negative log-likelihood is unique: for a sample whose sample covariance `S` (divisor `n`) is positive definite, the value at `(m, C)`, `C` positive definite, equals the value at `(x̄, S)` only if `m = x̄` and `C = S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.wishart_determinant_law
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.31: for `p ≤ n` and positive definite `Σ`, the determinant of a Wishart matrix `W ∼ W_p(n, Σ)` has the law of `det Σ · ∏_{i<p} χ²_{n-i}` with independent chi-squared factors (Bartlett's decomposition).

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussian_sample_correlation_student_law
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.32: for `N > 2` independent pairs of independent standard normal variables, the sample correlation coefficient `r` satisfies `√(N - 2) r / √(1 - r²) ∼ t_{N-2}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleColumns
declarations.doc: The `p × κ` matrix whose columns are the vectors of a sample indexed by `κ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_sampleColumns
declarations.doc: `sampleColumns` is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_sampleColumns_pi_stdGaussian
declarations.doc: Sample columns of independent standard Gaussian vectors are matrix normal `MN(0, 1, 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleColumnsEquiv
declarations.doc: `sampleColumns` as a measurable equivalence.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_sampleColumns_pi_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: Sample columns of independent `N(M_k, Σ)` vectors are matrix normal `MN(M, Σ, 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_orthogonalMix_pi_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: Orthogonal mixing of a Gaussian sample: if `Bᵀ B = 1` and `x₁, …, x_n` are independent `N(m, Σ)`, then the vectors `y_k = ∑ᵢ B i k (xᵢ - m)` are independent `N(0, Σ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_orthogonal_matrix_last_column
declarations.doc: A unit vector `v` of `ℝⁿ` is the last column of a real orthogonal `n × n` matrix whose columns are indexed by `Fin (n - 1) ⊕ Unit`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_orthogonal_matrix_last_column_const
declarations.doc: A real orthogonal `n × n` matrix, with columns indexed by `Fin (n - 1) ⊕ Unit`, whose last column is the constant vector `n^{-1/2}`; the other columns are then orthogonal to the constants.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_helmert_decomposition
declarations.doc: The Helmert decomposition of a Gaussian sample: for `n ≥ 1` independent `N(m, Σ)` vectors there are measurable maps `Y` to `n - 1` vectors and `U` to one vector, jointly distributed as `n` independent `N(0, Σ)` vectors, with `x̄ = m + n^{-1/2} U` and with the scatter matrix equal to the Gram sum of `Y`.

declarations.name: CKSD.matrixQuadraticForm_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The Euclidean quadratic form in coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_orthogonal_first_column
declarations.doc: For a nonzero vector `u` there is an orthogonal matrix `N` whose first column is `u / ‖u‖`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_quadForm_div_quadForm_inv_wishartGramMeasure
declarations.doc: For a Wishart matrix `A ∼ W_p(ν, Σ)` with `p ≤ ν` and a fixed nonzero `u`, the ratio `uᵀ Σ⁻¹ u / uᵀ A⁻¹ u` is chi-squared with `ν - p + 1` degrees of freedom.

declarations.name: CKSD.matrixQuadraticForm_eq_mulVec_dotProduct
declarations.doc: The Euclidean quadratic form as a coordinate dot product.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_quadForm_inv_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: For `U ∼ N(0, Σ)` with `Σ` positive definite, `Uᵀ Σ⁻¹ U` is chi-squared with `p` degrees of freedom.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_matrixQuadraticForm_inv
declarations.doc: The quadratic form `uᵀ A⁻¹ u` is jointly measurable in a symmetric matrix `A` and `u`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_matrixQuadraticForm_inv_left
declarations.doc: Measurability of `A ↦ uᵀ A⁻¹ u` on symmetric matrices.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateGaussian_singleton_zero
declarations.doc: A centred nondegenerate Gaussian vector is almost surely nonzero.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_prod_quadForm_ratio
declarations.doc: Joint law of `U` and `Uᵀ Σ⁻¹ U / Uᵀ A⁻¹ U` for independent `U ∼ N_p(0, Σ)` and `A ∼ W_p(ν, Σ)`: the ratio is independent of `U` with law `χ²(ν - p + 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_hotelling_multivariateGaussian_wishartGramMeasure
declarations.doc: Hotelling's law: for independent `U ∼ N_p(0, Σ)` and `A ∼ W_p(ν, Σ)` with `0 < p ≤ ν` and `Σ` positive definite, `(ν - p + 1) / p · Uᵀ A⁻¹ U` has the F law with `p` and `ν - p + 1` degrees of freedom.

declarations.name: CKSD.matrixQuadraticForm_smul_smul
declarations.doc: Homogeneity of the matrix quadratic form in the matrix and in the vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.wilksLambda
declarations.doc: Wilks's determinant ratio for error and hypothesis scatter matrices.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateHypothesisRoots
declarations.doc: Roots of a positive-error multivariate hypothesis, computed after symmetric whitening.

declarations.name: CKSD.lawleyHotellingTrace
declarations.doc: Lawley–Hotelling trace statistic.

declarations.name: CKSD.pillaiTrace
declarations.doc: Pillai trace statistic.

declarations.name: CKSD.royLargestRoot
declarations.doc: Roy's largest root, with the value zero for a zero-dimensional response space.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleCovarianceMatrix_isHermitian
declarations.doc: Sample covariance is Hermitian, including an empty sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_wilksLambda_wishart_eq_beta_product
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.23: for independent Wishart matrices `E ∼ W_p(e, Σ)` and `H ∼ W_p(h, Σ)` with `p ≤ e`, `0 < h` and `Σ` positive definite, Wilks's `Λ = det E / det(E + H)` has the law of a product `∏_{i<p} Bᵢ` of independent `Bᵢ ∼ Beta((e - i)/2, h/2)`. This is the distributional core; the linear-model projection reduction and the Bartlett correction are not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleCovarianceMatrix_eq_empirical
declarations.doc: The sequence and finite-sample covariance conventions agree.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_gaussian_sample_covariance_eigenvalue
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.24: central limit theorem for a simple eigenvalue: for an i.i.d. sample from `N_p(m, Σ)` with `Σ` positive definite and a simple eigenvalue `λ_j` of `Σ`, the `j`-th largest eigenvalue `λ̂_j` of the sample covariance (divisor `n`) satisfies `√n (λ̂_j - λ_j) ⇒ N(0, 2 λ_j²)`. Multiplicities of the other eigenvalues are allowed.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sphericity_likelihood_ratio
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.33: Wilks's chi-squared limit for sphericity in fixed dimension `p ≥ 2`: under `N_p(m, v I)` with `v > 0`, the likelihood-ratio statistic `-n log(det S / (tr S / p)^p)` converges in distribution to `χ²` with `p(p+1)/2 - 1` degrees of freedom. The second-order Bartlett approximation is not stated.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_block_independence_likelihood_ratio
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.33: under `N_{p+q}(m, Σ)` with `Σ` positive definite and block diagonal, the likelihood-ratio statistic `-n log(det S / (det S₁₁ det S₂₂))` for independence of the two blocks converges in distribution to `χ²` with `p q` degrees of freedom.

declarations.name: CKSD.isHermitian_eigenvalues₀_eq_iff
declarations.doc: Two real symmetric matrices have the same ordered eigenvalues exactly when they have the same characteristic polynomial.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateHypothesisRoots_eq_iff_charpoly_eq
declarations.doc: When the whitened hypothesis matrices `E^{-1/2} H E^{-1/2}` are symmetric, two pairs have the same generalized roots exactly when these matrices have the same characteristic polynomial.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateHypothesisRoots_eq_iff_congruent
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.34: generalized roots classify scatter-matrix pairs under simultaneous congruence: for `E`, `E'` positive definite and `H`, `H'` positive semidefinite, the pairs `(E, H)` and `(E', H')` have the same generalized roots exactly when `E' = Aᵀ E A` and `H' = Aᵀ H A` for some invertible `A`. This is the algebraic maximal-invariant assertion for response transformations.

declarations.name: CKSD.isHermitian_det_one_add_eq_prod
declarations.doc: For a real symmetric matrix `M`, `det (1 + M) = ∏ᵢ (1 + λᵢ)` over its eigenvalues `λᵢ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isHermitian_trace_mul_inv_one_add_eq_sum
declarations.doc: For a real symmetric matrix `M` with nonnegative eigenvalues `λᵢ`, `tr (M (1 + M)⁻¹) = ∑ᵢ λᵢ / (1 + λᵢ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isHermitian_sum_eigenvalues₀_eq
declarations.doc: Sums over the ordered eigenvalues agree with sums over the matrix-indexed eigenvalues.

declarations.name: CKSD.isHermitian_prod_eigenvalues₀_eq
declarations.doc: Products over the ordered eigenvalues agree with products over the matrix-indexed eigenvalues.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariate_test_statistics_eq_roots
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.34: in terms of the generalized roots `λᵢ` of a positive definite `E` and a positive semidefinite `H`, Wilks's `Λ = ∏ (1 + λᵢ)⁻¹`, the Lawley–Hotelling trace is `∑ λᵢ`, and Pillai's trace is `∑ λᵢ / (1 + λᵢ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStarProjection.apply_apply
declarations.doc: A star projection is idempotent, pointwise.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStarProjection.inner_map_left
declarations.doc: A star projection is symmetric for the inner product.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsStarProjection.starProjection_range_apply
declarations.doc: A star projection is the orthogonal projection onto its range.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_inner_of_covariance_eq
declarations.doc: With uncorrelated coordinates of common variance `v`, the variance of `⟪b, Y⟫` is `v ‖b‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_inner_map_eq_of_map_integral_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.1, scalar Gauss–Markov comparison, unbiasedness: if the mean of `Y` lies in the range of the star projection `P`, then `⟪P a, Y⟫` and `⟪a, Y⟫` have the same expectation.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_inner_map_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.1, scalar Gauss–Markov comparison, variance: if the coordinates of `Y` are uncorrelated with common variance `v ≥ 0`, then for every star projection `P` the variance of `⟪P a, Y⟫` is at most that of `⟪a, Y⟫`. Together with `integral_inner_map_eq_of_map_integral_eq` this says that projecting the coefficient vector of a linear unbiased estimator onto the model space does not increase its variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateGaussian_smul_one_eq_map
declarations.doc: The Gaussian law `N(m, v I)` is the image of the standard Gaussian measure under `z ↦ m + √v z`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_smul_sub_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: Under `N(m, v I)` with `v > 0`, the standardized vector `(x - m) / √v` is standard Gaussian.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_norm_sq_sub_div_eq_chiSquared
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.2, residual chi-squared law: for `Y ∼ N(m, v I_n)` with `v > 0` and `m` in the range of the star projection `P`, the scaled residual sum of squares `‖Y - P Y‖² / v` has the chi-squared law with `n - rank P` degrees of freedom.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_map_norm_sq_sub
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.2, projection independence: for `Y ∼ N(m, v I_n)` with `v > 0` and any star projection `P`, the fitted value `P Y` and the residual sum of squares `‖Y - P Y‖²` are independent.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_matrixQuadraticForm_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.15, Craig–Sakamoto criterion: for `Y ∼ N(0, Σ)` with `Σ` positive definite and symmetric matrices `A`, `B`, the quadratic forms `Yᵀ A Y` and `Yᵀ B Y` are independent if and only if `A Σ B = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.quantileCheckLoss
declarations.doc: The quantile-regression check loss `ρ_τ(u) = u (τ - 1{u < 0})`; it vanishes at `u = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.quantileRegressionObjective
declarations.doc: The fixed-design quantile-regression objective `β ↦ ∑ᵢ ρ_τ(yᵢ - ⟪xᵢ, β⟫)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsQuantileRegressionEstimator
declarations.doc: A quantile-regression estimate minimizes the check-loss objective.

declarations.name: CKSD.quantileCheckLoss_nonneg
declarations.doc: The check loss is nonnegative for a level `τ ∈ [0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.twoStageLeastSquares
declarations.doc: The two-stage least-squares coefficient `(Xᵀ P_Z X)⁻¹ Xᵀ P_Z y`, with the instrument projection `P_Z = Z (Zᵀ Z)⁻¹ Zᵀ` (matrix inverses are Mathlib's, zero for singular matrices).

declarations.name: CKSD.expectedQuantileCheckLoss
declarations.doc: Expected check loss for a scalar location candidate.

declarations.name: CKSD.quantileCheckLoss_eq_add_max
declarations.doc: The check loss as a linear part plus a negative part.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_quantileCheckLoss
declarations.doc: Measurability of the check loss.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_quantileCheckLoss_sub
declarations.doc: The check loss at a translated location is integrable when the law has a first moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_add_mul_sub_indicator
declarations.doc: A constant multiple of a centred indicator is integrable under a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_add_mul_sub_indicator
declarations.doc: Integral of an integrable function plus a constant multiple of a centred indicator.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_le_integral_add_mul_sub_indicator
declarations.doc: Integrating a pointwise bound `g₁ ≤ g₂ + c (τ - 1_s)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_add_mul_sub_indicator_le_integral
declarations.doc: Integrating a pointwise bound `g₂ + c (τ - 1_s) ≤ g₁`.

declarations.name: CKSD.minimizes_expectedQuantileCheckLoss_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.5: expected check-loss minimizers are precisely the distributional quantiles. This characterization allows atoms; finite first moment makes every displayed risk finite.

declarations.name: CKSD.weightedDesignMoment
declarations.doc: Normalized weighted design second-moment matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_quantile_regression
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.5: fixed-design quantile-regression central limit theorem. Let the responses `Yᵢ` be independent with laws `Qᵢ` having densities `fᵢ`, with `τ`-quantile `⟪xᵢ, β⟫`, and `fᵢ(⟪xᵢ, β⟫) ∈ [a, b]` with `a > 0`, the densities equicontinuous at these quantiles. If `n⁻¹ ∑ xᵢ xᵢᵀ → D₀` (positive definite), `n⁻¹ ∑ fᵢ(⟪xᵢ, β⟫) xᵢ xᵢᵀ → D₁`, and `maxᵢ ‖xᵢ‖ / √n → 0`, then every sequence of quantile-regression estimates satisfies `√n (β̂ - β) ⇒ N(0, τ(1-τ) D₁⁻¹ D₀ D₁⁻¹)`. The limit `D₁ ≥ a D₀` is then positive definite. No identical-distribution assumption is imposed on the responses.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleCovarianceMatrix
declarations.doc: Sample covariance with the maximum-likelihood divisor `n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sphericityRatio

declarations.name: CKSD.sphericityRatio_smul

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_sphericityRatio

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_sampleMean

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_sampleCovarianceMatrix

declarations.name: CKSD.map_sphericityRatio_sampleCovarianceMatrix_eq_wishart

declarations.name: CKSD.sphericity_gamma_moment_eq_product

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sphericity_beta_product_pow_eq_gamma

declarations.name: CKSD.map_sphericityRatio_wishart_eq_beta_product
declarations.doc: The exact spherical Wishart sphericity law is a product of independent Beta factors.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_of_eventually_map_eq
declarations.doc: Convergence in distribution transfers across eventually equal laws.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_max_one_natCast_sub_div_two
declarations.doc: A lower truncation of an affine growing Beta shape tends to infinity.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_max_one_natCast_div_two_ratio
declarations.doc: Two affine shape sequences with the same leading scale have asymptotic ratio one.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_neg_natCast_mul_log_of_beta_product_law
declarations.doc: A statistic with the growing-shape Beta-product law has the corresponding logarithmic Gamma limit; only eventual equality of laws is needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_sphericity_beta_second_shape
declarations.doc: The sum of the spherical Beta second shapes equals half the dimension deficit.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_trace_wishartGramMeasure_smul_one
declarations.doc: The trace of a spherical Gaussian-Gram Wishart matrix has the corresponding Gamma law.

declarations.name: CKSD.det_le_trace_div_pow_of_posDef
declarations.doc: Matrix AM-GM bounds the determinant by the dimension-th power of the mean eigenvalue.

declarations.name: CKSD.det_trace_ratio_mem_Ioc
declarations.doc: The sphericity determinant ratio of a positive definite matrix lies in the unit interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.wishartNormalizer_smul_one
declarations.doc: Spherical Wishart normalizers combine the two scalar scales into their product.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_det_trace_ratio_pow_wishartGramMeasure
declarations.doc: Determinant tilting reduces sphericity moments to an inverse trace moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.wishartNormalizer_spherical_shift_ratio_mul_rate_pow
declarations.doc: The scale in a spherical determinant tilt cancels against the inverse trace-moment scale.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_det_trace_ratio_pow_wishartGram_eq_gamma
declarations.doc: Exact natural moments of the spherical Wishart sphericity ratio.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsLinearSEMMatrix
declarations.doc: A coefficient matrix of a linear structural equation model along `G`: the coefficient of `X_k` in the equation of `X_j` is nonzero exactly when `k → j` is an edge.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearSEMLaw
declarations.doc: The law of the solution `X = (1 - B)⁻¹ N` of a linear structural equation model with independent noises of laws `ν j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNonGaussianPositiveDensityLaw
declarations.doc: A real law is non-Gaussian with a strictly positive density.

declarations.name: CKSD.coordinateRestriction
declarations.doc: Restriction of a vector to the coordinates in `B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_coordinateRestriction
declarations.doc: Coordinate restrictions are measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsFaithfulLaw
declarations.doc: A law on `V → ℝ` is faithful to `G` when, for disjoint `A`, `B`, `C`, the coordinates in `A` and `B` are conditionally independent given those in `C` exactly when `A` and `B` are d-separated by `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.RespectsParentsReal
declarations.doc: The structural functions of an additive-noise model respect the parents of `G`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsAdditiveNoiseLaw
declarations.doc: The law of an additive-noise model `X_j = f_j(X_{pa(j)}) + N_j` with independent noises of laws `ν j`: the image of the noise law under a measurable solution map of the equations.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsNonlinearInParents
declarations.doc: Each structural function is nonlinear in each of its parent arguments: along every line in the direction of a parent coordinate it is not affine.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.edge_eq_of_linearSEMLaw_eq_of_nonGaussian
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.71, linear non-Gaussian models: if two linear structural equation models along `G` and `H`, with nonzero coefficients on the edges and independent non-Gaussian noises with strictly positive densities, have the same law, then `G = H`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsLinearSEMMatrix.apply_self
declarations.doc: The diagonal of a linear SEM matrix vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.IsLinearSEMMatrix.det_one_sub_ne_zero
declarations.doc: For a linear SEM matrix `B` along a causal graph, `1 - B` is nonsingular.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_linearSEMLaw_gaussianReal
declarations.doc: Variance of a linear functional of a linear Gaussian SEM with common noise variance: `Var(∑ₐ cₐ Xₐ) = σ² ∑ₖ (∑ₐ cₐ Mₐₖ)²` for `X = M N`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.edge_eq_of_linearSEMLaw_eq_of_equalVariance
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.71, linear Gaussian models with equal noise variances: if two linear structural equation models along `G` and `H`, with nonzero coefficients on the edges and independent Gaussian noises of one common positive variance within each model, have the same law, then `G = H`. The noise means are arbitrary.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.edge_eq_of_additiveNoiseLaw_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.71, nonlinear additive Gaussian-noise models: if two additive-noise models along `G` and `H`, with three times continuously differentiable structural functions that respect the parents and are nonlinear in each parent argument, and independent Gaussian noises of positive variances, have the same law, then `G = H`.

declarations.name: CKSD.CausalGraph.exists_linearGaussianSEM_iff_markovEquivalent
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.71, linear Gaussian models with unrestricted variances identify only the Markov equivalence class: for a linear Gaussian model along `G` whose law is faithful to `G`, a directed acyclic graph `H` carries a linear Gaussian model (nonzero edge coefficients, positive noise variances) with the same law faithful to `H` exactly when `H` is Markov equivalent to `G`. Faithfulness to both graphs makes the equivalence class the precise answer.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sum_mem_eq_sum_measureReal
declarations.doc: The mean of a sum over a random sample is the sum of the summands weighted by their first-order inclusion probabilities.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sum_sum_mem_eq_sum_sum_measureReal
declarations.doc: The mean of a double sum over a random sample is the double sum of the summands weighted by their joint inclusion probabilities.

declarations.name: CKSD.simpleRandomSampleDesign_real_superset
declarations.doc: Under simple random sampling of `n` units, the probability that the sample contains a given set `B` of at most `n` units is `C(N - |B|, n - |B|) / C(N, n)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_simpleRandomSampleDesign
declarations.doc: Simple random sampling of `n ≤ N` units is a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.simpleRandomSampleDesign_real_superset_eq_card
declarations.doc: Under simple random sampling, the probability that the sample contains `B` is the proportion of `n`-subsets containing `B`.

declarations.name: CKSD.simpleRandomSampleDesign_real_mem
declarations.doc: First-order inclusion probabilities of simple random sampling.

declarations.name: CKSD.simpleRandomSampleDesign_real_mem_mem
declarations.doc: Second-order inclusion probabilities of simple random sampling for distinct units.

declarations.name: CKSD.populationVariance_eq_sum_sq
declarations.doc: The finite-population variance as a difference of sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.inclusionProb
declarations.doc: The first-order inclusion probability `πᵢ = P(i ∈ s)` of unit `i` under the design `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.jointInclusionProb
declarations.doc: The second-order inclusion probability `πᵢⱼ = P(i ∈ s, j ∈ s)` under the design `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.horvitzThompson
declarations.doc: The Horvitz–Thompson estimator `∑_{i ∈ s} yᵢ / πᵢ` of the population total.

declarations.name: CKSD.horvitzThompsonVarianceEstimator
declarations.doc: The Horvitz–Thompson estimator of the design variance of `horvitzThompson P y`: `∑_{i, j ∈ s} (πᵢⱼ - πᵢ πⱼ) / πᵢⱼ · yᵢ yⱼ / (πᵢ πⱼ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_horvitzThompson
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.72, Horvitz–Thompson unbiasedness: when every unit has positive inclusion probability, the Horvitz–Thompson estimator is design-unbiased for the population total.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_horvitzThompson
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.72, exact design variance of the Horvitz–Thompson estimator: `Var(T) = ∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ (πᵢⱼ - πᵢ πⱼ) yᵢ yⱼ / (πᵢ πⱼ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_horvitzThompsonVarianceEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.72, unbiased estimation of the Horvitz–Thompson design variance: when all joint inclusion probabilities are positive, `horvitzThompsonVarianceEstimator` is design-unbiased for the variance of the Horvitz–Thompson estimator.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_horvitzThompson_eq_sen_yates_grundy
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.72, Sen–Yates–Grundy identity for a fixed-size sampling design: if almost every sample has `n` units, then `Var(T) = -(1/2) ∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ (πᵢⱼ - πᵢ πⱼ) (yᵢ / πᵢ - yⱼ / πⱼ)²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sum_simpleRandomSampleDesign
declarations.doc: The mean of a sample total under simple random sampling of `1 ≤ n ≤ N` units is `(n / N) ∑ᵢ wᵢ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_sum_simpleRandomSampleDesign
declarations.doc: The design variance of a sample total under simple random sampling of `1 ≤ n ≤ N` units is `n (N - n) / N · S²`, with `S²` the population variance.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sum_div_simpleRandomSampleDesign
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.73, finite-population correction for a simple random sample mean: the sample mean is design-unbiased for the population mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_sum_div_simpleRandomSampleDesign
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.73, finite-population correction for a simple random sample mean: the design variance of the sample mean is `(1 - n / N) S² / n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_sum_div_le_sum_sq_div_of_sum_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.73, the continuous Neyman allocation optimization, lower bound: for positive allocations `xₕ` with `∑ₕ xₕ = n`, `(∑ₕ aₕ)² / n ≤ ∑ₕ aₕ² / xₕ`. This is Mathlib's `Finset.sq_sum_div_le_sum_sq_div`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_sum_div_eq_sum_sq_div_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.73, the continuous Neyman allocation optimization, equality case: for positive `aₕ` and positive allocations `xₕ` with `∑ₕ xₕ = n`, the bound `(∑ₕ aₕ)² / n ≤ ∑ₕ aₕ² / xₕ` is attained exactly at the Neyman allocation `xₕ = n aₕ / ∑ₖ aₖ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.differenceInMeans
declarations.doc: The difference in means `(∑_{i ∈ s} y₁ᵢ) / n₁ - (∑_{i ∉ s} y₀ᵢ) / n₀` of a completely randomized experiment in which the units of `s` are treated.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_differenceInMeans
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.46, Neyman's unbiasedness in a completely randomized experiment: when `n₁ > 0` units drawn by simple random sampling are treated and the `n₀ > 0` others are controls, the difference in means is unbiased for the average treatment effect.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_differenceInMeans
declarations.doc: GAPS 105.46, Neyman's exact design variance in a completely randomized experiment: `Var = S₁² / n₁ + S₀² / n₀ - S²_{y₁ - y₀} / N`, with the population variances of the potential outcomes and of the unit-level effects.

declarations.name: CKSD.withDensity_det_pow_wishartGramMeasure
declarations.doc: A natural determinant tilt of a nonsingular Gaussian-Gram Wishart law.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_det_ratio_pow_wishartGram_prod
declarations.doc: Determinant-ratio moments reduce to one shifted Wishart determinant moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.wishart_normalizer_ratio_mul_negative_moment

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_det_ratio_pow_wishartGram_prod_eq_gamma

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_beta_product_pow_eq_gamma

declarations.name: CKSD.wishartNormalizer

declarations.name: CKSD.wishartNormalizer_pos

declarations.name: CKSD.det_pow_mul_wishartPDFReal

declarations.name: CKSD.withDensity_det_pow_nonsingularWishartMeasure

declarations.name: CKSD.totalVariationDistance

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_measureReal_sub_le_totalVariationDistance

declarations.name: CKSD.totalVariationDistance_nonneg

declarations.name: CKSD.tvDist_eq_two_mul_totalVariationDistance

declarations.name: CKSD.kolmogorovSmirnovStatistic

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteKernelDensityEstimator
declarations.doc: The kernel density estimator `(n h)⁻¹ ∑ᵢ K((t - xᵢ) / h)` of a finite sample `x` with kernel `K` and bandwidth `h`.

declarations.name: CKSD.kernelDensityEstimator_eq
declarations.doc: The kernel density estimator of a sequence is a sum over the first `n` indices.

declarations.name: CKSD.restrictedL1Norm
declarations.doc: The coordinate `ℓ¹` norm `∑_{j ∈ S} |x j|` restricted to a set `S` of coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparsity
declarations.doc: The number of nonzero coordinates of a finite-dimensional vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.bestSparseL1Error
declarations.doc: The best `s`-term approximation error `σ_s(x)₁ = inf {‖x - y‖₁ : y is s-sparse}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: `A` has the restricted isometry property of order `s` with constant `δ`: `(1 - δ) ‖x‖² ≤ ‖A x‖² ≤ (1 + δ) ‖x‖²` for every `s`-sparse `x`. The constant is a parameter, not the infimum of admissible constants.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjaminiHochbergCount
declarations.doc: The Benjamini–Hochberg rejection count at level `α`: the largest `k ≤ m` such that at least `k` of the p-values are at most `k α / m`, with value `0` when no `k ≥ 1` qualifies.
