declarations.name: CKSD.norm_toEuclideanCLM_le_of_rowSum_le
declarations.doc: Schur test for a symmetric matrix: the Euclidean operator norm is at most any bound on the absolute row sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_thresholded_covariance_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.52, deterministic sparse-row bound for hard covariance thresholding. If `Σ` and `S` are symmetric, `|S i j - Σ i j| ≤ λ` for all entries, and each row of `Σ` has at most `s` nonzero entries, then the hard-thresholded matrix `T_λ(S) i j = S i j 1{|S i j| > λ}` satisfies `‖T_λ(S) - Σ‖ ≤ 2 s λ` in Euclidean operator norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.euclideanCovarianceMatrix
declarations.doc: Population covariance in Euclidean coordinates, using Mathlib's covariance adapter.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCovarianceMatrix
declarations.doc: The sample-centred empirical covariance matrix, with divisor `n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.entrySum
declarations.doc: The entrywise `ℓ¹` norm `∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ |Aᵢⱼ|` of a square matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.inner_toEuclideanCLM_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The bilinear form of a matrix in coordinates: `⟪x, A y⟫ = ∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ xᵢ Aᵢⱼ yⱼ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.euclideanCovarianceMatrix_symm
declarations.doc: The covariance matrix is symmetric.

declarations.name: CKSD.centeredProduct
declarations.doc: The centered product statistic `(xᵢ - mᵢ)(xⱼ - mⱼ) - Σᵢⱼ`, with `m` the mean of `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.centeredCoord
declarations.doc: The centered coordinate statistic `xᵢ - mᵢ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleProdMean
declarations.doc: The sample mean of the centered product statistic.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleCoordMean
declarations.doc: The sample mean of the centered coordinate statistic, `X̄ᵢ - mᵢ` for `n ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleAverage_apply
declarations.doc: Coordinates of the sample average.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCovarianceMatrix_sub_eq
declarations.doc: For `n ≥ 1`, `Σ̂ᵢⱼ - Σᵢⱼ` is the sample mean of the centered product minus the product of the centered coordinate means.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_zero_of_abs_le'
declarations.doc: Eventual pointwise domination by a sequence tending to zero in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_finsetSum_zero
declarations.doc: Finite sums of sequences tending to zero in probability tend to zero in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBoundedInProbability.of_abs_le_of_tendstoInMeasure
declarations.doc: If `|Yₙ| ≤ K |Vₙ|` whenever `|Uₙ| < δ`, with `Vₙ` bounded and `Uₙ → 0` in probability, then `Yₙ` is bounded in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sqrt_mul_sampleCoordMean_mul
declarations.doc: Products of centered coordinate means are `o_P(n^{-1/2})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_entrySum
declarations.doc: The entrywise `ℓ¹` error of the empirical covariance tends to zero in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.isBoundedInProbability_sqrt_mul_entrySum
declarations.doc: The entrywise `ℓ¹` error of the empirical covariance is `O_P(n^{-1/2})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sqrt_mul_entrySum_sq
declarations.doc: The squared entrywise `ℓ¹` error of the empirical covariance is `o_P(n^{-1/2})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_empiricalCovarianceMatrix
declarations.doc: The empirical covariance matrix is a measurable function of the sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.inner_euclideanCovarianceMatrix_self
declarations.doc: The Rayleigh value of the covariance at its unit eigenvector `v` is the eigenvalue.

declarations.name: CKSD.quadStat
declarations.doc: The centered quadratic statistic `∑ᵢ ∑ⱼ vᵢ vⱼ ((xᵢ - mᵢ)(xⱼ - mⱼ) - Σᵢⱼ)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.quadStat_eq
declarations.doc: The centered quadratic statistic equals `⟪x - m, v⟫² - λ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_quadStat
declarations.doc: The centered quadratic statistic is square integrable under a fourth moment.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_quadStat
declarations.doc: The centered quadratic statistic has mean zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_quadStat
declarations.doc: The centered quadratic statistic is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_quadStat_sq_eq_variance
declarations.doc: The second moment of the centered quadratic statistic is `Var ⟪X - m, v⟫²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.leadingRayleighValue
declarations.doc: Largest Rayleigh value of a real matrix; the intended spectral interpretation is symmetric. The empty unit sphere in dimension zero gives the usual real `sSup ∅ = 0` convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.leading_empirical_covariance_eigenvalue_asymptotics
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.30: leading empirical covariance eigenvalue expansion and CLT in finite dimension. Let `X₁, X₂, …` be independent with law `P` on `ℝ^d` with finite fourth moment, and let the covariance `Σ` of `P` have a unit eigenvector `v`, `Σ v = λ v`, with `⟪u, Σ u⟫ ≤ (λ - gap) ‖u‖²` for `u ⊥ v` and `gap > 0`. Then the largest eigenvalue `λ̂ₙ` of the empirical covariance `Σ̂ₙ` satisfies `√n (λ̂ₙ - λ - ⟪v, (Σ̂ₙ - Σ) v⟫) → 0` in probability, and `√n (λ̂ₙ - λ)` converges in law to `N(0, Var ⟪X - E X, v⟫²)`. The Gaussian variance formula is not needed for this non-Gaussian fourth-moment version. Positivity of `λ` is not assumed (it follows from the gap when `d ≥ 2`).

declarations.name: CKSD.isBoundedInProbability_leading_empirical_eigenvector_error
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.30: the root-`n` bound for a leading empirical eigenvector. Under the hypotheses of `CKSD.leading_empirical_covariance_eigenvalue_asymptotics`, any choice of unit eigenvector `ŵₙ` of `Σ̂ₙ` for its largest eigenvalue, with sign fixed by `⟪ŵₙ, v⟫ ≥ 0`, satisfies `√n ‖ŵₙ - v‖ = O_P(1)`; the choice need not be measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCovarianceMatrix_zero
declarations.doc: The empirical covariance of the empty sample is the zero matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.empiricalCovarianceMatrix_isSymm
declarations.doc: An empirical covariance matrix is symmetric, for every sample including the empty one.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_kolmogorovSmirnovStatistic_gt_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.1: the Dvoretzky–Kiefer–Wolfowitz inequality with Massart's constant. For i.i.d. real observations and every `t > 0`, `P(√n sup_x |F_n(x) - F(x)| > t) ≤ 2 exp(-2 t²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_kernelDensityEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.4: the pointwise central limit theorem for the kernel density estimator. For a bounded symmetric probability kernel `K` with finite second moment `μ₂(K)` and a twice continuously differentiable density `f` with bounded `f''`, if `h → 0`, `nh → ∞`, and `nh⁵ = O(1)`, then `√(nh) (f̂_h(t) - f(t) - h² μ₂(K) f''(t) / 2) ⇒ N(0, R(K) f(t))` with `R(K) = ∫ K²`. When `f(t) = 0` the limit is the point mass at `0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_integral_abs_kernelDensityEstimator_sub
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.5: universal `L¹` consistency of the kernel density estimator, in dimension one. For a bounded compactly supported kernel with `∫ K = 1`, if `h → 0` and `nh → ∞`, then `∫ |f̂_n - f| → 0` almost surely for every density `f`.

declarations.name: CKSD.minimizer_mem_span_of_feature_vectors
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.8: the representer theorem, in its Hilbert feature-vector formulation. A minimizer `f` of `∑ᵢ L(yᵢ, ⟪f, vᵢ⟫) + λ ‖f‖²` with `λ > 0` lies in the span of the feature vectors `vᵢ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.natCast_mul_sum_perm_apply
declarations.doc: Summing `f (σ i)` over all permutations: `n * ∑_σ f (σ i) = n! * ∑_k f k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.natCast_mul_sum_perm_apply_mul_apply
declarations.doc: Summing `a (σ i) a (σ j)` over permutations for `i ≠ j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.uniformPermMeasure
declarations.doc: The uniform probability measure on the permutations of `Fin n`: the law of the rank vector of `n` independent observations from a continuous distribution.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearRankStatistic
declarations.doc: The linear rank statistic `∑ᵢ cᵢ a(σ i)` with regression constants `c` and scores `a`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_linearRankStatistic
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.14: the mean of a linear rank statistic under uniform ranks, `E T_N = N c̄ ā`.

declarations.name: CKSD.variance_linearRankStatistic
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.14: the variance of a linear rank statistic under uniform ranks, `Var T_N = (N - 1)⁻¹ ∑ᵢ (cᵢ - c̄)² ∑ᵢ (a(i) - ā)²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.multivariateGaussian_smul_one_eq_map_pi
declarations.doc: The isotropic Gaussian `N(m, σ² I)` on `ℝ^ι` is the product of its coordinate laws `N(m_i, σ²)`, transported to Euclidean space.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_exp_sq_div_gaussianReal
declarations.doc: The exponential moment `E exp(Z² / 4) = √2` of a centered Gaussian `Z` of variance `σ²`, written with `Z² / (4 σ²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_exp_sum_sq_inner_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: For an orthonormal family `v` and `ε ~ N(0, σ² I)`, the coordinates `⟪v i, ε⟫` are independent `N(0, σ²)`, so `E exp(∑ᵢ ⟪v i, ε⟫² / (4σ²)) = √2 ^ |ι|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_starProjection_add_sq
declarations.doc: Residual expansion for an observation `f + ε`: `‖(f + ε) - Π(f + ε)‖² = ‖f - Πf‖² + 2⟪f - Πf, ε⟫ + ‖ε‖² - ‖Πε‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_starProjection_add_sub_sq
declarations.doc: Risk expansion for an observation `f + ε`: `‖Π(f + ε) - f‖² = ‖f - Πf‖² + ‖Πε‖²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_starProjection_sq_eq_sum
declarations.doc: Parseval for a projection: `‖Πε‖² = ∑ₖ ⟪bₖ, ε⟫²` for an orthonormal basis `b` of `K`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_exp_norm_starProjection_sq_le
declarations.doc: Exponential moment of a projected isotropic Gaussian vector together with one orthogonal direction: for `g ⊥ K`, `E exp((‖Π_K ε‖² + ⟪g, ε⟫² / ‖g‖²) / (4σ²)) ≤ √2 ^ (dim K + 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteEmpiricalCDF
declarations.doc: Empirical distribution function of a finite sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.cramerVonMisesStatistic
declarations.doc: Cramér–von Mises statistic, with the factor `n` normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.twoSampleKolmogorovSmirnovStatistic
declarations.doc: Two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic, without the asymptotic scaling factor.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_finiteEmpiricalCDF_uncurry
declarations.doc: The finite empirical distribution function is jointly measurable in the sample and the argument.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_finiteEmpiricalCDF
declarations.doc: The finite empirical distribution function at a fixed point is measurable in the sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.uniformMeasure_zero_one_eq_restrict_Ioo
declarations.doc: The uniform law on `[0, 1]` is Lebesgue measure restricted to `(0, 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_pi_quantile
declarations.doc: Coordinatewise application of the quantile function is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.pi_eq_map_pi_quantile
declarations.doc: Inverse transform sampling for samples: `P^k` is the image of the uniform law on `(0, 1)^k` under coordinatewise application of the quantile function of `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_forall_mem_Ioo_pi_restrict
declarations.doc: Almost every sample from the uniform law on `(0, 1)` has all its values in `(0, 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_cramerVonMisesStatistic
declarations.doc: The Cramér–von Mises statistic is a measurable function of the sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_cramerVonMisesStatistic_eq_uniform
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.17: finite-sample distribution-freeness of the Cramér–von Mises statistic. For a probability measure `P` without atoms, the law of `n ∫ (F_n - F)² dF` under `P^n` equals its law under the uniform distribution on `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteEmpiricalCDF_mem_Icc
declarations.doc: The finite empirical distribution function takes values in `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_rat_finiteEmpiricalCDF_eq
declarations.doc: Two finite empirical distribution functions take at every real point the same pair of values as at some rational point slightly to the right.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_twoSampleKolmogorovSmirnovStatistic
declarations.doc: The two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic is a measurable function of the two samples.

declarations.name: CKSD.bddAbove_range_abs_finiteEmpiricalCDF_sub
declarations.doc: The range defining the two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic is bounded above by one.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteEmpiricalCDF_quantile_comp
declarations.doc: Composing a sample in `(0, 1)` with the quantile function of `P` turns its empirical distribution function into the original one evaluated along the CDF of `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_twoSampleKolmogorovSmirnovStatistic_eq_uniform
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.17: finite-sample distribution-freeness of the two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic. For a probability measure `P` without atoms and nonempty samples, the law of `sup_t |F_m(t) - G_n(t)|` under `P^m ⊗ P^n` equals its law under the uniform distribution on `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_unit_eigenvector_rayleigh_le
declarations.doc: A self-adjoint operator `M` on a nonzero finite-dimensional real inner product space has a unit eigenvector `w`, `M w = b w`, whose eigenvalue bounds the quadratic form: `⟪u, M u⟫ ≤ b ‖u‖²` for all `u`. The unit vector `x` only witnesses that the space is nonzero.

declarations.name: CKSD.mem_span_singleton_of_eigenvector_of_forall_inner_eq_zero
declarations.doc: If every eigenvector of `M` for the eigenvalue `b` orthogonal to `v` vanishes, then the `b`-eigenspace is spanned by any unit eigenvector `w` for `b`: the eigenvalue `b` is simple.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_eigenvector_norm_sub_le_of_rayleigh_gap
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.54: deterministic residual perturbation bound for the leading eigenvector. Let `A` and `E` be self-adjoint operators on a finite-dimensional real inner product space, and let `v` be a unit vector with `A v = a v` such that `⟪u, A u⟫ ≤ (a - gap) ‖u‖²` for all `u ⊥ v`. If `2 ‖E‖ < gap`, then the top eigenvalue `b` of `A + E` is simple, and it has a unit eigenvector `w` with `⟪w, v⟫ ≥ 0` and `‖w - v‖ ≤ 2 ‖E v - ⟪v, E v⟫ v‖ / (gap - 2 ‖E‖)`. The probabilistic spiked-covariance bound is outside this deterministic statement.

declarations.name: CKSD.precisionNeighbourhood
declarations.doc: The neighbourhood `N(j) = {k ≠ j | Θ j k ≠ 0}` of a vertex in the graph of a matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.principalSubmatrix
declarations.doc: The principal submatrix of a matrix on a set of indices.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIncoherentAt
declarations.doc: Incoherence at vertex `j`: every `k ∉ S ∪ {j}` has `‖Σ_{k S} (Σ_{S S})⁻¹‖₁ ≤ 1 - α`. When `S` avoids `j` this is the incoherence of the covariance of the coordinates other than `j` with respect to `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.RowSumNormLE
declarations.doc: The bound `‖A‖_{∞→∞} ≤ b` on the maximal absolute row sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.nodeLassoObjective
declarations.doc: The lasso objective for regressing coordinate `j` on the other coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNodeLassoEstimate
declarations.doc: `β` is a neighbourhood-lasso estimate for vertex `j`: it has zero `j`-th coefficient and minimizes the node lasso objective among such coefficient vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.andRuleEdge
declarations.doc: The "and" rule: `{j, k}` is an estimated edge when each lies in the other's estimated neighbourhood; `B j` are the coefficients of the regression of coordinate `j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.orRuleEdge
declarations.doc: The "or" rule: `{j, k}` is an estimated edge when one lies in the other's estimated neighbourhood.

declarations.name: CKSD.neighbourhoodSelection_graph_recovery
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.53, neighbourhood selection: with universal constants, under incoherence, the row-sum bound, unit-bounded variances, maximal degree `m`, and `n ≥ c₁ m log p`, the "or" rule includes no false edge and the "and" rule includes every edge with `|Θ j k| ≥ 7 b λ max (Θ j j) (Θ k k)`, with the stated probability; since the "and" edges are "or" edges, both rules have both properties. The edge condition bounds the regression coefficients `-Θ j k / Θ j j` and `-Θ k j / Θ k k` below by `7 b λ`; this is the bound proved by Wainwright (2019), Theorem 11.12, whose statement puts `|Θ j k|` in its place although `Θ j j ≥ 1` is not bounded above. The lasso estimates `B x j` are arbitrary minimizers.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleSecondMomentMatrix
declarations.doc: The second-moment matrix `n⁻¹ ∑ xᵢ xᵢᵀ` of a centered sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.graphicalLassoObjective
declarations.doc: The graphical lasso objective `tr(Θ S) - log det Θ + λ ∑_{j ≠ k} |Θ j k|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsGraphicalLassoEstimate
declarations.doc: `Θ` is a graphical lasso estimate: a positive definite minimizer of the objective.

declarations.name: CKSD.graphicalLasso_frobenius_error_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.53, graphical lasso: the Frobenius error bound under `σ`-sub-Gaussian centered coordinates and at most `m` nonzero entries per row of `Θ = Σ⁻¹`. With `λ = 8 σ² (√(log p / n) + δ)` and `6 (‖Θ‖ + 1)² λ √(m p) < 1`, with probability at least `1 - 8 exp (-n δ² / 16)` the graphical lasso estimate `Θ̂` satisfies `‖Θ̂ - Θ‖_F² ≤ 9 (‖Θ‖ + 1)⁴ m p λ²`. The estimator `T x` is required to be a graphical lasso estimate whenever one exists; the operator norm is the Euclidean one.

declarations.name: CKSD.leastConcaveMajorant
declarations.doc: Least concave majorant on `[0, ∞)` of a real function, as the infimum of the values of its concave majorants; the empty-set convention `sInf ∅ = 0` is never used for bounded functions such as distribution functions.

declarations.name: CKSD.grenanderEstimator
declarations.doc: The Grenander estimator at `x`: the left slope of the least concave majorant of the empirical distribution function of the first `n` observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsNonincreasingDensity
declarations.doc: A nonincreasing probability density on `[0, ∞)`, vanishing on the negative half-line.

declarations.name: CKSD.twoSidedBrownianPath
declarations.doc: The path of two-sided Brownian motion built from two one-sided paths: `B₁` on the nonnegative half-line and `B₂` reflected on the negative half-line.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsChernoffArgmax
declarations.doc: `Z` is a realization of Chernoff's random variable `argmax (W(t) - t ^ 2)` for the two-sided Brownian motion `W` built from independent Brownian motions `B₁` and `B₂`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsConcaveMajorant
declarations.doc: A concave majorant of `F` on `[0, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.leastConcaveMajorant_le
declarations.doc: The least concave majorant lies below every concave majorant on `[0, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_leastConcaveMajorant
declarations.doc: A function bounded above on `[0, ∞)` lies below its least concave majorant there.

declarations.name: CKSD.concaveOn_leastConcaveMajorant
declarations.doc: The least concave majorant of a function bounded above on `[0, ∞)` is concave there.

declarations.name: CKSD.ConcaveOn.monotoneOn_of_bddBelow
declarations.doc: A concave function on `[0, ∞)` that is bounded below is monotone there.

declarations.name: CKSD.ConcaveOn.chord_le
declarations.doc: A concave function lies above its chord between two points.

declarations.name: CKSD.ConcaveOn.le_chord_of_le
declarations.doc: A concave function lies below the extension of its chord to the right.

declarations.name: CKSD.ConcaveOn.le_chord_of_ge
declarations.doc: A concave function lies below the extension of its chord to the left.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_sample_grid
declarations.doc: The ordered distinct values of a positive sample, together with the origin.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_mul_le_of_partialSum_nonpos
declarations.doc: Summation by parts: a nonincreasing nonnegative weight sequence preserves nonpositivity of all partial sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_count_mul_div_slope_le
declarations.doc: The discrete core of the Grenander likelihood inequality: on the grid of a cumulative sum diagram with least concave majorant values `G`, slopes `s`, and counts `N`, weights `1 / s` integrate a nonincreasing nonnegative sequence `b` against the counts by at most `n` times its Riemann sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.concaveOn_affine
declarations.doc: An affine function is concave on `[0, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.leastConcaveMajorant_eq_affine
declarations.doc: The least concave majorant is affine on any interval where the majorized function is constant except possibly at the right endpoint.

declarations.name: CKSD.leastConcaveMajorant_eq_of_slope_lt
declarations.doc: At a strict kink of the least concave majorant on a grid of constancy intervals, the majorant touches the majorized function.

declarations.name: CKSD.grenanderEstimator_isMaximumLikelihood
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.11: the Grenander estimator is a nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator among nonincreasing densities on `[0, ∞)`. Scope: a fixed sample of `n ≥ 1` positive observations; the estimator is extended by zero to the nonpositive half-line, and the likelihood is the product of density values at the observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_grenanderEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.11: the cube-root limit law of the Grenander estimator at an interior point. Let `X₁, X₂, …` be independent with law `P`, whose density `f` vanishes on `(-∞, 0)` and is nonincreasing on `[0, ∞)`, and let `f` be differentiable at `x₀ > 0` with `f'(x₀) < 0` (which gives continuity at `x₀`). Then `n^{1/3} (f̂ₙ(x₀) - f(x₀))` converges in distribution to `|4 f(x₀) f'(x₀)|^{1/3} Z`, where `Z = argmax_t (W(t) - t²)` for a two-sided Brownian motion `W`. Positivity `f(x₀) > 0` is not assumed: it follows from monotonicity and `f'(x₀) < 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_hilbert_sampleAverage
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.29: the central limit theorem in a separable Hilbert space. For i.i.d. square-integrable `X_i` with mean `m`, `√n (X̄_n - m)` converges in law to a centred Gaussian measure `G`, characterized by its one-dimensional marginals `⟪u, ·⟫_* G = N(0, E ⟪u, X - m⟫²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_sub_sum_inner_smul_sq
declarations.doc: Pythagoras for the projection onto the span of an orthonormal family.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_ite_le_integral_norm_sub_sum_inner_smul_sq
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.31: principal components minimize the expected reconstruction error, in finite dimension and about any specified center `m`. If the second-moment operator of `X - m` is diagonal in the orthonormal basis `e` with nonincreasing eigenvalues `λ_j`, then no projection onto the span of `k` orthonormal vectors `q_i` has expected squared reconstruction error below the trailing eigenvalue sum `∑_{j ≥ k} λ_j`. Attainment by the leading eigenvectors, uniqueness, and the Hilbert-space case are not asserted.

declarations.name: CKSD.restrictedL1Norm_sub_smul_sub_le
declarations.doc: The coordinate `ℓ¹` norm is convex along segments: `‖x - h (x - y)‖₁ ≤ (1 - h) ‖x‖₁ + h ‖y‖₁` for `0 ≤ h ≤ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLassoEstimator.norm_apply_sub_sq_div_le
declarations.doc: The basic inequality of the lasso. Let `y = A β + ε` with `β` supported in `S`, and let `b` be a lasso estimate with penalty `λ > 0` on the noise event `|⟪ε, A δ⟫| / n ≤ λ ‖δ‖₁ / 2`. Then `‖A (b - β)‖² / n ≤ (3λ/2) ‖(b - β)_S‖₁ - (λ/2) ‖(b - β)_{Sᶜ}‖₁`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLassoEstimator.restrictedL1Norm_compl_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.34: the cone condition for the lasso. Under the noise event `|⟪ε, A δ⟫| / n ≤ λ ‖δ‖₁ / 2`, the error `δ = b - β` of a lasso estimate satisfies `‖δ_{Sᶜ}‖₁ ≤ 3 ‖δ_S‖₁`, where `S` contains the support of `β`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLassoEstimator.norm_apply_sub_sq_div_le_of_hasCompatibility
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.34: the lasso prediction bound under compatibility. Under the noise event and the compatibility condition with constant `κ` on the cone `‖δ_{Sᶜ}‖₁ ≤ 3 ‖δ_S‖₁`, a lasso estimate satisfies `‖A (b - β)‖² / n ≤ 9 λ² |S| / (4 κ²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLassoEstimator.restrictedL1Norm_sub_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.34: the lasso `ℓ¹` error bound under compatibility. Under the noise event and the compatibility condition with constant `κ` on the cone `‖δ_{Sᶜ}‖₁ ≤ 3 ‖δ_S‖₁`, a lasso estimate satisfies `‖b - β‖₁ ≤ 6 λ |S| / κ²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjaminiHochbergCount_le
declarations.doc: The Benjamini–Hochberg count is at most the number of hypotheses.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjaminiHochbergCount_le_card
declarations.doc: The Benjamini–Hochberg count `R` satisfies its defining inequality `R ≤ #{j : x j ≤ R α / m}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_benjaminiHochbergCount
declarations.doc: Every `k ≤ m` satisfying the Benjamini–Hochberg inequality is at most the count.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjaminiHochbergCount_le_update_zero
declarations.doc: Setting one p-value to zero does not decrease the Benjamini–Hochberg count.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_le_benjaminiHochbergCount_update_zero
declarations.doc: After setting one p-value to zero, the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure rejects at least once.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjaminiHochbergCount_eq_update_zero_of_le
declarations.doc: The Benjamini–Hochberg count is unchanged by setting the `i`-th p-value to zero whenever that p-value is rejected by the modified count.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjaminiHochberg_rejection_div_eq_sum
declarations.doc: Leave-one-out decomposition of a Benjamini–Hochberg rejection: the contribution of hypothesis `i` to the false discovery proportion splits over the value `k` of the count computed with `x i` replaced by zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_benjaminiHochbergCount
declarations.doc: The Benjamini–Hochberg count is a measurable function of the p-values.

declarations.name: CKSD.benjaminiHochbergFalseDiscoveryProportion
declarations.doc: The false discovery proportion of the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure at level `α` with p-values `x` and set of true null hypotheses `H₀`: the number of rejected true nulls divided by the number of rejections, with `0 / 0 = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_benjaminiHochbergFalseDiscoveryProportion_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.37: false discovery rate control by the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. For mutually independent p-values whose true-null p-values are superuniform, `P(p_i ≤ t) ≤ t` for `t ∈ [0, 1]`, the expected false discovery proportion at level `α ∈ (0, 1)` is at most `α |H₀| / m`.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderDensityClass
declarations.doc: Probability densities on the line with the Hölder bound `|f x - f y| ≤ L |x - y|^β`. Integrability is implied by `∫ f = 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_of_mem_holderDensityClass
declarations.doc: A member of the Hölder density class is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.mem_holderDensityClass_iff
declarations.doc: For nonnegative parameters, the Hölder density class consists of the measurable probability densities satisfying Mathlib's `HolderWith L β`.

declarations.name: CKSD.densityLaw
declarations.doc: The probability law represented by a real density.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderDensityPointwiseMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Pointwise minimax risk for density estimation on a Hölder class.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sampleMean_sub_le
declarations.doc: Mean squared error of a sample mean under a product law: bias squared plus at most the second moment divided by the sample size.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_of_mem_holderDensityClass
declarations.doc: A Hölder probability density of order `β ∈ (0, 1]` is bounded by `1 / 2 + L`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isProbabilityMeasure_densityLaw
declarations.doc: The law with a probability density is a probability measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_densityLaw
declarations.doc: Integrals against a density law.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_densityLaw_iff
declarations.doc: Integrability against a density law.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_comp_sub_div
declarations.doc: Change of variables `u = (x - y) / h` on the line.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteKernelDensityEstimator_risk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.26: the kernel upper bound for pointwise Hölder density risk with `0<β≤1`. The moment condition is the order-zero kernel condition appropriate in this range.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_densityLaw_le
declarations.doc: Kullback–Leibler divergence between laws with densities, bounded by the chi-square integral: `KL(f₁, f₀) ≤ ∫ (f₁ - f₀)² / f₀` for a positive density `f₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ofReal_mul_measureReal_le_lintegral_sq
declarations.doc: Markov's inequality for the squared error.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderDensityPointwiseMinimaxRisk_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.26: the matching pointwise minimax lower bound for Hölder orders at most one.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_uncurry_fixedDesignLocalConstant
declarations.doc: The box-kernel local average `(y, t) ↦ fixedDesignLocalConstant h y t` is jointly measurable in the observations and the evaluation point, so it is an admissible estimator in `CKSD.holderRegressionMinimaxRisk`.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderRegressionMinimaxRisk_le
declarations.doc: Upper half of GAPS 103.22: for `0 < β ≤ 1`, the fixed-design Hölder minimax mean integrated squared risk is at most `C n^(-2β/(2β+1))`, attained by the box-kernel local average with bandwidth `n^(-1/(2β+1))` (`CKSD.fixedDesignLocalConstant_risk_le`).

declarations.name: CKSD.holderRegressionMinimaxRisk_ge
declarations.doc: Lower half of GAPS 103.22: for `0 < β ≤ 1`, the fixed-design Hölder minimax mean integrated squared risk is at least `c n^(-2β/(2β+1))`. The proof applies Assouad's lemma to `m ≍ n^(1/(2β+1))` Hölder tents with Gaussian total variation bounds.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderRegressionMinimaxRisk_bounds
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.22: the fixed-design `L²` Hölder minimax rate for orders at most one. This states both bounds; sup-norm risk and higher local-polynomial orders are not asserted.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_abs_integral_mul_comp_sub_mul_sub
declarations.doc: **Approximate identity in `L¹(ℝ)`.** For a measurable integrable `f` and a bounded integrable kernel `K` with `∫ K = 1`, the smoothed functions `t ↦ ∫ K(u) f(t - h u) du` converge to `f` in `L¹` as `h → 0`. The kernel need not be nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_of_abs_le_of_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A bounded measurable kernel vanishing outside `[-R, R]` is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_integral_abs_finiteKernelDensityEstimator_sub
declarations.doc: **Expected `L¹` consistency of the kernel density estimator.** For a bounded measurable kernel vanishing outside `[-R, R]` with `∫ K = 1`, a law `P` with density `f ≥ 0`, and bandwidths `h_n > 0` with `h_n → 0` and `n h_n → ∞`, the expected `L¹` error `E ∫ |f̂_n - f|` of the kernel density estimator from `n` i.i.d. observations tends to `0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_integral_abs_finiteKernelDensityEstimator_sub
declarations.doc: Measurability of the `L¹` error of the kernel density estimator as a function of the sample.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_le_integral_abs_finiteKernelDensityEstimator_sub_le
declarations.doc: **Concentration of the `L¹` error** (Devroye): by McDiarmid's inequality, for `n ≥ 1` i.i.d. observations from `P` and `ε ≥ 0`, the `L¹` error of the kernel density estimator exceeds its mean by `ε` with probability at most `exp (-n ε² / (2 (∫ |K|)²))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLogConcaveDensity
declarations.doc: An upper semicontinuous log-concave probability density on `ℝ^d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.logLikelihoodFunctional
declarations.doc: The log-likelihood functional `∫ log f dP`, with value `⊥` when it equals `-∞`; it is intended for densities bounded above, such as log-concave densities.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLogConcaveProjection
declarations.doc: `f` is a log-concave projection of `P`: it maximizes `∫ log f dP` over `𝓕_d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tentFunction
declarations.doc: The tent function with heights `y` at the points `x`: the least concave function on the convex hull of the points with value at least `y i` at `x i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.densityHellingerSq
declarations.doc: Squared Hellinger distance `∫ (√f - √g) ^ 2` between two densities on `ℝ^d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.densityHellingerRisk
declarations.doc: Expected squared Hellinger loss of a density estimator from `n` independent observations with density `f₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.logConcaveUpperRate
declarations.doc: The log-concave rate: `n ^ (-4/5)` for `d = 1` and `n ^ (-2/(d+1)) log n` for `d ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.logConcaveLowerRate
declarations.doc: The log-concave minimax lower rate: `n ^ (-4/5)` for `d = 1` and `n ^ (-2/(d+1))` for `d ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_isLogConcaveProjection
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.28: existence and uniqueness of the log-concave projection, with its positivity set between the interior of the convex support of `P` and that support. The convex support is the closed convex hull of the support of `P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_logConcaveMLE_tent
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.28: the log-concave maximum likelihood estimator of affinely spanning data is unique, vanishes outside the convex hull `C_n` of the data, and its logarithm is a tent function on `C_n`. Affine spanning of `ℝ^d` forces `n ≥ d + 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.logConcaveMLE_hellingerRisk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.28: the worst-case squared Hellinger risk of the log-concave maximum likelihood estimator. The estimator `T` is required to be the maximum likelihood estimator on affinely spanning samples, which have probability one; the constant depends only on `d`.

declarations.name: CKSD.logConcave_minimax_hellingerRisk_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.28: the minimax lower bound for log-concave density estimation in squared Hellinger distance, with a constant `c_d` depending only on the dimension (Kim and Samworth, 2016, Theorem 1). Estimators are jointly measurable functions of the sample and the evaluation point.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_gaussianReal_gaussianReal
declarations.doc: Kullback–Leibler divergence between Gaussian laws of a common positive variance: `KL(N(a, v), N(b, v)) = (b - a)² / (2v)`, computed by exponential tilting.

declarations.name: CKSD.klDiv_pi_gaussianReal
declarations.doc: Kullback–Leibler divergence between finite products of Gaussian laws of a common positive variance, from the tensorization of Kullback–Leibler divergence.

declarations.name: CKSD.totalVariationDistance_le_sqrt_toReal_klDiv
declarations.doc: Pinsker's inequality in the statistical normalization of total variation: `TV(P, Q) ≤ √(KL(P, Q) / 2)` when the divergence is finite.

declarations.name: CKSD.totalVariationDistance_pi_gaussianReal_le
declarations.doc: Total variation between finite products of Gaussian laws with common variance `v`: `TV ≤ √(∑ (bᵢ - aᵢ)² / (4v))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_sub_totalVariationDistance_div_two_le_max_measureReal
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.39: Le Cam's two-point lower bound. If `dist θ₀ θ₁ ≥ 2 s`, every measurable estimator `T` satisfies `max_i P_i(dist(T, θ_i) ≥ s) ≥ (1 - TV(P₀, P₁)) / 2`, with total variation in the statistical normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_mul_neg_log_sub_log_two_le_klDiv
declarations.doc: Binary data processing for one event: if `KL(P, Q)` is finite, then `P(A) log (1 / Q(A)) - log 2 ≤ KL(P, Q)`. Uses Statlib's chain rule for an event and the binary Kullback-Leibler formula.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_sub_div_log_le_sSup_measureReal
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.40: Fano's method with a reference law. For `M ≥ 2` parameters with pairwise distances at least `2 s` and laws `P_j` of finite Kullback–Leibler divergence from a reference probability `Q`, every measurable estimator satisfies `max_j P_j(dist(T, θ_j) ≥ s) ≥ 1 - (M⁻¹ ∑_j KL(P_j, Q) + log 2) / log M`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_pow_hammingDist_eq
declarations.doc: Exponential moment of the Hamming distance to a fixed binary word: `∑_y x ^ d(c, y) = (1 + x) ^ m`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_hamming_packing
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.45: the Varshamov–Gilbert bound. For `m ≥ 8` there is a set `C ⊆ {0,1}^m` containing the zero word with `|C| - 1 ≥ 2^(m/8)` and pairwise Hamming distances at least `m / 8`.

declarations.name: CKSD.mul_one_sub_div_two_le_sSup_integral_hammingDist
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.46: Assouad's lemma in total variation form. If the laws `P_w` indexed by the cube `{0,1}^m` satisfy `TV(P_w, P_w') ≤ α` whenever `w` and `w'` differ in one coordinate, then every measurable estimator `T` with values in the cube has worst-case expected Hamming loss `max_w E_w d(T, w) ≥ m (1 - α) / 2`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSequenceLaw
declarations.doc: Gaussian sequence observation law with noise standard deviation `ε`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sequenceSquaredError
declarations.doc: Squared sequence error, taking value infinity when the difference is not square summable.

declarations.name: CKSD.sequenceEllipsoid
declarations.doc: Weighted ellipsoid; the radius convention is `sum (a_j theta_j)^2 ≤ R`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sobolevEllipsoid
declarations.doc: Sobolev ellipsoid indexed from frequency one.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSequenceMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Minimax squared risk over measurable Gaussian-sequence estimators.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianSequenceLinearMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Linear minimax risk with coordinatewise shrinkage estimators.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_gaussianSequenceMinimaxRisk_div_linear
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.9: Pinsker's theorem. On the ellipsoid `∑ (a_j θ_j)² ≤ R` with positive nondecreasing `a_j → ∞`, the ratio of the minimax squared risk to the linear minimax squared risk tends to `1` as the noise level `ε` decreases to `0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.nadarayaWatson
declarations.doc: Nadaraya–Watson estimator; the value when all weights vanish is zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.regressionPredictionError
declarations.doc: Squared regression prediction error under the feature law.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIsotonicRegressionEstimator
declarations.doc: An isotonic least-squares estimator is a minimizer over the monotone cone.

declarations.name: CKSD.lassoObjective
declarations.doc: The lasso objective, with the `1/(2n)` squared-error normalization.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLassoEstimator
declarations.doc: A lasso estimate minimizes the lasso objective.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasCompatibility
declarations.doc: The compatibility condition with constant `κ` on the cone `‖δ_{Sᶜ}‖₁ ≤ L ‖δ_S‖₁`: `κ² ‖δ_S‖₁² ≤ |S| ‖A δ‖² / n` for every `δ` in the cone.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparseGaussianLaw
declarations.doc: Gaussian finite-dimensional sparse estimation experiment.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparseGaussianMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Minimax squared risk over the `s`-sparse vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparseGaussianLaw_eq_map_pi
declarations.doc: The sparse Gaussian law `N(θ, σ² I_p)` is the product of the coordinate laws `N(θ_i, σ²)`, transported to Euclidean space.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_measureReal_le_one_add_totalVariationDistance
declarations.doc: Two-point bound on success probabilities: for disjoint events, `P₀(A₀) + P₁(A₁) ≤ 1 + TV(P₀, P₁)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_measureReal_le_of_klDiv_le
declarations.doc: Fano's inequality in averaged form: for `m > 4` laws at Kullback–Leibler divergence at most `K` from a reference law `Q` and pairwise disjoint events, the success probabilities satisfy `∑_j P_j(A_j) ≤ m / 4 + m (K + log 2) / log (m / 4)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.softThreshold
declarations.doc: Soft thresholding at level `λ`: `y ↦ y - max (-λ) (min λ y)`, which is `sign y (|y| - λ)₊` for `λ ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_softThreshold
declarations.doc: Soft thresholding is continuous.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_softThreshold_sub_le
declarations.doc: Soft thresholding at level `λ ≥ 0` moves each point by at most `λ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_softThreshold_le
declarations.doc: Soft thresholding at level `λ ≥ 0` satisfies `|η_λ(y)| ≤ (|y| - λ)₊`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_softThreshold_sub_sq_le
declarations.doc: Risk of soft thresholding at a nonzero mean.

declarations.name: CKSD.lintegral_softThreshold_sq_le
declarations.doc: Risk of soft thresholding at the level `t σ` at a zero mean: `≤ 4 σ² e^{1/2 - t²/2}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparseGaussianMinimaxRisk_bounds
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.33: the sparse minimax rate. There are universal constants `0 < c ≤ C` such that for `1 ≤ s` and `2 s ≤ p` the minimax squared risk over `s`-sparse means in `N(θ, σ² I_p)` lies between `c σ² s log(p / s)` and `C σ² s log(p / s)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sequenceSquaredError_self
declarations.doc: Any sequence has zero squared error against itself, including nonsummable sequences.

declarations.name: CKSD.nadarayaWatson_zero_bandwidth
declarations.doc: A zero bandwidth gives the unweighted mean when the kernel is nonzero at the origin.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicCone
declarations.doc: Cone of nondecreasing finite real vectors.

declarations.name: CKSD.convex_isotonicCone
declarations.doc: The isotonic cone is convex.

declarations.name: CKSD.finiteVectorVariation
declarations.doc: Variation of a finite real vector, including the empty-vector value zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicGaussianRisk
declarations.doc: Gaussian isotonic regression risk, divided by sample size.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicUnitBall
declarations.doc: The bounded monotone class used in the isotonic minimax lower bound.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicGaussianMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Gaussian isotonic minimax risk on the bounded monotone class.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockAverage
declarations.doc: Mean response over a contiguous block of indices.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicLeastSquares
declarations.doc: Isotonic least squares in its explicit max–min block-average form.

declarations.name: CKSD.existsUnique_isIsotonicRegressionEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.27: existence and uniqueness of the isotonic least-squares fit.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIsotonicRegressionEstimator.sum_mul_sub_nonpos
declarations.doc: Variational inequality for isotonic least squares: the residual of the fit has nonpositive inner product with every monotone direction `φ - θ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIsotonicRegressionEstimator.sum_ite_le_sub_nonpos
declarations.doc: Suffix sums of the isotonic residual are nonpositive: `∑_{j ≥ k} (yⱼ - θ̂ⱼ) ≤ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIsotonicRegressionEstimator.sum_sub_nonneg
declarations.doc: The total isotonic residual is nonnegative: `0 ≤ ∑ⱼ (yⱼ - θ̂ⱼ)`. Together with `IsIsotonicRegressionEstimator.sum_ite_le_sub_nonpos` for `k = 0` it vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIsotonicRegressionEstimator.sum_ite_le_sub_nonneg_of_lt
declarations.doc: At a jump `θ̂_{k-1} < θ̂_k` of the isotonic fit, the suffix sum of the residual from `k` on is nonnegative, hence zero by `IsIsotonicRegressionEstimator.sum_ite_le_sub_nonpos`.

declarations.name: CKSD.isIsotonicRegressionEstimator_isotonicLeastSquares
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.27: the max–min block-average formula is the isotonic least-squares fit.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicGaussianRisk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.27: the adaptive variation risk bound for Gaussian isotonic least squares. There is a universal constant `C` such that for every nondecreasing `θ ∈ ℝⁿ` and observations `yᵢ = θᵢ + εᵢ` with independent standard Gaussian errors, the isotonic least-squares fit `θ̂` satisfies `E[n⁻¹ ‖θ̂ - θ‖²] ≤ C ((V(θ)/n)^{2/3} + log(e n)/n)`, where `V(θ) = θₙ - θ₁`. The more general independent finite-variance-error version is not asserted here.

declarations.name: CKSD.isotonicGaussianMinimaxRisk_lower_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.27: no estimator improves the Gaussian bounded-isotonic minimax rate. There is a universal `c > 0` such that the minimax risk `inf_T sup_θ E[n⁻¹ ‖T(y) - θ‖²]`, over measurable estimators and nondecreasing `θ` with `|θᵢ| ≤ 1`, is at least `c n^{-2/3}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.projectionModelFit
declarations.doc: Orthogonal least-squares fit within a selected linear model.

declarations.name: CKSD.penalizedModelCriterion
declarations.doc: Penalized empirical residual criterion for linear model selection.

declarations.name: CKSD.selectedProjectionRisk
declarations.doc: Normalized prediction risk of a selected projection fit in Gaussian regression.

declarations.name: CKSD.selectedProjectionRisk_oracle_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.35: the countable-model oracle inequality for penalized least squares. For a countable family of linear models `S m ⊆ ℝⁿ` with prior weights `π m > 0`, `∑ π m ≤ 1`, Gaussian noise of variance `σ²`, and a penalty `pen m ≥ κ σ² (dim S m + log (1 / π m)) / n` with `κ > κ₀`, the measurable minimizer `m̂` of the penalized residual criterion satisfies `E[n⁻¹ ‖Π_{m̂} y - f‖²] ≤ C (inf_m (n⁻¹ ‖f - Π_m f‖² + pen m) + σ² / n)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.projectionModelFit_eq_self_iff
declarations.doc: The fitted value equals the response exactly when the response lies in the selected model.

declarations.name: CKSD.nadarayaWatsonSample
declarations.doc: The finite-sample Nadaraya–Watson predictor formed from paired observations.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_nadarayaWatson_prediction_error_probability
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.7: universal prediction consistency of the Nadaraya–Watson estimator. The regression mean is given as a version of conditional expectation, with its `L²` property explicit. The kernel has upper and positive local lower ball bounds.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderRegressionClass
declarations.doc: Measurable functions on the line with the Hölder bound `|f x - f y| ≤ L |x - y|^β` on the unit interval. There is no bound on an additive constant.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderOnWith_iff_abs_sub_le
declarations.doc: Mathlib's Hölder condition for real functions on a set of reals, in terms of absolute values.

declarations.name: CKSD.mem_holderRegressionClass_iff
declarations.doc: For nonnegative parameters, the Hölder regression class consists of the measurable functions satisfying Mathlib's `HolderOnWith L β` on `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fixedDesignRegressionLaw
declarations.doc: Fixed-design Gaussian regression law with noise standard deviation `σ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fixedDesignRegressionRisk
declarations.doc: Mean integrated squared error of a predictor under the fixed-design Gaussian experiment.

declarations.name: CKSD.holderRegressionMinimaxRisk
declarations.doc: Fixed-design Hölder minimax mean integrated squared risk over jointly measurable estimators.

declarations.name: CKSD.fixedDesignLocalConstant
declarations.doc: Box-kernel local-constant regression on the fixed design.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_linear_gaussian
declarations.doc: Mean squared error of a linear statistic of independent Gaussian observations with common variance `v`: the variance `v ∑ aᵢ²` plus the squared bias.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_fixedDesign_window_ge
declarations.doc: On the grid `(i + 1) / n`, a window of half-width `h ≥ 1 / n` around a point of `[0, 1]` contains at least `n min(h, 1) / 2` design points.

declarations.name: CKSD.natCast_mul_bandwidth_mul_rate_eq_one
declarations.doc: The bandwidth `n^(-1/(2β+1))` balances the variance `1/(n h)` against the rate `n^(-2β/(2β+1))`: `n · n^(-1/(2β+1)) · n^(-2β/(2β+1)) = 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_bandwidth_rpow_eq
declarations.doc: The squared bias `(h^β)²` of the bandwidth `h = c n^(-1/(2β+1))` is `c^(2β) n^(-2β/(2β+1))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fixedDesignLocalConstant_risk_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.22: a box-kernel local-constant estimator attains the `L²` rate for `0<β≤1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.nadarayaWatson_nonneg
declarations.doc: A Nadaraya–Watson predictor is nonnegative when observations and weights are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.nadarayaWatson_const
declarations.doc: A nonempty normalized set of kernel weights reproduces a constant response.

declarations.name: CKSD.restrictedL1Norm_add_compl
declarations.doc: The coordinatewise L1 norm splits over complementary coordinate sets.

declarations.name: CKSD.restrictedL1Norm_le_add_sub
declarations.doc: A restricted reverse triangle bound for coordinatewise L1 norms.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasNullspaceProperty
declarations.doc: The null space property of `A` on the coordinate set `S`: every nonzero vector `δ` in the kernel of `A` has `‖δ_S‖₁ < ‖δ_{Sᶜ}‖₁`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBasisPursuitEstimator
declarations.doc: `β` is a basis pursuit estimate with residual bound `η`: it minimizes `‖b‖₁` over all `b` with `‖A b - y‖ ≤ η`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasNullspaceProperty_iff
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.48: the null space property on `S` holds if and only if every `β` supported in `S` is the unique minimizer of `‖b‖₁` subject to `A b = A β`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparsity_smul_add_smul_le
declarations.doc: The support of `a • x + b • y` has at most `2 s` elements when `x` and `y` are `s`-sparse.

declarations.name: CKSD.inner_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero_or_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Vectors with disjoint supports are orthogonal.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_inner_apply_le_of_hasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: Restricted orthogonality from the restricted isometry property: for `s`-sparse vectors with disjoint supports, `|⟪A x, A y⟫| ≤ δ ‖x‖ ‖y‖` when `A` has the RIP of order `2 s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_decreasing_blocks
declarations.doc: Blocks of coordinates of size `s` in order of decreasing absolute value: `ℓ j` is the index of the block containing coordinate `j`. Blocks have at most `s` elements, a block followed by a nonempty block is full, and all block indices are smaller than `p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockVector
declarations.doc: The restriction `v_{B_k}` of `v` to the block `B_k = {j | ℓ j = k}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockVector_apply
declarations.doc: Coordinates of a block vector.

declarations.name: CKSD.sparsity_blockVector_le
declarations.doc: A block vector is supported in its block.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockVector_eq_zero_or_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Distinct block vectors have disjoint supports.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_blockVector_sq
declarations.doc: The squared norm of a block vector is the sum of squares over its block.

declarations.name: CKSD.eq_blockVector_zero_add_sum
declarations.doc: A vector is the sum of its blocks when all block indices are below `p`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_range_sum_abs_eq_restrictedL1Norm
declarations.doc: The block `ℓ¹` norms add up to the full `ℓ¹` norm.

declarations.name: CKSD.inner_apply_blockVector_zero_apply
declarations.doc: Expanding `⟪A v₀, A v⟫` over the blocks of `v`, where `v₀` is the leading block.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_le_sum_of_forall_le_of_card_le
declarations.doc: A sum of nonnegative values over a set `S` is at most the sum over a set `B` that dominates its complement and has at least as many elements as `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_le_sum_filter_eq_zero_of_decreasing_blocks
declarations.doc: For decreasing blocks, a sum over at most `s` coordinates of a quantity nondecreasing in `|v j|` is at most the sum over the leading block.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasNullspaceProperty_of_hasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.48, restricted-isometry sufficient condition for exact sparse recovery: if `A` has the restricted isometry property of order `2 s` with constant `0 ≤ δ < 1/3`, then `A` has the null space property on every set `S` of at most `s` coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.sqrt_sum_sq_le_sum_div_sqrt_add
declarations.doc: Square-root lifting bound used for the blocks of the restricted isometry argument: if at most `s` values lie in `[m, M]` with `0 ≤ m`, and `m = 0` unless there are exactly `s` of them, then their Euclidean norm is at most their sum divided by `√s` plus `√s (M - m) / 4`.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_sqrt_of_forall_two_mul_le
declarations.doc: If `2 lam c ≤ lam ^ 2 D + 1` for every real `lam`, then `c ≤ √D`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_inner_apply_le_sqrt_of_hasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: Sharpened restricted orthogonality: if `‖A x‖² = (1 + t) ‖x‖²`, then for `s`-sparse vectors with disjoint supports `|⟪A x, A y⟫| ≤ √(δ² - t²) ‖x‖ ‖y‖` when `A` has the RIP of order `2 s` with constant `δ > 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ripNullspaceRho
declarations.doc: The robust null space constant `ρ(δ) = δ / (√(1 - δ²) - δ / 4)` of the restricted isometry analysis of basis pursuit.

declarations.name: CKSD.ripNullspaceTau
declarations.doc: The robust null space constant `τ(δ) = √(1 + δ) / (√(1 - δ²) - δ / 4)` written as `4 √(1 - δ²) / ((4 √(1 - δ²) - δ) √(1 - δ))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ripNullspace_constants
declarations.doc: The constants of the robust null space property: for `0 ≤ δ < 4 / √41`, `0 ≤ ρ(δ) < 1` and `τ(δ) > 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasRobustNullspaceProperty
declarations.doc: The robust null space property of order `s` with constants `ρ` and `τ`: for every `v` and every set `S` of at most `s` coordinates, `‖v_S‖₂ ≤ ρ / √s ‖v_{Sᶜ}‖₁ + τ ‖A v‖`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_norm_blockVector_succ_le
declarations.doc: The tail blocks of a decreasing block decomposition are controlled by the lifting bound: `∑_{k ≥ 1} ‖v_{B_k}‖ ≤ (‖v‖₁ - ‖v_{B_0}‖₁) / √s + ‖v_{B_0}‖ / 4`.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_le_ripNullspaceRho_mul_add_of_hasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: The restricted isometry step for the leading block. Let `A` have the restricted isometry property of order `2 s` with constant `δ < 4 / √41`, let `u` and the `w k` be `s`-sparse with the support of `u` disjoint from those of the `w k`, and suppose that `⟪A u, z⟫ = ‖A u‖² + ∑_{k < K} ⟪A u, A w_k⟫` (as for `z = A v` with `v = u + ∑ w_k`) and `∑_{k < K} ‖w_k‖ ≤ c / √s + ‖u‖ / 4`. Then `‖u‖ ≤ ρ(δ) c / √s + τ(δ) ‖z‖`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasRobustNullspaceProperty_of_hasRestrictedIsometry
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.49, robust null space property: if `A` has the RIP of order `2 s` with constant `0 ≤ δ < 4 / √41`, then `‖v_S‖₂ ≤ ρ(δ) / √s ‖v_{Sᶜ}‖₁ + τ(δ) ‖A v‖` for every `v` and every set `S` of at most `s` coordinates.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_basisPursuit_error_bound
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.49: stable basis pursuit, with constants depending only on the RIP bound. For `0 ≤ δ < 4 / √41` there are `C, D > 0` such that whenever `A` has the RIP of order `2 s` with constant `δ`, `‖A β - y‖ ≤ η`, and `b` is a basis pursuit estimate with residual bound `η`, `‖b - β‖₁ ≤ C σ_s(β)₁ + D √s η` and `‖b - β‖₂ ≤ C σ_s(β)₁ / √s + D η`.

declarations.name: CKSD.airyLeadingAsymptotic
declarations.doc: The leading term `s ^ (-1/4) exp (-(2/3) s ^ (3/2)) / (2 √π)` of the Airy function as `s → ∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsHastingsMcLeodSolution
declarations.doc: The Hastings–McLeod solution of Painlevé II: a twice continuously differentiable solution of `q'' = s q + 2 q ^ 3` with `q(s) ~ Ai(s)` as `s → ∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tracyWidomOneCDF
declarations.doc: The Tracy–Widom distribution function `F₁` of the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble, built from a Hastings–McLeod solution `q`.

declarations.name: CKSD.standardGaussianMatrixLaw
declarations.doc: The law of an `n × p` matrix with independent standard normal entries.

declarations.name: CKSD.largestSampleCovarianceEigenvalue
declarations.doc: The largest eigenvalue of the sample covariance `n⁻¹ XᵀX` of an `n × p` data matrix.

declarations.name: CKSD.johnstoneCenter
declarations.doc: Johnstone's centering `(√(n-1) + √p) ^ 2 / n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_largestSampleCovarianceEigenvalue_tracyWidom
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.38: Johnstone's Tracy–Widom limit for the largest eigenvalue of a white Wishart matrix as `n → ∞` with `p / n → y ∈ (0, ∞)` (so that `p → ∞` as well), in the form of convergence of distribution functions to the continuous limit `F₁`.

declarations.name: CKSD.standardGaussianArrayLaw
declarations.doc: The law of a doubly infinite array of independent standard normal variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.spikedDataMatrix
declarations.doc: The `n × p` spiked data matrix with covariance `diag(α, 1, …, 1)` read off a standard normal array.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_largestEigenvalue_spiked_subcritical
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.38, subcritical spike: for `1 < α ≤ 1 + √y` the largest sample covariance eigenvalue converges almost surely to the bulk edge `(1 + √y) ^ 2`. Here `n → ∞` and `p / n → y > 0` (which force `p → ∞`). Scope: diagonal spiked covariance on the array coupling described in the module header.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_tendsto_largestEigenvalue_spiked_supercritical
declarations.doc: GAPS 103.38, supercritical spike: for `α > 1 + √y` the largest sample covariance eigenvalue converges almost surely to `α + y α / (α - 1)`. Here `n → ∞` and `p / n → y > 0` (which force `p → ∞`). Scope: diagonal spiked covariance on the array coupling described in the module header.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsWeaklyStationary
declarations.doc: A sequence `X : ℤ → H` in an inner-product space is weakly stationary when its Gram matrix is shift invariant: `⟪X s, X t⟫ = ⟪X 0, X (t - s)⟫` for all `s, t`. Applied to centred square-integrable random variables in `L²`, this is weak (second-order) stationarity of the process.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsWeaklyStationary.inner_eq_inner_sub_zero
declarations.doc: For a weakly stationary sequence, `⟪X s, X t⟫ = ⟪X (s - t), X 0⟫`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDNoise
declarations.doc: An iid centred noise sequence on `ℤ` with variance `σ² > 0`: the `Z t` are measurable, mutually independent and identically distributed, `𝔼 Z_0 = 0` and `𝔼 Z_0² = σ²`. Square integrability is not a separate condition: it follows from `𝔼 Z_0² = σ² ≠ 0` (`IsIIDNoise.memLp_two`).

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDNoise.identDistrib
declarations.doc: Each term of an iid noise sequence has the law of `Z 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDNoise.memLp_two
declarations.doc: Every term of an iid noise sequence is square integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDNoise.integral_eq_zero'
declarations.doc: Every term of an iid noise sequence is centred.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDNoise.integral_sq'
declarations.doc: Every term of an iid noise sequence has second moment `σ²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_id_two_of_variance_pos
declarations.doc: A real law with positive variance has a finite second moment: `0 < Var(P)` forces the integrand `(x - 𝔼x)²` to be integrable, since a Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is `0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sampleAutocovariance
declarations.doc: The sample autocovariance `γ̂(h) = n⁻¹ ∑_{i < n - h} (X_{i+h} - X̄_n)(X_i - X̄_n)` at lag `h` of `X 0, …, X (n - 1)`, with the sample mean `X̄_n` and divisor `n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.riskSetSize
declarations.doc: The size `#{j < n : min (T j) (C j) ≥ min (T i) (C i)}` of the risk set at the observed time of subject `i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.nelsonAalenEstimator
declarations.doc: The Nelson–Aalen estimator `Λ̂(t) = ∑ 1 / #(risk set)` of the cumulative hazard, with one term for each subject `i < n` whose failure `T i ≤ C i` is observed by time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.kaplanMeierEstimator
declarations.doc: The Kaplan–Meier estimator `Ŝ(t) = ∏ (1 - 1 / #(risk set))` of the survival function, with one factor for each subject `i < n` whose failure `T i ≤ C i` is observed by time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.brownianBridgeSupremum
declarations.doc: Supremum of the absolute Brownian bridge on the unit interval.

declarations.name: CKSD.cusumBridgeStatistic
declarations.doc: Standardized maximum of a finite partial-sum bridge.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_cusumBridgeStatistic
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.39: the iid finite-variance CUSUM statistic converges to the Brownian-bridge supremum: for iid observations with positive (hence finite) variance `σ²`, `max_{k ≤ n} |S_k - (k / n) S_n| / (σ √n) ⇒ sup_{t ∈ [0, 1]} |B_t - t B_1|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.cusumBridgeStatistic_zero
declarations.doc: At sample size zero, the standardized CUSUM statistic uses division-by-zero value zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.coxPartialLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: Cox's partial log-likelihood `∑_{i : δ_i = 1} (β·z_i - log ∑_{j : t_j ≥ t_i} e^{β·z_j})` of a finite sample with observed times `t_i`, failure indicators `δ_i` and covariates `z_i` in a real inner-product space, without correction for tied failure times.

declarations.name: CKSD.coxSampleLogLikelihood
declarations.doc: The Cox partial log-likelihood of the first `n` observations `D i = (Z_i, T_i, C_i)`, with observed times `min (T_i) (C_i)` and failures counted only when observed in `[0, τ]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.coxRiskMean
declarations.doc: The Cox risk-set average `ē(u) = 𝔼[Y(u) Z e^{β·Z}] / 𝔼[Y(u) e^{β·Z}]`, with `Y(u) = 1{min(T,C) ≥ u}`, for a law of `(Z, T, C)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.coxInformation
declarations.doc: The Cox information `𝓘 = 𝔼 ∫_0^τ (Z - ē(u))^{⊗2} dN(u)`, with `N` jumping at an observed failure `T ≤ C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_coxPartialLikelihoodMaximizer
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.30: consistency and asymptotic normality of the maximum partial-likelihood estimator in the Cox model, with the partial likelihood restricted to failures in `[0, τ]`, bounded covariates, conditionally independent censoring, `P(min(T,C) ≥ τ) > 0`, and positive definite information. The estimator is any measurable choice that maximizes the partial likelihood whenever a maximizer exists. The efficiency and log-rank interpretations are not restated.

declarations.name: CKSD.jumpIntegral
declarations.doc: The pathwise Lebesgue–Stieltjes integral `∫_(0,t] H dN = ∑_{0 < s ≤ t} ΔN(s) H(s)` of a pure-jump path with finitely many jumps on `(0, t]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCountingPath
declarations.doc: A counting path: starts at `0`, nondecreasing, right-continuous, integer-valued, with jumps of size at most one.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsCountingProcessWithIntensity
declarations.doc: A `k`-variate counting process without simultaneous jumps, with nonnegative predictable locally integrable intensities `λ_h` for which `N_h - ∫_0^· λ_h` are martingales.

declarations.name: CKSD.countingMartingaleTransform
declarations.doc: The counting-process martingale transform `M_j(t) = ∑_h ∫_0^t H_{jh} (dN_h - λ_h ds)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_countingMartingaleTransform
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.34: Rebolledo's central limit theorem for counting-process martingale transforms, in finite-dimensional form: under convergence in probability of the predictable variations to a continuous deterministic `V` and the Lindeberg condition, the values of `M^{(n)}` at finitely many times in `[0, τ]` converge jointly in law to those of the continuous Gaussian martingale with covariance `V(s ∧ t)`. Restrictions: the compensated counting processes are martingales rather than local martingales, all processes live on one probability space, and weak convergence in `D[0,τ]^k` is replaced by convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions. The limit `V` automatically satisfies `V 0 = 0` and has positive-semidefinite increments on `[0, τ]`, as a limit in probability of predictable variations with these properties.

declarations.name: CKSD.pastSigmaAlgebra
declarations.doc: The past σ-algebra `σ(X_s : s ≤ t)` of a real process on `ℤ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_pastSigmaAlgebra_of_le
declarations.doc: The coordinate `ε_s` is measurable with respect to the past `σ(ε_r : r ≤ t)` when `s ≤ t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.pastSigmaAlgebra_mono
declarations.doc: The past σ-algebras increase with time.

declarations.name: CKSD.pastSigmaAlgebra_le
declarations.doc: The past σ-algebras of a measurable process are sub-σ-algebras.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_of_measurable_pastSigmaAlgebra
declarations.doc: A function of the strict past `σ(ε_s : s < t)` of an independent sequence is independent of `ε_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.futureSigmaAlgebra
declarations.doc: The future σ-algebra `σ(X_s : s ≥ t)` of a real process on `ℤ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.strongMixingCoefficient
declarations.doc: The strong mixing coefficient `α(k) = sup |P(A ∩ B) - P(A) P(B)|` over `A ∈ σ(X_s : s ≤ 0)`, `B ∈ σ(X_s : s ≥ k)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.blockMean
declarations.doc: The mean of the block `x_i, …, x_{i+b-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.movingBlockBootstrapLaw
declarations.doc: The moving-block bootstrap law of `√(ℓb) (X̄*_n - 𝔼* X̄*_n)` given data `x_0, …, x_{n-1}`, for block length `b` and `ℓ = ⌊n/b⌋` blocks with starting indices uniform on `n - b + 1` positions.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_kolmogorovDistance_movingBlockBootstrapLaw
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.11: consistency of the moving-block bootstrap for the mean of a strictly stationary strongly mixing sequence with `𝔼|X|^{2+δ} < ∞` and `∑ α(k)^{δ/(2+δ)} < ∞`: the autocovariances are absolutely summable, `√n (X̄_n - μ) ⇒ N(0, σ²_∞)`, and the Kolmogorov distance between the bootstrap law and the law of `√n (X̄_n - μ)` tends to `0` in probability, for block lengths `b → ∞` with `b/n → 0` (so that eventually `1 ≤ b ≤ n`).

declarations.name: CKSD.kernelGram
declarations.doc: The Gram matrix `(k i j)_{i,j<n}` of a covariance kernel on the first `n` indices.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearPredictionError
declarations.doc: The error `ψ - ∑_i a_i h_i` of the best linear predictor of `ψ` from the first `n` coordinates, computed as if the covariance were `k`, with cross-covariances of `ψ` taken under the law `Q` whose coordinate covariance is `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eventually_abs_linearPredictionError_div_sub_one_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.21: Stein's theorem on asymptotically efficient prediction under equivalent Gaussian laws. The coordinates are linearly independent under `k₀`, the laws `P₀` and `P₁` are centred Gaussian with covariances `k₀` and `k₁`, and `ψ` ranges over the closed linear span `H` of the coordinates in `L²(P₀)`. Uniformly over `ψ ∈ H` with nonzero `P₀`-error, the relative excess error of the `k₁`-predictor and the relative misstatement of its error tend to zero; the exchanged roles are the same statement applied to `(k₁, P₁, k₀, P₀)`. The Gram matrices of `k₁` are automatically positive semidefinite: otherwise the marginal of `P₁` is a Dirac mass, which is not equivalent to the nondegenerate marginal of `P₀`.

declarations.name: CKSD.distributionUpperEndpoint
declarations.doc: Right endpoint of a real distribution, allowed to be infinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.thresholdExcessLaw
declarations.doc: The conditional law of the excess over a threshold.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasExtremeValueDomainOfAttraction
declarations.doc: Membership in the domain of attraction of the unit-scale generalized extreme-value law.

declarations.name: CKSD.thresholdParetoDiscrepancy
declarations.doc: Uniform discrepancy over all nonnegative excesses, including the terminal jump, against a fitted generalized Pareto law.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasExtremeValueDomainOfAttraction_iff_pareto_excesses
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.47: Pickands–Balkema–de Haan theorem. `F` lies in the domain of attraction of the generalized extreme-value law with index `γ` if and only if there is a positive scale function `σ(u)` such that the excess law over `u` is uniformly approximated by the generalized Pareto law with scale `σ(u)` and shape `γ` as `u` increases to the upper endpoint, finite or infinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasSecondOrderTailQuantile
declarations.doc: Second-order regular variation of the tail quantile `U` with index `γ`, second-order parameter `ρ` and auxiliary function `A`: `A(t) → 0` with eventually constant sign, and `(U(tx)/U(t) - x^γ) / A(t) → x^γ (x^ρ - 1) / ρ` for every `x > 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.hillEstimator
declarations.doc: The Hill estimator `k⁻¹ ∑_{i<k} log X_{(n-i)} - log X_{(n-k)}` from the `k + 1` largest order statistics of `x`; it is defined to be zero unless `1 ≤ k < n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_hillEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.49: Hill central limit theorem. For iid positive observations whose tail quantile is second-order regularly varying with index `γ > 0` and parameter `ρ < 0`, and intermediate sequences `k_n → ∞`, `k_n / n → 0` with `√k_n A(n / k_n) → b`, `√k_n (γ̂_n - γ) ⇒ N(b / (1 - ρ), γ²)`. Regular variation of the tail `1 - F` with index `-1/γ` follows from the second-order condition and is not assumed separately.

declarations.name: CKSD.hillEstimator_zero
declarations.doc: The Hill estimator of order zero uses the explicitly specified zero convention.

declarations.name: CKSD.thresholdExcessLaw_generalizedPareto
declarations.doc: Threshold stability of the generalized Pareto laws: the excess law over `u ≥ 0` of the generalized Pareto law with scale `s` and shape `γ` is generalized Pareto with scale `s + γ u` and the same shape (TauCeti's `map_sub_cond_generalizedParetoMeasure`).

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_integral_binomial_poissonMeasure
declarations.doc: Poisson limit of the binomial law tested against bounded functions: if `n p_n → τ`, then `∫ f d Bin(n, p_n) → ∫ f d Po(τ)`. The pointwise limit of the probabilities is Mathlib's `tendsto_choose_mul_pow_of_tendsto_mul_atTop`; the bound `C (sup_n n p_n)^k / k!` allows Tannery's theorem.

declarations.name: CKSD.card_filter_univ_fin_eq_card_filter_range
declarations.doc: Counting indices in `Fin n` and in `range n` agree.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_card_exceedances_binomial
declarations.doc: The number of exceedances of a level among the first `n` iid observations is binomial, by TauCeti's Poisson-binomial law of counts of independent events.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_sub_cdf_eq_measureReal_Ioi
declarations.doc: The tail of a probability measure on the line is the mass of the open upper ray: `1 - F(c) = P(c, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_forall_le_eq_pow
declarations.doc: The probability that the first `n` iid observations do not exceed `c` is `F(c)^n`, written as `(1 - (1 - F(c)))^n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_measureReal_forall_le_of_tendsto_mul
declarations.doc: If `n (1 - F(u_n)) → τ`, the probability that none of the first `n` iid observations exceeds `u_n` tends to `e^{-τ}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tailQuantile
declarations.doc: The tail quantile `U(t) = F^←(1 - 1/t)`, TauCeti's quantile of `P` at level `1 - 1/t`; it is used for `t > 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_sub_cdf_tailQuantile_le
declarations.doc: At the tail quantile the tail mass is at most `1/t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lt_one_sub_cdf_of_lt_tailQuantile
declarations.doc: Below the tail quantile the tail mass exceeds `1/t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.HasRegularlyVaryingTail
declarations.doc: The tail `1 - F` is positive everywhere (the upper endpoint is infinite) and regularly varying at infinity with index `-1/γ`: `(1 - F(tx)) / (1 - F(t)) → x^{-1/γ}` for every `x > 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_tailQuantile_atTop
declarations.doc: Under an everywhere positive tail, the tail quantiles `U(n)` tend to infinity.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_mul_one_sub_cdf_tailQuantile
declarations.doc: If `1 - F` is regularly varying with index `-1/γ`, `γ > 0`, then `n (1 - F(U(n))) → 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_maximum_of_hasRegularlyVaryingTail
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.46, sufficient condition for the Fréchet limit: if `1 - F` is regularly varying with index `-1/γ`, `γ > 0`, then `P(max_{i<n} X_i ≤ U(n) x) → exp(-x^{-1/γ})` for every `x > 0`, with `U` the tail quantile.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_card_exceedances
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.50, finite-intensity exceedance limit (also the independent case of GAPS 106.48): if `n (1 - F(u_n)) → τ`, the number of exceedances of `u_n` among the first `n` iid observations converges in law to the Poisson law with mean `τ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_norm_sum_range_mul_cexp
declarations.doc: The squared modulus of a real discrete Fourier transform: `|∑_{t<n} z_t e^{-itν}|² = (∑_{t<n} z_t cos tν)² + (∑_{t<n} z_t sin tν)²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_euclidean_of_forall_apply
declarations.doc: Convergence to `0` in probability of Euclidean vectors follows from convergence of each coordinate.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sq_norm_sub_sq_norm
declarations.doc: Stochastic algebra for squared moduli: if `‖a_n - b_n‖ → 0` in probability and `‖b_n‖ ≤ C R_n` with `R_n` bounded in probability, then `‖a_n‖² - ‖b_n‖² → 0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsBoundedInProbability.congr'
declarations.doc: Boundedness in probability depends only on the eventual values of the sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_tsum_mul_cexp
declarations.doc: Continuity of the transfer function `x ↦ ∑_j ψ_j e^{-ijx}` of an absolutely summable filter.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_tsum_mul_cexp_le
declarations.doc: The transfer function of an absolutely summable filter is bounded by `∑_j |ψ_j|`.

declarations.name: CKSD.eventually_round_fourier
declarations.doc: Nearest Fourier frequencies to distinct frequencies `x_j ∈ (0, π)`: with `k_n(j) = round(n x_j / (2π))`, eventually `0 < 2 k_n(j) < n` and the `k_n(j)` are distinct, and `2π k_n(j) / n → x_j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDNoise.tendstoInDistribution_periodogram_filter_div
declarations.doc: Fourier-frequency form of the limit law of the periodogram of a linear process: for iid noise of variance `σ²`, `∑_j |ψ_j| < ∞`, integer frequencies `k_n(j)` with eventually `0 < 2k_n(j) < n` distinct, `2πk_n(j)/n → x_j` and `ψ(e^{-ix_j}) ≠ 0`, the ratios `I_n(2πk_n(j)/n) / f(x_j)` of the periodogram of `X_t = ∑_l ψ_l Z_{t-l}` to the spectral density `f = σ² |ψ(e^{-i·})|² / (2π)` converge jointly in law to independent standard exponential variables (Brockwell–Davis, Theorem 10.3.2).

declarations.name: CKSD.posSemidef_mul_mul_transpose
declarations.doc: A real congruence `A S Aᵀ` of a positive-semidefinite matrix is positive semidefinite; this is Mathlib's `Matrix.PosSemidef.mul_mul_conjTranspose_same` for real matrices.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_toEuclideanLin_multivariateGaussian_zero
declarations.doc: A matrix image of a centered multivariate Gaussian vector is centered Gaussian with the congruent covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.hasLaw_toEuclideanLin_add_of_indepFun
declarations.doc: For independent centered Gaussian vectors `ε` and `v`, the combination `A₁ ε + A₂ v` is centered Gaussian with covariance `A₁ S₁ A₁ᵀ + A₂ S₂ A₂ᵀ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_toEuclideanLin_add_of_indepFun
declarations.doc: Two linear combinations `A₁ ε + A₂ v` and `B₁ ε + B₂ v` of independent centered Gaussian vectors are independent when their cross-covariance `A₁ S₁ B₁ᵀ + A₂ S₂ B₂ᵀ` vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianShiftKernel
declarations.doc: The Gaussian location kernel `m ↦ N(m, S)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.gaussianShiftKernel_apply
declarations.doc: The Gaussian shift kernel at `m` is the Gaussian law with mean `m` and covariance `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_multivariateGaussianPDF_uncurry
declarations.doc: The multivariate Gaussian density is jointly measurable in the mean and the point.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_prodMk_add_eq_compProd
declarations.doc: If `Z` has law `N(0, S)` and is independent of `Y`, then the joint law of `Y` and `g(Y) + Z` is the composition of the law of `Y` with the Gaussian kernel `y ↦ N(g y, S)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.condDistrib_add_eq_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: If `Z` has law `N(0, S)` and is independent of `Y`, then the conditional law of `g(Y) + Z` given `Y = y` is `N(g y, S)` for almost every `y`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_of_measurable_biSup
declarations.doc: Functions measurable with respect to the σ-algebras generated by disjoint index sets of an independent family are independent.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_biSup_sum
declarations.doc: A finite partial sum over indices in `S` is measurable for the σ-algebra generated by `S`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_of_measurable_biSup_of_notMem
declarations.doc: A function measurable with respect to `σ(Y_s : s ∈ S)` is independent of `Y_k` for `k ∉ S`, for an independent family `Y`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_randomIndex
declarations.doc: Evaluating a sequence of measurable functions at a measurable random index is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_prodMk_of_indepFun_of_indepFun_prodMk
declarations.doc: If `X` is independent of `Y` and the pair `(X, Y)` is independent of `Z`, then `X` is independent of the pair `(Y, Z)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.iIndepFun_of_indepFun_finPrefix
declarations.doc: A sequence of random variables is mutually independent when each term is independent of the vector of its predecessors.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_prodMk_left_of_indepFun_prodMk
declarations.doc: If `A` is independent of the pair `(B, C)` and `B` is independent of `C`, then the pair `(A, B)` is independent of `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indep_fun_apply_prefix_of_indep_fun
declarations.doc: In a family consisting of an initial value `x₀`, a sequence `w`, and a mutually independent sequence `v`, with `x₀` independent of `(w, v)` and `w` independent of `v`, the term `v t` is independent of `x₀`, the whole sequence `w`, and the terms `v i` with `i < t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.indepFun_apply_prefix_of_indepFun'
declarations.doc: In the setting of `indepFun_apply_prefix_of_indepFun`, with `w` mutually independent, the term `w t` is independent of `x₀`, the terms `w i` with `i < t`, and the whole sequence `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs
declarations.doc: The hypotheses of the Kalman filter theorem: positive-semidefinite noise and initial covariances, a Gaussian initial state, independent Gaussian white noises independent of the initial state, and nonsingular innovation covariances.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.predCov_posSemidef'
declarations.doc: Every predicted covariance is positive semidefinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.aemeasurable_indepFun_predErr
declarations.doc: The prediction error and the observation record at time `t` are jointly almost everywhere measurable, and the observation noise at time `t` is independent of them.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.aemeasurable_indepFun_filtErr
declarations.doc: The filtering error at time `t` and the observation record up to time `t` are jointly almost everywhere measurable, and the state noise at time `t` is independent of them.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.measurement_update
declarations.doc: Measurement update. If the prediction error at time `t` has law `N(0, P_{t|t-1})` and is independent of `y_0, …, y_{t-1}`, then the innovation has law `N(0, Σ_t)`, the filtering error has law `N(0, P_{t|t})` and is independent of `y_0, …, y_t`, and the innovation is independent of `y_0, …, y_{t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.time_update
declarations.doc: Time update. If the filtering error at time `t` has law `N(0, P_{t|t})` and is independent of `y_0, …, y_t`, then the prediction error at time `t + 1` has law `N(0, P_{t+1|t})` and is independent of `y_0, …, y_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.predErr_hasLaw_indepFun
declarations.doc: The prediction errors: at every time `t`, `x_t - x_{t|t-1}` has law `N(0, P_{t|t-1})` and is independent of `y_0, …, y_{t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.condDistrib_state
declarations.doc: Conditionally on `y_0, …, y_t`, the state `x_t` is Gaussian with the filtered mean and covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.condDistrib_state_succ
