declarations.doc: Conditionally on `y_0, …, y_t`, the state `x_{t+1}` is Gaussian with the predicted mean and covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.hasLaw_innovation
declarations.doc: The innovation at time `t` has law `N(0, Σ_t)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.indepFun_innovation_obsPrefix
declarations.doc: The innovation at time `t` is independent of `y_0, …, y_{t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.iIndepFun_innovation
declarations.doc: The innovations are mutually independent.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.GaussianInputs.map_obsPrefix_eq_withDensity
declarations.doc: The law of `(y_0, …, y_{n-1})` has density the product of the one-step predictive densities.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.kalman_filter
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.7: the Kalman filter for a finite-dimensional time-varying linear Gaussian state-space model with positive-semidefinite noise and initial covariances, independent Gaussian white noises independent of the Gaussian initial state, and nonsingular innovation covariances. Conditionally on `y_0, …, y_t`, the state `x_t` is Gaussian with the filtered mean and covariance and `x_{t+1}` with the predicted ones; the innovations `y_t - H_t x_{t|t-1}` are independent with laws `N(0, Σ_t)`; and the density of `(y_0, …, y_{n-1})` is the product of the one-step predictive densities.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel
declarations.doc: Coefficients of a time-varying linear Gaussian state-space model whose state coordinates are indexed by `ι` and whose observation coordinates are indexed by `κ` (finite types in all results).

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovCovOf
declarations.doc: Innovation covariance `H_t C H_tᵀ + R_t` for a predicted covariance `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.gainOf
declarations.doc: Kalman gain `C H_tᵀ (H_t C H_tᵀ + R_t)⁻¹` for a predicted covariance `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtCovOf
declarations.doc: Filtered covariance `C - K_t H_t C` for a predicted covariance `C`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predCov
declarations.doc: Predicted covariances `P_{t|t-1}`, with `P_{0|-1}` the initial covariance.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovCov
declarations.doc: Innovation covariances `Σ_t = H_t P_{t|t-1} H_tᵀ + R_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.gain
declarations.doc: Kalman gains `K_t = P_{t|t-1} H_tᵀ Σ_t⁻¹`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtCov
declarations.doc: Filtered covariances `P_{t|t} = P_{t|t-1} - K_t H_t P_{t|t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predMean
declarations.doc: Predicted means `x_{t|t-1}` as functions of the observations, with `x_{0|-1}` the initial mean and `x_{t+1|t} = F_t x_{t|t}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtMean
declarations.doc: Filtered means `x_{t|t} = x_{t|t-1} + K_t (y_t - H_t x_{t|t-1})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.state
declarations.doc: The state process `x_0 = x₀`, `x_{t+1} = F_t x_t + w_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.observationProcess
declarations.doc: The observation process `y_t = H_t x_t + v_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.extendObservations
declarations.doc: Extension of a finite observation record `y_0, …, y_{n-1}` by zeros.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_extendObservations_apply
declarations.doc: A zero-extended observation record is measurable in each coordinate.

declarations.name: CKSD.extendObservations_of_lt
declarations.doc: The zero extension of a finite record returns the recorded values.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predMean_congr
declarations.doc: The predicted mean at time `t` depends only on the observations before time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtMean_congr
declarations.doc: The filtered mean at time `t` depends only on the observations up to time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predMean_succ
declarations.doc: The time update of the mean: `x_{t+1|t} = F_t x_{t|t}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_predMean
declarations.doc: The predicted mean is a measurable function of a measurably parametrized observation sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_filtMean
declarations.doc: The filtered mean is a measurable function of a measurably parametrized observation sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.state_congr
declarations.doc: The state at time `s` is unchanged by a change of sample space that preserves the initial state and the state noises before time `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_state
declarations.doc: The state process is measurable when the initial state and the noises are.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_observationProcess
declarations.doc: The observation process is measurable when the state and the observation noise are.

declarations.name: CKSD.extendObservations_snoc
declarations.doc: Appending a value to a finite record does not change its zero extension below the old length.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovDensity
declarations.doc: The product of the one-step predictive densities `∏_{i<n} φ(y_i; H_i x_{i|i-1}, Σ_i)` of an observation record `(y_0, …, y_{n-1})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_predMean_extendObservations
declarations.doc: The predicted mean computed from a zero-extended record is measurable in the record.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_filtMean_extendObservations
declarations.doc: The filtered mean computed from a zero-extended record is measurable in the record.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_innovDensity_factor
declarations.doc: Each one-step predictive density factor is measurable in the record.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_innovDensity
declarations.doc: The product of predictive densities is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovDensity_snoc
declarations.doc: The product of predictive densities factors over the last observation.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.gain_mul_innovCov
declarations.doc: With a nonsingular innovation covariance, `K_t Σ_t = P_{t|t-1} H_tᵀ`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtErr_innovation_cross
declarations.doc: The cross-covariance of the filtered error and the innovation vanishes: `(I - K_t H_t) P_{t|t-1} H_tᵀ - K_t R_t = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtCov_eq_joseph
declarations.doc: Joseph form of the filtered covariance: with a nonsingular innovation covariance, `(I - K_t H_t) P (I - K_t H_t)ᵀ + K_t R_t K_tᵀ = P - K_t H_t P`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.pred_cov_pos_semidef
declarations.doc: Under positive-semidefinite noise and initial covariances and nonsingular innovation covariances, every predicted covariance is positive semidefinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtCov_posSemidef
declarations.doc: Under the hypotheses of `predCov_posSemidef`, every filtered covariance is positive semidefinite.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovCov_posDef
declarations.doc: Under the hypotheses of `predCov_posSemidef`, every innovation covariance is positive definite.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.obsProc
declarations.doc: The observation process `y_t = H_t x_t + v_t` driven by `x₀`, `w`, and `v`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.obsPrefix
declarations.doc: The observation record `(y_0, …, y_{n-1})`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predErr
declarations.doc: The prediction error `x_t - x_{t|t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtErr
declarations.doc: The filtering error `x_t - x_{t|t}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovation
declarations.doc: The innovation `y_t - H_t x_{t|t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.innovation_eq
declarations.doc: The innovation is `H_t (x_t - x_{t|t-1}) + v_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtErr_eq
declarations.doc: The filtering error is `(I - K_t H_t)(x_t - x_{t|t-1}) - K_t v_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predErr_succ
declarations.doc: The prediction error at time `t + 1` is `F_t (x_t - x_{t|t}) + w_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.obsPrefix_succ_eq
declarations.doc: The observation record up to time `t` is obtained from the record before time `t` and the innovation at time `t` by appending `e_t + H_t x_{t|t-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.obsProc_congr
declarations.doc: Observations up to time `s` are unchanged by a change of sample space that preserves the initial state, the state noises before time `s`, and the observation noise at time `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.predErr_obsPrefix_congr
declarations.doc: The prediction error and the observation record at time `t` are unchanged by a change of sample space that preserves the initial state and the noises before time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.filtErr_obsPrefix_congr
declarations.doc: The filtering error at time `t` and the observation record up to time `t` are unchanged by a change of sample space that preserves the initial state, the state noises before time `t`, and the observation noises up to time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_obsProc
declarations.doc: The observation process is measurable for measurable inputs.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_obsPrefix
declarations.doc: The observation record is measurable for measurable inputs.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_predErr
declarations.doc: The prediction error is measurable for measurable inputs.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.measurable_filtErr
declarations.doc: The filtering error is measurable for measurable inputs.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.exists_predErr_obsPrefix_eq_comp
declarations.doc: The prediction error and the observation record at time `t` are a measurable function of the initial state, the state noises, and the observation noises before time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.KalmanModel.exists_filtErr_obsPrefix_eq_comp
declarations.doc: The filtering error at time `t` and the observation record up to time `t` are a measurable function of the initial state, the state noises before time `t`, and the observation noises.

declarations.name: CKSD.brownianBridge
declarations.doc: The bridge `t ↦ B(t) - t B(1)` of a process `B` indexed by `ℝ≥0`, pinned at times zero and one; for a Brownian motion `B` it is the Brownian bridge on `[0, 1]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.thresholdHittingTime
declarations.doc: The first time `n` with `a ≤ V n ω`, with value `⊤` if the level is never reached.

declarations.name: CKSD.cusumStatistic
declarations.doc: Page's CUSUM likelihood-ratio statistic `W_0 = 0`, `W_{n+1} = max(1, W_n) · L_n`, for likelihood ratios `L 0, L 1, …`; the CUSUM procedure stops when `W_n ≥ A`.

declarations.name: CKSD.shiryaevRobertsStatistic
declarations.doc: The Shiryaev–Roberts statistic `R_0 = 0`, `R_{n+1} = (1 + R_n) · L_n`, for likelihood ratios `L 0, L 1, …`.

declarations.name: CKSD.shiryaevRobertsStatistic_nonneg
declarations.doc: The Shiryaev–Roberts statistic of nonnegative likelihood ratios is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.cusumStatistic_le_shiryaevRobertsStatistic
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.44, pathwise comparison: for nonnegative likelihood ratios the CUSUM statistic is at most the Shiryaev–Roberts statistic, `W_n ≤ R_n`. Hence the CUSUM stopping time is at least the Shiryaev–Roberts stopping time for the same threshold, which underlies the false-alarm bound `𝔼_∞ T_CS(A) ≥ A`.

declarations.name: CKSD.brownianBridge_one
declarations.doc: The bridge is pinned at its right endpoint.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_range_exp_two_pi_mul_div_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Sums of `n`-th roots of unity: `∑_{t < n} e^{2πi r t / n} = 0` when `n ∤ r`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_range_cos_two_pi_mul_div_eq_zero
declarations.doc: `∑_{t < n} cos (2π r t / n) = 0` when `n ∤ r`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_range_sin_two_pi_mul_div_eq_zero
declarations.doc: `∑_{t < n} sin (2π r t / n) = 0` when `n ∤ r`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_range_cos_mul_cos_fourier
declarations.doc: Discrete orthogonality of cosines at Fourier frequencies `2πk/n`, `0 < k < n/2`: `∑_{t < n} cos (2πkt/n) cos (2πlt/n) = (n/2) 1{k = l}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_range_sin_mul_sin_fourier
declarations.doc: Discrete orthogonality of sines at Fourier frequencies `2πk/n`, `0 < k < n/2`: `∑_{t < n} sin (2πkt/n) sin (2πlt/n) = (n/2) 1{k = l}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_range_cos_mul_sin_fourier
declarations.doc: Discrete orthogonality of cosines and sines at Fourier frequencies `2πk/n`, `0 < k < n/2`: `∑_{t < n} cos (2πkt/n) sin (2πlt/n) = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.fourierTrig
declarations.doc: The trigonometric coordinate functions: `cos` for `i = 0` and `sin` for `i = 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.abs_fourierTrig_le_one
declarations.doc: The trigonometric coordinate functions are bounded by one.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_range_fourierTrig_mul
declarations.doc: Discrete orthogonality of the cosine and sine vectors at distinct Fourier frequencies `2π k_j / n`, `0 < k_j < n/2`: `∑_{t < n} φ_p(t) φ_{p'}(t) = (n/2) 1{p = p'}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_inner_stdGaussian
declarations.doc: The scalar projection `z ↦ ⟪z, s⟫` of the standard Gaussian law is `N(0, ‖s‖²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_fourierTrig_sum
declarations.doc: Central limit theorem for the discrete Fourier transform of iid noise at Fourier frequencies: if eventually `0 < k_n(j) < n/2` with distinct `k_n(j)`, the normalized cosine and sine sums `√(2/(nσ²)) ∑_{t<n} Z_t φ_i(2π k_n(j) t / n)` converge jointly in law to independent standard normal variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_half_sum_sq_pi_gaussianReal
declarations.doc: Half the squared norm of two independent standard normal variables is standard exponential: `(Z₀² + Z₁²)/2 ∼ Exp(1)`, from `χ²₂ = Exp(1/2)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_stdGaussian_half_sum_sq
declarations.doc: The halved squared lengths of the coordinate pairs of a standard Gaussian vector on `Fin m × Fin 2` are independent standard exponential variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDNoise.integral_sq_sum_mul
declarations.doc: Second moments of weighted sums of iid noise at distinct times: `𝔼[(∑_{t<n} a_t Z_{s(t)})²] = σ² ∑_{t<n} a_t²` for injective `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDNoise.integral_norm_sum_mul_le
declarations.doc: First absolute moments of complex weighted sums of iid noise at distinct times: for `‖c_t‖ ≤ 1`, `𝔼‖∑_{t<n} Z_{s(t)} c_t‖ ≤ 2 √(σ² n)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_norm_sum_shift_sub_le
declarations.doc: Shift bound: if `𝔼‖W_s‖ ≤ M` for integrable `W_s`, then `𝔼‖∑_{t<n} (W_{t-j} - W_t)‖ ≤ 2 |j| M`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDNoise.integral_abs_le_sqrt
declarations.doc: First absolute moment bound `𝔼|Z_t| ≤ σ` for iid noise of variance `σ²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDNoise.ae_summable_abs_mul
declarations.doc: For iid noise and an absolutely summable filter, almost surely `∑_j |ψ_j| |Z_{s-j}| < ∞` for every `s`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsIIDNoise.tendstoInMeasure_dft_filter_sub
declarations.doc: Linear-process approximation of the discrete Fourier transform, uniformly along any frequency sequence `ν_n`: for iid noise and `∑_j |ψ_j| < ∞`, `n^{-1/2} ‖∑_{t<n} X_t e^{-itν_n} - ψ(e^{-iν_n}) ∑_{t<n} Z_t e^{-itν_n}‖ → 0` in probability, where `X_t = ∑_j ψ_j Z_{t-j}` and `ψ(e^{-iν}) = ∑_j ψ_j e^{-ijν}` (Brockwell–Davis, Theorem 10.3.1).

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_comp_eq_zero_of_iid
declarations.doc: Integrating out one coordinate of an iid sequence: if `G z w` has `P`-mean zero in `z` for every `w`, then `𝔼 G(Z i, (Z l)_{l ∈ T}) = 0` whenever `i ∉ T`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_eq_zero_of_iid_left
declarations.doc: For an iid sequence and a bounded kernel `g` with `P`-mean zero in its first argument, `𝔼[g(Z a, Z b) g(Z c, Z d)] = 0` whenever the index `a` occurs only once.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_mul_eq_zero_of_iid_right
declarations.doc: For an iid sequence and a bounded kernel `g` with `P`-mean zero in its second argument, `𝔼[g(Z a, Z b) g(Z c, Z d)] = 0` whenever the index `b` occurs only once.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_comp_pair_of_iid
declarations.doc: Integrability of a bounded measurable function of two coordinates of an iid sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sum_le_of_iid
declarations.doc: Second moment of a sum of a bounded kernel with mean zero in its second argument: `𝔼 (∑_{j<n} g(Z i, Z j))² ≤ n B²`, since the off-diagonal products have mean zero.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sum_sum_le_of_iid
declarations.doc: Second moment of a degenerate `V`-statistic: for a bounded kernel `g` with `P`-mean zero in each argument, `𝔼 (∑_{i,j<n} g(Z i, Z j))² ≤ 3 n² B²`, since a product `g(Z i, Z j) g(Z k, Z l)` has mean zero unless the indices pair up.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_zero_of_integral_le
declarations.doc: Markov's inequality in sequential form: nonnegative random variables whose means are eventually bounded by a null sequence converge to zero in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_zero_of_integral_sq_le
declarations.doc: Chebyshev's inequality in sequential form: random variables whose second moments are eventually bounded by a null sequence converge to zero in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sqrt_mul_sum_sum_div_of_iid
declarations.doc: A normalized degenerate `V`-statistic of a bounded kernel is negligible: `√n n⁻² ∑_{i,j<n} g(Z i, Z j) → 0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_riskSet_remainder
declarations.doc: The quadratic remainder of the risk-set expansion is negligible: with `Yᵢ = n⁻¹ #{j < n : x(Z i) ≤ x(Z j)}` and `y(s) = P(x ≥ s)`, the sum `√n n⁻¹ ∑_{i<n} A(Z i) (Yᵢ - y(x(Z i)))² / (y(x(Z i))² Yᵢ)` tends to zero in probability when `0 ≤ A ≤ 1` vanishes off `{x ≤ t}` and `y(t) > 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.riskSetSum_decomposition
declarations.doc: The algebraic decomposition behind `tendstoInDistribution_sqrt_mul_riskSetSum_sub`: with risk-set counts `Nᵢ = ∑_j I i j ≥ 1`, fractions `Yᵢ = Nᵢ / n` and `a = A / y²`, the normalized estimator splits into a linear term, a quadratic remainder and a `V`-statistic, using `1 / Y = 1 / y - (Y - y) / y² + (Y - y)² / (y² Y)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sqrt_mul_riskSetSum_sub
declarations.doc: Central limit theorem for a risk-set estimator `∑_{i<n} A(Z i) / #{j < n : x(Z i) ≤ x(Z j)}` of `θ = ∫ A / y(x) dP`, with `y(s) = P(x ≥ s)`, a weight `0 ≤ A ≤ 1` vanishing off `{x ≤ t}` and `y(t) > 0`. The estimator is expanded around `y` to first order; the first-order term is a `V`-statistic whose Hájek projection adds `-b` to the influence function, with `b(z') = ∫ a(z) (1{x z ≤ x z'} - y(x z)) dP(z)` and `a = A / y(x)²`, and the degenerate part and the quadratic remainder are negligible.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_stopped_sum
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.37, Wald's stopped-sum identity under the past/future independence condition, integrability part: if the `X i` have a common integrable law `P`, `N` is integrable, and each `X i` is independent of the event `{i < N}`, then `∑_{i < N} X i` is integrable. In particular this holds for iid `X` and a stopping time `N` of their natural filtration.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_stopped_sum_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.37, Wald's stopped-sum identity under the past/future independence condition: under the hypotheses of `integrable_stopped_sum`, `𝔼 ∑_{i < N} X i = 𝔼 N · ∫ x dP`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ofReal_mul_measure_exists_le_supermartingale_le_one
declarations.doc: Finite-horizon maximal bound `c · P(max_{k ≤ n} M_k ≥ c) ≤ 1` for a nonnegative supermartingale with `M_0 ≤ 1`, by optional stopping at the capped hitting time of `[c, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measure_iSup_supermartingale_ge_le
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.38: infinite-horizon Ville inequality, including a supremum not attained. For a nonnegative supermartingale `M` with `M 0 ≤ 1` and every `α > 0`, `P(sup_n M_n ≥ 1/α) ≤ α`; the bound is trivial for `α ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_mul_measureReal_exists_le_abs_sum_le
declarations.doc: **Kolmogorov's maximal inequality** for independent, centred, square-integrable variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_sum_shift
declarations.doc: For independent standardized variables, a block sum of length `n` has second moment `n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_mul_measureReal_exists_le_abs_sum_shift_le
declarations.doc: Kolmogorov's maximal inequality for a block of `r` standardized independent variables.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sum_randomIndex_sub
declarations.doc: Anscombe's comparison: when `N n / n → k` in probability, the partial sum at the random index `N n` differs from the partial sum at `⌈k n⌉` by `o_P(√⌈k n⌉)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_mul_sub_self
declarations.doc: If `W n` converges in law and `R n → 1` in probability, then `R n W n - W n → 0` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInMeasure_sqrt_ceil_div
declarations.doc: If `N n / n → k > 0` in probability, then `√(⌈k n⌉ / N n) → 1` in probability.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_sqrt_mul_sampleAverage_sub
declarations.doc: The standardized sample average at a fixed sample size is measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_random_sampleAverage
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.42: Anscombe's theorem for an observation-dependent random sample size. For iid observations with positive (hence finite) variance `σ²` and random sample sizes `N n` with `N n / n → k > 0` in probability, `√(N n) (X̄_{N n} - m) / σ ⇒ N(0, 1)`. No independence between `N n` and the observations is assumed. On the event `N n = 0` the statistic is `0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearProcess
declarations.doc: The two-sided linear process `X_t = ∑_j ψ_j Z_{t-j}`, as a pointwise series.

declarations.name: CKSD.transferFunction
declarations.doc: The transfer function `∑_j ψ_j e^{-ijx}` of a two-sided filter.

declarations.name: CKSD.linearProcessSpectralDensity
declarations.doc: The spectral density `σ² |∑_j ψ_j e^{-ijx}|² / (2π)` of a linear process with innovation variance `σ²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.periodogram
declarations.doc: The periodogram `I_n(x) = (2πn)⁻¹ |∑_{t<n} X_t e^{-itx}|²` of `X_0, …, X_{n-1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.nearestFourierFrequency
declarations.doc: The Fourier frequency `2πk/n` nearest to `x`, with `k` the rounded value of `nx/(2π)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsLagWindow
declarations.doc: A lag window: an even function with `w 0 = 1`, `|w| ≤ 1`, vanishing outside `[-1,1]`, continuous at `0` and continuous on `[-1,1]` off a finite set (this contains the piecewise continuous windows).

declarations.name: CKSD.lagWindowEstimator
declarations.doc: The lag-window spectral estimator `(2π)⁻¹ ∑_{|h| ≤ r} w(h/r) γ̂(h) e^{-ihx}`, written with `γ̂(-h) = γ̂(h)` as a cosine sum.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_periodogram_div_spectralDensity
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.6: periodogram ordinates at Fourier frequencies nearest to fixed frequencies in `(0, π)`, divided by the spectral density, converge jointly in law to independent standard exponential variables, for a linear process with absolutely summable coefficients and iid innovations of finite positive variance. Positivity of the spectral density is needed only at the fixed frequencies. The non-consistency corollary is not restated.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_lagWindowEstimator_moments
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.6: asymptotic mean and variance, and mean-square consistency, of a lag-window spectral estimator for a linear process with `∑ |ψ_j| |j|^{1/2} < ∞` and iid innovations with finite fourth moment, when the truncation point `r` satisfies `r → ∞` and `r/n → 0`. The window is assumed continuous at `0` (see `IsLagWindow`). The condition `∑ |ψ_j| |j|^{1/2} < ∞` implies absolute summability of `ψ`, and positivity of the spectral density is not needed.

declarations.name: CKSD.infDist_past_sq_eq_kolmogorov
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.16: Kolmogorov's (Szegő's) formula for the one-step prediction error of a centred weakly stationary sequence from its infinite past. Here `X` lies in a complex inner-product space, `⟪X s, X t⟫ = γ(t - s)` (`IsWeaklyStationary`), the spectral measure `F` lives on `(-π, π]`, and `f` is the density of its absolutely continuous part. The value `0` is taken exactly when `log f` fails to be integrable or `f` vanishes on a set of positive measure, i.e. when `∫ log f = -∞`.

declarations.name: CKSD.arPolynomial
declarations.doc: The autoregressive polynomial `φ(z) = 1 - ∑_{i=1}^p φ_i z^i`.

declarations.name: CKSD.maPolynomial
declarations.doc: The moving-average polynomial `θ(z) = 1 + ∑_{j=1}^q θ_j z^j`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armaSpectralShape
declarations.doc: The ARMA spectral shape `g(x; β) = |θ(e^{-ix})|² / |φ(e^{-ix})|²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lastArCoefficient
declarations.doc: The last autoregressive coefficient `φ_p`, read as `0` when `p = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.lastMaCoefficient
declarations.doc: The last moving-average coefficient `θ_q`, read as `0` when `q = 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armaAdmissibleParameters
declarations.doc: Causal, invertible, identifiable ARMA(p,q) parameters: `φ(z) θ(z) ≠ 0` on the closed unit disc, no common zeros, and `(φ_p, θ_q) ≠ (0,0)` (vacuous for `p = q = 0`).

declarations.name: CKSD.whittleObjective
declarations.doc: The Whittle objective `n⁻¹ ∑_j I_n(ω_j) / g(ω_j; β)` over the Fourier frequencies `ω_j = 2πj/n`, `0 ≤ j < n`; by `2π`-periodicity this equals the sum over `(-π, π]`.

declarations.name: CKSD.armaAsymptoticInformation
declarations.doc: The asymptotic information matrix `W(β) = (4π)⁻¹ ∫_{-π}^{π} ∇ log g ∇ log gᵀ` of ARMA estimation.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_whittleEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.17, Whittle-estimator case: for a causal invertible ARMA(p,q) process with iid, not necessarily Gaussian, innovations of variance `σ² > 0`, every measurable approximate minimizer of the Whittle objective over the admissible parameters (to within `(n+1)⁻²`) is strongly consistent, the Whittle innovation-variance estimator `2π · min` converges almost surely to `σ²`, and `√n (β̂ - β) ⇒ N(0, W(β)⁻¹)`. The process is any `L²`-bounded solution of the ARMA equations, which is the stationary causal solution. The Gaussian maximum-likelihood and least-squares estimators, and the autoregressive identity `W⁻¹ = σ² Γ_p⁻¹`, are not covered.

declarations.name: CKSD.twoPointPhaseLaw
declarations.doc: The phase law of the random field, uniform on the two points `{0, π}`; its first circular moment `𝔼 e^{iφ}` vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_exp_twoPointPhaseLaw
declarations.doc: The first circular moment of the two-point phase law vanishes.

declarations.name: CKSD.normalizedSpectralMeasure
declarations.doc: The spectral measure normalized to a probability measure, with the Dirac mass at the origin for the zero measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.real_mul_integral_normalizedSpectralMeasure
declarations.doc: Integrating against the spectral measure is the total mass times integrating against the normalized spectral measure.

declarations.name: CKSD.spectralRandomField
declarations.doc: The random-phase field `f(x)(w, φ) = √mass · e^{i(⟨w, x⟩ + φ)}` on a real inner-product space `E`, as a function of a frequency `w` and a phase `φ`; with `mass` the total mass of a spectral measure `F`, `w` drawn from `F` normalized and `φ` from `twoPointPhaseLaw`, its covariance is the Fourier transform of `F`.

declarations.name: CKSD.spectralRandomField_eq
declarations.doc: The random-phase field factors into a frequency part and a phase part.

declarations.name: CKSD.norm_spectralRandomField
declarations.doc: The random-phase field has constant modulus `√mass`.

declarations.name: CKSD.continuous_spectralRandomField
declarations.doc: The random-phase field is jointly continuous in location and randomness.

declarations.name: CKSD.spectralRandomField_mul_star
declarations.doc: The product `f(x) f(y)^*` of the random-phase field depends only on the frequency and on `x - y`.

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_stationary_field_of_spectral_measure
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.24, realization part of Bochner's theorem for random fields: for a finite measure `F` on a real inner-product space `E` there is a probability space carrying a square-integrable centred complex field `f(x)`, `x ∈ E`, with covariance `𝔼 f(x) f(y)^* = ∫ e^{i⟨w, x - y⟩} F(dw)` that is continuous in mean square. The mean-square differentiability criterion and the Matérn family are not covered.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsRandomCensoringModel
declarations.doc: The random censoring model: the pairs `(T i, C i)` of failure and censoring times are independent copies with law `F ⊗ C₀` (so failure and censoring are independent), and both laws are concentrated on `[0, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_sub_cdf_eq_measureReal_Ici_of_hasDensity
declarations.doc: A law with a Lebesgue density has no atoms, so `1 - F(s) = F[s, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_eq_integral_mul_of_hasDensity
declarations.doc: Integration against a law with a real density `f`: `∫ g dF = ∫ f g`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_ite_fst_le_snd_prod
declarations.doc: Under random censoring, `∫ 1{T ≤ C} φ(T) d(F ⊗ C₀) = ∫ f(s) φ(s) C₀[s, ∞) ds` for a bounded measurable `φ` and a density `f` of `F`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measureReal_le_min_prod
declarations.doc: The at-risk probability under random censoring: `P(min(T, C) ≥ s) = F[s, ∞) C₀[s, ∞)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_eq_zero_of_hasDensity_of_measure_Ici
declarations.doc: A density of a law concentrated on `[0, ∞)` vanishes almost everywhere on `(-∞, 0)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sq_integral_eq_two_mul_integral_mul_integral_le
declarations.doc: For an integrable `g` on `ℝ`, `(∫ g)² = 2 ∫ g(s) ∫_{r ≤ s} g(r) dr ds`: the square splits into the two triangles `r ≤ s` and `s < r`, which agree after swapping the variables because the diagonal is Lebesgue-null.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_sq_integral_mul_ite_le
declarations.doc: For an integrable measurable `k` and `c(u) = ∫_{s ≤ u} k`, the second moment of `c(x)` under a probability measure `P` is `2 ∫ k(s) P(x ≥ s) c(s) ds`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_ite_le_mul_eq_intervalIntegral
declarations.doc: For a density `f` of a law on `[0, ∞)` and `t ≥ 0`, `∫ 1{s ≤ t} f(s) G(s) ds = ∫_0^t f G`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_nelsonAalenEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.28, fixed-time Nelson–Aalen central limit theorem: in the random censoring model with a failure law `F` of density `f` and `P(min(T, C) ≥ t) > 0`, `√n (Λ̂_n(t) - Λ(t)) ⇒ N(0, v)` with `Λ(t) = ∫_0^t f / (1 - F)` and `v = ∫_0^t f / ((1 - F)² C₀[s, ∞))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.cdf_eq_intervalIntegral_of_hasDensity
declarations.doc: For a law on `[0, ∞)` with density `f`, `F(s) = ∫_0^s f` for `s ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: CKSD.one_sub_cdf_eq_exp_neg_integral_of_hasDensity
declarations.doc: For a law on `[0, ∞)` with density `f` and `F(t) < 1`, the survival function is the exponential of minus the cumulative hazard: `1 - F(t) = exp (-∫_0^t f / (1 - F))`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_kaplanMeierEstimator
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.29, fixed-time Kaplan–Meier central limit theorem: under the assumptions of `tendstoInDistribution_nelsonAalenEstimator`, `√n (Ŝ_n(t) - S(t)) ⇒ N(0, S(t)² v)` with `S(t) = 1 - F(t)` and `v` the Nelson–Aalen asymptotic variance (Greenwood's formula).

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_martingale_array_sum
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.1: triangular-array martingale central limit theorem. For each `n`, let `X n 0, …, X n (k n - 1)` be square-integrable martingale differences for the filtration `F n` (`X n j` is `F n (j + 1)`-measurable with `𝔼[X n j | F n j] = 0`). If `∑_j 𝔼[X_{n,j}² | F n j] → v` and `∑_j 𝔼[X_{n,j}² 1{|X_{n,j}| > ε} | F n j] → 0` in probability for every `ε > 0`, then `∑_j X_{n,j} ⇒ N(0, v)`. The limit `v` is automatically nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.garchCoeff
declarations.doc: The GARCH coefficient `b + a ε_{t-j-1}²`.

declarations.name: CKSD.garchTerm
declarations.doc: The GARCH product `∏_{j<n} (b + a ε_{t-j-1}²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.garchTerm_nonneg
declarations.doc: The GARCH products are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_garchTerm
declarations.doc: The GARCH product at time `t` is a function of the strict past of the noise.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_garchTerm_biSup
declarations.doc: The GARCH product at time `t` is measurable with respect to the noise at any set of times containing `t - j - 1` for `j < n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.ae_summable_garchTerm
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.18: when `a + b < 1`, the GARCH series `∑_n ∏_{j<n} (b + a ε_{t-j-1}²)` converges almost surely, for an iid noise with `𝔼 ε_0² = 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_tsum_garchTerm
declarations.doc: When `a + b < 1`, the GARCH series is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_tsum_garchTerm
declarations.doc: When `a + b < 1`, the GARCH series has mean `(1 - (b + a))⁻¹`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_tsum_garchTerm_past
declarations.doc: The GARCH series at time `t` is a function of the strict past of the noise.

declarations.name: CKSD.garchVariance
declarations.doc: The GARCH conditional variance `σ_t² = a₀ ∑_n ∏_{j<n} (b + a ε_{t-j-1}²)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.garchProcess
declarations.doc: The GARCH process `X_t = σ_t ε_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.garchVariance_nonneg
declarations.doc: The GARCH conditional variance is nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_garchVariance_past
declarations.doc: The GARCH conditional variance at time `t` is a function of the strict past of the noise.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_garchVariance
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.18: the GARCH conditional variance has mean `a₀ / (1 - a - b)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.integrable_garchVariance
declarations.doc: The GARCH conditional variance is integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.garchVariance_ae_eq
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.18: the GARCH recursion `σ_t² = a₀ + a X_{t-1}² + b σ_{t-1}²` holds almost surely.

declarations.name: CKSD.memLp_garchProcess
declarations.doc: The GARCH process is square integrable.

declarations.name: CKSD.covariance_garchProcess
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.18: the GARCH process with `a + b < 1` is weak white noise of variance `a₀ / (1 - a - b)`: `Cov(X_s, X_t) = a₀ / (1 - a - b)` if `s = t` and `0` otherwise.

declarations.name: CKSD.lagCountWeight
declarations.doc: The lag-counting weight `#{(i, j) : i, j < n, i - j = h} / n`.

declarations.name: CKSD.sum_sum_eq_tsum_lagCountWeight
declarations.doc: A normalized double sum over `i, j < n` of a function of `i - j`, regrouped by lag.

declarations.name: CKSD.lagCountWeight_nonneg
declarations.doc: Lag-counting weights are nonnegative.

declarations.name: CKSD.lagCountWeight_le_one
declarations.doc: Lag-counting weights are at most one.

declarations.name: CKSD.le_lagCountWeight
declarations.doc: The lower bound `(n - |h|)/n` for the lag-counting weight.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_lagCountWeight
declarations.doc: Lag-counting weights tend to one at each fixed lag.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendsto_mul_variance_sampleAverage
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.12, long-run variance from summable autocovariances: if the autocovariance `Cov(X_s, X_t) = γ(s - t)` is absolutely summable, then `n Var(X̄_n) → ∑_h γ(h)`, with `X̄_n` the mean of `X 0, …, X (n - 1)`.

declarations.name: CKSD.tendstoInDistribution_sample_autocorrelations
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.4, independent-observation case of Bartlett's theorem: for iid observations with finite positive variance, the normalized sample autocorrelations `√n ρ̂(h) = √n γ̂(h) / γ̂(0)` at lags `h = 1, …, m` converge jointly in law to independent standard normal variables. Finite variance follows from `0 < Var` (`memLp_id_two_of_variance_pos`).

declarations.name: CKSD.euclideanSelect
declarations.doc: Coordinate selection `x ↦ (x (σ k))_k` as a continuous linear map of Euclidean spaces.

declarations.name: CKSD.euclideanSelect_apply
declarations.doc: Coordinates of a coordinate selection.

declarations.name: CKSD.map_euclideanSelect_multivariateGaussian
declarations.doc: The image of a centred multivariate Gaussian law under the coordinate selection `x ↦ (x (σ k))_k`, with `σ` not necessarily injective, is the centred Gaussian law with covariance `S.submatrix σ σ`. This generalizes Mathlib's `measurePreserving_restrict₂_multivariateGaussian`; the selection is the matrix `(1_{σ k = i})_{k,i}`, and TauCeti's `map_affine_multivariateGaussian` applies.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPositiveSemidefiniteSequence
declarations.doc: A real sequence `γ` on `ℤ` is positive semidefinite (nonnegative definite) when it is symmetric and all its quadratic forms `∑_{i,j} a_i γ(t_i - t_j) a_j` are nonnegative; these are exactly the autocovariance functions of real weakly stationary processes.

declarations.name: CKSD.stationaryCovMatrix
declarations.doc: The stationary covariance matrix `(γ (t k - t l))_{k,l}` at times `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPositiveSemidefiniteSequence.posSemidef_stationaryCovMatrix
declarations.doc: A positive-semidefinite sequence gives positive-semidefinite covariance matrices at every finite family of times.

declarations.name: CKSD.stationaryGaussianFamily
declarations.doc: The finite-dimensional Gaussian laws with stationary covariance `γ`, indexed by finite sets of times.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPositiveSemidefiniteSequence.isProjectiveMeasureFamily_stationaryGaussianFamily
declarations.doc: The stationary Gaussian laws form a projective family.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPositiveSemidefiniteSequence.map_eval_projectiveLimit_stationaryGaussianFamily
declarations.doc: The Kolmogorov extension of the stationary Gaussian family has centred Gaussian finite-dimensional laws with covariance `γ (t k - t l)`, for any finite family of times, with repetitions allowed.

declarations.name: CKSD.IsPositiveSemidefiniteSequence.exists_stationary_gaussian
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.14, real Gaussian realization of a stationary covariance: for every positive-semidefinite sequence `γ` there is a shift-invariant probability measure on `ℤ → ℝ` whose finite-dimensional laws are centred Gaussian with covariance `γ(t_i - t_j)`; that is, `γ` is the autocovariance of a strictly stationary centred Gaussian process.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.past
declarations.doc: The closed linear span of `X s`, `s ≤ t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.hull
declarations.doc: The closed linear span of the whole sequence.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.past_mono
declarations.doc: The closed pasts increase with time.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.mem_past_self
declarations.doc: `X_t` lies in the closed past at time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.isClosed_past
declarations.doc: The closed past is closed.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.past_le_hull
declarations.doc: The closed past lies in the closed span.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.inner_eq_zero_of_forall_le
declarations.doc: A vector orthogonal to `X s` for every `s ≤ t` is orthogonal to the closed past.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.isClosed_hull
declarations.doc: The closed span is closed.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.mem_hull
declarations.doc: `X_t` lies in the closed span.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.coeffMap
declarations.doc: The coefficient map `c ↦ ∑ c_t X_t` into the closed span.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.shiftedCoeffMap
declarations.doc: The shifted coefficient map `c ↦ ∑ c_t X_{t+1}` into the closed span.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.denseRange_coeffMap
declarations.doc: The finite linear combinations of the `X_t` are dense in the closed span.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.norm_shiftedCoeffMap
declarations.doc: Under a stationary Gram matrix, shifting the coefficients preserves norms.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.exists_bound_shiftedCoeffMap
declarations.doc: The shifted coefficient map is bounded by the coefficient map.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.shiftIsometry
declarations.doc: With a stationary Gram matrix, the shift `X_t ↦ X_{t+1}` is a linear isometry of the closed span.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.shiftIsometry_apply
declarations.doc: The shift isometry sends `X_t` to `X_{t+1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.shift
declarations.doc: The shift extended by zero on the orthogonal complement of the closed span.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.shift_apply_of_mem
declarations.doc: On the closed span, the shift is the shift isometry.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.shift_apply_X
declarations.doc: The shift sends `X_t` to `X_{t+1}`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.inner_shift_shift
declarations.doc: The shift preserves inner products on the closed span.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.shift_mem_past
declarations.doc: The shift maps the closed past at time `t` into the closed past at time `t + 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.inner_shift_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The shift of a vector of the closed span orthogonal to the closed past at time `t` is orthogonal to the closed past at time `t + 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.proj_eq_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The orthogonal projection is characterized by membership and orthogonality.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.proj_of_mem
declarations.doc: The projection fixes the closed past.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.proj_proj
declarations.doc: Tower property of the projections onto the closed pasts.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.innov_mem
declarations.doc: The innovation at time `t` lies in the closed past at time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.inner_innov_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The innovation at time `t` is orthogonal to the closed past at time `t - 1`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.inner_innov_innov
declarations.doc: Innovations at different times are orthogonal.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.sub_proj_eq_smul_of
declarations.doc: One step of the innovations decomposition, for a vector `e ≠ 0` in the closed past at time `t`, orthogonal to the closed past at time `t - 1`, with `X_t - e` in the latter: for `x` in the closed past at time `t`, `x - P_{t-1} x` is the component of `x` along `e`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.sub_proj_eq_smul_innov
declarations.doc: One step of the innovations decomposition: for `x` in the closed past at time `t`, `x - P_{t-1} x` is the component of `x` along the innovation at time `t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.innov
declarations.doc: The innovation `X_t - P_{t-1} X_t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.Wold.eq_apply_zero_of_succ

declarations.name: CKSD.exists_wold_decomposition
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.2, Wold decomposition of a weakly stationary sequence `X` in a real Hilbert space. Let `P t` be the orthogonal projections onto the closed pasts `past X t` and `e t = X t - P (t - 1) (X t)` the innovations, with `e 0 ≠ 0`. There are coefficients `a` with `a 0 = 1` and `∑ a_j² < ∞`, and a sequence `V` lying in every closed past (the remote past) and orthogonal to every innovation, such that `X t = ∑_j a_j e (t - j) + V t`.

declarations.name: CKSD.rangePartialSum
declarations.doc: Partial sums of a finite coordinate vector indexed by `range n`, truncated at `k`.

declarations.name: CKSD.measurable_rangePartialSum
declarations.doc: Truncated partial sums of a finite coordinate vector are measurable.

declarations.name: CKSD.rangePartialSum_restrict
declarations.doc: Up to the length of the vector, truncated partial sums of the restriction of a sequence are its partial sums.

declarations.name: CKSD.integral_stopped_exponential_eq_one
declarations.doc: GAPS 106.41: Wald's fundamental stopped exponential identity at a first exit time. Let `Z` be iid with law `law`, `S_k = ∑_{i < k} Z_i`, and let `t` be such that `exp (t z)` is `law`-integrable with mean `m(t) ≥ 1`. If `N` is a measurable, finite-valued first exit time of `S` from the open interval `(a, b)` (almost surely `S_k ∈ (a, b)` for `k < N` and `S_N ∉ (a, b)`), then `exp (t S_N) / m(t)^N` is integrable with mean one. The finite-valued time `N` is a measurable version of the almost surely finite first exit; its existence is a hypothesis.
